prs.title: client: mDNS discovery prefers the daemon address on the local subnet
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's automatic search for telescope rigs now shows an address that actually works from your network. Before, a Raspberry Pi running its own Wi-Fi hotspot could show up on the connect screen with its hotspot address, which never connects from the home network. Now the app gathers all of a rig's addresses and keeps the ones on the same local network as your computer, falling back to listing all of them if none match. The diff also updates the setup guide to say tapping a discovered rig is now fine, and it notes known gaps as follow-ups: virtual-machine or Docker network setups can still hide the right address, and the new address-gathering step has no automated test yet.

prs.title: test: cross-driver contract sweep, tier 1, with a registration gate (#571)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds one shared set of standard checks that every supported device driver now runs through, in place of copies of the same tests scattered across drivers. It also adds an automatic check that fails the build if a new driver is added without being included. The shared checks turned up real bugs, and those are fixed: some telescope mounts and rotators sent back the wrong kind of error when disconnected, when asked for a command they don't support, or when given an invalid angle. One remaining issue is logged for later: four mounts still report whether they are parked even while disconnected. Checks that need a connected device will come in a follow-up.

prs.title: ci: layering gate counts vendor includes in AlpacaHTTP and catalog schema files
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds an automatic build check that stops the web server layer and the new device catalog from picking up any more direct ties to individual vendors' code. The current count (40) is locked as a ceiling. It can only go down as later work removes those ties. Only tooling and docs change; the app itself does not. Maintainers still need to make the check required in the repository settings.

prs.title: [P2] Device catalog: core types, DeviceCatalog class and unit tests over a stub descriptor
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Lays the groundwork for a new device catalog: one central place that describes each kind of device, checks and cleans up its settings, and creates it. New settings from users are rejected if invalid, while saved settings are repaired with a warning so the device still loads. Secrets like API keys are hidden when settings are displayed. Nothing uses it yet, so users see no change, and the PR includes tests for the new code.

prs.title: test(router): pin the route table and rejections; build the device and setup route regexes once (#646)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds tests that lock down every request the server accepts for each device type and the exact error it returns for bad requests. Any accidental change to either now gets caught. The new tests also exposed a speed problem: the server was redoing slow setup work on every device request. That is now done only once, making those requests about 15 times faster with no change in behavior. The description admits this goes beyond the original tests-only plan.

prs.title: test: round-trip every (vendor, device) config from both sources (#647)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds tests only. They confirm that every supported vendor-and-device setup is saved and loaded back the same way, whether it was created through the app or read from the saved file at startup. They also lock in how odd or invalid settings are handled today, so future fixes show up as deliberate changes. No app code changes.

prs.title: test: pin Sky-Watcher sync off the pole, consecutive flips, the HA 0 side change, and plate-solved southern rows
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds Sky-Watcher mount tests for the southern hemisphere: a sync followed by moving away and back, repeated flips across the meridian (the north-south line overhead), and the mount switching sides when a target crosses that line. Tests also compare the pointing math against 14 photos from a real telescope session whose actual sky positions were measured from the images. The mount's documentation now marks southern flip handling and sync as confirmed on real hardware. The driver itself does not change.

prs.title: docs(gphoto): Canon EOS 250D ConformU report (#611)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Canon EOS 250D is now listed as a tested, fully passing camera for the DSLR/mirrorless driver, backed by a clean run of the standard compatibility checker on a Raspberry Pi 5. No driver code changed, only the report and documentation. The docs now note that this camera only works with the lens switched to manual focus, because with autofocus on every capture fails. Long exposures on this body are still being tracked separately.

prs.title: docs(gphoto): Canon EOS 70D ConformU report (#637)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Canon EOS 70D is now listed as a tested, fully passing camera for the DSLR/mirrorless driver, based on a clean compatibility-checker run on a Raspberry Pi 5. No driver code changed. The docs now record practical setup notes: the mode dial must be on M, exposures top out at 30 seconds, and a Raspberry Pi 3 is too slow to pass the checks with this camera. It also tidies the list of confirmed pixel sizes to include the earlier Canon EOS 4000D.

prs.title: fix(gphoto): show "DSLR / Mirrorless" instead of the library name in user-visible text
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The DSLR/mirrorless camera option now shows up to users as "DSLR / Mirrorless" instead of mentioning "gphoto2", the name of a software library that means nothing to most users. The change covers the add-device menu, the settings heading, default camera names and error messages. A connected camera still shows its own model name. Developer-facing notes now use the library's correct name, and new tests check that the library name no longer appears in what users see.

prs.title: chore(skill): review-note follow-ups from #1101 + two PORT_TODO entries
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal cleanup of the team's developer helper tools, following up on review notes from #1101. The helper programs are now kept in a private folder instead of a shared temporary one, which closes a small security gap. The test virtual machine now stops clearly when a package install fails, and it still starts when some optional network ports on the Mac are already in use. It also adds two to-do notes, including a known problem where a fresh server install keeps crashing until a storage folder is created.

prs.title: docs: device-catalog and task-clock, CONTEXT.md glossary, module names (#633)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This is mostly internal documentation. It adds a glossary that defines terms contributors often mix up, two new design decision records describing planned changes to how devices are set up and how the software handles waiting and timing, and an overview of six planned internal building blocks. It also widens the automated documentation checks so broken links or stale file references in the new glossary and the architecture page get caught. Nothing changes for users of the software.

prs.title: chore: add /ara-pr-investigation and /ara-sbc-vm skills + fresh-profile Tonight's Sky test
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds two internal helper tools for the team's AI assistant. One investigates a contributor's pull request from start to finish, including running the app and taking screenshots, but it only makes recommendations and never merges or comments. The other runs a virtual Raspberry Pi on a Mac so server builds can be tested without real hardware. It also adds a test confirming the "Tonight's Sky" panel suggests targets for a new user in every month, and it records a server startup problem found along the way for a later fix. Nothing changes for end users.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine internal update that moves the project's automated tooling to newer versions: the AI code-review helper and the automated security scanner. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 1 update
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine internal update of a small outside component the server uses for its interactive API documentation page, moving it up two minor versions, with the third-party license list updated to match. Nothing should change for users.

prs.title: client: Run toolbar keeps Delete and friends reachable on narrow screens
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Run tab's toolbar now adapts to screen width, so on phones, portrait tablets or half-width windows the Delete, Validate and Export buttons no longer vanish off the edge. Run, Pause, Skip and Abort always stay visible (as icons with tooltips on a phone), and whatever doesn't fit moves into a "More" (⋯) menu. The status text steps aside when space is tight. New tests check the layout down to very narrow screens, though the author has not yet tried it by hand on a real phone or a shrunk window.

prs.title: fix(telescope): an async slew that fails after the initiator returns now surfaces through Slewing (#575)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: When a telescope was told to move to a target and the move then failed in the background, the software used to report "not moving," which looks the same as a successful arrival. Now, for Sky-Watcher, SynScan, iOptron, Celestron and ZWO mounts, the failure is kept and reported as an error the next time the app checks whether the telescope is moving. The error clears once the user starts a new move, aborts, or reconnects. The author says some similar cases are still open, including parking, homing and a Celestron timeout, and that ZWO's Abort now also cancels a move that is still being set up, which goes slightly beyond the original issue.

prs.title: Reject NaN in telescope driver range checks (six vendors) (#627)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Telescope drivers for six mount brands now reject invalid "not a number" values for target positions, site location and elevation, and guiding speed. Before, those values slipped past the range checks and could be stored or even sent to the mount. This is a safety fix that works alongside an earlier change catching such values at the front door. A few spots are left for later, including some Bisque checks and Sky-Watcher target settings handled in another pull request.

prs.title: Stop a moving telescope axis when the client goes silent (#547)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds a safety watchdog: if a telescope is moving and no app has contacted it for 30 seconds (for example because the controlling app crashed or the network dropped), the bridge stops the mount and logs an error, while keeping the connection up so a returning app can see what happened. Normal tracking and guiding never trigger it, and a long move the app is still waiting on doesn't count as silence. The 30-second limit can be changed or turned off in settings. It covers every telescope brand and has been tested in software, but not yet on real hardware.

prs.title: docs(gphoto): Canon EOS 4000D ConformU report (#611)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Canon EOS 4000D is now listed as a tested, fully compatible camera, the first Canon model on the list. A user ran the standard compatibility test on a Raspberry Pi 5 and it passed with no errors or warnings. No camera code changed. The PR also adds an automatic check that stops the internal notes from falling out of sync with the list of tested cameras.

prs.title: fix: DeviceState returns the empty list when disconnected
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: When a device is disconnected, its status report is now completely empty, as the ASCOM standard requires. Before, it still returned a timestamp, and some devices also returned made-up default values. This applies to all ten device types. The behaviour of connected devices is unchanged. Many existing tests were updated to expect the empty report, and new tests were added. It was checked only with automated tests, not on real hardware.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): one pulse task per axis so an RA pulse no longer cancels a running Dec pulse (#620)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a serious guiding bug on Sky-Watcher mounts. If a guide nudge on one axis arrived while the other axis was still being nudged, the first axis could be left moving on its own while the software reported that nothing was moving. Each axis now keeps track of its own nudge, so one axis no longer cancels the other. Overlapping guide requests are also handled one at a time. The PR notes one smaller, older timing edge case that is still there; an existing automatic retry covers it.

prs.title: Router: reject NaN/inf, wrong-verb requests and oversized device numbers before the driver (#574)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The server now rejects three kinds of bad requests before they reach a device. First, number values like "nan", "infinity" or hex notation are refused; before, a "nan" coordinate could start a real Sky-Watcher slew. Second, a request sent with the wrong method (for example, trying to write a read-only setting) now gets a clear error instead of a misleading "not implemented" reply. Third, device numbers too large to be valid are refused; before, some of them silently wrapped around to a different device. The Sky-Watcher driver also got its own extra check against these invalid numbers, but other mount drivers still lack it and are tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): IsPulseGuiding follows the pulse's real end (#559)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: On Sky-Watcher mounts, the "is guiding" indicator now turns off when the guide nudge actually ends, not about a second later. It also no longer turns off by mistake when one nudge quickly replaces another while the mount is still moving. This should help autoguiding software, which relies on this indicator. It is one half of a larger issue; the other half is handled in #616.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): retransmit a lost :K/:L stop reply on serial (#559)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: On Sky-Watcher mounts connected by cable, a lost "stop" message is now sent again quickly, up to three times. Before, a lost stop let a guide nudge run about a full second too long. Only stop messages are resent, because sending them twice is harmless; other commands still get one try. Links set up as slow keep their longer wait. This does not fully close the related issue, since the guiding indicator part is handled separately.

prs.title: docs: hand controller setup notes for the SynScan and Sky-Watcher direct drivers
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds two setup warnings to the supported-drivers guide, based on testing with an EQM-35 Pro mount. For the SynScan driver, the hand controller's date, time, time zone and location must be correct, and the mount must be switched on at its home position; otherwise the mount can report the wrong side of the pier. For the Sky-Watcher direct driver, users should not use the hand controller and this driver without restarting the mount in between, because the hand controller shifted the mount's stored position by 90 degrees and could make a 'go home' command drive it the wrong way. Documentation only.

prs.title: client: the planetarium works on Android and iPad tablets (JS on, touch zoom, FOV guard)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The planetarium sky map now works on Android and iPad tablets. On Android it was stuck on 'Loading planetarium…' because the built-in web view had scripts switched off. On both platforms, a pinch could zoom the sky out into a broken 'tunnel' view, so the app now snaps the view back to a usable zoom level and adds on-screen zoom in, zoom out and reset buttons for touch devices. The change also records several follow-up problems found along the way, including that the only automated test for this page no longer runs against it.

prs.title: Let FakeSkyWatcherMount answer a real zero to :s, as the EQ-AL55i Pro does (#306)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test-only change: the simulated Sky-Watcher mount used in tests can now tell apart a mount that rejects the 'steps per worm' question and one that answers it with zero. The EQ-AL55i Pro model now answers zero, which matches a real reading from an owner's mount. A new test checks the answer for all three simulated mount models. The real driver does not change.

prs.title: packaging: allow AF_NETLINK so equipment auto-detect works on a packaged Pi
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes equipment auto-detect on Raspberry Pi installs that use the official package. It had never worked there, because the server's security sandbox blocked the kind of network access needed to list the Pi's network connections before searching for devices. The sandbox now allows that access, and the package build refuses to produce a package if the setting is missing. The trade-off is that the service can now read, but not change, the network configuration. Existing installs get the fix on their next upgrade, or through a one-line manual override.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of three automated build tools (the AI code-review helper and the security scanner) to newer versions. No change to the product.

prs.title: client: USB GPS dongle on the computer running the app (time + site to the rig)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now plug a USB GPS receiver into the laptop or desktop running the app instead of into the Pi, which frees a USB port on the rig. A new 'GPS on this computer' setting reads the receiver and sends the exact time and the observing location to the rig, and the server trusts it as much as a receiver plugged into the Pi. 'Fill from GPS' now uses this receiver first. If the setting is off, it also searches for a receiver and switches the setting on when it finds one. This works on desktop computers only, and it was tested with a real receiver on a Mac sending its location to a Pi.

prs.title: plate-solve: a fresh Pi can solve — astap-cli dependency, correct binary, database dir via -d
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Plate solving, the step that works out where the telescope is pointing from a photo, now works on a freshly installed Pi. Before this, nothing installed the solving program, the settings pointed at the wrong program name, and the solver was never told where its star catalog lives, so polar alignment and centering could not solve at all. The install now pulls in the solver automatically, uses the correct program name, and points it at the star catalog folder. The large star catalog (about 1.7 GB) is still a one-time manual download, and people who already have saved settings keep the old wrong program path until they change it.

prs.title: guider: supervise the real openastro-guider unit; push the param name PHD2 actually has
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now watch and restart the guiding program on the Pi, and the guiding strength settings actually reach it. It had been looking for the guider under an old name that no longer exists, so crash recovery and the Restart button quietly did nothing. It also sent the strength setting under a name the guider does not recognize, so that setting was rejected every time. The install now includes a narrow permission that lets the app start or restart only the guider. A known side effect: if an admin deliberately stops the guider during a session, the app will now try to restart it, which is noted for follow-up.

prs.title: packaging: the Pi install ships the SOFA/NOVAS31 astrometry natives
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Pi install now includes two astronomy math libraries it needs but never actually shipped. Without them, slews quietly used slightly wrong coordinates, and features like altitude and sun/moon conditions, meridian flips and polar alignment would crash the first time they ran. The build now produces these libraries for the Pi, refuses to make an install package without them, and the app says in its first log lines whether they loaded. Automated checks also confirm they load on the Pi's system.

prs.title: camera: frames carry the mount's RA/Dec in their FITS header
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every photo taken while a mount is connected now records where the telescope was pointing. Until now no photo saved this information, so later plate solving always had to search the whole sky blind, and stacking software could not group manually aimed shots by target. Positions are converted to the standard star-chart reference when possible; if the math libraries are missing, the photo records the mount's own position and clearly says so.

prs.title: camera: plate-solve centering can take its exposure
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automatic centering on a target can now take its test photo; before this it failed right away with a "not ported" error. That had broken the Center and Rotate sequence step, the centering button, recentering after a meridian flip, and the safety recenter. It reuses the same quick capture that autofocus uses, and these test photos are not saved to the library. Bad plate-solving exposure or binning settings now show a clear message up front. A few other rarely used capture paths still are not supported, and this has not yet been tried on real equipment under the sky.

prs.title: guider: sequences drive the live PHD2 mediator, not the headless stub
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imaging sequences now actually control the guider. Before, sequences were wired to a placeholder that did nothing, so stop-guiding and dithering reported success without happening, and guiding was never paused and resumed around a meridian flip. This is a one-line wiring fix that connects sequences to the real guider.

prs.title: sequencer: run ETA follow-ups: blend order, item sets, side effects, per-tick cost (#1080)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The time-remaining figure shown while a sequence runs now comes straight from the sequencer, and the app only falls back to its own rough guess when the sequencer sends nothing. That estimate is also more honest. Blocks that are turned off no longer count toward the total, and steps that run side by side count only as long as the longest one. A zero-length exposure or a wait whose time has already passed no longer adds a made-up 15 seconds, and the figure is recalculated a few times a second at most instead of on every update, which saves work.

prs.title: telescope: bounded MoveAxis snap-up; speed presets respect the reported minimum (#1085)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Manual mount nudges no longer quietly run far faster than the user picked. Before, a very slow speed setting on a mount whose slowest speed is high could turn a gentle 1% nudge into a fast press-and-hold. Now a request more than 4 times slower than the mount can go is refused with a clear message, and the speed buttons skip settings the mount cannot do and offer its true minimum as the slowest option. Limiting the borrowed speed range for the second axis was left for later.

prs.title: filter wheel: profile policy to turn the first-connect home off (#1075)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: There is a new setting under Options → Filter wheel, "Park on slot 0 on first connect", so users can stop the filter wheel from moving itself to the first slot when it first connects. It is on by default, which keeps the current behavior, and it is saved with the user's profile. Turning it on partway through a session will not move a wheel that is already connected.

prs.title: Carry the sub-count remainder in FakeSkyWatcherMount, which modelled slow-rate motion ~21% short
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This is test-only and does not change the product. The simulated Sky-Watcher mount used in tests was losing about a fifth of its movement at slow guiding and tracking speeds because it threw away small fractions on each update. It now keeps those fractions, and two new tests check that guide pulses of different lengths move the expected amount on two mount models. This gives a trustworthy baseline for investigating a real user's report of short guide pulses.

prs.title: Add the Sky-Watcher EQ-AL55i Pro (mount code 0x09) as a known board
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Sky-Watcher EQ-AL55i Pro mount is now recognized by name instead of showing up as an unknown board. It also gets its own measured direction setting for the declination axis. Nothing changes in the northern hemisphere, but it should prevent a 12-hour pointing error in the southern hemisphere, which is based on geometry rather than an actual southern test. The test mount simulator also learned that this board has different step counts on its two axes, and a test was added for that.

prs.title: test(http): make join_or_abandon()'s fallback branches testable (#561)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This is an internal change so tests can reach the web server's rarely used backup steps for shutting down a background task when the normal method fails. The code was moved into its own piece with test-only controls that are not included in shipped builds, and new tests cover both backup paths. Behavior for users is unchanged. One of the three test goals in the original issue was attempted but not delivered, because the test could not tell working code from broken code.

prs.title: ci: run the ASan+UBSan pre-flight pass by default (#588)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The local pre-release check that contributors run now includes the extra memory-safety and undefined-behavior test pass by default, instead of only when someone asked for it. Before this, almost nobody ran that pass, which is how a test that failed every single time went unnoticed. Most of the PR updates developer instructions so people rebuild into their own separate folders rather than reusing the leftover build from that check. It also folds in two small unrelated doc fixes that remove stale mentions of a test framework the project no longer supports. The core script change itself was not visible in the trimmed diff.

prs.title: cooling fan: sequencer path, fail-closed states, fan-first on cooler-on, late-connect catch-up (#1076)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The safety rule that keeps the camera's cooling fan running while its cooler is on now covers more situations. Automated sequences can no longer switch the fan off while the camera is cooling. Turning the cooler on now starts the fan first and refuses to start cooling if the fan won't start. If the camera's cooler status can't be read, the system assumes it might be on and blocks fan-off. A fan controller that connects late is switched on automatically if cooling is already running. The unattended warm-up routine now always finishes by turning the cooler off and disconnecting the camera, even if one of its steps fails.

prs.title: filter wheel: in-flight home token; SwitchFilter waits for the slot list (#1079)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes two cases where the filter wheel could jump back to its default first slot right after a sequence had picked a different filter. A filter change now reliably cancels that automatic 'return to slot 0' move, even one already under way. A sequence's first filter change right after the wheel connects now waits up to about 6 seconds for the wheel's filter list, instead of being silently skipped. The docs note a tiny remaining timing window that is not fully closed.

prs.title: telescope: MoveAxis band snapping, secondary-axis fallback, time-based settle (#1072, #1078)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Manual mount nudges now adjust the requested speed to the nearest speed the mount actually supports, instead of only capping the top speed. Before, a slow preset below the mount's minimum was sent unchanged and rejected. A mount that never reports its north/south speeds now borrows the east/west ones, so north/south nudges keep working. One side effect, noted in the PR and tracked separately: on some mounts a small preset can now move much faster than its label suggests.

prs.title: mount pad: show the daemon's refusal of a nudge (#1071)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The mount's direction pad now shows a short error message when the server refuses a nudge, such as when the mount isn't connected or isn't ready yet. Before, the button did nothing and gave no explanation. The message appears only once per press, and releasing the button stays silent.

prs.title: fix: injectable root and fixtures for docs-drift check 7 (#452, #556, #583)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This is internal tooling work on the scripts that check the project's documentation for broken or outdated file references. The checks can now be tested against small sample repositories. Doing so exposed and fixed some false alarms, such as new docs being flagged before they were added to git. It also fixed a case where a check could silently scan nothing and still report success. No product behavior changes.

prs.title: ci: run ctest at twice nproc instead of nproc
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The automated test run now runs twice as many tests at the same time as before, because most tests spend their time waiting on simulated hardware rather than doing real work. On the build servers this roughly halved test time, from about 12 minutes to under 8. The extra load exposed one fragile test that could fail depending on timing, so this change also fixes that test. There is also a setting to dial the parallelism back on slower machines.

prs.title: ci: run the AlpacaCore unit tests in every build job (#586)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Three of the automated build checks had been silently skipping the main core test suite for months, because a test tool was missing, yet they still reported success. They now actually run those tests, and a check that finds no tests at all now fails instead of passing. Turning the suite on also stopped it from running twice per build, which roughly halved build time. One test that fails only under special debugging builds is now skipped there, and one test exposing a real, still-open telescope-mount bug (tracking can be left on when it should stop) is marked so it can't block builds until that bug is fixed.

prs.title: sequencer: run ETA published by the daemon, not re-derived by the client (#1068)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "time left" estimate shown while a sequence runs now comes from the server's sequencer instead of being guessed by the app from the saved plan. The server works it out from the live run, accounting for loops, finished steps and each step's own expected duration, and sends updated figures with progress updates. The app still blends this with how fast the run is actually going once enough steps have finished, and shows nothing if no estimate is available.

prs.title: guider wizard: proxy the Alpaca device-name lookup through the daemon (#1067)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When setting up the guider, the friendly equipment names (for example a specific camera model instead of a generic "Alpaca Camera" label) are now looked up by the server rather than by the user's laptop. This means the proper names appear even when the laptop cannot reach the telescope's local network directly. If the lookup fails, the generic labels are shown as before.

prs.title: filter wheel: first-connect home to slot 0 is daemon policy (#1066)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moving the filter wheel to its first slot when it is first connected is now handled by the server instead of the app, so it happens even with no app open, such as when equipment connects automatically at startup. It happens only once per session, so a reconnect after a brief dropout will never move the filter out from under a running sequence. If a user or sequence picks a filter first, that choice wins and the automatic move is cancelled.

prs.title: docs: record EQM-35 Pro over an EQDIR cable (FTDI FT232R, 9600 baud)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Documentation only: it records that the Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro mount works over a common EQDIR adapter cable, not just its built-in USB port. In testing on a Raspberry Pi the mount was found automatically, slewed and returned home accurately, and ran thousands of commands without errors. The notes also say this cable runs at a slower speed than the built-in port and that full certification testing was not done over it.

prs.title: cooling fan: daemon-side fan sync + fan-off interlock (#1065)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The rule that the camera's cooling fan must run whenever the camera's cooler is on is now enforced by the server itself, not just the app on the user's screen. Previously the automatic end-of-night shutdown, a second connected app, or a direct command could bypass it. Now every time the cooler is switched, the server turns the fan on or off to match, and it refuses any request to turn the fan off while the cooler is running. If the fan can't be set, the cooler change still goes through and a warning appears in the notifications. The author notes some gaps remain for a follow-up, including automated imaging sequences, which can still set the fan directly without this check.

prs.title: telescope: clamp MoveAxis rate server-side (#1064)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now caps the speed of manual telescope nudges at the fastest speed the mount says it supports, instead of relying only on the speed picker in the app. It refuses a nudge when it doesn't yet know a safe speed for that direction, including for a second or two right after connecting. It also now rejects requests for the telescope's rarely used third axis and nonsensical speed values. Stop commands are never blocked, so the mount can always be halted.

prs.title: feat(client): Android + iOS platforms, one-source launcher icons, shared discovery sweep
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now be installed on Android and iOS tablets and phones, and was tested on a Pixel Tablet and an iPad. It is sideload-only for now, with no app-store release yet. App icons for every platform are now generated from a single image. It also fixes a bug on all platforms where the app's automatic search for the observatory computer on the local network restarted too early and could miss it. Messages shown when filling in the site location from GPS now make sense on mobile devices.

prs.title: port-driver guards: run the §5 step 2 fence under bash against a throwaway origin
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal test-only change. It adds tests that actually run the automated development agent's branch-setup instructions against a throwaway copy of the code history, so mistakes like the one found in an earlier review get caught. It also adds a short note to the agent's instructions explaining these tests.

prs.title: port-driver: probe origin/<B> before the whole §5 branch split, fresh-create arm included
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal tooling fix for the automated development agent. Before starting work on a branch, it now checks whether an old copy of that branch was left behind on the shared server. It now does this check even when starting a completely fresh branch, and stops and asks a human instead of hitting a confusing upload failure later. The matching test and process documentation were updated too.

prs.title: port-driver: probe origin/<B> before both §5 arms; UserAgent reports real OS and architecture
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This makes two small internal fixes. The automated development agent now checks for a leftover copy of a branch on the shared server in more situations before reusing or replacing that branch, and stops for a human if the leftover would block its work. Separately, the identification string the software sends over the internet now reports the real operating system and processor type instead of wrongly claiming Windows. Nothing uses that string yet.

prs.title: xisf alpha cross-check + UserAgent + alignment guard; port-driver remote-ref and truncation Holds, wider probe pins
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Bundles several small fixes. Image files that carry an extra transparency channel are no longer mislabeled as broken; they now get the clearer message that this kind of image isn't supported yet. The app also identifies itself as OpenAstro Ara instead of N.I.N.A. when it talks to web services. On the internal side, the automated merge helper now pauses for a person when an old branch still exists on the server or when a list it checks may be cut off, and new tests make sure every copy of a key safety check stays identical.

prs.title: image(xisf): name OpenAstro Ara as creator, declare pixelStorage and block alignment, cross-check colorSpace vs channels
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Images saved in the XISF format now name OpenAstro Ara as the program that created them, instead of the old N.I.N.A. name. The same new name appears in the log file header. Saved files also state their internal layout more explicitly, so other programs such as PixInsight read them correctly. When opening a file, the app now rejects one whose color type doesn't match its number of channels, with a clear error message.

prs.title: image(xisf): zstd compression on both sides; bounds per spec on integer formats; frame-independent UInt32 scale with logged clipping
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds Zstandard, a modern compression method, for XISF image files. The app can now open Zstandard files made by PixInsight and can save them too. For now, saving with it is only possible through a profile setting, since there is no on-screen control yet. It also fixes a case where an odd but harmless setting made some files unopenable, and keeps brightness values consistent across all frames of a session so calibration frames line up.

prs.title: image(xisf): honour bounds, validate pixelStorage/colorSpace, reject multi-channel clearly, scale UInt32 writes by bit depth
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a serious bug where 32-bit XISF images saved by the app appeared almost completely black when opened by the app itself or by PixInsight; saved values now come back exactly. The file reader also handles more of the format correctly: it respects the brightness range stored in the file, rejects damaged or invalid settings with a clear error instead of crashing, and reports color images as unsupported instead of showing them scrambled.

prs.title: image(xisf): spec-correct sample converters, fatal checksums, inline/embedded blocks, Image.Tests project
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes opening and saving XISF image files much more reliable. Some images used to read back as garbage because of a math error in brightness scaling, and damaged files were only warned about and then used anyway; damaged files are now refused. The save side can no longer write a file whose layout overlaps itself. On Macs, choosing an unavailable checksum type now falls back to a working one instead of failing the save. The PR also adds 74 automated tests covering these files.

prs.title: port-driver: mirror the fork-head and chore/* probes in Python; fold the #1036 follow-up Notes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal only: updates the written instructions and automated tests for the AI tooling that reviews and merges pull requests. It narrows when that tooling stops to ask about project milestones, so routine or outside contributions no longer get stuck. It also makes sure a branch with the same name on someone else's copy of the project can't approve deleting one of ours. Nothing in the app itself changes.

prs.title: port-driver: retire a squash-merged local ref; hash-pin the guard mirror
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated porting assistant can now clean up a leftover local copy of a branch after that branch's work has already been merged, but only when the copy exactly matches what was merged. Anything else still stops and waits for a person. Before this, a leftover like that would permanently stall the assistant when it tried to reuse a branch name in a later phase. A new test also fails whenever someone edits these rules without re-checking the matching test logic. One change the description doesn't mention: brand-new branches are now always started from the latest shared version of the project, rather than from whatever local copy happened to be on the machine.

prs.title: ci: per-prefix inert allowlist, YAML-parse codeql.yml in tests, classify-step timeout
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal follow-up to the build-and-test system. The check that decides which tests a change needs now has its own two-minute time limit, so a stuck check can't mark the whole run as failed. The accompanying tests are more robust: one allows settings files only inside the issue-template folder, and another reads the security-scan configuration properly instead of depending on the order of lines in it. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: ci: skip CodeQL on prose-only PRs; harden the docs-only path gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The security code scan no longer runs on changes that only touch documentation or other prose, which saves time on those changes. Automatic scans of the main line of code and the weekly scan still cover everything. The step that decides which tests a change needs can no longer show up as a red failure when it hiccups. In that case it simply runs all the tests. It also now handles file names with non-English characters correctly, and a new check makes sure no real code or build files ever end up in the folders that are treated as documentation-only.

prs.title: docs: reconcile the driver, /pr-checker and playbook with the live CI and branch rules
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A documentation-only update that brings the written rules for the automated porting assistant and the PR-merging helper in line with how the build system and branch protections actually work today. The most notable rule changes are these: a PR that finishes a project phase must now get its milestone tag before it is merged, and branches that come from outside contributors are never deleted after merging. The description of the automated test setup was also corrected to match reality. No code or build files were touched.

prs.title: build: Bump file_picker from 12.3.0 to 13.1.0 in /client/openastroara_client in the pub group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: The client app's file-picker library was upgraded to a new major version, which required a small code change. When importing a profile, if the app can't tell how big the chosen file is, it now stops and shows "Couldn't read the selected file." instead of trying to continue. That new message is a small user-visible change and is noted in the changelog. The license list and a few comments and notes were updated to match.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is a routine automated update of three server-side libraries to newer patch versions: the API documentation page and the image-drawing library used to produce JPEG previews. No behavior changes are expected. The license list also records newer versions of the image library's Mac and Windows components, which the description doesn't mention, most likely because they come along automatically with the main update.

prs.title: ci: gate the .NET and client jobs on what the PR actually changed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated checks that run on each pull request now skip the slowest jobs when a change can't affect them. For example, a change that only touches the mobile/desktop app no longer triggers the ~19-minute server code analysis, and vice versa. This should noticeably cut waiting time for many PRs. The checks that must pass before merging are deliberately left unchanged, so a mistake in the new sorting logic can't let a broken change slip through. The team's internal guides were updated to explain the new skips.

prs.title: ci(client): supersede older Flutter bump PRs instead of stacking them
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The weekly automation that proposes Flutter updates now closes its older, unmerged update proposals when it opens a new one. Before this, one proposal piled up each week, all doing the same job. It only touches proposals it created itself, never ones opened by people or from outside copies of the project. If someone has added their own work to an old proposal, that work is kept rather than deleted. Proposals that are already piled up today will only be cleaned up the next time a new Flutter version is released.

prs.title: docs(playbook): reconcile tag mechanics and the branch allowlist with the driver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only update to the project's internal rulebook and the matching instructions for the automated assistant. It fixes the steps for marking completed project milestones, so the milestone marker lands on the right change and private backup markers are no longer published by accident. It also allows the assistant to work on its own maintenance branches, which previously caused it to stop mid-task. Two notes that flagged disagreements between the rulebook and the assistant's instructions were removed, because those disagreements are now resolved.

prs.title: Vendor ascom-alpaca-protocol skill and fix /driver-build contract drift
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds a detailed reference guide on the ASCOM Alpaca standard, the standard the project's telescope, camera and focuser drivers must follow, so the AI assistant uses it when building drivers. It also corrects several wrong statements in the driver-building instructions, including error codes, interface versions and which platforms need conformance testing. It now makes clear that the official standard, not existing drivers, decides how a device should behave. New automatic checks catch broken references in these guides and fail the build if the device specification changes without the reference guide being updated to match.

prs.title: test: exercise one-fault-per-episode, and share the poll helper
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a test-only change with no effect on the product itself. It adds a test that disconnects a device, reconnects it, and disconnects it again, confirming exactly one fault alert is raised each time. The earlier test could not actually check this. It also merges three near-identical "wait until something happens" helpers used by the tests into one shared helper, which has its own tests and gives clear messages when a wait times out.

prs.title: chore(skills): drive port-driver off master, not the retired port/ara
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated assistant that drives the porting work was still set up to use an old working branch that was removed back in June. Its first step would therefore have failed. It now works directly against the main branch, and the old separate promotion step is gone. Milestone markers are now added right before the final change of each phase merges, and that change is merged in a way that keeps the marker valid. The rulebook, the review command and the changelog were updated to match. New tests check the logic the assistant uses to tell unfinished work from work that has already been merged.

prs.title: Flip the Sky-Watcher 6 h home term with hemisphere and board sense (#458)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a Sky-Watcher telescope pointing bug where some mounts aimed half a sky away (12 hours off) depending on which side of the equator they were used. On an EQM-35 Pro in the northern hemisphere, a goto could send the telescope below the horizon while the software reported the correct target. The driver now accounts for both the hemisphere and how each motor board counts its movement. This is only confirmed for the EQM-35 Pro and Wave 150i; other Sky-Watcher boards keep the old behavior until someone measures them. If the driver can't identify the board at connect time, it now logs a clear warning that pointing may be wrong.

prs.title: ci: gate client-test at step level so its required contexts still report
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal build-system fix: a recent change meant to skip heavy checks on documentation-only pull requests left those pull requests stuck forever, unable to merge. The client test checks now always start but skip their actual work on docs-only changes, so they report success and no longer block merging. Related process docs were corrected to match.

prs.title: chore(skills): add the /pr-checker review-loop command
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds an internal tooling instruction file for the AI assistant. It lets the assistant work through open pull requests one by one, fixing review feedback, waiting for the automated reviewer, and merging each once it is clean. It stops and asks a human when something is unclear. It was adapted from a similar tool in the AlpacaBridge project, and nothing in the app itself changes.

prs.title: ci: skip the heavy build/test jobs on docs-only PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal build-system change: pull requests that only touch documentation no longer run the full ~20-minute build and test suite, which speeds up review of docs changes. Anything that isn't clearly documentation still runs everything, and any error in the detection step also falls back to running everything. Process docs were updated to explain the new rules. A follow-up (#1025) later found this left docs-only pull requests stuck and unable to merge.

prs.title: ci(client): watch the Flutter stable channel and open bump PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a weekly automated check that looks for new stable releases of Flutter, the toolkit the desktop client is built with. When a new one appears, it tests the client against it and opens a pull request to upgrade. Until now the Flutter version was only updated by hand, usually after something broke. Major version jumps are not automated and are just reported. Pull requests the check opens won't run the full test suite automatically unless a special access token is configured.

prs.title: fix(test): wait for the fault instead of racing the Error transition
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a test that failed randomly and blocked unrelated pull requests from merging. The test checked for a device-disconnect alert a moment too early, before the app had published it. It now waits for the alert to appear. The app's behavior is unchanged; only the test was fixed.

prs.title: docs(design): retire the remaining CodeRabbit-era instructions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal documentation cleanup that removes the last leftover instructions about CodeRabbit, the automated code reviewer the project stopped using in May. Guides that told contributors to set up or work around that tool now describe the current automated reviewer, which needs no setup and runs on every pull request. Dated historical records that mention CodeRabbit were intentionally left in place.

prs.title: chore(skills): point port-driver at the claude[bot] review gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updates the instructions the project's AI assistant follows when it builds and merges work on its own, so it waits for the current automated reviewer instead of the retired CodeRabbit tool. The main fix closes a loophole: the assistant could have merged changes based only on its own self-review while the real review was still running. Changes can now only be merged once a finished review of the latest version has signed off, and cases where no review can ever arrive are handed to a human. Only instructions and design documents changed, with no change to the app itself.

prs.title: build(client): update Flutter to 3.47.5 (#997)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the desktop app to a newer version of Flutter, its underlying toolkit, because the old version could not build the Mac app with the latest Apple developer tools (Xcode 27). Along the way it also fixes a mistake in the third-party license notices shipped with the server: one component had been labeled with the wrong license since July. The team reports all app tests pass and the Mac build works end to end. A planned automatic checker for future Flutter updates is not included and will come separately.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group across 1 directory with 6 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of the tools used by the project's build and review automation, including the Docker image build steps, the security scanner, and the automated code reviewer. No change to the app itself.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 12 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of a dozen server-side and testing libraries to their latest minor versions, with the bundled license notices updated to match. No intended change in behavior.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group across 1 directory with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of four libraries used by the desktop app, including the one that handles network requests and the embedded web view, with the license notices updated to match. The network library update includes an upstream fix that stops large downloads from piling up in memory.

prs.title: ci(review): port AlpacaBridge's injection hardening + rubric, move the bot to opus
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated code reviewer that comments on pull requests was hardened and upgraded. Before it starts reviewing, it now swaps in the main branch's copies of its own instruction and settings files, so a pull request can no longer quietly rewrite the reviewer's rules or sneak in commands that would run with its credentials. It also gets a clearer rulebook that separates real blocking problems from non-blocking suggestions, switches to a stronger AI model, and allows one more contributor's fork to trigger it. Because the reviewer refuses to review changes to its own setup, this change was checked by a person instead.

prs.title: GPhoto: fix Nikon bulb close failing and hanging the camera
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a serious bug where long exposures (over 30 seconds) on a Nikon D3300 opened the shutter but then failed to close it cleanly, returned no picture, and froze the camera until it was power-cycled. The driver now talks to the camera one setting at a time, the way the standard gphoto2 command-line tool does, and keeps checking in with the camera while the shutter is open. It also waits longer for the photo when the exposure is long, and always tries to close the shutter even if something goes wrong mid-exposure. Tested on real hardware with 60- and 300-second exposures and an early stop, and the docs now recommend turning off the camera's long-exposure noise reduction for astrophotography.

prs.title: Validate GPhoto Nikon D3300 on arm64 (ConformU 4.5.1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Nikon D3300 is now officially listed as a supported camera after passing the standard compatibility test suite on an ARM64 Linux board with no errors. It is the third Nikon body confirmed to work on the same setup, and no code changes were needed. The test report and supported-device documentation were updated.

prs.title: Add a fault-injection seam for the gphoto camera driver (#489)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Makes the DSLR camera driver testable without a real camera attached, by letting tests plug in a simulated camera and a simulated image decoder. This adds automated tests for connecting, reading camera settings, taking normal and long exposures, stopping an exposure, and handling bad images, none of which could be tested before. It is meant to change nothing for users. Along the way it fixed a few flaws in the new tests themselves, such as one test that could never fail and tests that quietly stopped checking anything after their first run.

prs.title: Sky-Watcher link health: latch a silent board, decide surviving motion at relink, fix a vacuous test guard
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Makes the Sky-Watcher mount driver notice when the mount stops responding, for example when it is powered off but the USB cable is still connected. Before, the driver kept reporting the mount as live and even showed moving coordinates. Now, after three unanswered requests in a row, it flags the connection as broken, and when the mount comes back it detects if the mount has reset itself. After a brief cable drop, the driver also decides whether to keep the mount moving (if the outage was under 5 seconds) or stop it. One limitation remains: after a reconnect, the usual 'stop moving this axis' command still does nothing against motion that survived the drop, so users need 'abort slew' to stop it. The PR also fixes a test that could never fail.

prs.title: Fix scoped INFO destroyed before CHECK in test_fake_pty_write.cpp
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test fix only. One test's error message about a timing failure was thrown away before it could appear in the failure report, and it could show a misleading stale value. The message now reaches the report correctly. No test results or user-facing behavior change.

prs.title: Stop documenting personal /triage, /wayfinder, /domain-modeling tooling
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal documentation cleanup with no effect on the shipped server. It removes the setup notes for three helper tools that one developer uses on his own machine. The project should not carry settings for those tools, and PR #540 in this same batch had added them. The one useful fact that remains is where issues are tracked, and it is now a single line in the main contributor guide. As the author points out, a safety check that catches broken or missing documentation links is now weaker. It can only notice if the whole folder disappears, and that gap is left for a separate issue.

prs.title: Fix HTTP server join-flag leak and joinable-thread destruction on a failed join
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a rare situation where the web server could freeze or crash while shutting down. If one of its background tasks failed to close cleanly, later stop requests could hang, or the program could abort. Now the server logs an error, lets that task go, and finishes shutting down normally. The downside is that it can no longer confirm the task has actually ended, and the updated notes admit this edge case is still not fully guarded. The PR also lets tests use any free network port instead of a fixed one, adds a regression test, and updates the design notes.

prs.title: Fix three unfalsifiable CI/pre-flight gates (#512, #513, #514)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal testing fix. Three automated checks could never actually fail, so they gave false confidence. One test could hang forever instead of reporting a problem, and another only checked a file as a whole instead of checking each test inside it. All three can now catch the problems they were built for, and the author showed each one failing when the bug was put back on purpose. It also tightens a timing-sensitive telescope test so it fails with a clear message rather than quietly passing, though its small safety margin remains and is tracked separately.

prs.title: Configure agent skills tooling
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal setup notes for AI coding assistants. They cover how to use the issue tracker, which labels to use, and where design notes live. The notes themselves say the tools they describe are not installed yet and most of the labels do not exist yet. It also widens a documentation safety check to cover the new notes. PR #557 in this same batch removed nearly all of this again.

prs.title: Fix telescope CanMoveAxis/AxisRates axis validation
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Telescope connections now reject bad axis requests with a proper error, in line with the ASCOM Alpaca standard. Before, if an app left out which axis it meant, the server quietly assumed the first axis. An impossible axis number, such as 5, also got a plain "no" or an empty answer instead of an error. Both now return a clear "invalid value" error across all seven supported telescope brands, even when the telescope is not connected. Error messages were also made consistent, and new tests cover each brand.

prs.title: Bundle docs-only fixes: issues 483, 486, 497, 518
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: A bundle of four small documentation corrections, with no code changes. The supported-hardware list now names test-tool version 4.5.0, with a warning about its unreliable timing results. The Sky-Watcher section is renamed so it covers the newer EQM-35 Pro mount as well as the Wave models, and an outdated to-do note is removed. The instructions AI assistants follow when updating hardware notes now say not to delete useful per-model details. Two changelog entries are also reworded so they accurately describe what those checks do.

prs.title: Release 4.0.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Version 4.0.0 of AlpacaBridge is officially released. It is a major release with nine new device drivers, more hardware confirmed working, and many fixes. It also has three changes that users must act on: the direct Sky-Watcher driver now needs a site location, the server's clock is now set from connected apps by default, and the web management page blocks certain requests coming from other websites. The code in this PR itself mostly updates the version number and release paperwork, adds plain-language release notes for the GitHub release page, and adds a helper that automates future releases.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automatic update of three tools used by the project's automated build and review system: the AI code-review bot and the security scanner. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: Add QHYCFW3 standalone USB filter wheel driver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge can now control a QHY CFW3 filter wheel plugged in directly by its own USB cable, instead of only through a QHY camera. In the web setup page, users pick whether the wheel is connected through the camera (the default, so existing setups are unchanged) or over USB. The first connection takes about 18 seconds because the wheel resets and re-homes itself, and the wheel's internal switch must be set to USB mode. It passed the standard compatibility test on real hardware, but not yet on the Raspberry Pi test setup. The PR also renames the upcoming release to 4.0.0 in the changelog and lists its breaking changes.

prs.title: Fix Q-Focuser link loss and sync connect/disconnect race (#527, #528)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If a QHY Q-Focuser is unplugged mid-session, AlpacaBridge now correctly shows it as disconnected, and reconnecting works without first switching it off manually. It also fixes a timing problem across several devices (iOptron focuser and power box, ToupTek and ZWO ASIAIR power switches, WeeWX weather) where a disconnect request arriving during a connect could be ignored, leaving the device connected when the user thought it was disconnected. The unplug fix was tested with simulated hardware; the real-hardware cable-pull test has not been done yet.

prs.title: Route pre-flight clean rebuilds through ccache (#529)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal developer tooling change: the pre-submission check script now reuses previously compiled code, so repeated full rebuilds run faster on developer machines. One code-analysis step deliberately skips this reuse so it keeps finding problems. No effect on users.

prs.title: Add QHY Q-Focuser focuser driver, ConformU 4.5.1 validated on arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now supports the QHY Q-Focuser (standard and High Precision models), which lets users control telescope focus from their astronomy software and set it up in the web page with auto-detection. It passed the standard compatibility test with no errors on a Raspberry Pi. The work also fixed a hardware quirk where the focuser's replies arrive one message late on a real USB connection, which would otherwise make it hang. At the time of this PR, unplugging the focuser mid-session left it still showing as connected. A later PR (#531) fixed that.

prs.title: Persist client-set site coordinates to the device's registered entry
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When an app sets a telescope's location (latitude, longitude or elevation), the bridge now saves it to that telescope's settings, so the location survives a restart. Before this, rigs that got their location from a phone's GPS or a GPS feed had to resend it every session, and Sky-Watcher mounts depend on it for correct pointing and tracking. A new per-mount "Learn site from clients" checkbox, on by default, lets owners of a precisely measured pier stop a phone's rougher GPS from overwriting it. The change also makes the settings file save safely when two requests arrive at once, blocks location changes from unrelated websites, and skips over hand-edited bad entries instead of failing; the real-rig restart check was still unticked at merge.

prs.title: docs: split agent guidance and record failure memory
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This reorganizes the project's guidance for AI coding assistants: the large shared guide is split into one file per hardware vendor plus shared core rules, and new records capture past incidents and design decisions (including three about Sky-Watcher EQMOD-style mount problems). Automated checks now confirm the new structure stays consistent. The description says no device behavior changed, but the diff also edits a number of driver, server and test source files that it doesn't explain; those parts were not visible here to confirm what changed in them.

prs.title: Validate QHY QHY5-III585M on arm64 (ConformU 4.5.1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The QHY5-III585M guide camera is now listed as a supported, tested camera after passing the standard compatibility checker on a 64-bit ARM Linux board with no errors or warnings. No code changed, since it already works with the existing QHY camera driver; this adds the test report and updates the supported-hardware list and changelog. One oddity: the saved report's header labels the device as a "Sky-Watcher Wave Mount", although the camera itself correctly identifies as the QHY5III585M in the results.

prs.title: Validate SVBONY SC571CC via ToupTek driver: ConformU 4.5.1 clean
prs.author: kern2011
prs.summary: The SVBONY SC571CC cooled color camera, a rebranded ToupTek ATR2600C, is now listed as supported after passing the standard compatibility checker on 64-bit ARM Linux with no errors or warnings. No code changed; it already works through the existing ToupTek driver. The PR adds the test report and new entries for both brand names in the supported-hardware list and changelog.

prs.title: Sky-Watcher direct driver: Connected follows the serial link (#445)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: On Sky-Watcher mounts connected directly by USB cable, unplugging the cable used to leave the mount showing as still connected, with every request failing on a confusing error; reconnecting after plugging it back in also silently did nothing. Now the bridge notices the unplug within one status check, shows the mount as disconnected, gives a clear "not connected" error, and actually reconnects when asked, which was confirmed on a real EQM-35 Pro. It also stops two configured mounts from interfering with each other's connection, and makes an app's disconnect request always clean up properly for every device type. The author notes one Sky-Watcher test that fails intermittently, but it fails the same way without this change.

prs.title: Report the host time zone and render the web UI clock in it
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The web page's header clock now shows the time in the time zone of the computer running the bridge, not the viewer's own zone, so it matches the times in the server's logs. The server now reports its time zone name, and the page falls back to the viewer's zone if the server can't determine one or the browser doesn't recognize it. A zone change on the server shows up on the next refresh. The check on a real rig set to a different zone from the browser was still unticked at merge.

prs.title: Add gphoto2 DSLR/mirrorless camera driver (Nikon D5300/D3200 validated)
prs.author: kern2011
prs.summary: The bridge can now control ordinary Canon, Nikon and Sony DSLR and mirrorless cameras as astronomy cameras, using free, open-source camera software instead of a manufacturer's private kit. It was tested on two real Nikon bodies (D5300 and D3200), which passed the standard compatibility test with no problems. Testing and review also found and fixed several bugs, including ones that could crash the software if a camera was disconnected at the wrong moment. The change also makes sending full-size images to client apps about five times faster for every camera brand, not just these new ones.

prs.title: Keep the dec-axis branch at the exact pole: decide the home term on the sign bit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a Sky-Watcher mount bug where pointing the telescope exactly at the celestial pole could make it report a position 12 hours off, and say it was on the wrong side of its mount. The mount's position sensor can't tell the two possible arrangements apart at that exact spot, so the driver now remembers which one it last moved to. Resets like homing, parking and reconnecting go back to the default, and new tests cover these cases. Only the reported position was wrong; the telescope itself pointed correctly.

prs.title: Make /driver-build ask for the test seam and the [stress] registration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updates the step-by-step instructions for building new device drivers so they now require tests that check the driver stays safe when many things happen at once. Before, a driver built by following the guide would ship without these tests, and an error message even suggested skipping them. The instructions and that message now say not to skip, and describe how to run the check locally. No driver code changed.

prs.title: Re-validate Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro with ConformU 4.5.1
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Re-ran the standard compatibility test on the Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro mount with the newer test version (4.5.1), this time on a Raspberry Pi with the mount plugged in directly. It passed with no errors, issues or timing problems, including measured checks for custom tracking speeds. The saved test report and docs were updated; no driver code changed.

prs.title: Answer get_connected() lock-free in the four wrapper-backed switch drivers
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Four power-box and ASIAIR switch devices (iOptron iMate PowerBox, ToupTek StellaVita, ZWO ASIAIR and ASIAIR Plus) can now answer "are you connected?" instantly, instead of sometimes waiting behind a connect or disconnect in progress. This makes them behave like the other drivers and removes a possible cause of the program freezing. An automated check will now fail if any of these four starts waiting again.

prs.title: Point the ZWO camera notes at the table instead of naming two of nine models
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Docs-only change to the ZWO camera section of the supported-hardware list. The old text named only two tested cameras, even though the table right above it lists nine tested models. It now simply points readers to that table, where each model links to its own test report.

prs.title: Clear Gemini driver state before the port close, and own the fakes' pty pair
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When you disconnect a Gemini focuser, flat panel, or power hub, the driver now marks itself disconnected and clears its stored firmware version before it closes the connection to the device. This means a failed close can never leave the driver claiming it is still connected. For the power hub, this also fixes a short window, up to about half a second, where the web page could show the device as disconnected but still display an old firmware version; a new test checks for this. Most of the change is to the test setup: six pretend devices used in testing now share one tidier piece of setup code that no longer leaks resources when setup fails.

prs.title: Add ZWO EAFN (EAF Robotic Focuser) ConformU 4.5.1 report
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The ZWO EAF Robotic Focuser (EAFN) is now listed as officially validated, with its own entry in the supported-hardware list and a passing ASCOM compatibility report (no errors, issues, or slow responses). It uses the same driver and settings as the existing EAF focuser, and the older EAF entry and report are left unchanged. No driver code changed; this is documentation plus the new test report.

prs.title: ci: allow kern2011 to trigger the review bot on fork PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds contributor kern2011 to the list of people whose pull requests from their own copy of the project can trigger the automated review bot. This is a one-line change to the build and review automation.

prs.title: Derive the RTC probe interval from the probe's rate limiter, and state HostClock's construction contract
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server regularly checks whether the machine has a hardware clock, and it must do so slightly less often than a separate built-in limit on those checks. Previously the two timings were separate hard-coded numbers that could quietly drift apart. Now the check interval is calculated from the limit, and a test enforces the relationship. It also adds a written note that setting up the clock component can be slow and must only happen at startup. Nothing changes for users; the timings stay the same.

prs.title: Pin both clock log ladders by level in test_routing.cpp
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tests only. New checks confirm that the messages the server logs about questionable system time are written at the right severity (for example, a warning rather than routine information), not just with the right wording. This covers the cases that had no tests before.

prs.title: Check the repo paths in the Cursor rule files, and fix the two that were stale
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated documentation check, which already verified file paths mentioned in the main contributor guide, now also checks the AI-assistant guidance files and the vendor SDK setup instructions. It also fails if a new guidance file is added without being checked. Running it found three out-of-date file paths, all fixed here; the PR title says two, but the change fixes three. This is internal and has no effect on users.

prs.title: Make the AGPL header form a CI check, and fix the two files that diverged
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated checks now fail a change if any of the project's own source files is missing the current, correct license notice at the top. Before this, the rule was only written down, and two recently added test files had slipped through with an older notice that left out the project's exact license terms and its permission to work alongside hardware makers' software kits. Those two files are fixed here, and the pre-submission checklist now just points to the automatic check. This is internal and changes nothing for users.

prs.title: Pair each TSan zero-test grep with the run it reads in check 8
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This tightens an internal consistency check that makes sure a stress-testing step runs the same way in the online build system and in the local pre-submission script. Previously the check only counted the steps, so a mix-up where a safeguard read the wrong run's results could slip past it. It now pairs each safeguard with the specific run it protects, and the check gained its own automatic self-test. The description says there is no self-test yet, but the code does add and run one. This is internal only, with no change for users.

prs.title: Re-validate ZWO ASI120MM Mini with ConformU 4.5.1
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The ZWO ASI120MM Mini guide camera was re-tested on a Raspberry Pi with the latest version of the standard compatibility checker, and it passed cleanly with no errors or timing problems. The new run also covers a newer set of tests that the old report never exercised. No driver code changed; this replaces the stored test report and updates the date on the supported-devices list.

prs.title: Warn once when a client UTCDate disagrees with a disciplined host on mounts that keep their own clock
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Five telescope mount drivers (OnStep, Celestron, SynScan, iOptron and ZWO AM) now log a single warning per connection when a connected app sends a time that is more than about two seconds off from the computer's own internet-synced clock. These mounts keep their own clocks and will still follow the app's time as before, but a badly set clock on the app side now shows up in the logs instead of silently throwing off pointing. Nothing else about the drivers' behavior changes, and new tests cover each of the five drivers.

prs.title: Guard every [stress] call individually, and close the race that exposed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The stress tests for all fifteen device drivers were reworked so each individual action is tested separately, instead of the whole test quietly stopping at the first error. Doing this let the tests reach code they had never reached before, and that exposed a real timing bug in the Celestron mount driver: two parts of the driver could read and change the same setting at the same time, which is now fixed. The test cleanup steps were also made more reliable so they no longer fail on drivers that are working correctly.

prs.title: Fix the Cursor rule files' uncompilable ZWO mock, misaligned CMake template and stale SDK paths
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This corrects the built-in guidance files that AI coding assistants use when helping write drivers, plus the instructions for where to put hardware makers' software kits. The old guidance included a ZWO testing example that could never have compiled, a build template that did not match the real one, and folder locations that were wrong. It now points to the testing approach the project actually uses and gives the exact folder layout for each vendor. The changes are documentation only, with no code changes.

prs.title: Wake the QHY polling workers on stop instead of sleeping through it
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Disconnecting a cooled QHY camera is now practically instant. Before, it could stall for up to about a second while a background temperature check finished a sleep it could not be woken from. That stall used up most of the time the ASCOM compliance tester allows for a disconnect. A stuck temperature check can also no longer hang a disconnect forever: the wait is now capped, matching how the camera's other background tasks already behave.

prs.title: Make the QHY seam safe before the [stress] registration lands
prs.author: joeytroy
