prs.summary: Test-only changes that make the simulated QHY camera safe to use in upcoming heavy connect/disconnect stress tests. The simulator could write past the end of a memory buffer, did not copy a real safety refusal the driver depends on, and could hold up a cancel request behind the very operation it was meant to cancel. All three are fixed. The PR also adds automatic checks that no simulated call quietly starts blocking, and a helper that sets up tests so their objects are always torn down in a safe order. The real camera driver itself is not changed.

prs.title: Count the calls a stress guard saw, and gate the whole idiom
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal test tooling. Stress tests now count how many calls actually ran, so a test that silently stopped doing anything can no longer report a pass. An automated check now requires every stress test to follow the full reporting pattern, and fifteen older test files are temporarily exempted until they are updated. The PR also fixes a bug in that check's own self-tests that had kept some rules from ever being exercised.

prs.title: Self-test check_conformu_reports.py and check-unicode.py so a broken gate cannot read as a pass
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal CI change. Two automated checks, one that validates ConformU compliance reports and one that scans source files for hidden or deceptive Unicode characters, now test themselves before they run. This means a broken check fails loudly instead of quietly reporting that everything is fine. The Unicode scan now also fails if it finds no files at all, and its success message states how many files it checked.

prs.title: Add the ZWO ASI533MC Pro ConformU report and list it as supported
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The ZWO ASI533MC Pro camera is now officially listed as supported, backed by a clean ConformU compliance report from a Raspberry Pi. No driver code changed; the existing ZWO driver already handled this camera. The team's internal notes also close out a long-running investigation into slow response times on Raspberry Pi: the slowness turned out to be a bug in version 4.5.0 of the ConformU testing tool, fixed in 4.5.1. A few small wording fixes to earlier Sky-Watcher notes are also included.

prs.title: Harden Sky-Watcher goto landing and tracking restart; validate EQM-35 Pro with ConformU
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Sky-Watcher mount driver now passes full ConformU compliance testing on an EQM-35 Pro. During testing, a mount once kept tracking at roughly double speed after a long slew. To guard against this, the driver now waits until the mount has truly stopped before calling a slew finished, and it checks the tracking speed afterward, restarting once and logging a warning if the speed is wrong. The timing used to aim slews slightly ahead of the moving sky is now learned from each mount instead of fixed values tuned on a different model. The testing guide also now requires accurate clock syncing (chrony), after small clock jumps caused false test failures. The description notes this PR also carries changes from an earlier, not-yet-merged PR (#441), and the diff shown here does not cover every part of that.

prs.title: Replace the host clock's hooks in place instead of swapping the object
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes a possible crash in how the server's clock-checking code gets swapped out for testing. Before, replacing it could delete something another part of the server was still using at that moment. Now only the pieces inside are swapped and the clock itself stays in place, so the clock's saved settings also carry over without extra handling. The swap is only used by tests, so real users are not affected directly, and new tests check it under heavy parallel load.

prs.title: Fix the Sky-Watcher direct driver's pointing model: the 6 h home offset and the southern RA sense
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a serious aiming bug in the Sky-Watcher direct mount driver: every goto was off by a quarter turn, and in the southern hemisphere tracking ran the wrong way. Automated conformance checks never caught it because the driver always agreed with itself; a user pointing at a real star did, and the fix was checked by moving a real mount to known positions. It also keeps tracking correct when the site latitude is changed across the equator while the mount is connected, and fixes a few cases where rate changes were silently dropped during guiding. The authors note that one part of the new model is based on measurements rather than theory, so northern Synta boards and southern Wave mounts may still point wrong until more hardware readings come in (tracked in #458).

prs.title: Answer NotConnected from the focuser TempComp and StepSize properties
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Five focuser drivers (Astroasis, iOptron iEAF, ToupTek, ZWO and Gemini) now answer "not connected" when asked about temperature compensation or step size while disconnected. Before, they returned made-up answers without talking to the hardware, which breaks the ASCOM rules. Behaviour while connected is unchanged, and tests were updated to match. The iOptron focuser's connected behaviour still has no test coverage because there is no fake device to test against.

prs.title: Correct the QHY wrapper API in driver_build.mdc, and sweep the file
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Documentation-only fix to the build guide that AI coding assistants read before working on drivers. The QHY camera section was mostly wrong: wrong file locations, a wrong way of identifying cameras, and a function that does not exist. The guide also wrongly said the build searches for vendor SDK folders, when each one is set to a fixed location. The iOptron section is fixed too, and no code changed.

prs.title: Gate the TSan filtered runs between ci.yml and ci_preflight.sh
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal CI change: an existing consistency check now also confirms that the thread-safety test runs in the CI pipeline match the ones in the local pre-flight script. That includes the safeguard that fails a run when no tests actually ran. Without it, one copy could quietly drift from the other while the local script kept reporting a pass. No product behaviour changes.

prs.title: Report the driver's connect-failure reason to the client
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a device refuses to connect, clients like NINA or SkySafari now show the driver's actual reason, for example "site latitude and longitude must be set", instead of a bare "Connection failed". Before, that reason only appeared in the server log. For the newer connect method, which has no place to return an error, the reason now appears on the device card in the web UI. All 38 affected drivers were updated, and a new CI check fails the build if a driver forgets to pass its reason along. The branch also fixed an existing rare crash in the iOptron mount driver when connecting and disconnecting rapidly.

prs.title: Stop the pty-backed test fakes hanging the suite on an undrained pty
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes an occasional problem where the automated test run would freeze completely instead of finishing, using up the whole time allowance before reporting anything. Some pretend devices used in testing could get stuck forever trying to send a reply nobody was reading. They now give up after a short wait, and the fix was applied to all six such devices, not just the one that was caught. This is internal to testing and does not change the product itself.

prs.title: Give every state-changing management endpoint the cross-origin guard
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Closes a security gap where any web page open in a browser on the same home network could quietly tell the server to restart, shut down, change or remove devices, lower logging, change the server description, or delete log files. These eight admin actions now refuse requests that come from another website, as two others already did. The built-in web interface and non-browser tools keep working as before, and simply reading information is unaffected. Admin access still has no password, which is intentional for trusted home networks.

prs.title: Keep persisted device configs in the web UI when portPath/host/connectionType is bad
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved telescope setups with a missing port, missing network address, or unrecognized connection type no longer disappear from the web interface when the server starts. Before, the only way to fix such an entry was to edit a settings file by hand on the device. Now the device still shows up so it can be corrected in the web interface. A warning is written to the log, and connecting fails with a clear reason until the setup is fixed. New setups entered through the interface are still rejected with the same error messages as before.

prs.title: Add build-branch badge to the web UI header
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The web interface header now shows a small highlighted tag with the branch name and code version whenever the running build is not an official release. It links to the exact code on GitHub and marks builds that contain unsaved local edits. Before, a test build looked the same as a real release, which made it easy to confuse the two. On official release builds the tag stays hidden.

prs.title: Name both Sky-Watcher vendor picker entries after the mount and its connection method
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Renames the two Sky-Watcher choices in the web interface's device list so they read as a matching pair: "Sky-Watcher Mount via SynScan (Hand Controller)" and "Sky-Watcher Mount via EQMOD (Direct)". The old names were "SynScan V3/V4" and "Sky-Watcher Wave (Direct)", which was misleading because the direct option works with many more mounts than the Wave series. The two entries also move next to each other in the list, and the matching section titles and description were updated. This changes wording only, so existing saved devices are unaffected.

prs.title: Split the shared target set-flag in five more telescope drivers
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Five more telescope brands (Celestron, OnStep, Bisque, SynScan and iOptron) now keep track of the target position's two coordinates separately, fixing an issue already solved for the Sky-Watcher direct driver. Before, setting just one coordinate made the other read back as zero instead of reporting that it had not been set, which fails the standard compatibility checker. The change also uncovered a real bug: on Celestron and SynScan, the "move to target" command would swing the telescope to a default position if no target had been set. It now refuses instead.

prs.title: Unit-test the web UI's pure formatters, not just their syntax
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The web control page's clock display now has real automated tests instead of just a check that the code is written correctly. The formatting code was moved into its own small file so it can be tested on its own, and nine tests now run on every change, including one for a case where the page could quietly show a believable but wrong time. Users should see no difference; the goal is to catch that kind of mistake before it ships.

prs.title: Make StressCallGuard's report distinct-keyed and gate the QHY seam lists
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal test tooling only. When the stress tests fail, the failure report now lists each different kind of error once with a count, so a single noisy error can no longer hide other, rarer ones that matter more. An automated check was also added to make sure the tests for one camera maker's hardware keep up when new functions are added, and that each of those functions stays properly protected against simultaneous use.

prs.title: Gate the blocking-get_connected() list and drop the counts nothing checked
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal documentation and checking work with no change to how the app behaves. Code comments used to state hand-counted numbers of which devices can briefly freeze while connecting, and those numbers kept going out of date. The numbers are removed, and a new automated check now reads the actual code and fails the build if the written list of those devices doesn't match reality. A few inaccurate notes in the contributor guide were also corrected.

prs.title: Harden the HTTP config and server-lifecycle failure paths
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Several error cases in the web server now fail cleanly instead of badly. If the server's network port is already in use, the program no longer crashes when it shuts down or tries again on another port. A device setting left blank as "null" now gets a clear message instead of a confusing technical error. Impossible telescope site locations, such as a latitude of 200, are now rejected for new setups and cleared with a warning for saved ones. One kind of rejected request also now carries the ID the client sent, so the client can tell which request failed.

prs.title: Close three FakeQHYSDK parity gaps and share the one-camera setup
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is test-only work. The pretend version of one camera maker's hardware used in tests was made more realistic in two ways: it now reports an "unsupported" setting the same way the real camera does, and its cooler now cools down gradually instead of instantly. A third known difference, about image memory size, was investigated and turned out to be a wrong assumption, so that code was left as is and only its notes were corrected. A shared setup step that had been copied into three test files now lives in one place.

prs.title: Close four holes in check_stress_registration.py
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal build-checking work with no change to the app. The automatic check that makes sure every device driver gets proper stress testing had four gaps, and all four are closed. The biggest gap: a test file could be added in a way that made the safety check look satisfied when it wasn't actually testing any device. The check's own self-tests grew from 21 to 53.

prs.title: Bound every CI job with timeout-minutes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every automated check job now has a time limit. Before, a stuck job could run for GitHub's default of six hours before anyone found out. The main target is the concurrency stress test, which can hang instead of failing, so a problem there now shows up within about 30 minutes. Two test comments and the contributor guide were updated to match, and test behaviour is unchanged.

prs.title: Guard the web UI clock offset and correct the Sync Time method in docs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The web interface's live server clock no longer breaks if the server sends back a time value that isn't a number. Before, a bad value made the clock display throw an error every second and stopped the clock-drift warning from showing. Now the clock just keeps its last good reading. The docs also now correctly say the Sync Time button sends a POST request, not a PUT; both already worked.

prs.title: Validate SVBONY SC715C via ToupTek driver, document ConformU 4.5.1 arm64 bug
prs.author: kern2011
prs.summary: The SVBONY SC715C camera is now listed as supported. It turned out to be a rebadged ToupTek camera, so it works through the existing ToupTek driver with no code changes, and it passed the official conformance test cleanly. The PR also records a known timing bug in version 4.5.0 of that test tool on arm64 that falsely flags cameras as slow. The maintainer testing instructions now install a fixed pre-release build instead. That build comes from an unsigned, unpinned download link outside GitHub, a trade-off the PR flags on purpose.

prs.title: Retitle the #287 UTCDate case and explain the unconditional invalidation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a wording-only cleanup for the Sky-Watcher telescope driver. A test was renamed to say accurately that a client's time setting only changes the telescope's sky-time calculation when the host has no network time sync. A code comment now explains why a cache refresh always happens. There is no change in behaviour.

prs.title: Re-sample Sky-Watcher host discipline behind a testable seam
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky-Watcher telescope driver now re-checks about every 30 seconds whether the host computer's clock has become properly synced to network time. Once it has, the driver stops pointing by the time a client app supplied. Before, it only checked once, so a host that got synced later kept using the client's possibly wrong time for the whole session. The change also lets automated tests cover both the synced and unsynced cases on any build machine. Before, the tests only covered whichever case the build machine happened to be in.

prs.title: Log the Sky-Watcher client-clock disagreement once per connection
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky-Watcher telescope driver now logs its warning about a client's clock disagreeing with the host clock only once per connection. Before, it logged on every time update, so apps that resend the time regularly flooded the log with the same line. A separate, similar message from the network layer still appears on every write. A new test covers this, but it only really checks the behaviour on machines with network time sync.

prs.title: Publish the Sky-Watcher target before dispatch on every writer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: On Sky-Watcher mounts driven directly, the mount now always remembers the target position a user asked for, even if the move or sync fails partway through. Before, the answer depended on which kind of move command the software used, so two programs could see different results after the same failure. Two new tests cover a failed move and a failed sync.

prs.title: Catch the Sky-Watcher docs up with dual-baud detection
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only. It updates the Sky-Watcher notes to say the mount connection is now tried at two speeds, and records that each unrelated USB adapter adds roughly 3 to 4 seconds to automatic mount detection. It also adds a step to the testing checklist: if the compatibility tester reports a star-time problem, check the clock on the tester's own computer before blaming the driver.

prs.title: Fix Sky-Watcher UTCDate origin guard, target locking and session reset
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Several Sky-Watcher fixes ahead of the 3.6.0 release. A web page in someone's browser can no longer secretly change the server's date and time. The driver now reports 'not connected' rather than 'not set' when asked for a target while disconnected, and handles target values safely when several requests arrive at once. A time correction supplied by one session is also cleared on reconnect instead of carrying over. The web-server part of the code was left out of the material provided, so that part is taken from the description, and a test on real hardware is still owed before release.

prs.title: fix(web): render the header clock in local time with a zone label
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The clock at the top of the web dashboard now shows the time in the viewer's own time zone, with a zone label such as NZST or GMT+12, instead of always showing UTC. This makes it match the server's log times, so people no longer have to convert time zones in their heads. If the browser cannot format the time properly, it falls back to showing UTC with a clear label. Showing the server's own time zone is left for a later change, and there are no automated tests, only hand checks.

prs.title: docs: record EQ-class Sky-Watcher support in the changelog
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Documentation only. It adds the missing changelog entry for the already-merged support for EQ-class Sky-Watcher mounts connected directly over USB. It also corrects an older note that wrongly said the faster connection speed was not yet in the main code. The mount is deliberately not yet listed as officially supported, because it has not passed a full compatibility check.

prs.title: docs(async_connectable): correct the list of drivers whose get_connected() locks
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal code comments and developer notes only; nothing about how the software runs changes. The notes listed which mount drivers can briefly hold things up while checking whether they are connected, and the list was wrong: one driver was named that no longer does this, and two were missing. Several related driver counts that had gone out of date were also corrected.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): require site latitude and longitude instead of defaulting to 0.0
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Sky-Watcher mounts now refuse to connect until the observing site's latitude and longitude have both been set, instead of quietly assuming 0,0. That silent default made southern-hemisphere rigs use northern-hemisphere math, so they tracked backwards, guided the wrong way and chose the wrong side of the pier, undoing three earlier fixes. New device setups missing either coordinate are rejected, and the web form checks for them too. Existing saved devices without a site still appear in the web UI so they can be fixed, but they will not connect until the site is filled in, and the client only sees a generic "Connection failed" with the real reason in the server log.

prs.title: fix(gemini): give the focuser a transition mutex and guard double connects
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a race in the Gemini focuser driver where two connect requests arriving at the same moment could both open the serial port, leaking the first connection for as long as the server ran. Connects and disconnects for this focuser now happen one at a time, the same way the other Gemini drivers already work, and a second connect on an already-open link now fails loudly instead of silently leaking. It also adds a simulated focuser so the race can be reproduced in tests. This has not been tried on real hardware.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): do not let a client's clock error drive pointing on an NTP-good host
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: On Sky-Watcher mounts, a client app with a wrong clock, such as a tablet running 30 minutes off, can no longer throw off pointing when the server's own clock is kept accurate by internet time. Before, that error could shift every goto by about 7.5 degrees, and a test on a real rig confirmed the fix removes the shift. The app still reads back the time it set, as the standard requires, and off-grid setups with no internet time still use the app's time as before. A warning is logged when the two clocks disagree by more than 2 seconds.

prs.title: perf(clock): prime the hardware-RTC probe at startup, off the request path
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Checking whether the server has a battery-backed hardware clock now happens once at startup and then on a background timer every 31 seconds, instead of during device connects and web page refreshes. On a board with a faulty clock chip, that check could stall a telescope connect for about a second. The trade-off is that a change in the hardware clock's status is only noticed on the next background check. This was not tested on hardware with that kind of fault.

prs.title: test(http): add a Router host-clock seam and cover the #289 wiring
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test work: makes it possible for automated tests to use a fake system clock, and adds tests for how the server handles time sent by telescope apps and the clock warnings shown at connect. Until now, removing any of that logic would have gone unnoticed by the tests. The clock handling itself does not change.

prs.title: fix(http): give the synctime management endpoint the same Origin guard as wifi
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Closes a security gap where any web page open on a browser on the same network could quietly change the server's system clock. That could throw off telescope pointing while also hiding the warning that would explain the problem. Requests to set the time now get the same cross-site check the Wi-Fi settings already had, while other apps and the built-in web page are unaffected. Several other management actions, such as restart, shutdown and device setup, still lack this protection, and that is tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(skywatcher): give TargetRightAscension and TargetDeclination their own set-flags
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a bug in the Sky-Watcher mount support where setting only one of the two target coordinates (the east-west position or the north-south position) made both look as if they had been set, so reading the other one quietly returned zero instead of an error. Each coordinate is now tracked separately. A slew or sync to the target is still refused until both are set, and a normal imaging session that sets both coordinates behaves exactly as before. This clears a failure reported by the standard compatibility checker, and it was confirmed on a real mount. The same flaw exists in several other brands' mount drivers and will be handled separately.

prs.title: test: add StressCallGuard, a shared per-call guard for [stress] operate callbacks
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test tooling only. It adds a shared helper for the automated multi-threading stress tests, so every device test no longer needs its own copy. Each individual test step keeps running even when an earlier one fails, and any unexpected kind of error is now counted and reported instead of silently ignored. It also closes a gap where the automated check could pass with no device stress tests actually running, and it tightens the rule that checks every device has stress test coverage. No change for users.

prs.title: test: add a fault-injectable QHY SDK seam and the first QHY connect coverage
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Makes the QHY camera and QHY filter wheel testable without real hardware for the first time. It adds a simulated stand-in for QHY's software library and 41 new tests covering connecting, disconnecting, error recovery, and a camera and filter wheel sharing one physical device. The driver changes are mostly mechanical rewiring, and the description says real-world behaviour is unchanged. One small difference is that the QHY library helper is now created when a device is set up rather than on first use, which the author explains is harmless as things stand. This is stage one of two; the stress-test registration for QHY comes next.

prs.title: test: register the Gemini switch, cover calibrator, and focuser with [stress]
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test coverage only. It adds automated multi-threading stress tests for three Gemini devices: the power/dew switch, the flat panel cover calibrator, and the focuser. The switch and flat panel are tested with simulated hardware in a fully connected state, while the focuser only gets a basic test because no simulator exists for it. The flat panel's cover open/close movement is not yet covered. No change for users.

prs.title: test: register the four WandererAstro drivers with the [stress] suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test coverage only. It adds automated multi-threading stress tests for four WandererAstro devices: the cover calibrator, filter wheel, power box switch, and rotator. Three of them are tested with simulated hardware in a fully connected state, while the rotator only gets a basic test because no suitable simulator exists for it yet. No change for users.

prs.title: test: register the Player One thermal switch with the [stress] suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test coverage only. It adds automated multi-threading stress tests for the Player One camera's dew heater and fan switch. Anyone running these tests with a real Player One camera attached should know the test repeatedly sets the heater or fan to 1%. No change for users.

prs.title: test: register the WeeWX ObservingConditions driver with the [stress] suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal test work: the weather-station connection used for observing conditions (WeeWX) is now part of the automated tests that hammer a driver from many threads at once, looking for crashes and timing bugs. Because there is no stand-in for the weather station, the test only covers connecting, failing to connect, and shutting down, not normal operation while connected. The description also flags a small possible thread-safety issue in this driver for a separate fix, and this PR does not change it.

prs.title: fix: serialize every hidapi library call on one process-wide mutex
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a hidden bug with Astroasis Oasis focusers when more than one is in use. Scanning for devices and connecting to a different focuser could run at the same moment and collide inside the shared USB library, so those steps now take turns. Normal reads and writes to each focuser still run in parallel. If the USB library fails to start, users now get a clear 'initialization failed' message instead of a misleading one that suggested a cabling or permissions problem. The new test cannot actually catch the original bug, as the PR itself admits, so the fix relies on careful review.

prs.title: Report ClockSource "rtc" when the host booted from a hardware RTC
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The server's clock status can now report a fourth source, 'rtc', meaning the computer set its time at boot from a hardware clock chip, where before it said 'none'. A chip that is obviously dead (reporting a date before 2020) does not count. This only says where the time came from, not whether it is accurate, so clients can still correct it. On such machines the telescope-connect message is now a calmer note instead of a warning. It stays a warning if client time correction is turned off or the system has already refused a time change, and in that case the message says to set the clock from outside the service. The web page shows the new state too.

prs.title: test: register the Astroasis Oasis focuser with the [stress] concurrency suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The Astroasis Oasis focuser is now included in the automated tests that stress drivers from many threads at once, and those tests exposed real bugs that this PR also fixes. Two simultaneous connect requests could both open the device and leak a connection, and a disconnect during a connect could be lost. The driver now makes these requests take turns. One trade-off: reading the focuser's position or temperature while a connect is still in progress now waits about a second before reporting 'not connected', instead of answering at once.

prs.title: Add test-first fix discipline to /pr-checker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal process change: the instructions for the automated PR-fixing assistant now require it to reproduce each reported problem before fixing it, prove the fix with the same check, include that check in the repo where possible, and run only the relevant automated checks before pushing. It also adds a short project note about how the Sky-Watcher driver handles the client-set time when the computer's clock jumps. No product behavior changes.

prs.title: Take the host clock from a client's UTCDate on NTP-less SBCs; direct driver LST honours UTCDate
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: On small field computers with no internet time and no clock battery, such as a Raspberry Pi at a dark site, the clock is wrong after every power-up, which makes telescope pointing miss. When astronomy software sends the current time on connect, AlpacaBridge now uses it to set the computer's clock, but only if the clock is not already kept correct by an internet or GPS time source. This can be turned off in the web page. The status page now shows where the clock's time came from, and a warning is logged if a telescope connects before the time has been set. The Sky-Watcher direct driver also now uses the client-provided time for its pointing math, where before it ignored it. The code also drops that client time if the computer's clock is changed afterward, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: test: register the ToupTek AAF focuser with the [stress] concurrency suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal testing change. Adds automated tests that repeatedly connect, disconnect and operate the ToupTek AAF focuser at the same time, using a simulated device, to catch crashes or timing bugs in multi-threaded code. The list of devices still missing this kind of testing shrinks to 15, and the team notes are updated to match. The code matches the description.

prs.title: docs: SkyWatcher direct driver reports equinox of date; precess solver output before comparing or syncing
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Documentation only. It adds a note to the developer guide saying the direct SkyWatcher driver reports sky positions for today's date, while plate-solving tools report them for the year 2000. The two now differ by about 22 arcminutes. The note warns that syncing the mount to an unconverted solver position builds that error into the mount, so people should rule this out before blaming the driver for a roughly 20-arcminute pointing miss.

prs.title: check_stress_registration: anchor device-type detection, add a self-test
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal tooling change. A build check that confirms every device driver has concurrency tests could be misled about what kind of device a driver is, for example by a stray mention in a comment. It now reads the device type only from the place where the driver actually declares it. If one file declares conflicting types, it fails loudly instead of guessing. A small built-in self-test was also added and now runs in the automated build and the local pre-check.

prs.title: test: register ZWO focuser, rotator, and dew-heater switch with [stress]
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal testing change. Adds connect/disconnect stress tests for the ZWO focuser, rotator and dew-heater switch, and removes them from the list of untested devices. No simulated device exists for these, so without hardware attached the tests only exercise the failed-connection path. The code also records a known gap in the notes: the two ZWO ASIAIR power switches still have no such tests, but the coverage check now counts them as covered because the dew-heater switch is the same device type.

prs.title: test: register iOptron iEFW filter wheel, iEAF focuser, and PowerBox switch with [stress]
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal testing change. Adds connect/disconnect stress tests for three iOptron accessories (filter wheel, focuser and PowerBox power switch) and removes them from the list of untested devices. No simulated device exists for these, so without hardware attached the tests mainly exercise the failed-connection and cleanup path. The PowerBox test is only built when the required system library is available. Its test file was not included in the diff provided, so that part could not be checked here.

prs.title: test: register the SkyWatcher telescope with the [stress] concurrency suite
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Internal testing change. Adds a new set of stress tests for the SkyWatcher mount driver, run against a simulated mount over the network. The tests hammer slewing, guiding, manual axis moves and tracking-rate changes while connecting, disconnecting and shutting down, which targets the kind of timing bug that previously left the mount stuck reporting it was still slewing. The SkyWatcher telescope comes off the list of untested devices.

prs.title: Review bot rubric: defects block the merge, notes never do
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated code-review bot now uses stricter rules for blocking a merge. Only real problems block approval, such as wrong results, crashes, security holes, missing tests for changed behaviour, or docs that no longer match the code; smaller suggestions are listed as notes (at most five) and never block. It also closes a loophole where an outside contributor could plant a fake approval or rewrite the bot's reference instructions in their own PR. The team's merge helper now reads the bot's result more reliably and stops with a clear reason when no verdict is coming, instead of waiting out the full 30 minutes.

prs.title: Fix the non-blocking review notes left from the 2026-09-10 PR batch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This PR cleans up small leftover suggestions from the automated reviewer on five earlier PRs. It tidies unneeded code references in about fifteen driver files, fixes edge cases in three internal checking scripts, and adds tests for the Sky-Watcher SynScan mount's display name. The code also fixes a timing problem the description doesn't mention: two parts of the program could read and write the SynScan mount's model number at the same time, and that is now safe. It also adds steps to the maintainer's merge instructions for deleting leftover branches after merging.

prs.title: Move the review bot to Opus; add capped cleanup rounds to /pr-checker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated code-review bot now runs on a stronger AI model (Opus instead of Sonnet), to better tell real bugs from nitpicks in the complex device-driver code. The maintainer's merge helper now fixes easy reviewer suggestions before merging, capped at three extra rounds per PR so a PR can't loop endlessly. It also spots merge conflicts right away instead of stalling for 30 minutes, and reports any contributor changes that land while it is working. This is internal tooling only; users are not affected.

prs.title: Sky-Watcher: keep identity across disconnect, SynScan/EQMOD Name suffixes, AGENTS.md fixes
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Sky-Watcher mounts now keep their real model name (for example "EQM-35 Pro") after a normal disconnect, instead of falling back to a generic name in the web UI and device lists. When the same mount is reachable two ways, the names now say which connection is which: "(SynScan)" for the hand-controller route and "(EQMOD)" for the direct connection. Before, both showed the same name and couldn't be told apart in astronomy software. The internal notes also record that a SynScan handset in "PC Direct Mode" works as a direct connection. The description also mentions correcting a note about which vendors use the serial-port registry, but that change does not appear in this diff.

prs.title: ci: add a docs drift check and fix the drift it currently finds
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This PR adds an automatic check, run on every PR and in the local pre-submit checks, that catches the project's own docs and settings drifting out of step. It checks that every build option is documented, that tool versions match in two config files, that the version number matches the README, and that file paths in the contributor guide still exist. It also fixes the drift it found: five build options were missing from the developer docs, and the PR-submission guide wrongly said fork contributors never get automated reviews. It also brings the required-tests list up to the stricter standard and removes a hard-coded, outdated ConformU version.

prs.title: ci: validate ConformU reports on every PR, not only via /submit-pr
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Every PR now automatically checks any changed ConformU compliance report (the ASCOM validation results for a driver) and blocks the merge if the report shows errors, issues, or slow responses. Before, this was only enforced when contributors used the team's PR-submission assistant, so a hand-opened PR could merge a failing report and wrongly advertise a driver as validated. Unlike the description, which says the older AlpacaHTTP report folder is intentionally left out, the code checks that folder too and accepts a second wording of ConformU's success message.

prs.title: ci: fail when a driver has no [stress] concurrency-test registration
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds an automatic check that fails the build when a device driver has no multi-threading stress test and is not on an approved exceptions list. The check looks at each brand and device type separately, so gaps like ZWO's untested focuser and rotator are no longer hidden just because another ZWO driver has a test. It starts with 20 known untested drivers on the exceptions list, and an entry must be removed once its test is added, so the list can only shrink. The developer notes were also updated to list OnStep as already covered.

prs.title: Sky-Watcher direct driver: audit pier-side branch selection for the south (#261)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Reviews how the direct Sky-Watcher mount driver decides which side of the pier the telescope is on, with a focus on southern-hemisphere users, and adds two simulated-mount tests that swing the telescope across the meridian. The review found that the reported side is at least consistent and switches correctly when the target crosses the meridian. Software tests alone cannot prove the label matches the real physical side south of the equator, so that question stays open until a hardware check under the night sky. No driver behavior changed; this adds tests and developer notes only.

prs.title: Add /pr-checker skill: loop PRs through the review bot until clean, then merge
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds an AI-assistant command for maintainers that takes one or more open pull requests and repeatedly fixes and resubmits each one until the automated reviewer approves it, then merges them in order. It captures lessons learned from recent contributions from outside the core team, such as how to trigger the reviewer, how to spot outdated reviews, and when to stop and ask a human. This is internal tooling only, and nothing changes for end users.

prs.title: Verify RightAscensionRate/TrackingRate live step-period changes in the background
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: When a user changes the tracking speed on a Sky-Watcher mount (for example switching to lunar tracking), the driver now checks in the background that the mount actually changed speed, and resends the command if it did not. Previously a stalled change could leave the telescope silently tracking at the wrong speed until the next adjustment. The check takes longer for small speed changes so it can reliably measure them, and it is skipped for changes too small to detect. The PR also fixes an issue found during review where this check could make some guiding nudges run longer than requested. It was tested on real EQM-35 Pro hardware.

prs.title: Replace std::strerror(errno) with a thread-safe util::errno_string()
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Makes error messages from device connections safe to produce when two parts of the program fail at the same moment, for example when a USB device drops off and both reading and writing fail together. Before this, the two could overwrite each other's error text. The change is applied across all device drivers and the web server, and it replaces four duplicate homemade workarounds with one shared version. Error wording stays the same, except that unrecognized error codes now read "errno N" instead of "Unknown error N".

prs.title: Reword the DeclinationRate branch-sign TODO: holding the sign is correct (#255)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: This change only rewrites a code comment and does not change how the software behaves. A note in the Sky-Watcher driver had described the way declination speed adjustments behave near the celestial pole as a bug to fix. An attempt to fix it showed the current behavior is correct and the change made the mount oscillate, so the comment now explains why and points to the closed issue.

prs.title: Add tagged GitHub Releases workflow (source only, notes from CHANGELOG)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every time a new version is tagged, the project now automatically publishes a GitHub Release. The release notes come from that version's entry in the changelog, and only the source code archives are attached. Installing still happens only through the OpenAstro apt repository. The automation refuses to publish if the tag doesn't match the project's version number or if the changelog entry is still marked unreleased, and the developer docs now explain the three-step release process.

prs.title: Sky-Watcher DeclinationRate and PulseGuide N/S ran backwards south of the equator
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where Sky-Watcher mounts used south of the equator moved the wrong way in declination (the up-down sky direction) when guiding or when asked to drift at a set rate. A 'north' correction pushed the star further south, so autoguiding would spiral out of control instead of settling. Northern users were never affected. New tests cover the fix, and the description reports it was measured on real hardware in both relevant positions. However, some internal notes and code comments added in this change still describe the second hardware check as not yet done.

prs.title: Remove the EQM-35 Pro from SUPPORTED-DRIVERS.md until ConformU is clean
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro mount has been taken off the list of officially supported hardware. Its conformance test run flagged an issue with how it reports which side of the mount the telescope is on. The software still recognizes and works with the mount; only the 'supported' claim is withdrawn until a clean test run exists.

prs.title: Allow diegopereiran's own pushes to run the review bot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal change: a trusted outside contributor is added to the list of people whose updates automatically trigger the automated code-review bot. Until now, a maintainer had to manually re-trigger the review after each of their pushes. No repository access is granted.

prs.title: Auto-detect Sky-Watcher Synta EQ boards at 115200 over direct USB (#230)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The direct Sky-Watcher mount connection can now automatically find classic Synta EQ mounts, such as the EQM-35 Pro, that talk at a faster connection speed through their built-in USB port. It previously missed them entirely, and even when found would have reconnected at the wrong speed. The scan also now skips ports already in use by other connected devices, so it can't disrupt them, and the web settings page offers a two-choice speed selector. Trade-offs: scanning silent ports can take about twice as long, and saved settings with an unusual speed are quietly reset to the default. The test with a hand controller attached at the same time and the test with a second device sharing a port were still unchecked when this merged.

prs.title: Stop reversing Sky-Watcher RA tracking direction in the southern hemisphere
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes Sky-Watcher mounts in the southern hemisphere tracking the sky in the wrong direction. The mount was doubling the stars' apparent drift instead of cancelling it, which would have left stars trailing badly. The mistake was a reversal that turned out to be wrong when tested on a real mount in Australia, and removing it also changes the southern direction of east/west guiding and manual moves, which was checked on hardware. New automated tests confirm tracking direction in both hemispheres, but they cover only basic tracking, not guiding.

prs.title: Re-latch Sky-Watcher live step-period changes with ":J" and verify in motion
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes Sky-Watcher mounts sometimes ignoring short autoguiding nudges in the east/west direction: the mount would accept a new speed but keep moving at normal tracking speed. The driver now sends an extra 'start' command after each speed change, which makes the motor actually apply it. For longer nudges it also briefly checks that the speed really changed and retries if not. This resolved the conformance-test failures seen on the EQM-35 Pro. As the description says, the separate custom tracking-rate setting gets the extra 'start' command but not the check, which is tracked for later.

prs.title: Require observing-site coordinates to be scrubbed from ConformU reports
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Adds a required step to the conformance-test instructions: contributors must round the observing site's location and elevation before publishing a test report, so a home address can't be worked out from it. The rule is also added to the reports folder's readme. Although described as docs only, it also rounds the elevation in the existing EQM-35 Pro report from 80 m to 100 m. No change to how the software behaves.

prs.title: Decode the Sky-Watcher ":e" mount code as an identity, not a firmware patch level
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Sky-Watcher mounts now report their real model name, such as 'Sky-Watcher EQM-35 Pro' or 'Sky-Watcher Wave 100i', once connected, and 'Sky-Watcher Mount' when disconnected. Previously every mount was called 'Sky-Watcher Wave Mount'. The firmware version is also shown correctly now, for example '3.58' instead of '3.58.68'; the extra number was actually a model code. The SynScan hand-controller driver also recognizes the EQM-35 Pro by name. The Wave 100i name change has not been checked on real Wave hardware.

prs.title: Shape-check Sky-Watcher serial replies and make the ":i" step-period readback a diagnostic
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Makes the USB serial connection to Sky-Watcher mounts more reliable. The driver no longer mistakes a late reply to an earlier command for the answer to the current one, and it waits for the line to go quiet after a timeout. Each speed change is now read back from the mount, and any mismatch is logged as a warning without causing an error. Detailed command logging is also available for troubleshooting. This was groundwork for the guiding fix that followed.

prs.title: Give each Sky-Watcher MoveAxis axis its own stop-completion task
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes a Sky-Watcher bug that could leave the mount stuck reporting 'slewing' forever and stop tracking while still claiming to track. It happened when both axes were stopped close together, for example on releasing manual direction buttons in an imaging app. That could hang an automated imaging session or produce images from an untracked mount. Each axis now handles its own stop, and stopping one axis no longer prevents the other from resuming tracking.

prs.title: Fix SynScan hand-controller connect stall and Sky-Watcher probe wedging a SynScan handset (#130)
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: Fixes connections to SynScan hand controllers that hung for about 25 seconds and then reported a connection that did not work. Connecting now checks that something actually answers and fails quickly if nothing does. Clients also get a timely response instead of the request being blocked, which applies to several mount types. It also adds protection so the Sky-Watcher auto-detect scan can't freeze a SynScan handset by talking to it at the wrong speed; that protection only matters once a future change adds higher-speed scanning, so it has no effect yet. The change also adds an EQM-35 Pro conformance report to the published test results.

prs.title: feat(switch): lay the Switches panel out by what each port is, and stop trusting Connected as proof of life
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Switches panel now groups a power box's controls by what they do instead of showing one long list of identical rows. Measurements like voltage, current and temperature appear as readout tiles, on/off outlets are grouped together, and each dew heater gets a single card with its power level and mode. It also fixes several problems found on real hardware: values that didn't save correctly, sliders that stayed on a setting the device had refused, outlets that never appeared after connecting, and readings that never updated. Separately, a device that has lost its hardware link but still claims to be connected is now marked as disconnected after about 20 seconds, so users can reconnect it.

prs.title: Fix cache-backed serial drivers serving stale status over a dead link
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a problem where the Gemini power hub and several WandererAstro devices kept showing old readings for as long as 30 minutes after their USB connection dropped, which made them look healthy. After a few seconds of silence these devices now report a communication error and refuse commands, and they recover on their own when data starts arriving again. It includes automated tests, but the planned test of unplugging a real hub has not yet been done.

prs.title: Add Gemini Power & Data Hubs Advanced 3 Switch driver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for the Gemini Power & Data Hub Advanced 3. Users can switch its USB and 12 V outlets, control the two dew heaters and their modes, and see voltage, current, power, temperature, humidity and dew point. The vendor publishes no documentation, so the hub's commands were worked out from the vendor's own Windows driver and then checked on the real device, where it passed the standard compatibility test with no errors. The setup page can now also find the hub automatically, and the team's guide for building drivers gained steps for this reverse-engineering approach.

prs.title: Park idle HTTP connections on a poll() reactor instead of a worker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Changes how the server handles connections that are open but not sending anything, so many connected apps no longer use up the server's limited pool of request handlers. It also adds a limit on total open connections, and new apps wait in line rather than being turned away when that limit is reached. Shutting down or restarting the server is now nearly instant instead of taking up to about 14 seconds. The description says the two new limits can't be set from the config file, but the code does let users set them from the config file and environment variables. The quoted shutdown time also differs between the description (7 ms) and the internal notes (114 ms).

prs.title: Keep HTTP connections alive between requests
prs.author: diegopereiran
prs.summary: The server now keeps each app's connection open between requests instead of reconnecting every time, which cuts delay on frequent calls such as autoguiding pulses. Limits on how long, and for how many requests, a connection can stay open keep a few apps from hogging the server, and restarting the server no longer hangs behind an active app. Beyond what the description summarizes, the code also sets aside a few request handlers as a temporary safeguard and closes connections more gently. PR #235 later replaced that temporary safeguard. The change was investigated as a fix for some slow-response warnings in a compatibility test, but it did not resolve them.

prs.title: ci: bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.210 to 1.0.216 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update to the version of the automated code-review tool used in the project's build pipeline. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of the automated tools the project uses behind the scenes: the AI code-review helper and the security-scanning tool now run slightly newer versions. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 1 update
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine minor version update of the library that provides the server's built-in API reference page, with the third-party license list updated to match. No visible change is expected for users.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of the automated tools the project uses behind the scenes: the AI code-review helper and the security-scanning tool now run slightly newer versions. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: Fix ToupTek camera DeviceState timing; validate ATR585M camera + switch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cooled ToupTek cameras such as the ATR585M now answer status requests quickly. Temperature and cooler readings are checked in the background once a second instead of on every request, and that background checking pauses during exposures, where it had been causing dropped frames at higher binning. The camera and its heater/fan switch now pass the standard compatibility tests on a Raspberry Pi with no problems. Not mentioned in the description: the change also fixes how every camera reports its exposure progress value in status summaries, so it is now sent as a whole number as the standard expects.

prs.title: Fix iOptron HAE16 EQ GOTO settle, dual-stack HTTP listener, SideOfPier cache
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The iOptron HAE16 EQ mount now lands accurately after a GOTO. It gets the same small correction already used for the HAE29C, which fixes a firmware quirk that left it slightly off target. Two speed fixes are included. Asking which side of the pier the mount is on no longer triggers a slow round trip to the mount when a recent reading is available, and the network server now accepts both IPv4 and IPv6 connections so some clients stop wasting time on a failed first attempt. Not mentioned in the description: the code also makes the mount report "slewing" right away when an alt-az move starts, and cleans up that state if a move fails to start.

prs.title: Add iOptron iCAM camera support (Player One SDK) and /deploy-remote-test skill
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: iOptron iCAM cameras (iCAM178M, iCAM462C and iCAM464C) can now be set up as iOptron devices in the web interface. These cameras are rebranded Player One cameras, so they reuse the existing Player One support and no new driver code was needed. All three models, plus a ToupTek GPM662M, passed the standard compatibility tests cleanly. The PR also adds a developer helper for installing test builds on remote Raspberry Pis that can only be reached through a browser shell.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of the automated build and checking tools the project uses behind the scenes (the Docker image builder, the AI code-review bot, and the security scanner) to their latest minor versions. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: Add Gemini Motorized Flat Panel V3 (INDI Pro) CoverCalibrator support
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now supports the Gemini Motorized Flat Panel V3, so users can pick it in the web setup page and open, close and light it like the existing Gemini panels. The bridge now warns if the panel model chosen in settings doesn't match the one actually plugged in. The panel now reports its cover position quickly by briefly remembering its last reading, and turning the light on or off finishes in about a quarter of a second instead of appearing to take several seconds in apps like NINA. It passed the standard compatibility test suite on real hardware with no problems and comes with new automated tests and documentation.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine minor updates to three outside software packages: two used by the server's API documentation pages and one used only for running tests. The API documentation package update includes small bug fixes from its authors. No visible change is expected for users.

prs.title: build: Bump geolocator from 13.0.4 to 14.0.3 in /client/openastroara_client in the pub group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Updates the location library the app uses for its "Fill from GPS" feature to a new major version. The new version adds Linux support, but this change does not switch it on, so Linux users still see the same explanation that their computer can't provide a location. Apart from the version bump, only explanatory code comments were updated. Behavior on Mac and Windows should be unchanged.

prs.title: fix(flat): drive the cover and light, don't just display them
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now actually control a connected flat panel from Ara, not just see its status. The panel's settings card gains Open/Close buttons for the cover, a light on/off switch and a brightness slider, and it hides controls the hardware doesn't have. The switch now responds right away, a light command sent while the cover is still moving waits for the cover instead of silently failing, and a light that is still warming up no longer looks like a failed command. A known gap remains: pressing Open while the cover is already opening can still fail without the user being told.

prs.title: Probe serial auto-detect candidates concurrently (issue #218)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automatic device detection now checks all candidate USB ports at the same time instead of one after another. This makes connecting much faster when several similar adapters are plugged in, such as a telescope mount that uses the same USB chip as a focuser. It applies to iOptron focusers and filter wheels and to Gemini focusers and flat panels. On a test setup with two mounts attached, detection dropped from about 2.5 seconds to 1.3 seconds, and devices are still numbered in the same order as before.

prs.title: Fix Park async-initiator timing in SynScan and Celestron (#208)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Parking a SynScan or Celestron mount no longer freezes the connection for the whole park movement. The command now returns right away, and the mount reports it is moving until it settles into the parked position. This keeps these mounts within the response times the standard compatibility checker now enforces. The change was checked with new automated tests and a hardware run on an iOptron mount, but it has not yet been tried on real SynScan or Celestron mounts; the same fix for TheSkyX-controlled mounts is still on hold.

prs.title: Add SkyWatcher RA/Dec tracking rate offsets with duty-cycled slow rates
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sky-Watcher Wave mounts can now apply small custom speed adjustments on top of normal star tracking, which is what you need to follow comets or other objects that drift against the stars. Very slow adjustments that the motor can't do directly are produced by running it in short on-off bursts. The code also substantially rewrites the team's internal instructions for running the compatibility tests, which the description doesn't mention: they now run on the test computer itself, and the instructions include that computer's login details. A final full hardware test on the Wave 100i was still pending at merge.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine internal update that moves the automated review and code-scanning tools used by the build system to newer versions. There is no effect on the product itself.

prs.title: Add iOptron iEFW filter wheel driver, ConformU 4.5.0 validated on arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for iOptron's iEFW-15 (5-slot) and iEFW-18 (8-slot) filter wheels. It includes automatic detection that won't confuse the wheel with an iOptron mount or focuser plugged in alongside it, plus a web setup section for choosing the model and naming filters. Both wheels passed the standard compatibility checker on real hardware. The notes also record that the iEFW-18 really has 8 usable positions rather than the advertised 9, and that its always-on indicator light cannot be switched off in software. One small oddity: the saved test report for the iEFW-18 labels the device as an iEFW-15 in its header, even though the device itself reported iEFW-18 during the test.

prs.title: Release the driver mutex during SkyWatcher axis-stop waits
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sky-Watcher mounts stay responsive while an axis is slowing to a stop. Previously, other requests could be held up for up to 5 seconds during that wait, which likely caused occasional slow-response marks in compatibility testing. A new automated test confirms requests still get quick answers while the mount decelerates, and a fresh hardware test passed cleanly. The code also adds a note, not mentioned in the description, that some of those slow-response marks came from the test computer's power-saving setting rather than from the driver.

prs.title: Add iOptron iAFS2/3 focuser support, ConformU 4.5.0 validated on arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for iOptron's iAFS2/3 focusers, which use the same communication method as the already-supported iEAF focuser, so they run on the existing driver. A new Model menu in the web setup lets users pick which unit they own, and that choice sets the displayed name. Existing saved devices keep their identity. It passed the standard compatibility checker on real iAFS2 hardware.

prs.title: Add iOptron iEAF focuser driver, ConformU 4.5.0 validated on arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for iOptron's iEAF electronic focuser, so users can connect it, move it, stop it, and read its temperature through the bridge. It can be set up from the web page, and auto-detect can tell the focuser apart from an iOptron mount that uses the same kind of USB chip. It passed the official ASCOM compatibility test cleanly on a Raspberry Pi and includes new tests and documentation. The change also adds a step, not mentioned in the description, to the AI assistant's driver-building instructions: check whether a newer version of the ASCOM device standard has been published before starting.

prs.title: Add hardware-free async state-machine tests for the SkyWatcher driver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Test-only change that adds a simulated Sky-Watcher mount, so the new Sky-Watcher driver's behavior can be checked automatically without real hardware. Seven new tests cover slewing to a target, parking and unparking, finding home, guiding nudges, stopping manual moves, and cancelling a slew. No shipped code changed.

prs.title: Add Sky-Watcher Wave mount driver with AutoHome, ConformU 4.5 validated
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new driver for Sky-Watcher Wave 100i/150i mounts (and similar mounts) that talks to the mount directly over USB or its built-in Wi-Fi, with no hand controller or phone app needed. It can find the mount's physical home position using its built-in sensors, and it passed the official ASCOM compatibility test cleanly over both connection types. The change also fixes a crash when the server shuts down and makes the web server restart its listener instead of quietly stopping. It adds a firm safety rule to only run the compatibility test on a mount with no telescope attached. The diff also includes a camera test report (ZWO ASI462MM) that the description does not mention.

prs.title: Fix review agent output path: /tmp writes are permission-denied
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal fix to the automated code-review bot. The bot was not allowed to save files outside the project folder, so it could never save its review and every review silently failed. It now saves the review inside the project folder, where the posting step can find it.

prs.title: Fix Claude review workflow: deterministic comment posting
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal change to the automated code-review bot. The bot used to post its own review comment and often failed to do so on large changes. Now the bot only writes the review to a file, and a separate step posts it. The bot is also told to skip test-log files so they don't use up its review effort.

prs.title: fix(sequencer): tab shortcuts decline keys they don't act on
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the sequence editor's keyboard shortcuts, which were grabbing keys even when they did nothing with them. Before this fix, users could not type a space in a settings field such as a note or a container name, the up and down arrows didn't move the cursor, and Cmd/Ctrl+Z didn't undo typing. Keys the shortcuts don't use now pass through to whatever the user is typing in. Pressing Space on a focused toolbar button now presses that button, instead of also triggering the shortcut and sending a duplicate command to the equipment.

prs.title: fix(client): watchdogs so a dead link stops showing stale 'connected'
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: When the connection to the telescope rig silently drops, the app now shows the server and all equipment, including the guider, as offline after about 45 seconds. Before, it could keep showing a stale green "connected" for minutes or indefinitely. A separate check also marks a device offline after about a minute of failed status checks, while brief hiccups still change nothing and everything turns green again once the link returns. The code applies the 45-second check only to the app that holds the control session, so a second app just watching the rig won't get it; the description doesn't mention this.

prs.title: feat(client): Run editor numeric fields take digits/./- only; note field grows
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: In the Run (sequence) editor, number fields such as exposure time and gain now block letters and symbols as you type. The note field on Annotation steps now wraps and grows to fit longer text. The code is stricter than the description suggests: whole-number fields block the decimal point at the keystroke, and fields that can't be negative block the minus sign.

prs.title: fix(client): Delete/Backspace while editing a sequence field no longer removes the instruction
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug in the Run (sequence) editor where pressing Delete or Backspace while editing a setting could delete the whole step instead of the value. The protection now covers every kind of setting control, including dropdowns and switches, not just text boxes. Delete still removes a step when the step list itself is selected. The change also stops arrow keys and undo/redo from acting on the step list while you're in a setting, and the new tests check text boxes and dropdowns but not switches.

prs.title: feat(client): Fill from GPS falls back to this Mac's location
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: "Fill from GPS" for the observing site now uses the computer's own location when no USB GPS dongle is available. This requires location permission and a recent location fix, and each failure shows a clear message on what to do. The profile setup wizard and the Site settings panel now behave the same, and the filled-in values appear right away instead of only after reopening the panel. The description only mentions Macs, but the code also adds this for Windows, and it won't overwrite site fields you edited while the lookup was running.

prs.title: fix(client): human-readable switch panel errors
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Errors in the switch panel (for example, turning on a dew heater on a device that isn't connected) now show a plain message like "switch … is not connected" instead of a raw technical error. This makes it clear you need to reconnect the device. The rest of the diff is mostly reformatting and new tests.

prs.title: feat(client): night mode (red display) for dark-site observing
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Adds a Night mode that turns the whole app red, so using it at the telescope doesn't ruin your night vision. You can switch it on from Settings → About, a moon button in the top bar, or the N key (ignored while typing in a field), and the choice is remembered between launches. The sky map, which the app can't normally paint over, gets a matching red tint on Mac, Windows and Linux.

prs.title: feat(mount): move the direction pad above Manual control
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: On the mount settings screen, the press-and-hold direction pad and its speed picker now sit near the top, right under the auto-connect option, so you no longer have to scroll past the GoTo form to nudge the telescope. The pad now appears for any mount that can be moved manually, even if it can't do GoTo. The Manual control section now holds only the GoTo form and is hidden on mounts that can't slew. The pad itself works the same as before, and the tests were updated to match.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 7 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is a routine automated update of the server's supporting libraries, with no intended change for users. It includes a major version jump (3.x to 4.x) for the ASCOM libraries the server uses to talk to astronomy equipment, plus smaller updates to testing and API-documentation tools. The diff also updates a test-runner component and an ASCOM error-handling library that the description doesn't clearly list. The license notices were updated to match.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is an internal update to the automated build and review tooling: the AI code-review bot and the security-scanning step move to newer versions. Nothing changes in the app itself.

prs.title: build: Bump file_picker from 12.0.0-beta.7 to 12.0.0 in /client/openastroara_client in the pub group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: The app's file open and save dialogs now use the finished release of the file-picker component instead of a pre-release test version. The description only mentions the version bump, but the new version works slightly differently, so the diff also adjusts the app everywhere files are chosen or saved. That includes exporting and importing profile shares, exporting frames from the library, and importing and exporting sequences. Users should see the same behaviour, including the saved file name shown in the confirmation message.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is an internal update to the bridge project's automated tooling: the AI code-review bot and the security-scanning step move to newer versions. Nothing changes in the bridge itself.

prs.title: feat(imaging): bin as a dropdown of the camera's supported modes
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: On the Imaging tab, the binning setting is now a dropdown of the modes the connected camera actually supports (1x1, 2x2, and so on) instead of a free number box. This stops people from entering values the camera can't handle. With no camera connected, it offers 1x1 to 8x8 as before. The description says an out-of-range saved value is only adjusted for display, but the code also corrects the saved value itself, so a capture won't be sent with a binning the camera can't do.

prs.title: feat(camera): cooling-fan toggle via the bridge's Thermal Switch device
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Camera settings screen now has a Cooling fan on/off switch for the ATR2600M camera. It uses the camera bridge's existing fan control and appears only when a fan is actually available. Turning the fan off while the camera is actively cooling is refused with a warning, because cooling without the fan can damage the camera. The code goes further than the description says: the same safety block also applies in the general Switches screen, and it refuses when the camera's cooling state can't be read. The version bump in the code is one step higher than the description states.

prs.title: feat(camera): cooling controls + readout chips + Imaging rail polish (UI only)
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Camera settings screen has a redesigned Cooling section. It shows the sensor temperature, a cooler on/off switch, one-tap target temperatures with a custom field, and tappable options for the camera's readout mode instead of a dropdown. A compact version of the temperature picker now appears on the Imaging tab, 'CCD temperature' is relabeled 'Sensor temperature', and the Imaging side panel gets even spacing. The title says 'UI only', but this change also makes the camera's fan switch on and off automatically with the cooler. At this point, nothing yet stops someone from manually turning the fan off while cooling.

prs.title: Guard 5 GHz hotspot behind regulatory country, dual-interface WiFi UI fixes (3.5.1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The bridge now refuses to start a 5 GHz Wi-Fi hotspot until a country has been chosen, and the web page explains why. Without a country, the hotspot could end up on a channel that phones and laptops won't see, so the network seemed to disappear. The Wi-Fi screen also now shows the right state on boards that run a hotspot and join another network at the same time. It also got a usability tidy-up: the hotspot is at the top, the connected network is highlighted, and you can forget the network you're currently on. This is released as version 3.5.1 and includes a new automated test for the country check.

prs.title: Add server profile name, web UI layout updates, and release 3.5.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The bridge can now store an editable Profile Name. It is shown as a badge in the web page header, and apps like Ara can read and change it. The web page layout was reworked: a live clock sits in the header, Sync Time, Restart and Shutdown buttons appear on every tab, and the Wi-Fi country picker moved under the Wi-Fi switch. The code also makes saved settings safely handle quotes, backslashes and line breaks, which the description doesn't mention. This is released as version 3.5.0, with the README hardware list updated.

prs.title: feat(mount): show the slew target (Target RA/Dec) in the mount panel
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Mount settings screen now shows Target RA and Target Dec, which is where the telescope was last told to go, next to where it's currently pointing. Parking or sending the mount home hides the old target so it doesn't linger. A new target reappears after the next move, whether it comes from Ara or from another app or handset. This was checked on real hardware and comes with new automated tests.

prs.title: fix(client): friendly errors for every remaining raw-exception site
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The remaining screens that still showed long technical error dumps now show plain, helpful messages instead. For example, 'Couldn't read the camera — your rig didn't answer. Check it's powered on and on the same network as this computer.' This covers about two dozen places, including camera optics, polar alignment, the stop-mount overlay, calibration, the image library, backups and the first-run setup.

prs.title: feat(client): live capture progress + cancel for Imaging Take One
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Imaging tab's Take One button now shows a live progress card while a photo is being taken. Previously it just said "Exposing…" with no feedback. The card shows a progress bar, seconds left, and an estimate of when the frame will be ready, then moves to a downloading stage. It also adds a Cancel button that stops the exposure, a brief "Frame ready" message, and a failure message with a Retry button. The change also quietly swaps out a web-view component in the macOS build, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: test(server): fix flaky polar-align Complete session-row test
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes an automated test for polar alignment that sometimes failed at random. The test checked for a finished step too early, before the step had actually been counted. It now waits for a more reliable signal. Only the test changed; the app itself is unchanged.
