prs.title: Fix QHY camera exposure hang and HDR readout timeout
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: This fixes a bug where QHY cameras, such as the miniCam8M, could freeze during an exposure without showing any error, sometimes taking the camera offline. The cause was that two steps of taking a picture were handled in different parts of the program, which the camera's software doesn't allow. They now run together, and the program can no longer get stuck forever waiting on the camera. It also stops the slow "Linearity HDR" mode, which takes about a minute to download, from being wrongly flagged as stuck. Both fixes were confirmed on real hardware.

prs.title: Auto-apply safe-to-review to PRs from trusted authors
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal automation change. Pull requests from a trusted contributor (currently just zeroastroboy) are now automatically marked safe for automated review, so a maintainer no longer has to tag each one by hand.

prs.title: feat(client): Polar Align panel always shows its live data
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Polar Align panel in the Imaging tab now always shows its live alignment target and error readings, instead of hiding them until you tap to expand the panel. Since polar alignment is done hands-on at the mount, the numbers now stay visible at a glance. Everything else about how it works is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(client): show observing-site lat/long in the Mount panel (mount setting improvements)
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Mount settings panel now shows your observing site's latitude and longitude, such as "12.60° N" and "75.84° W", right below the mount's current sky position. The rows only appear once a site has been set up, and the panel fetches the site from the server when it opens. Not mentioned in the description: the sky-position labels were also renamed to "RA (Right Ascension)" and "Dec (Declination)".

prs.title: feat(client): HIG-style filter-wheel panel + browser WebSocket transport
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: In the Filter Wheel settings screen, you can now tap anywhere on a filter's row to select it, instead of reaching for a small button at the far right. The app responds right away: the chosen row shows a spinner, the other rows are locked, and a check mark moves to the new filter within a couple of seconds, rather than after up to 15 seconds. The browser version of the app can now also keep a live connection to the rig, so live equipment status and notifications work in a web browser instead of hanging on "Server connecting…".

prs.title: Fix WiFi dual-interface device roles, in-range Forget; release 3.4.1
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Joining a WiFi network from the device's web page no longer knocks out the device's own hotspot on boards that can run both at once, such as the Orange Pi 4 Pro and ASIAIR. Saved networks that are currently in range now have a Forget button, so a network saved with the wrong password can be removed and re-joined correctly. The connection-drop warning is also skipped when you are browsing over the hotspot and it will stay up. This PR also ships release 3.4.1.

prs.title: fix(client): Imaging filter picker follows the physical filter wheel
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The filter picker on the Imaging tab now stays in sync with the physical filter wheel in both directions. Picking a filter there moves the wheel, and moving the wheel from anywhere else updates the picker. This means photos are no longer labeled with a filter that wasn't actually in place. On the first connection of a session, the wheel also moves to the default L filter, and the picker shows a clear busy-then-confirmed indicator while the wheel moves. The visible changes also refresh the third-party license list and rearrange the changelog, including removing an older entry about the camera cooler fix; the description does not mention either.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 10 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automatic update of ten server-side libraries to their latest minor patch versions. No intended change in behavior.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group in /client/openastroara_client with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Automatic update of two app libraries: the secure storage library and the web-view library. The secure storage update is a major version with breaking changes. Data saved with its older, now-removed encryption methods becomes unreadable, and Android devices now need to be version 7.0 or newer, so saved logins and secrets are worth a quick check.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal only: updates the automated code-review and security-scanning tools that run on the project's build system. No change to the app.

prs.title: fix(client): profile/daemon errors read as sentences, not raw XHR text
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: When the app can't reach the telescope rig, the profiles screen and the setup wizard's equipment check now show a plain sentence like "your rig didn't answer — check it's powered on and reachable". Before, they showed confusing browser error text. If the server sends back its own explanation, that explanation is still shown word for word. The error wording in the guider setup and guiding-tuning screens was also made consistent ("Couldn't …"), and new tests lock in the wording.

prs.title: Revert "fix(client): equipment errors read as sentences, not raw DioE…
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This undoes #946, so the equipment panels and connection cards go back to their older, terser error messages while the friendlier wording is reworked. The shared friendly-message tool and its tests stay in place for the rest of the app. One side effect visible in the code: the restored equipment messages show only an error code (for example "server returned 409") instead of the server's explanation, so the clearer cooler message from #945 won't reach users in the equipment panels for now.

prs.title: fix(server+client): cooler toggle on a camera without cooling returns a clean message, not a 500
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Turning the cooler on or off for a camera that can't cool, or can't accept a target temperature, now gets a clear refusal such as "this camera does not support cooling". Before, the request crashed on the server, and browsers showed it as a misleading network error. This was seen on a Player One Mars-C II. The camera panel now also shows a greyed-out "Does not support cooling" line when a camera has no cooler. The description also says the app's equipment error text was changed to show the server's explanation, but that change does not appear in this diff.

prs.title: feat(client): mount manual slew gets a speed ladder
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The mount's manual direction pad now offers speed buttons at 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100% of the mount's top speed when the mount reports only one speed. This helps mounts like the ZWO AM5N, which previously could only nudge at full speed. Each button shows the percentage and the actual speed, and the default is a gentle middle setting. Mounts that report their own list of speeds keep that list, and no option can ever exceed the mount's maximum.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of three tools used by the project's automated checks (the AI code reviewer and the security scanner) to newer versions. There is no change to the product itself.

prs.title: fix(client): equipment errors read as sentences, not raw DioException dumps
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Error messages across all equipment panels (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, dome, rotator, switches) and the connection cards were switched from raw technical dumps to plain sentences. For example, they now say "your rig didn't answer — check it's powered on and on the same network", or show the server's own explanation when it gave one. New tests lock in the wording. Note that this change was later reverted in #949 while the wording is reworked.

prs.title: Add WiFi/synctime API reference and privilege-model docs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only. This adds a reference guide for the WiFi and clock-sync controls, written for app developers building on them such as the Ara app. It also explains how the service gets just enough system permission to manage WiFi, marks the WiFi design document as shipped, and records lessons learned while building it. The 3.4.0 release notes were corrected to match what actually shipped: the permission rule covers six actions rather than four, and the WiFi country is applied when the service starts rather than on first use.

prs.title: Add WiFi manager with web UI, NM D-Bus backend, and 3.4.0 release
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The AlpacaBridge web portal can now manage the device's WiFi from the browser. Users can scan for and join networks, manage saved networks, run a personal hotspot on 2.4 or 5 GHz for field use, turn the radio on or off, and pick the WiFi country setting. The country setting is re-applied at startup because some devices refuse to run a 5 GHz hotspot without it. The feature was tested on all eight supported devices and hides itself on setups with no WiFi. This change also cuts the 3.4.0 release and updates the build and packaging requirements.

prs.title: fix(server): a parked mount can never read as slewing (phantom-motion guard)
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Ara will no longer show a parked mount as "Slewing." Previously, a faulty or phantom device reporting both "parked" and "moving" at once made the app claim the mount was moving while it sat still. This happened with a ZWO bridge setup that had no mount attached. The app now treats "parked" as the more trustworthy signal, and new tests cover the possible combinations.

prs.title: fix(client): wizard reports bridge reachability, not a phantom device count
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The setup wizard no longer tells users it saw cameras when it has only confirmed that AlpacaBridge is reachable. Before, placeholder device slots with no hardware behind them were counted as "cameras seen." The wizard now says how many devices are advertised and that their connection is not yet verified. In that case the message also shows as an amber warning instead of a green success, a visual change the description does not mention. The device picker also labels each entry as unverified until you connect.

prs.title: ci(review): sync fork-contributor trust list with AlpacaBridge (adds zeroastroboy)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal CI change: the list of outside contributors whose pull requests get automated review is now synced with the AlpacaBridge repo. This lets their later updates keep getting reviewed. The title mentions only zeroastroboy, but the change actually adds three contributors: htly9981, Knetus56, and zeroastroboy.

prs.title: docs: true up §34 apt-repo state (live, alpacabridge 3.3.0) + DEPLOY fix + stale ROADMAP entries
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation now reflects that the OpenAstro package server, apt.openastro.net, is live and serving AlpacaBridge 3.3.0. The install instructions were corrected to match the real server setup. Planning documents now mark polar alignment and the extra sky catalogs as shipped. The installer's package description refers to the Ara app instead of the old WILMA name. The description does not mention it, but the roadmap entry for mosaic imaging was also reworded to say shooting mosaics already works and only saving mosaic progress across nights remains.

prs.title: client: retire the WILMA codename; versioned title with alpha stage + build date
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop and mobile app no longer shows the internal codename "WILMA" anywhere. The window title, About screen, dialogs, help text, and the macOS permission prompt now say "OpenAstro Ara" or "the client". The window title also shows the current version with an alpha marker (for example "OpenAstro Ara 0.0.1a"). The About screen and bug-report dialog show the build date on official builds and "(dev)" on hand-made ones. It also fixes the macOS app menu, which still showed leftover placeholder text like "About APP_NAME".

prs.title: server: scrub pre-#923 demo fixtures from real installs on boot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Some people who installed from older packages found fake demo data mixed into their own records: a sample M31 imaging night, sample notifications, and sample diagnostics. Their stats also counted images they never took. The server now quietly deletes exactly those demo entries each time it starts, and it cannot touch real data. It also keeps the demo session in place if a user had moved real images into it. Affected users will only get the cleanup once the updated install package is republished.

prs.title: Fix deb postinst udev trigger so rules apply to already-plugged devices
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Some equipment that was already plugged in when AlpacaBridge was installed could not be used right away. For example, a ZWO focuser failed on first connect until the user unplugged it or rebooted. The installer now makes the system reapply its device-access rules to hardware that is already connected, so it works immediately after installing.

prs.title: Release 3.3.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the official 3.3.0 release of AlpacaBridge, dated 2026-08-08. It bundles previously merged work: the new OnStep telescope driver, clock syncing for computers without internet, and several newly verified cameras and mounts. The README was rewritten to match the openastro.net website and now lists 50 drivers across fourteen brands and a new Orange Pi 4 Pro setup guide. The rewrite also drops the old "In the news" section, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: Add clock sync for internet-less SBCs (sync-clock.sh + troubleshooting)
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: Small telescope computers with no internet access often boot with the wrong time, which throws off image timestamps. There are now two ways to fix that. A helper script can copy the correct time from another computer, and a new "Sync Time" button in the web control page sets the clock from your browser's time. The web page also now shows a live server clock that turns red when it drifts from your computer's time. The description doesn't mention this clock, and it no longer matches one detail: reading the time is now allowed rather than refused. A troubleshooting guide was added as well, and the clock setting is open to anyone on the local network, like the existing restart and shutdown controls.

prs.title: Validate ToupTek GPCMOS02000KPA + fix LastExposureStartTime timing
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The ToupTek GPCMOS02000KPA guide camera is now officially verified to work, passing the standard ASCOM test suite with no problems. Testing turned up a bug in the ToupTek camera support: the reported start time of an exposure could be about 2 seconds early after changing the image size or area. It now records the moment the exposure actually starts.

prs.title: Validate Player One Mars-C II: ConformU 4.5.0 clean
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The Player One Mars-C II, a small uncooled guide camera, is now officially listed as tested and working. It already worked with the existing Player One support, but had never been formally checked. It passed the standard compatibility test on a Linux arm64 computer with no problems. No software behavior changed; this PR adds the test report and updates the supported-hardware list and changelog.

prs.title: Validate ZWO ASI585MC Pro ConformU 4.5.0 on arm64
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: The ZWO ASI585MC Pro, a cooled color astronomy camera, is now officially listed as tested and working. It passed the standard compatibility test with no problems using the existing ZWO camera support, so no code changes were needed. This PR adds the test report and updates the supported-hardware list and changelog.

prs.title: Validate Gemini Astro Automatic FlatPanel v2 on ConformU 4.5.0
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: The Gemini Astro automatic flat panel was re-tested with the newer version of the standard compatibility checker and passed with no problems. The re-test confirms that recent changes to how the software finds USB devices did not break this panel. Only the test report, the supported-hardware list and the changelog were updated; no software behavior changed.

prs.title: Photos-style Image Library, §65.4 caching + warmer, §69 self-documenting UI, six add-on catalogs with offline-first seeds
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a large update across the image library, in-app help and sky catalogs. The image library now has a phone-photos-style layout, and thumbnails are saved after the first view instead of being rebuilt every time. On the Pi this cut thumbnail loading from about 1.5 seconds to near-instant, and there is now a button to clear that saved data. Every setting and equipment control now has an info button with written help, including notes for the specific connected hardware, and these buttons replace a separate manual. Six new deep-sky catalogs (about 3,000 nebulae and galaxies) ship inside the installer so they work with no internet, and planning search can now find them. Manual brightness adjustment was removed from the image viewer at the user's request.

prs.title: Add OnStep telescope driver
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: Adds support for telescope mounts running OnStep, a popular open-source controller used in home-built and upgraded mounts. The mount connects over USB and supports guiding, manual slewing at any speed, and tracking, and it can be set up from the web page. It passed the standard compatibility test on a real mount with no errors. The PR also includes automated tests and detailed notes on the mount's quirks for future maintainers.

prs.title: Exclude cpp/cleartext-transmission CodeQL query (serial-port false positive)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to the automated security scanner. The scanner raised a false alarm that telescope location data was sent unencrypted, but that data only travels over the USB cable to the mount, not over a network. That single check is now switched off for the whole project, so it will no longer flag this or any similar code anywhere in the project. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: ci(review): force single-pass inline reviews (fixes the #932 no-comment failure)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated code-review bot now has to do its whole review in one go and post its comment before it finishes. It is no longer allowed to hand work off to background helpers. This fixes why large pull requests such as #932 never got a review: the bot would say it was waiting for its helpers, and the run shut down with the review still unposted. It also gets a few more read-only commands so it can compare large changes properly.

prs.title: ci(review): upload the review agent's execution transcript as a run artifact
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each review-bot run now saves a record of everything the bot did, kept for a week. This covers only the review job for branches inside the repository, not contributor forks. Before this, the record was thrown away, which made it very hard to work out why reviews were failing. That record is what later revealed the real cause of the #932 problem. It has no effect on whether checks pass.

prs.title: ci(review): restore the claude[bot] path for same-repo PRs; forks keep the label-gated flow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This puts back the original review-bot setup for pull requests made from branches inside the repository, which had reliably reviewed more than 900 changes. A recent change, #931, had quietly stopped the bot from posting reviews on those pull requests. Pull requests from outside contributors keep the newer setup, where a maintainer must add a "safe-to-review" label before the bot runs. Both paths keep the recent fix for paging through large changes and the check that fails if no review gets posted.

prs.title: ci(review): allow read-only diff paging so the bot can review large PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The review bot may now use a few extra read-only commands to page through very large changes. On the roughly 24,000-line change in #932, these commands were being blocked, and the bot gave up before posting a review. This alone did not fully fix #932; the real cause was found and fixed later in #937.

prs.title: fix(packaging): normalize Debian package file modes
prs.author: Jewber11
prs.summary: The Linux install package now sets file permissions correctly. Ordinary files such as libraries and documents are no longer marked as runnable programs, and stray permission settings from the build machine no longer carry over into the package. The code also does something the description doesn't mention: it makes the helper scripts used for storage and USB setup runnable again. Before this, they shipped unrunnable, which the changelog says broke those features. The contributor tested this on a real ARM64 package.

prs.title: ci(review): adopt AlpacaBridge's label-gated fork review
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The review bot can now review pull requests from outside contributors, but only after a maintainer adds a "safe-to-review" label. Only contributors on an approved list are covered, currently one person. This copies a setup already working in a sister project. The description says same-repo pull requests were unchanged, but the code switched all runs to a different login method. That change silently stopped reviews from posting on same-repo pull requests and was reverted in #934. It also quietly lets the review step fail without failing the job, leaving a separate follow-up check to catch missing reviews.

prs.title: ci(review): fork PRs take a maintainer-review path instead of dying on the withheld secret
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Pull requests from outside contributors were always blocked because the automatic review bot cannot run on them. It needs a secret key that GitHub withholds from outside copies of the project for security reasons. Now the bot only runs on the team's own pull requests. For outside contributions, the required check passes once a maintainer reviews the change and posts an approval or 'issues found' comment written after the latest code. One small difference from the description: that timing check uses the time recorded on the latest commit, not the moment it was actually pushed.

prs.title: §29 exFAT take-home drives: format choice, Check disk, Eject, live device watch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: New storage drives are now formatted by default in a format that Windows and Mac can read directly, so users can unplug the drive at the end of a night and read their images at home. Drives are set up the way store-bought drives are and labeled ARA-DISK, which fixes two problems that made Macs refuse to open them. The Storage settings gain a 'Check disk' button for repairs after a power cut and an 'Eject' button for safe removal. Plugged-in or removed drives now appear in the app within seconds. The code also includes two changes the description does not mention: a new Settings option to wipe and rebuild the imaging stats from the connected drive, and new setups now file images in a folder per target by default.

prs.title: Widen udev_mangle() charset and fix stale exists() doc (#183, #184)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This makes automatic detection of USB-serial astronomy devices more reliable when a device's maker or product name contains punctuation such as commas or parentheses. The matching logic now follows the same character rules Linux itself uses when naming these devices. It also corrects a misleading code comment and adds a test.

prs.title: Fix serial raw-fallback udev patterns and throwing exists() (#181)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes two bugs from the earlier auto-detect cleanup. First, eight device types (including Celestron, SynScan, iOptron and several WandererAstro accessories) could fail to be found when detection fell back to a slower search, because names were compared with underscores in one place and spaces in the other. Second, a permissions problem while checking for devices could abort the whole search, including backup detection paths such as ZWO's WiFi fallback. The change also adds the first tests for this shared detection code and developer notes explaining both traps.

prs.title: Fix serial auto-detect directory_iterator/is_symlink TOCTOU (#179)
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: Automatic detection for ten kinds of mounts, focusers, filter wheels and other accessories could fail entirely if a device was unplugged mid-search, losing devices it had already found. That search now lives in one shared, crash-proof piece instead of ten separate copies. It also lets most device types find a second identical USB adapter that Linux's naming used to hide. The change was tested on real hardware with no regressions seen.

prs.title: §44 mirror naming, capture/preview speedups, Imaging tab redesign, frame Statistics, docs reconciliation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: After taking a picture, the preview now appears in about 5 seconds instead of roughly a minute on a Raspberry Pi 4, and at higher resolution. The Imaging tab was redesigned so the image fills the screen, with controls in a side panel and a new statistics readout showing brightness figures and clipping warnings. Desktop backups now use the same readable file and folder names as the rig instead of random IDs. The change also fixes typed exposure and gain values being ignored unless Enter was pressed, supports setting up brand-new blank drives, and fills in missing release notes for many earlier changes.

prs.title: chore: regenerate 3rd-party licenses for the #926 nuget bumps
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal housekeeping. This updates the project's list of third-party software licenses to match the library versions updated in #926. That update was merged while the automated license check was failing, and this change gets that check passing again. No behavior changes for users.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of three outside libraries to newer minor versions: one used for the server's interactive API documentation page, and two used to turn processed images into JPEGs. The release notes list no specific changes, and no user-visible effect is expected. The matching license list was not updated here, which caused a failing check that #928 later fixed.

prs.title: Fix Gemini flat panel undetectable on by-id name collision
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: Fixes a case where a Gemini flat panel (Lite or v2) could go missing from automatic device detection. This happened when it was plugged in alongside another generic USB-serial device, such as an OnStep mount. These cheap adapters identify themselves identically, so the system's usual device list only shows one of them. Detection now always scans the raw serial ports as well and skips any port already tried. The fix was re-verified with the official compatibility checker and on real hardware. The trimmed diff omitted the actual code change, so only the refreshed test report and documentation updates could be confirmed directly.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal update to the automated security-scanning tool used in the project's build checks, moving it to a slightly newer version. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: Fix Gemini flat panel auto-detect missing ttyACM devices
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: Fixes automatic detection of Gemini flat panels (Lite and v2) on systems where Linux's usual list of connected serial devices isn't available. In that situation, the backup search only checked one family of port names. The panel's controller actually shows up under a different name, so a working, plugged-in panel was never found. The backup search now checks both port types, and it was confirmed working on real hardware.

prs.title: Release 3.2.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Marks the official 3.2.0 release by dating the changelog entry and updating the version shown on the project's front page to 3.2.0 (August 5, 2026). This is a documentation-only change with no code changes.

prs.title: Update docs to openastro.net, add local logo image, bump to 3.2.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The project's documentation now points to the OpenAstro website instead of the old GitHub wiki, including the setup guide for each supported device and the FAQ. The logo in the main documents now comes from a copy stored in the project itself, because the old web address for it stopped working. The platform badge was shortened, and the version number was raised to 3.2.0 ahead of a release that will be published separately. The image file itself does not appear in the trimmed changes, but every document now points to it.

prs.title: §29 storage & filenames: USB drive flow, human file naming, full FITS headers, notification inbox
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This large update changes how and where images are saved. Users can now pick a USB drive in the app, have it mounted or reformatted, and scan it for images already on it; the app refuses to switch drives while a capture or sequence is running. Saved images now get readable names based on the night and frame type instead of random codes. They also carry much more descriptive information, such as location, telescope, temperature, weather, and sun and moon positions, with a switch for each group so users can leave out things like where they live. A missing astronomy data file that caused wrong sun and moon positions is now included, and the update also adds a notification inbox and rewrites many settings screens in plainer language.

prs.title: Fix QHY exposure watchdog false-failing miniCam8 on slow readout
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Fixes QHY cameras, notably the miniCam8, wrongly reporting a failed exposure when the image was simply slow to download on devices like a Raspberry Pi. The time the driver waits after an exposure before giving up went from 15 seconds to 60 seconds. That is long enough for slow downloads but still catches a truly stuck camera within a minute. Other camera brands are unchanged.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal maintenance: updates the automated code security scanning tool to a slightly newer version. There is no effect on users.

prs.title: Validate ZWO AM5N ConformU 4.4.0 + park/tracking/connect timing fixes
prs.author: zeroastroboy
prs.summary: The ZWO AM5N mount now passes the standard ASCOM compatibility test with no errors, and it is marked as supported. Getting there required four fixes: the mount now correctly stays reported as parked, refuses to start tracking while parked, and answers quickly right after connecting and when asked whether it is parked. The changes also include something the description doesn't mention: a new option to find a ZWO mount automatically over USB or WiFi and connect to it, with a matching choice in the web interface.

prs.title: fix(client): settings tell the truth + rig-operator conveniences (pre-sky cleanup 1–2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes fake or placeholder information from the app's settings and replaces it with real data. Storage now shows actual free and total disk space, and the profile screen shows the real active profile and opens the full profile manager. The weather and safety screens now show the real safety limits instead of invented numbers. The update also adds handy controls: restarting the server from the app (right away or once it's idle), seeing the server's version, and opening health details from the Imaging screen. Long sequence lists now load completely, and a few dead menu entries were removed. The storage and restart features have not yet been tested on real equipment.

prs.title: refactor: relocate §77 planetary to the feature/planetary incubation branch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The unfinished planetary (high-speed video) capture work has been taken out of the main codebase and moved to a separate long-term side branch. This undoes four earlier planetary changes (#910, #911, #914, #915), including their tests and installer pieces. The capture engine itself works on real hardware, but a usable planetary feature still needs months of work on the interactive experience. The team chose not to ship half a feature and will return to it once the deep-sky experience is polished. The design documents stay in the main project.

prs.title: Add Gemini Astro Automatic FlatPanel v2 driver (ConformU 4.4.0)
prs.author: Knetus56
prs.summary: Adds support for the Gemini Astro Automatic FlatPanel v2, a flat panel with a motorized cover, alongside the existing light-only Gemini model. Users choose between the two models in the web settings page. The driver was built from open-source reference code and then confirmed on a real unit, passing the standard compatibility checker with no problems. It also fixes a bug where turning the light on or off could freeze for several seconds while the cover was still moving. The cover's "stop" button cannot physically stop this model's motor; it only stops the driver from reporting that the cover is moving.

prs.title: fix(client): server discovery survives broken in-app multicast
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now find the observatory server on the local network even when the usual automatic discovery fails. This was prompted by a real outage on Macs where the server list stayed empty. Found servers are now saved by their numeric network address rather than a name that only works while automatic discovery is healthy. If automatic discovery finds nothing within about 2.5 seconds, the app scans the local network directly. The description says both methods run side by side, but the code only starts the scan as a fallback. The change also adds automated tests and makes sure a scan stops when the connect screen no longer needs it.

prs.title: feat(video): max ZWO USB bandwidth + high-speed mode for video capture
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Planetary video capture now asks ZWO cameras to use their full USB speed and fast readout mode, which were off or limited by default. In hardware testing this raised frame rates substantially, in one case from 280 to about 480 frames per second. The code also applies similar settings to Player One cameras (full USB bandwidth and no frame-rate cap), which the description does not mention. This change was later removed from the main codebase by #917 and now lives on the planetary side branch.

prs.title: feat(video): §77 on-hardware spike fixes — SDK enumeration, arm64 O_DIRECT, Player One glue
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes three problems found in the first real-hardware test of planetary video capture. Cameras are now properly detected before being opened. Fast direct-to-disk saving now works on the ARM-based devices the project ships on; previously it was silently falling back to a slower method. Player One cameras are now supported alongside ZWO, with the camera brand chosen when entering planetary mode. Testing showed the SD card was the only bottleneck. This work was later removed from the main codebase by #917 and moved to the planetary side branch.

prs.title: feat: relay SQM + sky temperature; weather panel lists the full sky picture
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The weather panel now shows sky darkness readings (SQM) and the sky sensor's temperature from stations that report them. It also calculates related figures: the faintest visible star magnitude, sky brightness, and a darkness index. Sun and Moon altitude are now shown when the site location is set. These calculated sky rows appear even if the station reports no sensors, with a note explaining that. The formulas were checked against the weather station's own published values, and the whole path was verified on real hardware.

prs.title: fix: wizard/guider polish batch + framing mosaic runs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A batch of fixes found while testing the setup wizard on a real telescope rig. Cameras on the same computer no longer show up twice when searching for equipment, the guider is now labeled "OpenAstro Guider" everywhere instead of "PHD2", and the guiding setup screen now shows real device names, has a Refresh button that actually works, and lets you pick a mount and rotator. Typing in a latitude and longitude now fills in the time zone automatically unless you set it yourself, and all power/dew switch hubs are added on first setup. Most importantly, a mosaic laid out in the sky map now creates one target per panel; before, it quietly produced a single-target run.

prs.title: feat(server): §77 P2 — planetary mode arbitration, usbfs auto-tune, capture REST/WS surface
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now switch a camera into a high-speed "planetary mode" and record planet videos, controlled remotely from an app. It refuses to do this while a normal imaging run is using the camera, and it hands the camera back when you leave the mode. On Linux it also enlarges a USB memory setting based on how much memory the machine has, so fast video doesn't choke. This is the behind-the-scenes piece only: there is no user screen for it yet, and it has not been tried on a real camera.

prs.title: ci: allow Knetus56 to trigger the label-gated fork review
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal CI change: an outside contributor, Knetus56, can now have the automated code review run on their own pull requests. They get no extra access, and a maintainer still has to label each pull request before it is reviewed. The onboarding steps for trusted outside contributors are now written down in the project notes.

prs.title: feat(server): §77 P1 — planetary video capture core (IVideoCapture, ring buffer, SER writer, ZWO P/Invoke)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the core engine for recording high-speed planet video on the server. It saves frames to disk in the standard format used by planetary stacking tools, and it counts exactly how many frames were captured, saved, or dropped, so nothing is lost silently. It supports ZWO cameras first. Nothing uses the engine yet, and the camera part has only been checked with test data, not a real camera.

prs.title: docs: §77 placement amendment — capture engine in Ara Server, AlpacaBridge stays pure Alpaca
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Design documents only: the team decided the planet video recorder will live in the main Ara server rather than in AlpacaBridge. AlpacaBridge stays a plain, standard equipment bridge with no Ara-specific features, and the earlier AlpacaBridge version of this work was closed and kept only as a reference. The documents also drop the old statement that planetary imaging is permanently out of scope, since it will now be handled by this separate recording path.

prs.title: docs: §77 planetary/SER capture design + parked daytime-PA note
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Design documents only: this lays out the plan for adding planetary video capture, covering fast recording, pointing at planets, and a Live-tab mode and sequence steps in the app. The work is split into six steps. It also records a daytime polar alignment idea, using the Moon or Sun, which is on hold until the maintainer decides. This first draft placed the recorder inside AlpacaBridge, a choice reversed the same day by #909.

prs.title: feat(client): §76 S5 — save-time derivations + §37 supersession note
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a new equipment profile is saved, the app now works out two plate-solving and autofocus settings from the user's gear, since the wizard no longer asks about them. One controls how much images are shrunk before the app matches them against star maps (plate solving); the other sets how far the focuser moves between autofocus test shots. If a needed detail is missing, such as a focuser that doesn't report its step size, or if the user had already hand-tuned a value in a copied profile, the existing setting is kept. The design doc also marks the old 17-step wizard spec as replaced, and notes that the plate-solve search area is deliberately left at its default rather than calculated, which is narrower than the original plan.

prs.title: feat: §76 S4 — Finish provisions the guider, kicks darks, Done view with live progress
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Finishing the setup wizard now also sets up the guiding software with the new profile and starts building a library of calibration 'dark' frames for the guide camera. The wizard then shows a 'You're all set' screen with live progress, and the user can leave at any time because the work continues on the server. The guide exposure range chosen in the wizard is now saved with the profile, and the server rejects ranges that are backwards or not positive. If guider setup or the darks build fails, the user sees a note instead of an error, and saving partway through the wizard skips both steps.

prs.title: feat(client): §76 S3 — Guiding screen: decisions, exposure range, darks toggle
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The wizard's Guiding screen now asks only the essential questions: separate guide scope or off-axis guider, the shortest and longest guide exposure to use, and whether to build the dark-frame library now (on by default). The exposure range feeds both the dark library and the guiding limits so the two always match, and the user can't continue if the shortest is set longer than the longest. The guide camera's pixel size is now read from the camera itself, with a manual entry field kept under Advanced for cameras that can't report it. The previous button that pushed the camera choice to the guider right away was removed, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: feat(client): §76 S2 — five-screen wizard shell + "Your equipment" screen
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The profile setup wizard shrinks from 17 steps to 5: Welcome, Connect, Your equipment, Guiding, and Review/Save. The new 'Your equipment' screen finds the user's devices, assigns them automatically when there's no ambiguity, reads their details directly from the hardware, and shows them as cards. Missing details come with a link to the device's own setup page and a Recheck button, plus a manual fallback field. The old per-device and capture-setup screens are gone; those settings now use defaults and can be changed later in Options.

prs.title: feat(client): §76 S1 — wizard equipment readiness model + fact-fetch layer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes groundwork for the redesigned setup wizard's equipment screen. It connects to each assigned device at the same time, reads its details, and decides whether each device is ready or is missing something important. It also builds the link to each device's standard setup page for fixing problems. There are no visible changes yet; the screens that use this came in a later PR.

prs.title: docs: §76 Wizard 2.0 design — five-screen setup wizard
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only: this adds the design plan for 'Wizard 2.0', which shrinks the 17-step profile setup to five screens. The idea is to read equipment details straight from the connected hardware instead of asking for them, and to ask the user only real decisions like profile name, guiding setup, and guide exposure range. It also plans for finishing the wizard to set up guiding and start building calibration frames automatically, and splits the work into five follow-up PRs.

prs.title: feat(client): guider rebrand — PHD2 wording becomes OpenAstro Guider
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Everywhere the app used to say "PHD2" to users, it now says "OpenAstro Guider". That covers settings, help text, setup wizard steps, error messages, and pop-ups. Behind-the-scenes names and saved setting keys were deliberately left alone so nothing breaks, and searching settings for "phd2" still finds the guider page. The parts of the change visible in the trimmed diff match this description.

prs.title: §45 capture-fetch + solver profile bridge + guider profile-follow + stuck-device removal
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a batch of problems found while testing on the real telescope rig. The biggest one is that polar alignment now works when the guider runs on a different machine: the server downloads the captured picture from the guider instead of failing right away and wrongly blaming the sky. Plate solving no longer fails on a fully configured rig because of missing focal length or solver location. A connected guider now follows along when you switch profiles mid-session. You can also delete a stuck, disconnected switch device, and the launch button goes back to the server chooser screen.

prs.title: Serve saved capture frames over HTTP so remote clients can retrieve them
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider can now hand saved capture images to other computers over the network, which is what the main app needs for polar alignment when the guider runs elsewhere. It also reports the saved file's name so the other computer knows what to ask for. Safeguards stop anyone from using this to read files outside the capture folder. It also fixes a bug where auto-named saves ignored a custom capture folder setting.

prs.title: §25 Setup-stage flow + §63.20 guider setup wizard (client + server)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new "Setup" stage between Planning and Run, with a "Tonight" checklist: connect equipment, polar align, and calibration frames. Running without polar alignment now shows a gentle warning instead of blocking you. It also adds a step-by-step guider setup wizard that shows real device names, can find equipment across the whole network, fills in the camera's pixel size automatically, and builds dark frames with a progress bar. Behind the scenes, the guider's saved profile now uses the same name as your app profile, and older profiles are renamed without losing data.

prs.title: Collapse released 3.1.1 and 3.0.2 CHANGELOG sections
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tidies the change log so the two older releases, 3.1.1 and 3.0.2, fold up like the others, leaving only the newest release expanded. This is formatting only and changes no behavior.

prs.title: Release 3.1.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Marks version 3.1.2 as released by updating the version number, the README badge, and the change log date. This release contains two already-merged fixes: shared devices are more reliable when several computers use them at once, and a slow memory buildup when devices are repeatedly added and removed is fixed.

prs.title: Fix #162, #163: prune op-mutex map; per-address Connected client keys
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Follow-up to the shared-device fix. Clients are now told apart by both the name they send and the computer they connect from, so two apps on different machines can no longer accidentally disconnect each other's shared telescope or camera. Removing a device now also cleans up the bookkeeping kept for it, so repeatedly adding and removing devices no longer slowly eats memory. The code goes a little further than the description: it also blocks late-arriving requests for an already-removed device from re-creating that bookkeeping, and it builds the client identity in a tamper-resistant format rather than the simple 'name@address' the description mentions.

prs.title: Fix #160: per-client Connected refcounting in the Alpaca router
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a serious problem where several apps shared one device, such as an imaging program and a guider on the same mount. When any one app disconnected, the bridge cut the link for all of them, and it could also freeze the iOptron driver until a restart. The bridge now tracks which apps are connected to each device and only drops the link when the last one leaves. Apps that go silent for more than 10 minutes are forgotten so they can't hold a device open forever. This was confirmed on real hardware, and the PR also publishes release 3.1.1, whose notes also cover earlier filter-wheel and web-page fixes.

prs.title: ci: allow Jewber11 as trusted fork contributor for label-gated reviews
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal automation change: adds contributor Jewber11 to the list of trusted outside contributors. Their own updates to an approved pull request will now re-run the automated code review without a maintainer having to step in.

prs.title: ci: label-gate Claude review so maintainers can enable it on fork PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal automation change, copied from the AlpacaBridge setup. The automated code review can now run on pull requests from outside contributors, but only after a maintainer adds a 'safe-to-review' label, and removing the label stops it. Pull requests from within the project are still reviewed automatically, and dependency-update pull requests are skipped. The change also bundles several setup fixes needed to make this work safely.

prs.title: fix(client/macos): workstation window opens normal-sized, not maximized
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: On Mac, the main workstation window no longer forces itself to fill the whole screen. The first time it opens at a comfortable default size, centered on the screen. After that, macOS remembers wherever the user last moved or resized it. The small launch screen no longer overwrites that saved size.

prs.title: feat(client): guiding tuning moves from inline panel to a Tune dialog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guiding section of the Imaging screen now shows only live guiding status and its accuracy chart. The adjustment sliders have moved into a separate 'Tune' pop-up window, following a more Mac-like design. The existing safeguards still apply, and the Apply button is now also disabled while the guider is disconnected. Because this builds on an earlier PR, the code also includes some layout fixes that the summary only hints at: the lower panels and the bottom toolbar now scroll instead of overflowing on smaller windows, and the polar-alignment target graphic is smaller. It also includes a small behind-the-scenes server wiring change for the polar-alignment history.

prs.title: fix(server): resolve IPolarAlignmentLog against IAraDatabase, not the concrete type
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Urgent fix: every polar alignment request to the server was failing with an error because of a setup mistake introduced in #889. It slipped through because the automated tests used a stand-in instead of the real component. The change also includes app changes the description doesn't mention. On the Imaging screen, the stack of panels below the image now scrolls within a limited area instead of overflowing smaller windows, and the polar alignment target graphic is slightly smaller.

prs.title: feat(client): §45 polar-align bullseye panel in the Imaging tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now polar align their telescope from the Imaging tab. A new panel lets them start the routine, shows progress while it measures the mount's axis, and then displays a live bullseye target. The target is colored red, yellow, or green by how far off the alignment is, and it zooms in as the error shrinks. The panel also gives plain directions for which way to turn each adjustment knob. The Done button only activates once alignment is within the tolerance set in the user's profile, and the panel warns when frames repeatedly fail to solve or the routine pauses or fails.

prs.title: feat(client): §45 polar-align API + WS state layer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork in the desktop app for the new polar alignment feature. It lets the app talk to the server to start, stop, and finish an alignment and to read and save alignment settings. It also keeps track of live progress updates, including errors and failed-solve streaks. Nothing is visible to users yet; the on-screen panel arrived in the next PR.

prs.title: feat(server): §45.12/§45.13 polar-align settings, session log, complete endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds user-adjustable polar alignment settings to each equipment profile, such as exposure length and how accurate the alignment must be. Older profiles automatically get sensible defaults. The server now keeps a record of each alignment session, noting whether it was completed, aborted, or failed, along with the accuracy achieved. It also adds a way to mark an alignment as done. One piece of this setup was wired up incorrectly and caused the alignment features to fail on a real server; that was fixed shortly after in #892.

prs.title: feat(server): §45 polar-align engine — 2-point seed, live adjust loop, WS stream
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now run a complete polar alignment routine. It takes two measurements with the guide camera, moving the telescope between them, to work out how far the mount is pointing from the celestial pole. It then enters a live mode that updates the error as the user turns the mount's adjustment knobs. The routine pauses and keeps retrying if the sky can't be read five times in a row, reports clear reasons when it fails, and always restores the mount's tracking and cleans up its temporary images. It also streams live progress updates for the app to display.

prs.title: feat(client): §63.18 live guiding panel — real-time RMS + on-the-fly tuning
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a Guiding panel to the Imaging tab that shows the guider's current status and live guiding accuracy, plus a chart of the last five minutes. From the same panel, users can adjust several guiding settings, such as how aggressively it corrects and dithering distance. These changes take effect without interrupting guiding. Settings that would require reconnecting equipment are deliberately left out, and the controls are disabled when no guider is connected.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group in /client/openastroara_client with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of three third-party libraries used by the client app: one handles network requests, and two manage app state. The bundled license list was updated to match, with a note that the licenses themselves did not change. This is internal maintenance with no intended change for users. The code raises the required version for two of the three libraries, but leaves the minimum version setting for the second state-management library as it was.

prs.title: feat: §63.19 guide setup type — guide scope vs OAG with derived focal length
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now say whether their rig guides through a separate guide scope or through an off-axis guider (OAG), both in Settings and in the setup wizard. With a guide scope, you still type in its focal length. With an OAG, the app works it out from the main telescope's focal length and reducer and shows how it got the number, so the guiding software gets the right figure without manual math. In the wizard, the OAG figure ignores the reducer until settings are next saved. Beyond what the description mentions, the server also replaces any unrecognized setup choice with the guide-scope default.

prs.title: Fix QHY CFW mid-move position spam and stale web-UI config edits
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Fixes a problem with the QHY built-in filter wheel. While the wheel was turning, it reported whatever slot it happened to be passing, which led imaging software like NINA to show false 'wrong filter' errors. It now reports 'moving' until the wheel settles on the requested filter, which was confirmed on real hardware. Separately, the web setup page now reloads the latest device settings before opening the Edit form, so an old browser tab can no longer overwrite newer settings. It also finds the device by its identity rather than its position in the list, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: ci: Bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.181 to 1.0.183 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine version bump of the automated AI code-review tool used in the project's build pipeline. Internal only, with no effect on users.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.17 manual guider restart + polish — campaign close-out
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a way to manually restart the guiding program from Ara. It works even when the guider is frozen or disconnected, and the result is reported back through the usual status updates. The error message about guider connections now points users to the full guider equipment settings. The user guide was updated to explain that all guider setup, including equipment and the dark library, is done inside Ara, with no need for the guiding program's own web page. This completes the planned guider-configuration work, and adds tests for the restart and for the 'dark library is out of date' alert.

prs.title: feat(client): §63.17 dark-library management — delete with confirm + invalidation banner
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the guider calibration window, users can now delete the stored dark library or defect map, each with its own button. A confirmation step is required, and the buttons are disabled while a build is running. If the guide camera is changed while a dark library exists, a dismissible warning now appears saying the darks may be out of date and a rebuild is recommended. The warning clears automatically after a successful rebuild. When the guiding program refuses a delete, its own explanation is now shown to the user.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.17 dark-library delete + invalidation on guide-camera change
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now delete the guider's stored dark frames and bad-pixel map from Ara, either both together or just one of them. The system also warns when the guide camera is switched while those calibration files exist, since they belong to the old camera and should be rebuilt. To avoid pointless warnings, it only compares against the camera sent earlier in the same session, so the first settings push after a restart never triggers the warning.

prs.title: feat(client): §63.17 guider equipment panel — pickers, Alpaca discovery, apply-to-guider
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's Guider settings now have a 'Guider equipment' section. Users can pick the guide camera, mount, secondary mount and rotator, search the guider's network for Alpaca devices and tap one to fill in its address, then send everything to the guider with an Apply button. The setup wizard's guider step gains a guide-camera picker. This means users no longer need the guider's own web page to choose equipment.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.17 guider equipment apply + on-demand profile push
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now store the user's guider equipment choices (camera, mount, secondary mount, rotator and Alpaca device address) in the profile. It sends them to the guider on connect, or on demand through a new 'push settings now' action, and blank choices are skipped. Because the guider only accepts these changes while its equipment is off, the push briefly disconnects and reconnects it. If the reconnect fails, the push is reported as an error rather than a success.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.17 guider equipment choices + daemon-side Alpaca discovery
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now ask the guider which cameras, mounts and other devices it can use, and have the guider search its own network for Alpaca devices. This is groundwork for letting users pick guider equipment inside Ara. The code also rejects any search that would run longer than 60 seconds in total, a limit the description does not spell out, so each search stays quick.

prs.title: docs(design): §63.17 — guider equipment management in Ara Client (plan)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Planning document only. It adds a six-step plan for moving all guider setup into the Ara app: listing and searching for equipment, applying choices, adding pickers to the app, managing dark frames, and a manual guider restart. The goal is that users never need the guider's separate web page.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal maintenance: updates three automated tools used by the project's build checks, namely the automated code-review bot and the security scanner. There is no change to the product itself.

prs.title: feat(server): §38.10a — resume refinement skips a target below the horizon limit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a paused imaging run is resumed, the server now checks whether the target has since sunk below the user's horizon limit. If it has, the server skips the re-centering and refocusing it would otherwise do and shows a warning with the target's current height and the limit. The plan's own rules then decide what happens next. If the height can't be worked out, the resume goes ahead as normal, so this check can only save wasted time and never block a resume.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.10a — generated target blocks carry an AboveHorizonCondition
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imaging runs built from the Planning tools now stop working on a target once it sets below the horizon limit, and move on to the next target. Before this, they kept taking frames of a target that had dropped too low. The code also adds a hidden "run once" rule to each target, which the description doesn't mention. Without it, the horizon check would have made each target repeat all night. A server-side test was added to lock in that behavior.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.10 resume dialog — re-center + optional refocus choice
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Resuming a paused run in the app now opens a short dialog with three choices: resume and re-center the target (the default), re-center and also refocus, or just resume. Closing the dialog cancels the resume. The Resume button and the keyboard shortcuts all use this same dialog, and a brief message appears while the telescope re-centers. One change the description doesn't mention: resuming from the emergency-stop screen now always re-centers without asking, and "skip this target" resumes without re-centering.

prs.title: feat(server): §38.10 resume refinement — plate-solve re-center + optional refocus before the gate releases
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a paused run resumes on the same target, the server can now re-aim the telescope precisely at that target, and optionally refocus, before imaging continues. Older versions of the app get the re-centering automatically, without refocus. The server skips this step if the run has already moved past that target or no aiming solver is set up. It always tells the user the outcome, and a failure never leaves the run stuck in pause. Stopping or aborting during this step cancels it cleanly.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.9 live mid-run editing — edits join the executing run
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now lets people change a sequence while it is running. Adding a target from Planning, Framing, or Tonight's Sky puts it into the run that is already going, placed before the end-of-night warm-up and parking steps; previously this created a separate new sequence. In the sequence editor, users can add, delete, and reorder steps that haven't started yet. Anything already underway is locked, other kinds of edits are refused with a message, and undo is turned off while live. One gap versus the description: if the end-of-night steps have already begun, adding a target still falls back to creating a new sequence.

prs.title: feat(server): §38.9 live mid-run sequence editing (add/remove/reorder pending items)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now accept changes to a sequence while it is running: adding new targets, removing steps that haven't started, and reordering them. Steps that have already started, and positions before the current step, are protected. Edits are refused once the run is wrapping up, the saved sequence file is kept matching what is actually running, and other connected apps are told to refresh. The code also changes the core run loop so that a step removed while the run is paused is never run after resuming.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine dependency update with no user-facing change. It moves the testing library FluentAssertions from 7.0.0 to 7.2.2, deliberately staying on the free 7.x line for licensing reasons. It also moves the API-description library Microsoft.OpenApi from 2.7.5 to 2.11.0 and updates the third-party license list to match. A nearby code comment still says to stay on 2.7.x, but the new version is within the same 2.x series that comment is meant to protect.

prs.title: Release 3.1.0: README badge overhaul, Claude-first dev guide, new skills
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Marks the AlpacaBridge 3.1.0 release, dated 2026-07-27. It bundles the new drivers and fixes merged since 3.0.2. The README gains a row of status badges at the top, loses its donation/PayPal section, and moves Raspberry Pi lower in the supported-hardware list. The developer guide was reorganized around the AI-assisted workflow, and a new helper builds the software and installs it on a test device, while the existing compliance-test helper now checks that it is using the latest version of the testing tool.

prs.title: Fix review follow-ups: iOptron park wrap, serial drain, AsyncConnectable, Astroasis
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes several reliability issues found in earlier code reviews. iOptron mounts parked near due north (around 0/360 degrees) are now correctly recognized as parked. Disconnecting from an iOptron mount can no longer hang indefinitely on a stuck serial port; it now waits at most a quarter second. If a disconnect fails partway, a connect request queued behind it is now dropped rather than run against hardware in an unknown state, and new tests cover this. The Astroasis focuser now rejects incomplete replies from the device instead of silently using padded data.

prs.title: Add Astroasis Oasis Focuser driver, ConformU 4.4.0 validated
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Adds support for the Astroasis Oasis Focuser, controlled over USB using a communication method worked out from the vendor's own Windows driver, without bundling any vendor software. Users can move the focuser to a position, stop it, and read its built-in temperature sensor, and it can be set up from the web interface. It passed the standard ASCOM compliance test on real hardware with no errors. Per the notes, the temperature conversion has not yet been checked against a real thermometer, and the web-interface setup was not tested in a browser before merging.

prs.title: Add WandererAstro WandererBox Pro V3 driver, ConformU 4.4.0 validated
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for the WandererBox Pro V3 power box, letting users switch its power and USB ports on and off, set the adjustable voltage output, and control dew-heater strength from any compatible astronomy app. It also exposes the box's voltage, current, temperature, humidity and dew-point readings as read-only values. Hardware testing uncovered two problems that are fixed here: an unplugged humidity sensor crashed the test tool, and the maximum voltage setting was rejected. The final run passed the ASCOM compliance test cleanly. Automatic dew-heater modes still have to be set in the vendor's own app.

prs.title: Add WandererAstro SFW filter wheel driver, ConformU 4.4.0 validated
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for WandererAstro SFW filter wheels (the 8-slot SFW50, SFW50S and SFW36S), which can be set up from the web interface with custom filter names. The wheel homes itself once each time it connects, and it needs its separate 12 V power supply to actually move. It requires recent firmware (January 2026 or newer). Only the SFW36S was tested on real hardware, where it passed the ASCOM compliance test with no errors on the first try; the SFW50 models are expected to work because they use the same protocol.

prs.title: Add QHY integrated CFW filter wheel driver with HTTP/UI integration
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Adds support for the filter wheel built into certain QHY cameras, such as the miniCam8M, so it can be set up in the web interface and controlled like any other filter wheel. Because the wheel and camera share one USB connection, the camera and wheel can now connect and disconnect independently without cutting each other off. The wheel passed the standard compatibility test on real hardware, and a bug where the reported position froze at the old slot was fixed along the way. The description doesn't mention that the change also replaces the bundled QHY vendor software with a newer release (2025-09 to 2026-06), which accounts for most of the 300 changed files and also affects the existing QHY camera support.

prs.title: ci: opt out of the review action's subprocess secret scrubbing
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal fix to the automated code-review setup. The previous change, which let trusted outside contributors trigger reviews, accidentally stopped the review bot from posting its comments, so every review run failed. This turns off the setting that caused it and restores the earlier security arrangement, where a maintainer's label still decides which pull requests get reviewed.

prs.title: ci: allow listed fork contributors to trigger the label-gated review
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal change to the automated code-review setup so pushes from a named, trusted outside contributor no longer make the review job fail immediately. The maintainer's label is still the per-pull-request approval, and this adds a per-person allow list, currently one username. A side effect broke review posting, which the follow-up change (#150) fixed.

prs.title: Add WandererAstro Rotator Mini driver, ConformU 4.4.0 validated
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for the WandererAstro WandererRotator Mini (V1 and V2), a motorized camera rotator, including web-interface setup, automatic detection over USB, and moving, stopping, and syncing its angle. Testing on real hardware showed the V2 firmware reports positions differently from older units and that partial messages were being lost, and both issues are now handled. The device passed the standard compatibility test with no problems. It also makes the rotator and the existing WandererAstro dust cover avoid each other's USB ports when searching for devices.

prs.title: fix(client): equipment notifiers crash on resume (ref.read inside onResume)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a crash in the app when it reconnected after the server restarted, which left cameras, filter wheels, focusers, mounts, and other equipment unable to reconnect. The app now waits a moment before refreshing equipment status after resuming, which avoids the crash. It is a small, targeted change, and the author confirmed devices reconnect normally.

prs.title: ci: Bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.180 to 1.0.181 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of the tool that runs automated code reviews, to a newer minor version. There is no effect on the app itself.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal dependency housekeeping. The description says it upgrades a testing library (FluentAssertions) from version 7 to 8.10, but the code does not do that. It keeps that library on version 7 because version 8 and later require a paid commercial license, and it also locks two other libraries to their current versions because their newer releases would break the build or remove serial GPS support. The only actual upgrade is a small patch update to the API documentation page component, and the automated update bot is now told to stop proposing those major upgrades.

prs.title: Add Gemini Astro Flat Panel Cover Lite driver
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Adds support for the Gemini Astro Flat Panel Cover Lite, a light panel used to take calibration images. It has no motorized cover, so only light on/off and brightness are supported. There was no vendor documentation, so the team worked out how to talk to the device by watching the vendor's own Windows app. The panel is detected automatically and is checked carefully so it is not confused with the Gemini focuser when both are plugged in. It passed the standard compatibility checker on Linux with no issues and ships with tests, a web setup page and docs, but the web setup has not yet been tried in a browser against real hardware.

prs.title: ci: pass an explicit github_token to the review action
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal fix to the automated review bot. Reviews on outside contributors' pull requests were failing because of a login step, so the bot now uses the project's built-in credentials instead. This is meant to be the last of three fixes needed to get label-approved reviews working.

prs.title: ci: opt in to fork checkout in the label-gated review workflow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal follow-up to the review bot setup. It explicitly allows the bot to read code from outside contributors' pull requests once a maintainer has approved it with the review label, which a newer version of the checkout tool otherwise blocks. The code also makes the bot step's failures non-fatal so that a later check decides pass or fail, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: ci: label-gated review bot for fork PRs (safe-to-review)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Changes the automated code-review bot so it can also review pull requests from outside contributors, but only after a maintainer adds a "safe-to-review" label. Removing the label stops the bot, and pull requests from the team's own branches are still reviewed automatically. The bot now reviews the contributor's actual code, and the team docs explain the security trade-off behind the label.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 5 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal update to the automated build and security-scan tools, bringing five of them to newer versions. One of them, the .NET setup tool, moves up a full major version (5 to 6). Some notes in the files still list the old version numbers, but this does not affect how anything works.

prs.title: CI: CodeQL scanning + review-comment assertion (DevSecOps parity with openastro-ara)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal security and automation change with no effect on the software itself. AlpacaBridge now gets an automatic weekly and per-change security scan of its code, with results shown in GitHub's security tab rather than blocking merges. The automated code-review check now fails if the reviewer bot never actually posts its review, instead of showing a misleading green checkmark. The repository-settings changes the description mentions were made outside this PR and are not part of the code.

prs.title: Brand: Ara constellation app icon for macOS, Windows and Linux
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now uses the new Ara constellation icon on macOS, Windows and Linux. The Windows icon was rebuilt in several sizes so it looks sharp on the taskbar and desktop. On Linux the app previously showed no window icon at all and now does, falling back quietly if the image is missing. The image files themselves are binary and not visible in the diff, but the Linux loading code and the packaging entry match the description.

prs.title: Run redesign: palette drag-to-position, lifecycle keys, arrow navigation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor gets three conveniences. You can drag an instruction from the palette and drop it exactly where you want it in the plan, and tapping to add still works. Keyboard shortcuts now run or resume a sequence (Cmd/Ctrl+R) and pause or resume it (Space), and the up and down arrow keys move through the plan. To avoid accidents, Space can never start a run, the keys do nothing while you are typing or while a button has focus, and Abort still needs a mouse click and a confirmation.

prs.title: CI: review agent gets read-only tools; freshness anchored to run start
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal fix to the automated code-review bot, with no change to the app. The bot can now read the project's files, so it no longer wastes its attempts on 'permission denied' errors and gives up before posting. The check that confirms a review was posted now only counts comments made during the current run, so an old review from an earlier round can no longer make the check pass by mistake.

prs.title: Planning + Run redesign: Tonight's Sky panel, night-anchored ranking, run dashboard
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A large combined update that redesigns night planning and running an imaging session. The 'Tonight's Sky' panel was overhauled: all targets are now shown as equal cards, and target scores are always calculated for the coming night, so they no longer drift during the day. The run side adds a live dashboard with time estimates, undo/redo in the editor, an end-of-run summary, filter plans such as SHO or LRGB when creating a run, and a new 'wait for user' step that pauses a run for manual work like a filter swap. It also adds an optional measured sky-brightness setting that sharpens exposure suggestions. The code shows two changes the description barely mentions: generated runs can now include guiding and dithering steps, and the filter setting was changed from a wavelength value to a passband-width value.

prs.title: CI: review check must fail when no review comment was posted
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal fix to the automated code-review check, with no change to the app. On an earlier PR the check showed green even though the review bot never posted a review. Now the bot has a reliable way to post, and the check fails if no fresh review comment from the bot appears. The '30 minutes' time window used here was later tightened in #863.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is a routine automated update to the project's build and review tooling, with no change to the product itself. It moves the code-checkout step to a newer patch release and updates the automated code-review helper to a newer build. One pinned step still carries an outdated "v4.x" label even though it now points to the new version.

prs.title: Fix QHY PulseGuide blocking, Connect() race, and disconnect hang
prs.author: htly9981
prs.summary: Fixes three bugs found while testing a QHY camera with the standard ASCOM compliance checker. Guiding nudges no longer freeze the camera's web connection for the length of the pulse. Disconnecting no longer hangs when the camera's own software stalls. A reconnect made right after a disconnect is no longer silently ignored, and that fix sits in the shared connection code, so it helps every supported device, not just QHY.
