The camera now passes the compliance checker with no errors, and new hardware-free tests guard the shared connection behavior.

prs.title: Tonight's Sky: session planner, curated imaging regions, WX disconnect probe + UI polish
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky becomes a planning tool. You give it your imaging window and up to four targets, and it splits the time sensibly between them, allowing for setup time such as slewing, focusing and guiding pauses. The target list also now ranks famous nebula regions by how imagers actually frame them, with familiar names like the Heart, California and Thor's Helmet. A server fix means a weather station that goes offline is now flagged as an error within seconds, instead of appearing connected with empty readings. The older "what-if optics" dialog was removed, and the panel's layout and spacing were tidied up.

prs.title: Tonight's Sky #858 review follow-ups: pole-safe azimuth + starter type codes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Two small follow-up fixes to Tonight's Sky ranking from the previous review. The horizon check no longer breaks for objects sitting exactly at the celestial pole. The Pleiades and the Hercules Cluster in the built-in fallback target list are now labeled with the proper cluster types, so the newer cluster-ranking adjustments apply to them too.

prs.title: Tonight's Sky: honest framing tiers + capability-aware ranking (§36.8)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky now ranks targets more honestly for your equipment. "Fills frame" is reserved for objects that truly fill the view, and a new "Good fit" label covers mid-sized ones. The list respects your custom horizon, such as trees or buildings in certain directions. Open and globular clusters are nudged down, and gas nebulae are boosted or lowered depending on whether you own narrowband filters. The list also grows from 10 to 30 entries, and every adjustment is explained in the "Why?" breakdown.

prs.title: Shared FlatDevice/CoverCalibrator alias helper + Sky data re-homed under System
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Mostly internal tidy-up with one visible settings change. Three server components each kept their own copy of the rule that treats the flat panel and the cover calibrator as the same device, and they now share a single definition. The sky data download page moves from a separate "Sky Atlas" section to System → Sky data, with its text corrected to describe what is actually offered: the deep-sky and star catalogs. Existing links to the page still work. A behind-the-scenes note in the code still mentions plate-solving catalogs and planet-position data that the new page text says are not offered.

prs.title: Wizard polish round 3+4: live-walkthrough fixes from real-rig testing
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This round of fixes came from testing the setup wizard on real telescope equipment. Finishing the wizard now connects every device you assigned, and it forgets devices you set to "None" so the app stops showing false warnings for gear you don't own. You can also browse and create folders on the telescope computer when choosing where images are saved, and every device type now auto-connects at startup by default. Other changes: two power/dew hubs on one bridge no longer knock each other offline, GPS locations are rounded to about 1 km, Tonight's Sky loads on a fresh launch, and Save buttons in Options now stay pinned at the top of each panel.

prs.title: Telescope optics in mm across mount UIs; /submit-pr review loop; 3.0.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Telescope aperture and focal length are now entered and shown in millimetres in the web setup pages for all five mount brands, instead of metres. Behind the scenes the values are still stored in metres, so existing setups and connected apps are unaffected. The page also rejects suspiciously small numbers, to catch someone typing 0.48 when they meant 480 mm. This PR also publishes release 3.0.2 and updates the maintainers' internal pull-request checklist to wait for and act on the automated code review.

prs.title: feat: any profile is deletable — deleting the last one resets to a factory Default
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: You can now delete any profile, including the one in use or the only one left. Deleting the active profile switches to the most recently used remaining profile, and deleting the last one creates a fresh factory "Default" profile; the confirmation message explains which will happen. The code also contains sizable changes the description doesn't mention. The PHD2 guider can now auto-connect at startup and reconnect on its own, which helps meridian flips that need it. The guider also now uses the profile's saved address instead of falling back to the local machine, and the wizard gets a clearer message when it tries to search for a guider. There are also further wizard and GPS changes, plus a new add-on library for working out the time zone from a location.

prs.title: Release 2.1.0 + collapsible CHANGELOG convention
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This publishes version 2.1.0 of the guider. Its headline additions are dark-frame library builds that no longer make the app wait, and a clear signal when a camera reconnect finally gives up, along with many fixes. The changelog now folds older versions into collapsible sections so it reads as a version list. The script that builds the Linux package history was updated to understand the new layout.

prs.title: Fix 404 web UI on .deb installs: resources dir fell back to app-name path
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the guider's web page showing "Not found" on installs from the Linux package. The underlying data and controls were still working, but the page itself wasn't. The app was looking for its web files in a folder named after the new app name, but the package puts them in the old "phd2" folder. It now falls back to that folder when the first one is missing.

prs.title: feat: NINA import goes client-side — the last planning flow that needed a server (PR F)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Importing a sequence from N.I.N.A. now happens entirely in the app, without sending the file to the telescope computer, so it works even when offline. If you are connected, the imported sequence is saved as usual. If you are offline, it is kept as a draft and uploaded when you reconnect, with the same warnings about unsupported steps either way. The old server-side import feature was removed, along with the extra backup copy of the original file it used to keep on the server.

prs.title: feat: idempotent sequence creates end-to-end + trust-boundary hardeners (PR E)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Creating or importing a sequence can no longer produce accidental duplicates when a connection drops mid-request and the app retries. The app now tags every create attempt with a unique label, and the server recognizes a repeat. This also covers drafts made while offline, which are pushed to the server later. For regular creates, the server saves this record on disk so it survives restarts and has no expiry, going beyond the in-memory, 24-hour approach the description focuses on; imports use the 24-hour in-memory version. Also, the offline gear picker now shows how old the cached equipment data is, and notes were added reminding developers to keep the app's and server's copies of the astronomy math in sync.

prs.title: feat: retire dead planning leftovers — HorizonService + the broken in-page Tonight panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes leftover planning code that nothing was using anymore. This includes a server feature that drew the horizon line for sky charts, which no part of the app called, and an old Tonight's Sky panel inside the planetarium view that had been broken since an earlier change and duplicated the newer panel. The catalog data service was reviewed and deliberately kept because the catalog-rings feature relies on it. No visible behavior changes for users beyond the broken panel disappearing.

prs.title: build: Bump the nuget group with 30 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of about 30 server-side libraries. It includes a major version jump for the ASCOM telescope-hardware libraries (2.1 to 3.1) and the testing helper library (7 to 8), plus a newer patched copy of the bundled SQLite database engine that keeps an earlier security fix in place. No intentional feature changes, but the hardware library jump is the one most worth watching for surprises.

prs.title: build: Bump package_info_plus from 10.2.0 to 10.2.1 in /client/openastroara_client in the pub group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated bump of a small app library that reports the app's version, from 10.2.0 to 10.2.1. No user-facing change.

prs.title: feat: remove server planning compute — the client is the planning brain (PR C)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Finishes moving the observing-planning calculations out of the server and into the app. Tonight's Sky rankings and exposure-length advice are now always worked out on the user's device, whether or not the telescope computer is connected. About 4,300 lines of now-unused server code and tests were deleted. The astronomy math the telescope still needs during unattended runs, such as altitude safety checks and polar alignment, was set aside and kept on the server. Using a custom horizon profile in the rankings is noted as a follow-up.

prs.title: feat: offline planning knows your gear — Tonight's Sky, Optimal Sub, and the OpenNGC catalog go client-side
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Offline planning now uses your actual equipment. Tonight's Sky rankings, exposure-length advice, and filter suggestions are calculated in the app from your cached gear, and the full deep-sky object catalog is downloaded from the telescope computer each time you connect. The 'Plan offline' button is now disabled until a profile has been saved from a connected session, instead of letting you continue with generic defaults. Profiles can also now be deleted straight from the launch screen, with a confirmation step.

prs.title: feat: launchpad-compact / workstation-maximized window modes + shell Launchpad button
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now opens as a small, centered window for the connect-and-pick-a-profile step and switches to full screen once you enter the main workspace. A new 'Launchpad' button in the bottom status bar asks you to confirm, then takes you back to that starting screen so you can switch server, profile, or offline mode without restarting the app. This fixes the app opening too small for the main workspace, and it lets people change setups mid-session. The Linux and Windows window changes were only checked to build, not tried by hand; only macOS was tested live.

prs.title: feat: §2 offline planning — server-less shell entry, local draft sequences, cached profile gear
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: You can now plan an imaging night without the telescope's server connected. A new 'Plan offline' option appears on the first-run screen, when the server can't be reached, and even if saved server settings fail to load. Plans made offline are saved as local drafts that you can reopen, edit, delete, or push to the server later. If the server is unreachable when you create a plan, it is saved as a draft automatically. While connected, the app now keeps a copy of your profiles and gear settings, so when offline you can pick a profile and plan with your real equipment instead of defaults.

prs.title: feat: §30.2/§30.3 launch profile box — profile picker on every launch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: After connecting to a server, the app now shows a profile chooser on every launch instead of dropping you straight into the main screen. It pre-selects your last-used profile and has an 'Image' button to continue, plus always-visible options to add a new profile or import one. If there are no profiles yet, only add and import are shown. The existing profile-import steps were moved so both this screen and the settings page share them, with no change in how import works.

prs.title: Release 3.0.1
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This marks the official 3.0.1 release of AlpacaBridge, dated July 14, 2026. It only updates the version number, the README badge, and the changelog heading, with no code changes. The release bundles earlier work: a broad code audit cleanup, a web request size-limit fix with its test, better error codes for parked mounts, and support and fixes for the iOptron HAE29C mount.

prs.title: Validate iOptron HAE29C: ConformU 4.4 clean, serial + connect fixes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The iOptron HAE29C telescope mount is now officially supported and passed the standard ASCOM compatibility checker with no errors. Testing it uncovered bugs that made the mount seem stuck. Leftover replies from the mount were confusing later commands, and a reconnect right after a disconnect could be silently dropped. The second fix applies to every driver, not just iOptron. There are also workarounds for two HAE29C firmware bugs, limited to that model: parking never reports as finished, and slews stop slightly off target. Other iOptron mounts were not retested on hardware, and the reconnect fix has no dedicated automated test yet.

prs.title: Add socket-level regression test for the HTTP header-size cap (#129)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds an automated test that was written earlier but never merged. It confirms the server correctly rejects web requests whose headers are too large, including when the request arrives in pieces. It is internal only and changes nothing for users.

prs.title: Fix parked-state error code for ITelescopeV4 (SynScan/ZWO/Celestron)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Telescope mounts from SynScan, ZWO, and Celestron now report the correct, standard error when someone tries to move or control them while they are parked, instead of a generic "not allowed" error. This clears a batch of failures reported by the official ASCOM compatibility checker for a user's mount. SynScan mounts also previously let tracking be switched on while parked without any complaint; that is now blocked like on the other brands. The code matches the description.

prs.title: ci: bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.166 to 1.0.173 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of the tool that runs AI code reviews on pull requests, moving it to a newer version. No effect on the product itself.

prs.title: Fix #127: enforce HTTP header-size cap on the terminating recv
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tightens a safety limit in the built-in web server so it now strictly rejects requests whose header section is larger than 64 KB. Before, a request could slip up to about 8 KB past that limit in one specific case. This is a small hardening fix and does not change normal behavior.

prs.title: Fix all Critical/High/Medium findings from full-codebase audit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A large cleanup that fixes every critical, high, and medium problem found in a full review of the codebase, touching the web server, nearly every camera and mount driver, and the installer package. Key user-facing gains include closing a hole that let outsiders read arbitrary files through the web interface, protection against slow or oversized requests, a locked-down system service, and fixes for several crash risks when devices disconnect mid-operation. It also adds stress tests for the telescope drivers, which caught and fixed four more hidden bugs. Some device behavior changes slightly, such as camera image-region rounding, exposure rules, and mount slew waits, so a full compatibility re-check on real hardware is recommended before release.

prs.title: Make the review bot post via --body-file to avoid substitution denials
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the automated AI code reviewer so its longer reviews actually get posted to pull requests. Before, long reviews were silently blocked by a permission rule and only short ones got through. The bot now writes its review to a temporary file first and posts from there. This affects only the review tooling, not the product.

prs.title: Give the review bot read-only code access for large-PR reviews
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Lets the automated AI code reviewer look at the project's source code and history, read-only, so it can properly review large pull requests. Before, it wasted its effort on blocked attempts to read files and never posted a review. This affects only the review tooling, not the product.

prs.title: Async dark builds, terminal reconnect event, API-consistency docs (#65/#66/#67)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Apps talking to the guider can now start a dark-frame calibration build and get an answer right away, instead of waiting two to three minutes and risking a timeout. They learn when the build finishes or fails through the usual progress messages, and the old waiting behavior is still the default. The guider now also sends a clear 'gave up reconnecting' message when a camera stays unplugged, so apps no longer wait forever, and several confusing naming differences in the API are now documented. The build still ties up the guider's main work loop while it runs; a deeper fix is tracked separately. The visible changes are only documentation and the changelog, since the code changes were cut from what was provided.

prs.title: fix: senior-audit remediation (non-auth findings)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A large cleanup based on a full engineering review, fixing dozens of smaller problems across the app. Among them: guiding pause and resume now work correctly, a failed meridian flip halts the sequence, abort operations can no longer hang, image files are checked more strictly on load, several sky-position calculations are more accurate, and a failed Sun or Moon position calculation is flagged instead of quietly returning bad numbers. Network login and access restrictions were deliberately left out, because the astronomy device standard the app relies on has no login support. Three fixes were withdrawn after they broke normal use on home networks. Most of the code changes were cut from what was provided, so only the license notices, removed unused files, and the sky-position fixes could be checked directly.

prs.title: event server: arm :4400 OUTPUT notify only while a write backlog exists
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an efficiency tweak to how the guider sends live updates to connected apps. It now watches for 'ready to send more' signals only when a slow app has fallen behind, rather than reacting to them all the time. Nothing changes for users, but the guider does less needless background work. The code matches the description.

prs.title: docs: add codebase audit under design/
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the full written engineering review of the guider codebase to the project's design documents. It lists the problems found, ranked by severity, and notes which ones were fixed in the companion change and which were deliberately postponed. It is a documentation-only change.

prs.title: Harden Alpaca layer, JSON parser, and daemon robustness from audit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes a batch of problems found in the guider's engineering review. Camera images from some network cameras came out scrambled or partly blank and are now correct, checked against real hardware. The guider can no longer accidentally send a guiding nudge twice after a dropped connection, and specially crafted messages can no longer crash or freeze it. It also shuts down cleanly when stopped by the system, and it handles running out of memory without crashing. Automated builds and tests now run on every change instead of only on one developer's device. The change also includes two fixes the description leaves out: some serial-port devices now work correctly, and secure network connections now always check certificates.

prs.title: feat: §18.I REST centering trigger — POST /platesolve/center as a background job
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Other programs can now ask the app to point the telescope at any sky position and fine-tune the aim until it is truly on target. This is the same aim-and-correct routine the app already uses after a meridian flip or a weather pause. Because centering takes minutes, the request returns right away as a background task that reports progress after each attempt and can be cancelled. A run that fails ends with a clear reason rather than appearing stuck. Only one centering runs at a time, so a second request with different coordinates quietly joins the first one and its new target is ignored; this known gap is noted for later.

prs.title: feat: §35 auto-resume pointing — re-center the target before releasing the run
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a weather or safety pause clears and the sequence resumes automatically, the telescope now re-aims at the target it was photographing before the imaging continues, instead of picking up wherever parking left it. This keeps the first images after a resume from being wasted on empty sky. The re-aim is best-effort: if it cannot be done, fails, or takes longer than 10 minutes, the sequence resumes anyway and the notification says plainly whether pointing was confirmed. If conditions turn unsafe again during the re-aim, the mount parks and the sequence stays paused.

prs.title: feat: §57 closers — watchdog abort reason + §57.5 latency logging
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the automatic safety check halts a stuck telescope move during a meridian flip, the system now reports it as a stopped move instead of wrongly saying the move finished. Every mount stop, whether from the panic button or this automatic check, now also records in the logs how long the stop took to reach the telescope, so the team can measure and tune how fast emergency stops respond.

prs.title: test: §38 schema check pinned + §42.2 dew-heater row marked N/A
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal only: adds two automated checks confirming that sequences saved from the app's editor are accepted by the server, so a future mismatch would be caught before it breaks saving. It also adds a note explaining that camera dew-heater control does not apply to the type of equipment connection this project uses. No change in behavior.

prs.title: feat: §68 verify pass — AlpacaBridge guidance on the post-setup empty scan
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app searches for equipment and finds nothing, it now explains the most likely cause: the equipment connection software (AlpacaBridge) is missing or not running. It shows the commands to install it and check its status, plus a note about equipment on another computer, instead of just saying "No devices found." This PR also includes a review confirming the rest of the equipment-connection setup already works as intended, and a new automated test for the message.

prs.title: feat: §57 slice 2 — WILMA Stop Mount overlay + post-stop modal
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a large red STOP MOUNT button to the app that appears on every screen whenever the telescope is moving on its own, and hides again when the move ends. On desktop, the Space key also triggers it. One tap stops the telescope without asking for confirmation, and a follow-up window shows where it stopped and offers to resume, skip the current target, or end the session. The option to check the telescope's position after a stop is left for later work.

prs.title: feat: §57 slice 1 — slew lifecycle events + panic-stop sequence pause
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now announces when the telescope starts moving, finishes moving, or is stopped mid-move, no matter what started the move. Pressing the mount stop now also pauses any running imaging sequence, even if the stop command itself runs into an error, so the camera does not keep taking pictures of the wrong part of the sky. This is the behind-the-scenes groundwork that the app's Stop Mount button builds on.

prs.title: feat: §31 slice 4 — time-sync status UI + manual entry modal (waterfall steps 4+5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The settings screen for your observing site now has a Time sync section. It shows whether the observatory computer's clock is correct, where the correct time came from and how much to trust it, how far off the clock is, what location the system knows, and whether a USB GPS is plugged in. It adds buttons to retry, to send this device's time with one click, and to type in the date, time and location by hand, which is the last-resort option for fully offline setups. Hand-entered times are always treated as low trust, and the section explains your options when the clock isn't synced.

prs.title: feat: §31 slice 3 — USB-GPS self-sync worker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If a cheap USB GPS receiver is plugged into the observatory's Raspberry Pi, the system now finds it and sets the clock and site location from it automatically, with no app connected. It checks every couple of minutes until it gets a good reading, then refreshes about every 50 minutes so long unattended runs don't drift. Faulty receivers, busy connections and nonsense dates are skipped without crashing anything. The code also fixes something the description only hints at: a GPS reading without altitude no longer wipes out the saved site elevation, and two sources updating the location at the same moment can no longer overwrite each other.

prs.title: feat: §31 client slice — WILMA pushes its clock on every connect
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each time the app connects or reconnects to the observatory, it now checks whether the observatory's clock has been set recently and reliably. If not, it quietly sends the correct time from your phone or laptop. There is nothing to configure, and a failed attempt is simply retried on the next connection. This keeps a Raspberry Pi with no internet or built-in clock on time in most sessions, and it never replaces a more trusted time source such as a GPS.

prs.title: feat: §31 time-sync server slice 1 — state machine, endpoints, NMEA parser
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the server-side foundation for keeping the observatory's clock and location correct. A planned check found the feature had never actually been built. The server can now report whether its time is fresh and trustworthy, and it accepts a correct time and location from outside. It sets its own clock when it has permission to, and otherwise keeps track of how far off it is. A received location updates the site settings right away, so twilight times and sky planning use it immediately. It also includes the code that reads GPS data, ready for the follow-up automatic GPS feature.

prs.title: docs: close the FITS keyword-convention audit — keep the de-facto set
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only change that closes out a review of the labels written into saved image files. The team decided to keep the current labels. They aren't part of the official file standard, but every common astronomy tool expects them, and renaming them would break existing images and compatibility with other software. No code changed.

prs.title: test: cover the palette action dispatch (#829 r1 note)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal test-only change. It adds an automated check that choosing an action from the keyboard command palette closes the palette and opens the right window, which was a spot flagged in an earlier review as easy to break by accident. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: feat: §61.10 slice 2 — ⌘K palette actions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The quick-search box (opened with Cmd+K) can now launch five common screens and tools directly: the Image Library, Calibration, Stats, Back up & restore, and the profile setup wizard. You can find them by typing everyday words like "dark library", "best frames", "snapshot" or "onboarding", and they open exactly as the matching buttons in the top bar do. These results show a lightning-bolt icon so they stand apart from settings, help and navigation results.

prs.title: feat: §61.10 slice 1 — ⌘K palette tab navigation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Cmd+K quick-search box, which previously only found settings and help, can now jump to the app's four main tabs: Planning, Run, Live and Options. It understands natural phrases such as "go to run", "tonight", "live view" or "preferences". Each result now shows an icon for its kind (arrow for navigation, question mark for help, slider for a setting), and the search box hint text now mentions navigation. This is the first step toward turning the settings search into a general command palette.

prs.title: fix: drop unkeyed Best Frames rows; surface non-array logs/tail bodies
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes two places where problems were hidden from users. The Best Frames list in Stats now leaves out entries the server sent without a proper identifier, because those entries were unusable, and it notes how many were dropped. The daemon log viewer in the Support tab now shows an error when the server sends back something that isn't a list of log lines, instead of quietly showing an empty log. A single malformed log line is now skipped rather than breaking the whole view.

prs.title: fix: stop offering plate-solve engines the daemon can't use (#363 offer side)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The plate-solving engine picker in Settings now offers only ASTAP, the only engine the server actually ships. Previously it also listed astrometry.net and PlateSolve 2, but choosing either one quietly used ASTAP anyway. A profile that still carries one of the old choices, for example one imported from NINA, shows it labeled "not supported — ASTAP is used" until the user switches it. The help text and setting description were rewritten to say this plainly.

prs.title: perf: §39 ListSessions — keyset pagination + batched page assembly
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The calibration sessions list now loads quickly even with a very large image catalog. Each page of results now needs a fixed, small number of database lookups, where before the number grew with every session on the page. Paging through the list is also more reliable: a new session arriving while you scroll can no longer make an entry appear twice or go missing. Links to pages from before the upgrade keep working.

prs.title: feat: §43-2 async backup create — worker + create-status + backup.create.* WS + 507 pre-flight
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Creating a backup no longer holds up the app while the archive is built. The server accepts the request right away and does the work in the background, and the app's spinner now follows the real progress. If something fails, the user sees the server's actual error message instead of a generic timeout. The server now also refuses a backup up front when the disk clearly lacks space, and retrying a timed-out request joins the backup already running instead of starting a second one. Much of the core server and app code was left out of the provided diff, so these details come mostly from the description.

prs.title: feat: §30.7.4 e-4b-2 — record guider calibration_state in the profile
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each profile now remembers whether its guide-camera dark files are usable and when they were last built, so this still holds after the server restarts. The record is only written when a build succeeds. It follows the profile when you switch profiles, and it is removed when a profile is shared, since the files stay on the original owner's machine. The code also checks whether you switched profiles during a long build, which the description doesn't mention, and the new information can be read but not edited.

prs.title: feat: §63.4 delete hook — an ARA profile delete removes its guider twin
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Deleting a profile now also removes its matching profile and dark files on the guiding software. Before, these leftovers piled up there forever. The cleanup is best-effort: if the guider isn't connected, it is skipped with a log note, and the profile delete itself always succeeds. The description says the guider's current profile can never be the one deleted, but code comments say an extra check is needed for that case. One known gap remains: renaming a profile and then deleting it without reconnecting the guider can leave the old leftover behind.

prs.title: feat: §37.5 wizard covers the unattended-failure shutdown
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup wizard's safety screen now asks about the automatic safe shutdown that runs when a failure pauses the night and nobody responds. That shutdown parks the mount, warms the camera cooler and disconnects. You can turn it on or off and set how many minutes to wait (1–720). Leaving the choice blank keeps the profile's default. The shutdown itself already existed and was set in Settings; this only adds it to the wizard.

prs.title: feat: §37.5 soft-warning altitude — Tonight's Sky advisory
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky now flags targets that never rise above a new "soft warning altitude" during the night (default 30°, set to 0 to turn it off). Low targets are viewed through more atmosphere and show less detail. Flagged targets are still listed and their ranking is unchanged; they just get a note in the "Why?" breakdown. The setting is available in Settings and in the setup wizard.

prs.title: feat: §54 log + bug-report downloads stream to disk
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Downloading the server log or a bug report now saves straight to disk bit by bit, instead of loading the whole file into the app's memory first. You now pick a folder before the download starts. If a file with the same name already exists, a numbered name is used instead of overwriting it. Empty downloads are still caught and reported as errors instead of being saved.

prs.title: perf: §29.9 log tail reads backwards and early-exits
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Showing the latest lines of the server log is now faster on large logs. It reads from the end of the file and stops once it has enough lines, instead of reading the whole file. What you see is unchanged: same order, same filters. This is a behind-the-scenes speed-up.

prs.title: feat: §37.5 max-sequence-runtime cap — enforcement-first
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds an optional time limit for how long a single imaging sequence may run. It can be set in Settings under Safety → Site or on the setup wizard's site screen. If a run goes past the limit, it is stopped exactly as if someone pressed Stop, and a warning notification explains why. The default of 0 means no limit, and the limit is re-checked every minute, so changing it during a run takes effect without restarting. This protects unattended setups from a stuck or overly long plan keeping the telescope running into the morning.

prs.title: feat: §37 wizard clear-field affordance — shed a cloned rig's paths
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the setup wizard creates a new profile, it copies the current one, and leaving a field blank means "keep the old value." Because of that, there was no way to get rid of an old rig's plate-solver program path, star database path, image save folder, or filename pattern. Those four fields now have a reset button that restores the default when you save. Typing a new value afterwards overrides the reset. Other wizard fields still keep the old value when left blank.

prs.title: feat: §63.8 — warn-once when a build's progress polls persistently fail
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: While building a dark library or defect map, the app checks the guider for progress once a second and quietly ignores occasional failures. If those checks kept failing, the only clue was a progress bar that never moved. Now the log records a single warning per build, either after five failures in a row or at the end if no check ever succeeded. The build itself works exactly as before.

prs.title: feat: §50 responsive dashboard tiles
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Stats dashboard's Overview tiles, Achievements tiles, and milestone badges now resize to fill each row instead of sitting at a fixed width. On a narrow window they drop to a single full-width column, and a size cap stops a lone tile from stretching too wide on large screens. On a window narrower than one minimum-size tile, a code comment says the tile runs past the edge and gets cut off, while the description says the page scrolls. The PR also removes an outdated roadmap entry for a custom-horizon feature that had already shipped.

prs.title: fix: §30 canonical active-server provider — re-confirming a rig makes it active
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug for people with more than one saved server, such as an observatory rig and a travel rig. Reconnecting to a server the app already knew did nothing, so the app kept talking to whichever server was saved most recently. Reconnecting now makes that server the active one and updates its stored details. Every part of the app now uses one shared definition of the active server, which will make a future server switcher easier to build. The change reaches more places than the description lists, including equipment status, faults, stats, and the image library, but the effect is the same everywhere.

prs.title: feat: §36.8 slice 4b — Tonight's Sky what-if optics/mosaic overrides
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Tonight's Sky panel now has a "what-if" button for trying a different setup. You can enter a different focal length, reducer, camera sensor size, or mosaic layout, and the list of recommended targets is re-ranked for that setup without changing your saved profile. Blank fields keep your profile's values, the button is highlighted while a what-if is active, and Reset goes back to your real equipment. The what-if lasts only until the app restarts. The PR also updates planning documents to record that the Smart Focus work is essentially complete.

prs.title: feat: §42.5 — persist guider faults to the fault log
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the guiding system loses its connection or reports that its guide camera dropped out, the problem is now saved in the permanent fault history, like every other piece of equipment. Before this, those outages triggered the usual reaction and alert but were never recorded, so the fault feed and the per-night fault timeline missed one of the most common causes of ruined images. Each record notes what the system did in response, such as pausing, skipping, aborting, or just notifying, and is marked resolved when the guider reconnects. For now, a guide-camera dropout is also closed on the next guider reconnect rather than when the camera itself comes back, and the PR describes this as a known stopgap.

prs.title: perf: §64/§59 — StarDetector measures only the brightest-N when capped
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Star detection is now much faster when only a limited number of stars is needed, as with the Live View overlay and autofocus. It used to measure every star in the frame and then throw most away, which meant thousands of wasted measurements on a dense star field. It now measures the brightest stars first and stops once it has enough. The code shows it picks exactly the same stars as before, and detection without a limit is unchanged.

prs.title: perf: §64 — run Live View render/detection off the capture gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Live View previews no longer hold up real photo captures. Previously the camera stayed reserved while each preview frame was being processed, including the slow star-finding step, so a manual or sequence capture had to wait. The camera is now freed as soon as the preview image is downloaded, and processing happens afterward. It also avoids some pointless re-sending of camera settings when only the preview processing fails.

prs.title: feat: §64 — Live View star annotation on OSC cameras (detect on super-pixel luminance)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Live View can now draw circles around detected stars on colour cameras. Before, the option was silently ignored on colour cameras, so users couldn't tell whether annotation was off or no stars were found. Stars are now found on a brightness version of the colour image produced in the same processing step, so the circles line up with the stars in the colour preview. Mono cameras and colour previews without circles are unchanged.

prs.title: feat: §36 — carry the framing position angle into created runs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When you set a rotation angle on the Sky Atlas framing tool and create an imaging run, that angle is now carried into the run. Previously it was silently dropped and the run just pointed the telescope at the target. The run's first step now centres on the target and rotates the camera to the framed angle, including when adding a target to an existing sequence. If the dial is left at 0°, the run keeps the plain move-to-target step, so users who didn't use rotation aren't suddenly required to have plate-solving set up.

prs.title: feat: §38 — CenterAndRotate rotation fidelity (solve-driven rotator moves)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "Center and Rotate" sequence step now actually rotates the camera on setups that have a rotator. Previously it deliberately failed on those setups because rotation wasn't built yet. It now works out the current sky angle from a photo, turns the rotator by the shortest equivalent amount to the planned angle, then centres the target as before. If either the rotation or the centring can't get close enough, the step fails. Setups without a rotator behave as before. The core rotation logic was cut from the diff provided, so only the step's routing and its tests could be checked here.

prs.title: feat: §42.6 — populate affected_frames at fault resolution (closes the §42 epic)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When an equipment problem is resolved, its record in the fault history now lists exactly which photos were taken while the problem was happening. That includes the one in progress when it started and any still running when it ended, limited to that night's imaging session. This closes the loop for the morning-after question "why are these few shots ruined?" and completes the larger equipment-fault project. Problems that happened outside an imaging session, or that never got resolved, deliberately get no photo list.

prs.title: feat: §42.3 — post-give-up linger re-adopt + disconnect-mid-wait regression harness
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If a device drops out and the quick automatic reconnect attempts give up, the system now keeps quietly retrying every two minutes for about an hour. As soon as the device comes back, whether on its own or because someone replugged it, it is picked up again automatically. Any imaging runs that were paused because of it are resumed and a notification is sent. If you deliberately disconnect a device, it is left alone. The PR also adds automated tests confirming that a device disconnecting mid-move is reported as a failure rather than a success.

prs.title: feat: §42.2 items 2+5 — persistent-op-fault escalation (mount abort+park, camera pause)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The system now acts when the same device keeps failing, instead of treating every failure as a one-off. Three real failures within ten minutes on the telescope mount stops the running sessions and parks the mount for safety. On the camera, the same pattern pauses the night's imaging. Smaller accessories like the focuser or filter wheel still only send alerts. The camera now also reports its own capture failures, which it previously didn't, so this check can see them.

prs.title: feat: §42.2 item 4 — rotator angle-drift watch with re-issue-once recovery
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The system now notices when the camera rotator ends up more than half a degree away from the angle it was told to go to, for example because of a slipping belt or a move that was silently ignored. It first quietly retries the same move once. Only if the rotator is still off after that does it raise an alert. Readings taken while the rotator is still moving are ignored, so slow devices aren't falsely flagged.

prs.title: feat: §42.2 — switch re-command-once before faulting + plate-solver exit-code diagnosis
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a power switch (such as a dew heater) doesn't end up in the state it was told to, the system now retries the command once before raising an alarm, so a one-time glitch that the retry fixes no longer bothers anyone. Separately, when the plate-solving program crashes or can't find its star database, the log now says so clearly. Previously this looked the same as simply not finding a solution.

prs.title: fix: §42.2 — peripheral op failures now fail the instruction (retries + instruction_failed engage)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a serious gap where failed equipment actions were treated as successes by the imaging sequence. This covered mount slews, focuser moves, filter changes, rotator moves, switch changes, and dome operations. A jammed filter wheel, for example, could quietly shoot a whole night through the wrong filter. These failures now properly fail the step, so the sequence's retries and error handling kick in. Restoring the filter after a plate-solve stays best-effort so it can't hide the actual result.

prs.title: fix: §42.5 — a device's reconnect resolves its standing disconnect fault rows
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The fault history now marks a disconnect as resolved as soon as the device reconnects, however it was fixed. Before this, if automatic recovery gave up and someone fixed the device by hand (for example by reseating a cable), the fault stayed listed as unresolved forever. The history, the live fault feed, and the status chips now reflect what is actually still broken. A reconnect only clears disconnect faults, not tracking-loss or warning-type faults, and the record of what the system tried to do is kept.

prs.title: feat: §42 WILMA fault surfaces slice 2 — fault feed panel + per-session timeline
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds two new places in the app where you can see equipment faults. The Imaging tab gets a collapsible Faults panel showing how many problems are currently active and a newest-first history that updates live and can page back further. In the Image Library, any imaging session that had faults gets an amber 'N faults' badge that opens that night's fault timeline. This helps explain the next morning why some images came out badly. The session timeline only loads the most recent 50 faults for a session.

prs.title: feat: §42 WILMA fault surfaces slice 1 — live fault chips + faults history client
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The equipment status indicators along the top of the app now show faults, not just whether a device is connected. A device that drops out or a mount that stops tracking turns its indicator red until it recovers or reconnects. Smaller one-off warnings, such as a stuck move or a cooler drifting off temperature, turn it amber and clear after ten minutes. This also adds the behind-the-scenes code for reading fault history, which the fault feed and session timeline build on.

prs.title: fix: paginated lists no longer report has_more=false on every page
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where the notifications list, the diagnostics history, and the image library's frame list always reported that there were no more pages. Anyone scrolling through these lists only ever saw the first page and silently missed the rest. The lists now correctly report when more results exist, and tests were added for all three.

prs.title: feat: §42.5 fault log — persist every equipment fault + GET /api/v1/faults
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Equipment faults are now saved permanently instead of only being announced live and then lost. Every detected problem is recorded: disconnects, lost tracking, stuck moves, power switches that ignored a command, and cooler drift. Each record includes what the system did about it, whether it recovered, and which imaging session was running at the time. A new way to look up this history, filtered by device, fault type, session, or unresolved-only, gives a clear answer to 'what went wrong overnight?'. The list of images affected by each fault is reserved but not yet filled in.

prs.title: docs: remove version-based planning; add design/ROADMAP.md design path
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only change to the project's planning documents. It drops the old approach of grouping upcoming work under release version numbers. In its place, a single new roadmap lists everything still to do, ordered by what depends on what. The other design documents were updated to point to the new roadmap, and no software behavior changed.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update to the automated build and checking tools. It brings the Docker image builder, the automated AI code reviewer, and the security code scanner up to newer versions. There is no change to the app itself.

prs.title: build: Bump webview_all from 1.2.0 to 1.2.1 in /client/openastroara_client in the pub group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of the component that shows the sky atlas web view inside the app, moving from version 1.2.0 to 1.2.1. The bundled third-party license list was updated to match. No other app changes.

prs.title: feat: §42.4 slice 4c — emit sequence.instruction_failed per failed leaf
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a step in an imaging sequence fails, Ara now immediately sends a live notice saying exactly which step failed and where it sits in the sequence. Before, you could only spot a failure by comparing statuses after the fact. Each failure is reported once, including failures after all retries are used up and repeat failures inside loops, and always before the 'sequence finished' notice. With the previous two PRs, this means every kind of failure now surfaces on one channel or the other. One internal progress note still describes an older design that the description says was dropped.

prs.title: feat: §42.4 slice 4b — op-channel fault publishes + switch read-back watch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a device gets stuck or errors during a sequence, Ara now reports it as a visible equipment fault instead of only writing it to a log. This covers a jammed filter wheel, a focuser that never settles, a slow mount, and dome, rotator, or power-switch commands. Ara also now double-checks power switch ports: if a port doesn't read back what it was told to do within a few seconds (for example, commanded on but still reads off), it raises a mismatch alert naming the port. The allowed margin is a new setting that defaults to 5%. The code also makes sure these alerts aren't swallowed when the same type of device is already being reconnected, a change the description only hints at.

prs.title: feat: §42.2 slice 4a — tracking-lost watch + cooling-drift monitor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Ara now catches two quiet problems that can ruin images without any error appearing. The first is a mount that stops tracking on its own: if tracking stays off for about six seconds with no slew, park, or user command to explain it, Ara flags it and tries to turn tracking back on. The second is a camera cooler that can't hold its target temperature: if the sensor stays more than 5 °C off target for over 5 minutes, Ara shows a warning but never stops the session. Both checks fire once per incident and are careful not to raise false alarms during normal moves or downloads.

prs.title: feat: §42.2/§42.3 slices 2+3 — fault policy matrix + reaction service with hot-reconnect
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Ara now reacts automatically when a piece of equipment drops out, following new options in the Safety settings. If the camera or mount is lost during a sequence, Ara pauses at the next safe point and tries to reconnect several times over about two minutes. If reconnecting works, it resumes; if not, it stays paused for a camera, or stops and tries to park the mount. Other accessories reconnect quietly in the background, and the guider is left to its own existing recovery. The author flagged 'pause first, then reconnect' as a choice needing maintainer sign-off. Note that the changelog entry also describes the dead-device detection itself, which came from an earlier PR.

prs.title: feat(server): §42.2/§42.3 slice 1 — equipment fault spine + Alpaca disconnect detection
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now tell when a piece of equipment (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, dome, rotator, flat panel, or switch) stops responding in the middle of a session. Before this, a device that dropped out kept showing as connected with stale readings. Now, after about six seconds of missed check-ins, the device is marked as errored and a fault alert goes out to the app. This is only the detection step: automatic recovery and reconnecting are planned for later changes, and weather and safety sensors are not covered yet.

prs.title: feat(client): §59.4/§59.14 telescope type in WILMA — settings dropdown, registries, wizard
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now pick their telescope type (refractor, SCT, Maksutov, RC, Newtonian, or other/unknown) in the app. The choice is available in the autofocus settings and in the setup wizard, and it is saved with the user's profile. It comes with a help entry explaining why the choice matters. This finishes the five-part work on telescope-aware Smart Focus, though the planned example star images for each telescope type have been left for later.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.3/§59.4 slice 4 — the Smart runner reads direction from the frame
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Smart Focus can now often tell from a single photo which direction the focuser needs to move, not just how far. On rigs where this works, focusing can finish in two exposures instead of three. When it isn't confident, it falls back to the old guess, and a wrong read is caught by the existing correction steps, so it shouldn't add extra exposures. The app also now receives the predicted move and whether it came from the new reading or the old guess, and this is the first change in the series recorded in the changelog as user-facing.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.4 telescope type — setting + typed magnitude key + gated side features
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now stores a telescope type setting, which defaults to 'other' and behaves exactly as before. For telescopes with a central mirror (SCT, Mak, RC, Newtonian), autofocus can estimate distance from focus using the size of the out-of-focus 'donut' ring, but only when the scope's own calibration data supports it; otherwise it uses the old method. The setting also controls which star-shape clues the direction detector is allowed to use. Nothing in the app lets users choose the type yet; that came in a later change.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.3 side-of-focus classifier — learn the arm signatures, classify one frame
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the logic that learns, from an autofocus calibration run, how stars look differently on each side of focus for a particular telescope, and then uses that to judge the side of focus from a single photo. If the telescope's optics give no clear difference, or the result isn't confident enough, it gives no answer rather than guessing. Nothing uses it yet; it was connected to autofocus in a later change.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.3 radial-profile skew — the intra/extra-focal asymmetry measurable
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Star analysis now records one more measurement of each star's shape: whether its light is bunched toward the middle or pushed out to a bright outer edge. On many telescopes this flips depending on which side of focus you are on, which later changes use to work out focus direction. Older saved calibrations still load (they just lack this value) and are refreshed on the next successful autofocus. Users see no change yet.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.2 Smart Focus slice D — calibration endpoints, mode-aware job progress, fallback notifications
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This finishes the Smart Focus feature by making it visible and controllable. Users can now look up the saved focus calibration for their setup, or wipe it so the next autofocus does a full recalibration. The autofocus progress bar now shows real progress for quick Smart runs; a two-shot run reads about two-thirds done instead of barely started. Unexpected problems, like a Smart run going the wrong way or a device fault, now raise a warning notification, while routine fallbacks caused by clouds or faint stars stay quiet. The code for the warnings was trimmed from the diff shown, so only the calibration controls and progress bar could be checked directly.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.2 Smart Focus slice C — the one-frame runner + §59.11 fallback ladder
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the main payoff of Smart Focus. Once a telescope setup has been calibrated, autofocus can now get sharp in two or three test pictures instead of the usual nine-picture sweep, turning a multi-minute job into typically under a minute. If anything looks off (too few stars, a calibration taken at a very different temperature, or focus getting worse), it puts the focuser back where it started and falls back to the old full sweep. At worst, users get the previous behavior plus a few quick extra shots. The app also now sends live updates as each Smart Focus step happens, so the interface can show a live progress panel.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.2 Smart Focus slice B — sweep records calibration on every successful sweep
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every successful regular autofocus now also saves the calibration data Smart Focus needs, using star measurements it already takes, so no extra pictures or steps are required. The saved data records the temperature and filter at the time. If a sweep's measurements aren't good enough, it keeps the previous good calibration instead of overwriting it. Nothing uses this data to focus faster yet; that comes in a follow-up change.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.2 Smart Focus calibration persistence primitive
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for Smart Focus: each equipment profile can now store a focus calibration, with an empty value meaning "not calibrated yet." Switching to a profile that has never been calibrated correctly clears the old one. Shared profiles leave the calibration out, because it only fits the original owner's telescope. Nothing writes or reads this data yet, so there is no visible change for users.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.10 surface the collimation verdict (WS event + notification)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Owners of telescopes with a central mirror obstruction now get told about their mirror alignment (collimation) after each successful autofocus, instead of the result only going into the log. Every confident reading is sent to the interface. Only noticeable problems raise a notification: a warning for slight misalignment, and a critical alert recommending realignment for significant misalignment. The check was also made more accurate by measuring only the most out-of-focus test picture, so the same star is not counted more than once.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.10 wire collimation read into the autofocus sweep (capture + evaluate + log)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: After a successful autofocus, the app now also checks mirror alignment (collimation) on suitable telescopes, reusing the star images it already took so no extra pictures are needed. In this step the result is only written to the internal log and users do not see it yet; a follow-up change adds that. If the check fails for any reason, the autofocus is still reported as successful.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.10 collimation verdict evaluator (pure aggregator)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the logic that turns a Smart Focus calibration's out-of-focus star images into a single telescope collimation (mirror alignment) verdict: Good, Slight, Significant, or "not enough data." It only trusts stars near the middle of the frame, and it averages them so random wobble cancels out while a real misalignment adds up, which keeps false alarms down. It reports how far off the alignment is and in which direction on the image. Users won't see anything yet: it isn't connected to the focusing run or to any notification, and translating the direction into an eyepiece-style clock position is left for later.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.10 per-star donut centroid-offset metric (collimation precursor)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Star detection now measures, for each out-of-focus "donut" star, how far the dark center hole has drifted from the middle of the ring. That drift is the raw signal of a misaligned secondary mirror on telescopes like SCTs, Maks, and Newtonians. This is groundwork for the collimation check and is intentionally kept separate from the focusing data. The code also merges this with the existing hole-darkness measurement so the hole is scanned once instead of twice.

prs.title: feat(server): §64/§59 wire mono Live View star annotation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Live View can now draw green circles around the stars it detects on monochrome camera frames, as a quick focusing and framing aid. It uses the same star detector as autofocus, and the circles are sized by how spread out each star is. It is off by default, is turned on with a new option when starting Live View, and is capped at 250 circles to keep the view readable. Color cameras are not covered yet. The description doesn't mention it, but the change also fixes the circle drawing from #774 so small circles no longer vanish when a large sensor image is shrunk for display.

prs.title: feat(stretch): §64/§59 star-marker annotated JPEG encoder primitive
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the drawing piece for a future Live View feature that circles detected stars: it can take a grayscale preview image and draw green rings at given positions before saving it as a JPEG. It is not connected to Live View yet, so nothing changes for users in this PR. As first built, the rings were drawn at full size and then shrunk along with the image, which made small rings disappear on large sensors; #775 later fixed this.

prs.title: fix(image): sample StarDetector background on a 2D grid, not a linear stride
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes star detection more reliable on frames whose brightness varies across the image, such as vignetted frames with dark corners. The background sky level that decides what counts as a star was previously sampled in a way that, on many image widths, kept hitting the same few columns, which could skew the threshold and cause missed or false detections. It now samples evenly across the whole frame. This improves everything that relies on star detection: autofocus, live-view star stats, and plate solving.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.4 Smart Focus obstruction-shadow depth metric
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Star detection now measures how dark the center hole of an out-of-focus "donut" star is compared with its bright ring. The value runs from 0 for no hole (refractors or in-focus stars) to 1 for a fully dark hole. It is added to the set of measurements that Smart Focus will use to judge focus on telescopes with a central obstruction. It is not yet used by the autofocus routine itself.

prs.title: feat(image): §59.3/§59.10 Smart Focus donut geometry per-star metrics
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Smart Focus star measurements now also capture the 'donut' shape a defocused star makes on telescopes with a central obstruction, such as reflectors and SCTs. For each star this records the overall ring size, the size of the dark hole in the middle, and how thick the ring is. On a refractor or an in-focus star it simply reports no hole, so no special handling is needed per telescope type. The code also ignores very small central holes of only a pixel or two as noise, which the description does not mention; nothing uses these new numbers yet, and collimation checks and telescope-specific tuning are left for later.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63.8 dark-build progress-poll loop (progress WS events)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Building a dark library or bad-pixel map through the guider now sends live progress updates, showing which exposure and frame it is on, instead of appearing frozen for several minutes. Ara checks the guider's progress about once a second while the build runs and stops checking as soon as the build finishes or fails. A single failed progress check is skipped without affecting the build. The code also adds an option for these progress checks to give up quickly if the guider stops responding, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63.8 dark-build progress poll (get_dark_build_progress DTO + client)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Groundwork that lets Ara ask the guider how far along a dark-library or bad-pixel-map build is, including the current exposure and frame out of the total. On its own this doesn't change anything users see. It lays the foundation for the live progress bar added in #770.

prs.title: feat(focus): §59.2 Smart Focus inverse map (feature→offset, magnitude)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the core math for Smart Focus to estimate, from a single blurry frame, how far the focuser is from best focus, rather than running a full focus sweep every time. It learns this from one normal focus sweep. It refuses to guess when the frame has no stars or is more out of focus than anything it has seen before. It only estimates the distance, not the direction to move, and it isn't hooked into autofocus yet, so users see no change for now.

prs.title: feat(polar-align): §45 PolarAlignService skeleton (PA-session lease lifecycle + WS)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Replaces the placeholder polar alignment feature with a real, but still early, version. Starting polar alignment now requires a connected guider and reserves the guide camera so nothing else can use it, and stopping releases the camera and announces the stop. It does not take pictures or give alignment corrections yet. Not mentioned in the description: starting without a connected guider, or being refused by the guider, now returns a clear error message instead of a generic server failure.

prs.title: feat(guider): §45 polar-align guider-client half (capture/centroids/PA-session + SingleFrameComplete)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Groundwork for polar alignment. Ara can now tell the guider to take a single picture for plate solving, fetch the positions of detected stars, and reserve or release the guide camera. It also checks settings such as exposure, gain, and the save location before sending them, so mistakes produce clear errors. Nothing uses this yet, so users see no change.

prs.title: feat(guider): §45 Drift Align polar-align RPC DTOs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the groundwork for talking to the guiding program's "drift align" tool, a classic way of lining a telescope mount up with the celestial pole by watching how a star slowly drifts. This covers how Ara describes each request and reads back the tool's progress, such as which axis is being adjusted, the measured alignment error, and where the telescope is pointing. Nothing uses it yet, so users see no change. It completes the preparation for all three polar-alignment methods before the actual feature is built on top.

prs.title: feat(guider): §45 Polar Drift polar-align RPC DTOs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the groundwork for talking to the guiding program's "polar drift" alignment tool, which estimates how far off the mount's alignment is by tracking a single star as it drifts. It defines how Ara starts, checks, stops, and closes that tool and how it reads back results like the alignment error and which way to correct. There is no user-visible change yet. This is the second of three preparation steps for polar alignment.

prs.title: feat(guider): §45 Static PA polar-align RPC DTOs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the groundwork for talking to the guiding program's "static" polar-alignment tool, which works near the pole and shows how far the mount's rotation centre is from where it should be. It defines how Ara starts the tool, records measurement points, and reads back details like reference stars, measured points, and how much to adjust altitude and azimuth. Nothing is wired up yet, so users see no change. This is the first of three preparation steps before the real polar-alignment feature is built.

prs.title: feat(guider): §42.2 route structured EquipmentDisconnected into the fault reaction
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If the guide camera drops out mid-session, for example from a loose USB cable, Ara now follows your "when guiding is lost" setting (pause, skip the target, or abort) instead of quietly continuing to shoot without guiding. It also alerts you even when no sequence is running. The guider connection stays up because the guiding program is still running and tries to recover the camera itself, and the alert no longer wrongly asks you to reconnect the guider. It only reacts to the first drop in each connected session, and it does not yet handle the case where the guiding program silently gives up reconnecting; both are planned follow-ups.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63.9 get_version handshake + fix openastro-guider fork identification
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where Ara failed to recognise the current guiding program after it was renamed, so it wrongly warned that some guiding features might be unavailable even on fully supported setups. Ara now asks the guiding program directly for its identity when connecting, falls back to older ways of checking when needed, and still accepts the old name. It also records whether the guider can handle several requests at once, for use by later work.

prs.title: feat(focus): §59.3 Smart Focus per-star feature vector (FWHM/roundness/peak)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds new measurements of each detected star, covering how wide it is, how round it is, and how bright its centre is compared with the sky around it. It also combines them into a typical value per image, using the middle value so stray hot pixels or cosmic rays don't skew the result. This is groundwork for a planned "Smart Focus" feature meant to focus from a single image. Nothing uses these measurements yet, so there is no user-visible change.

prs.title: feat(telescope): §28 real Alpaca mount Sync for the centering loop
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automatic centering routine can now tell the mount where it is really pointing (a "sync") after taking a picture and working out its position. Before, this step did nothing, so centering always used a less accurate workaround. If the mount can't sync, is parked, is disconnected, or doesn't answer in time, the routine quietly falls back to that workaround instead of failing the run. One thing the description doesn't mention: the code also tries to switch the mount's tracking on before syncing, because some mounts require it.

prs.title: feat(platesolve): §18.I hinted solve — near-solve from a body hint or the frame's FITS pointing
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Working out where a saved photo points in the sky can now be much faster when a rough position is known. The caller can supply an approximate location. If none is given, the system uses the position recorded in the image file when it was taken. Only when neither exists does it fall back to the slow search of the whole sky. A half-given position, or one that makes no sense, is ignored; the check for impossible values goes slightly beyond what the description mentions.

prs.title: feat: §48.4 SkyFlats twilight flats — native-flats arc close-out (PR 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds calibration images ("flats") taken from the twilight sky, for setups without a light panel. The generated plan waits for dusk, points the telescope at a suitable patch of sky, then captures each filter. It rechecks the brightness before every frame because twilight changes quickly, and stops cleanly if the sky becomes too bright or too dark. Choosing "sky at twilight" now starts this automatically, and the settings and sequence editor in the app gained matching options. This completes the three-part flats project.

prs.title: feat: §48.7 flat_panel policy + §39.5 generator emits FlatPanelFlats (PR 2 of the native-flats arc)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The end-of-night calibration plans the system builds for you now use the new self-adjusting light-panel step for each filter. Previously they took a fixed one-second exposure. Target brightness, tolerance, number of frames, and whether to park the mount afterwards are now real settings under Settings → Session → Calibration, and the system obeys them rather than treating them as suggestions. The step also shows up in a new Calibration section of the sequence editor. This is part 2 of 3 of the flats project.

prs.title: feat: §48.3 FlatPanelFlats — the auto-exposure flat set (PR 1 of the native-flats arc)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new sequence step that captures a full set of calibration images ("flats") with a light panel and sets the exposure time on its own. It turns on the panel and tries short test exposures until the brightness hits the target. It then takes the requested number of frames, which are saved to the library like normal captures. The step also works without a connected panel, fails with a clear reason if there isn't enough light, and always turns the panel off afterwards, even if cancelled. This is part 1 of 3 of the flats project.

prs.title: test: §58 side-of-pier projection matrix + vernal-equinox target heuristic gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Although labelled as a test change, this also fixes a real bug in the automatic meridian flip (the mid-night repositioning of the mount). A target located exactly at the sky's zero point used to be treated as "not filled in" and replaced with the mount's current position. Now it is trusted when the mount is actually pointing there. The rest adds a large set of automated checks for how the flip decides which side of the mount the telescope should be on.

prs.title: feat: §36 Catalogs overlay — highlight rings for Messier/Caldwell/NGC/IC + object types
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sky map has a new Catalogs panel that lets you highlight every object from a famous catalog (Messier, Caldwell, NGC, IC) or a type of object such as galaxies or nebulae with colored rings. It shows the brightest 500 of each, with bigger rings for brighter objects, and each catalog gets its own color. Your choices are remembered between launches, and the usual object names and tap-to-select still work underneath. It needs the OpenNGC sky-data package, and the panel says so if it's missing; the on-device manual check was still unticked when it merged.

prs.title: fix: §44 puller minors — server-switch reset, dead rethrow, stored-but-unacked memo
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The background backup of photos to the desktop app now copes better with two awkward situations. Switching to a different telescope server cleanly lets go of the old server and starts fresh on the new one, instead of getting confused for a round. If a photo was saved correctly but the "got it" confirmation to the server failed, the app now just re-sends the confirmation instead of downloading the whole file again, which saves bandwidth on shaky connections. The code also covers a server switch that happens while the app is still asking the server for its backup slot, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: feat: §43-2b(c) frames-catalog backup area — db snapshot in every zip + opt-in restore
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Backups now include a copy of the image library's records, such as sessions, ratings, tags and frame details, but not the image files themselves. The copy can be taken safely while the telescope is still capturing. When restoring, there is a new "Frame catalog" checkbox that is off by default, because rolling back the records would hide any photos taken after the backup (the files themselves stay on disk). A damaged backup file is now reported as a failed restore in the app, rather than being rejected the moment you ask to restore.

prs.title: feat: §59.9 autofocus conditions deferral — triggers wait out bad sky (closes the §59.5 arc)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automatic refocusing now waits when the sky is bad. If the system has flagged passing clouds, a blocked telescope opening or dew, every autofocus trigger holds off, shows one notification, and runs once conditions clear, instead of wasting several minutes on a focus attempt that would fail. Other problems, such as low disk space, never delay focusing, and if the condition check itself breaks, focusing goes ahead as normal. Nothing reports these sky problems yet, so the new waiting behavior won't kick in until that detection is built.

prs.title: feat: §59.5 live per-frame HFR analysis — StarDetector on captured lights feeds the catalog + HFR-drift trigger
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every photo of the sky is now checked for star sharpness and star count right after it's taken, in the background so the next exposure is never delayed. The results show up in the Image Library within seconds, instead of only after a later rescan. This also switches on the "refocus when stars get blurrier" trigger, which had no data to work with before. Frames with too few stars to measure reliably are skipped, and if photos arrive faster than they can be checked, some are left unmeasured.

prs.title: feat: §59.5 autofocus trigger family — time/temp/HFR/filter triggers + IImageHistory seam
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imaging plans can now refocus automatically in four new situations: after a set amount of time, when the temperature changes, when stars start getting blurrier, or when a new filter is selected. These triggers also work in plans imported from the popular NINA astronomy app. It also fixes a hidden bug where autofocus and dither triggers built in the app's plan editor did nothing when they fired. Not mentioned in the description, the code also fixes the reconnect trigger so it actually runs its reconnect step.

prs.title: fix(test): guard StubAlpaca's response write against the teardown race
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes an automated test that occasionally failed for no real reason when a fake test server shut down at the wrong moment. The cause turned out to be in the test code itself, not the product, so nothing changes for users. The project's to-do list now marks this flaky test as fixed and records the cause.

prs.title: feat: §37.5 wizard weather thresholds — screen 15 covers the enforced §35.1 fields
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The first-run setup wizard's Safety screen now lets users turn on weather-station reactions and set limits for wind, humidity, and dew during setup, instead of finding them in Settings afterwards.
