Blank fields keep the profile's defaults. Turning the option off clears any limits already entered, and invalid entries block the user from moving to the next step. Choosing different actions for each weather trigger and the alarm sound settings are deliberately left out.

prs.title: feat: §35.5 audible safety alarm — bundled tones, silent delay, device-local knobs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now sounds an audible alarm when the observatory reports unsafe conditions or an emergency stop. A warning window pops up right away. After a short silent pause (5 seconds by default), a looping tone plays at full volume until someone silences it or conditions become safe again. Users can pick from three built-in tones and set the pause length for each computer under the notification settings. This adds a new open-source audio library, and there is no vibration since the app is desktop-only.

prs.title: ci: gstreamer dev packages for audioplayers_linux (§35.5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Build-system change only: the Linux build machine now installs the audio system libraries that the new safety-alarm sound feature needs. Without them, the Linux build of that feature failed.

prs.title: feat: §44.4 backup-stream bandwidth cap + link measurement
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now set a bandwidth limit on the real-time image backup so it doesn't hog a shared or metered network, with 0 meaning unlimited. Each image still downloads at full speed, but the app then waits before fetching the next one so the average stays under the limit. The settings screen also shows the connection speed measured on the first download to help pick a sensible number, and the limit is remembered between restarts. This completes the backup-stream feature set.

prs.title: feat: §44 progress surfaces — footer chip + per-frame sync badges
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's bottom status bar now shows a small indicator of the image backup's progress (connecting, how many are pending, up to date, or a problem needing attention). The indicator stays hidden on setups that never turned backups on. In the Image Library, each photo gets a small cloud badge showing whether it has been backed up, but only when backups are configured. The code goes further than the description: a photo only counts as backed up if it was copied to this specific computer, so photos backed up to a different machine still show as pending.

prs.title: feat: §35.1 weather-threshold triggers — react to the numbers, not just the boolean
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The observatory software can now react to actual weather readings: wind speed, humidity, and how close the air is to the dew point. Before, it only reacted to a simple safe/unsafe signal. If any limit you set is crossed, the rig treats conditions as unsafe and runs your existing 'when conditions turn unsafe' action, and the alert names the exact reading, such as 'wind 54 km/h over the 36 km/h limit'. It only resumes on its own once every source reads safe again. The feature is off by default so upgraded setups don't park unexpectedly, the limits can be set in the desktop app's safety settings, and a sensor the weather station doesn't report is simply skipped.

prs.title: feat: §35.3 emergency stop — daemon ladder + WILMA's persistent red button
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now has a red Emergency Stop button that is always visible on its bottom bar, one tap from any screen. After you confirm, the rig works through a set of steps in order: it stops the running plan first, cancels the current exposure, stops guiding, parks the telescope mount, and turns off the flat panel light. Each step is tried even if an earlier one fails. The result is reported honestly, so a mount that couldn't be reached shows 'MOUNT NOT REACHED — verify it manually'. An accidental second press while a stop is already underway is ignored.

prs.title: feat: §48 auto-flats — WILMA client half (prompt dialog + Settings → Session → Calibration)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now shows the 'capture calibration frames tonight?' question when you start an imaging run. You can pick flats with a light panel at the end of the night, flats from the sky at twilight, or not tonight, with an option to remember your choice. A new Settings → Session → Calibration page lets you view or change that default at any time. If a newer run asks while an older question is still unanswered, the older one is replaced, and closing the dialog counts as 'not tonight'. This completes the feature on the app side; the server side arrived in #735.

prs.title: feat: §44 real-time backup stream — WILMA client half (puller + settings + registries)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now switch on 'Stream new frames to this device' in the desktop app's storage settings. The app then copies every new image off the observatory computer during the night, checks that each copy is intact, and saves it to a backup folder. If the imaging drive fails overnight, only the image being taken at that moment is lost. Copying pauses while the camera is downloading an exposure, and if another computer is already streaming, the app shows which one. The code also restarts streaming automatically when the app launches if it was left on, which the description doesn't mention, and it adds a small new library for the integrity checks.

prs.title: feat: §48 auto-flats prompt flow — server half (ask/decide/auto-execute via §39.5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The observatory server now handles the 'capture calibration tonight?' choice. The choice can be ask each time (the default), panel flats at the end, sky flats at twilight, or never. When a run finishes normally and the answer was yes, the server builds a matching set of flats from that night's own settings. Panel flats start right away with a reminder to switch on the panel, while sky flats are prepared for you to start at twilight, since automatic twilight timing doesn't exist yet. Runs that were stopped, aborted, or failed never trigger flats, and this change replaces the earlier placeholder along with the format of the answer the app sends back.

prs.title: feat: §44 real-time backup stream — server half (slot, queue, ack, lazy sha256)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The observatory server can now feed a live backup of captured images to one desktop computer at a time. Earlier this was only a placeholder that did nothing. The server keeps a list of images that haven't been backed up yet, attaches an integrity check to each one, and only marks an image as backed up once the desktop confirms its copy passed that check. If a different computer takes over the backup, it receives the full set of images. The image database gained a few new fields to support this, and this PR does not include the desktop app side of the feature.

prs.title: feat: §63.3 active hang-detection ping + auto-reconnect after recovery
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now actively checks on the guiding software every 2 seconds while guiding and every 10 seconds otherwise. Before, a guider that froze but stayed connected went unnoticed. Three missed check-ins in a row are now treated as a lost guider, which triggers the same recovery and sequence-protection steps as a real disconnect. After the guider service recovers, the app also reconnects to it automatically within the user's 'guider retry timeout' window and posts a notification, but it never resumes a paused imaging run on its own.

prs.title: feat: §42.2 mid-sequence guider fault flow — a guider link drop now enforces on_guider_lost
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If the guider connection drops while an imaging sequence is running, the app now immediately applies the user's 'on guider lost' setting: pause the run (the default), skip the current target, or abort. Before, it only showed a crash notification and kept taking unguided, wasted frames. The action fires once per disconnect and sends a critical notification. It stays quiet if nothing was running.

prs.title: feat: §35.4 unsafe-reaction engine — SafetyMonitor unsafe now enforces the on_unsafe policy
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a connected safety monitor reports that conditions have turned unsafe, such as weather, the app now enforces the user's chosen policy: pause the run, stop guiding and park the telescope (the default), park only, abort and park, or just notify. Before, that setting was saved but nothing acted on it. If 'auto-resume when safe' is on, the app waits for conditions to stay clear, then unparks and resumes only the runs it paused itself, with a reminder to check pointing. Runs waiting on the user are never resumed automatically.

prs.title: ci: guard against CRLF/LF line-ending flips in PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal build-check change. Pull requests now fail if they accidentally flip a changed file's line-ending style wholesale, the kind of invisible change that earlier turned a small feature into a 25,000-line diff. New files are not checked. The description says the error message suggests a sed command, but the code actually suggests the unix2dos or dos2unix tools.

prs.title: fix: harden the servers — resolve issues #58–#61
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes four hardening issues in the guider's network servers. The most important is a security fix: a single-frame capture could previously be saved anywhere on the machine by any client on the network, and saves are now confined to the app's data folder unless an admin configures another location. The code goes a bit further than the description says, since it also resolves shortcut-style links to block sneaky escapes and requires the target folder to already exist. The other fixes make text with tabs or other hidden characters produce valid data, cap overly long device-discovery requests, reject oversized requests up front, and log more helpful messages when a camera server tries to redirect.

prs.title: ci: bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.160 to 1.0.166 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is a routine dependency update with no effect on users. It moves the automated AI code-review tool used in the project's build checks to a newer version.

prs.title: docs: reorganize docs/ + design/ — guides under docs/, design index + archive, apt release channel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation housekeeping. The setup, deployment and release-notes guides now live in the docs folder next to the user guide, and all links were updated. The internal design notes got an index page, and finished planning documents were moved into an archive. The docs also record a new decision: the server will be released and updated through the project's own apt.openastro.net software repository instead of GitHub downloads. However, the system that actually publishes to that repository has not been built yet, so the documented install steps depend on work that is still pending.

prs.title: fix: restore CRLF line endings flipped by PR #57
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a cleanup with no change in how the guider behaves. It undoes an accidental formatting change from PR #57, which switched the invisible line-ending characters in four source files. That switch made those files hard to compare against the original PHD2 project they come from. The file contents are otherwise identical.

prs.title: feat: ARA integration events + get_version (PHD2-GAP gaps 1-3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider now sends live progress updates while it builds its calibration dark frames, which can take several minutes. It also sends clear, structured alerts when the camera drops out and when it automatically reconnects, so connected apps like ARA no longer have to interpret human-readable error messages. It also documents a way for apps to ask which version of the guider they are talking to and whether it is this fork or standard PHD2. The added documentation says this version check already existed but was undocumented, rather than new as the description claims. The failure message for dark-library builds also reports a count of completed groups, not completed frames as the description states. Separately, this PR accidentally changed the line-ending format of four whole files, which is why the change looks so large; PR #62 later reversed that.

prs.title: docs: Phase-15 close-out — fork CONTRIBUTING, user guide, ARA issue templates; PHD2-GAP status
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This PR finishes the remaining documentation for the first release. It adds a full user guide covering setup, planning, imaging, the safety features and backups. It also replaces the contributor guide, which was still the original NINA version, with one written for this project. The GitHub forms for bug reports and feature requests were replaced, and a new form was added for reporting misbehaving equipment drivers. Planning notes were updated to record that the related guider improvements were submitted upstream. Documentation only; no code changed.

prs.title: feat: §37.6 wizard recommended sky-data preset; §37.5 extras reclassified enforcement-first
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When someone sets up a new profile, the setup wizard's sky-data step now pre-selects the recommended star catalog and deep-sky object catalog and labels them "Recommended". This means a fresh setup gets the data the planner and sky atlas actually use. Any choices the user has already made are never overwritten, including a deliberate clear. A planned set of extra weather-safety settings was deliberately postponed instead, because the server does not yet have anything that would act on them.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 camera readout modes + cooler set-point read-back + pixel_size_y
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The camera panel can now switch between the camera's readout modes, using the list of modes the camera itself provides. It also keeps showing the cooling target (for example "Cooling to −10.0 °C") beside the actual sensor temperature, where before the target disappeared once it was entered. Cameras with non-square pixels now show both pixel dimensions. Switching the readout mode also refreshes the camera's sensor details, since those differ from mode to mode. Older and newer versions of the app and server continue to work with each other.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 dome FindHome/AbortSlew/SetPark/SyncToAzimuth — daemon + WILMA controls
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The dome control panel now has four more buttons: Find home, Set park here (saves the current position as the park spot), Sync (tells the software what direction the dome is really facing), and Stop. Each button only appears if the connected dome supports it. Stop stays clickable while the dome is moving, and the system confirms the stop command was actually sent before reporting success, so a slow connection can't quietly lose it while the dome keeps turning.

prs.title: feat: §36-2b(b) Data Manager graceful-shutdown drain + stale §36 doc corrections
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the software is shut down normally, any sky-data downloads still in progress are now cancelled properly and allowed to clean up before it exits. Leftover temporary files are removed right away, and the app shows the download as cancelled instead of leaving it half-finished until the next startup. The PR also corrects two outdated entries in the project's to-do list that were already done or no longer needed.

prs.title: feat: §43-2b backup retention — keep-N pruning after every create
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Configuration backups no longer pile up forever. After each new backup, the software keeps only the newest ones, 20 by default, and deletes older ones automatically. The number can be changed under Settings → Session → Storage, and setting it to 0 keeps every backup. If cleanup fails for any reason, the new backup is still kept and nothing is lost.

prs.title: feat: §63.6 e-4b-3/e-4c — live guider calibration builds in WILMA + cover-the-scope gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider calibration screen now shows when a dark-frame or defect-map build is running, refreshes itself when the build finishes, and shows the error message if it fails. Before any build starts, it now asks you to confirm the telescope is covered, because light on the sensor ruins these builds. Error messages now tell the difference between "another build is already running" and "the guider isn't connected." The server also accepts a new way of stating the connection version, so a future web-browser version of the app can connect.

prs.title: feat: §43-2b(b) remote BackupSourceUrl restore — download, verify, swap
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now restore a configuration backup from another machine's address, such as a second observatory computer on the local network. Before anything is changed, the file is downloaded and checked against a required fingerprint (a checksum) to make sure it is the right file and wasn't damaged. There is also a 512 MB size limit. The code also cancels a download that stalls for 60 seconds, which the PR description doesn't mention. Restores from backups stored on the same machine work as before, and the app screen for choosing a remote backup will come in a later update.

prs.title: feat: §51 diagnostics.snapshot on WS accept — the reconnect-replay gap closes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The health indicator in the app can no longer get stuck showing amber or red after a dropped connection. Each time the app reconnects, the server now sends the full list of problems that are currently open, and the app replaces its list with it. Previously, if a problem was resolved while the connection was down, the warning stayed until you switched servers. As a small side change, problems with an unknown severity are now reported as "unknown" instead of causing that update to be dropped.

prs.title: feat(client): §58.12 unattended-shutdown settings + friendly needs-attention badge
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's Safety settings now have a switch for the new overnight safety shutdown (on by default) and a box for how many minutes to wait before it kicks in (10 by default, and it won't accept less than 1). Both settings can be found through the settings search. In the list of saved sequences, a run that is paused waiting for a person now reads "needs attention" instead of an awkward internal name. This is the app-side companion to #719.

prs.title: feat: §58.12 unattended-failure graceful shutdown — countdown + put-the-rig-to-bed ladder
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: If an imaging run stops overnight because something went wrong, such as a failed meridian flip (when the mount turns the telescope over mid-session), and nobody responds within a set time (10 minutes by default), the system now safely shuts the equipment down on its own. It stops guiding, parks the mount, disconnects the accessories, warms the camera's cooler gradually, disconnects the camera last, and leaves a summary message for the morning. Any real sign that someone is back cancels the countdown, such as dismissing the alert, sending a command, or opening the app, but routine background checks do not. The run stays paused so it can still be resumed. This differs slightly from the plan in #717: the run is not marked as finished, and the shutdown does not turn off an alarm itself.

prs.title: feat(client): §58.12 — WILMA renders the pausedawaitinguser run state
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now recognizes the new "paused, needs your attention" state for imaging runs. The toolbar shows "Paused — needs your attention" with a Resume button ready to use, and the list of saved sequences marks the run in red instead of the calm blue used for a normal pause. Older servers are unaffected. This is the app-side companion to #717.

prs.title: feat: §58.12 prerequisite — PausedAwaitingUser sequencer state; failed flips pause resumable instead of failing
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a meridian flip fails (the mount turning the telescope over mid-session), the imaging run now pauses and waits for a person instead of ending as failed. Before, the night's run was lost even after the problem was fixed. No more pictures are taken while it waits, and pressing Resume tries the flip again after re-checking the equipment. The paused run's sequence is also protected from being edited or deleted, and the alert message now says the run is paused rather than halted.

prs.title: Release 3.0.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This marks AlpacaBridge version 3.0.0 as released, its first tagged release. It only adds the release date to the changelog and updates the outdated version shown in the README, so nothing in the software itself changes. It is a major version because the way ToupTek cameras are numbered changed.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 custom horizon editor — enter the skyline behind the toggle
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Turning on "Use custom horizon" in the app's Site settings now opens a simple editor where you can enter your local skyline, meaning the compass direction and height of trees or rooftops that block the view. The points are saved together with the other site settings, and the app shows the cleaned-up list the server sends back. If the site settings save but the skyline doesn't, the error message now says so. The line count is inflated by a lot of formatting-only changes that the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: feat: §36 custom terrain horizon — profile storage + both server consumers
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "use custom horizon" setting now actually does something. Users can save the real outline of their horizon (trees, rooftops, hills) as altitude readings around the compass. When the setting is on, Tonight's Sky and the planning chart use that outline instead of one flat height everywhere, so an object behind a building is no longer shown as visible. The outline is removed from shared profiles because it could reveal where someone lives. The screen for entering the outline comes in a later change.

prs.title: feat: §40 per-run capture sessions — a sequence run owns its catalog session
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each time a planned imaging sequence runs, its photos are now grouped under their own session in the image library. Before, they went into the same "manual capture" pile as one-off snapshots. This means the library and statistics can finally tell separate imaging runs apart. If creating a session fails, the run still goes ahead without one, so imaging is never blocked.

prs.title: fix(client): cap the WS reconnect backoff at 10s (was 30s)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the connection to the server drops, the app now waits at most 10 seconds between reconnect attempts, down from 30. After a server restart or a brief Wi-Fi drop, the app comes back up to three times faster.

prs.title: feat(client): §60.9 equipment chips go live — WS-driven refresh replaces waiting out the poll
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's equipment indicators now update the moment a device connects, disconnects, or fails. They used to wait for the next routine check, which could take up to 15 seconds. The switch panel benefits most: it had no routine check at all and previously needed a manual refresh to notice changes. Routine checks stay on as a backup for older servers. Much of the diff is automatic code reformatting with no effect on behavior.

prs.title: feat: §60.9 equipment connection WS events — catalogued from day one, now actually emitted
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now announces live when any piece of equipment (camera, mount, focuser, dome, weather sensors, and so on) connects, disconnects, or fails. These announcements were planned from the start but never actually sent, so apps had to keep checking to find out. Repeated reports of the same state are now filtered out to avoid noise. The app-side change that uses these announcements is a separate PR.

prs.title: refactor(client): §36 planning reuse — catalog-owned $type consts, buildFilterInfo, kRunTabIndex, one run-feedback surface
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is mostly internal cleanup of the planning screens, with one visible fix. "Add to Sequence" from the target bar and from Tonight's Sky now shows a "connect to a server first" message instead of failing silently. All three places that create an imaging run now share one set of messages. The large line count comes mainly from automatic code reformatting; the sequences the app produces are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: §37 profile snapshots normalize null sections at every disk read
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Profiles saved with an older version of the app no longer come back with empty sections when someone views, exports, or switches to them. Settings added later, such as camera electronics or optics, are now filled in with sensible defaults every time a saved profile is read. Before, only the active profile got this treatment. The default-filling logic was also moved into one shared place so both paths use the same rules.

prs.title: feat: §38 daemon guard — PATCH/DELETE of a sequence with an active run returns 409
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now refuses to edit or delete a sequence while it is running, paused, starting, or winding down. It tells the caller to stop or abort the run first. Before, only the WILMA app checked this, so a second device or a direct request could change or remove a sequence out from under a live imaging run. Finished or idle sequences can still be edited and deleted as before.

prs.title: docs(playbook): refresh the §-checklist ledger to post-#706 reality
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's feature checklist so it reflects what has actually shipped through PR #706. Several areas are now marked done, including single-client control, disk-space protection, calibration, backup, bug reports, and live view. Others such as polar alignment and meridian flip have their remaining work restated.

prs.title: feat(client): §27 single-client policy — claim/re-claim, takeover modal, 4004 session-transferred modal
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The WILMA app now takes part in the "one controlling device at a time" rule. It claims control when it connects and quietly reclaims it after a brief Wi-Fi drop. When another device asks to take over, it shows a "wants to connect — Allow / Keep me connected" prompt. If control is taken away, it shows a "Session transferred" message and only reconnects when the user presses a button; the live event feed still works against older servers or while another device is in control.

prs.title: feat: §27 single-client policy — connect handshake + 4004 takeover (server)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now allows only one controlling device at a time. A new device asks to connect, and the current device gets a prompt to allow or refuse the takeover; a device that has gone silent for 60 seconds loses control automatically. The server also sends regular check-in pings so a frozen app can't hold control forever. Older apps that never ask for control keep working exactly as before.

prs.title: feat: §54 push channels — Pushover + Telegram senders (the stored tokens finally send)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Warnings and more serious problems can now be sent to your phone through Pushover or Telegram. Previously, the token fields in settings were saved but nothing was ever sent. Each service now needs a second value (a Pushover user key or a Telegram chat ID), added under the notification settings, and critical alerts use Pushover's high priority to get through quiet hours. Sending runs in the background so a provider outage never slows the rig. The code also lets critical sequence alerts through even when "notify on sequence paused" is turned off, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: feat: §45 polar alignment phase 1 — guider RPC surface + the ARA-owned axis/refraction geometry
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This lays the groundwork for polar alignment, the step that lines a telescope mount up with the sky's pole. It adds the commands Ara will use to talk to the guider (take a frame, find stars, and temporarily reserve the guide camera so nothing interrupts) and the math that works out how far off the mount is, including a correction for the atmosphere bending starlight. The math checks inputs and refuses to give an answer from bad data rather than guess. Nothing is visible to users yet: the step-by-step routine, the screens, and testing against the real guider are still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §58.8/§58.10 surfaces in Safety → Policies — first-flip status + re-arm, dark-hours escalation toggle
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Safety settings screen now has two new controls. One is a switch for 'louder alerts during dark hours', on by default. The other shows whether the one-time warning before the first meridian flip is still waiting to fire, with a Re-arm button for rig changes the app can't detect on its own, such as re-balancing or swapping mounts. Although described as the app-side half, the change also includes notable server work. Saving settings from the app can no longer overwrite the server's record of whether that first flip has happened, and there is a new server action for re-arming the warning.

prs.title: feat: §29 per-frame pre-capture disk check — abort-policy captures refuse to start on a critically-low save volume
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the 'abort on critically low disk space' setting is on, each exposure now checks free space on the save drive before it starts, and refuses to start if the drive is nearly full. Before, the disk was only checked once a minute, so a quick run of large images could fill it and waste imaging time on frames that couldn't be saved. The default 'warn' setting still never blocks a capture. If the space check itself fails, the capture goes ahead anyway.

prs.title: Fix #120: guard ZWO exposure-status read; align ZWO copyright name
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes a small crash-type bug in ZWO camera support. If the camera disconnected just as the software asked for its exposure status, the software could return a raw error instead of a normal response. It now simply reports the camera as idle. The code also handles a second, related case this way (the camera already fully disconnected), which the description doesn't mention. A company name in the licensing notes was also corrected to 'ZWO Company'.

prs.title: Camera close-order audit + held-mutex conversion, exposure-failure recovery, TSan guard fix
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This makes ZWO, Player One and SVBONY cameras more reliable when they are disconnected while other commands are still running, closing gaps where a command could reach a camera that had just been shut. Separately, one random failed exposure on a ZWO or QHY camera no longer leaves the camera stuck in an error state for every later exposure. ZWO now retries a failed exposure up to twice, and both brands report the camera as ready again afterward. The PR also adds stress tests and fixes an automated test check that could wrongly pass when no tests had actually run.

prs.title: feat: §58.10 — unattended-hours severity escalation at the notification chokepoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: During full darkness at the user's site, warnings about equipment, the running imaging session, storage or safety are now automatically raised one level (warning to error, error to critical). This means the bedside alarm kicks in sooner for someone who is asleep. Raised alerts carry a note explaining they were escalated, so they can be read correctly in the morning. Daytime alerts are unchanged, the feature is on by default and can be turned off per profile, and if anything goes wrong in the check the alert is still sent at its original level.

prs.title: feat: §58.8 — the first flip on a profile announces itself (60 s proceed-on-timeout safety net)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The first meridian flip on a profile now raises a critical alert and waits 60 seconds before it runs, giving the user a chance to stop the sequence and check their settings. This targets the one mistake most likely to damage equipment: a new profile with a wrong timing value swinging the telescope into the tripod. Once that first flip goes ahead, later flips run without the wait, and changing the optics setup in the profile turns the warning back on. There is no button to skip the wait yet, so the full 60 seconds always passes unless the user stops the sequence.

prs.title: feat: §58.7 — meridian-flip failure notifications on the baseline paths
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A failed meridian flip now always sends a critical alert, even when the extra flip-safety features are turned off. Before, it could halt an unattended night's sequence without telling anyone. The alert also says whether guiding could be restarted. Two smaller problems now send alerts too: when re-centering on the target fails after a flip, and when refocusing fails after a flip. In both cases imaging continues, but the user is told the pointing or focus may be off.

prs.title: chore: §63/§65 hardening sweep — guider RMS in arcsec; stale PORT_TODO guard entry closed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Guiding accuracy is now also reported in arcseconds, the unit astronomers normally use, alongside the existing pixel figures. If the guiding software hasn't reported its scale yet, the value is left blank rather than shown as a misleading zero. Nothing on screen shows the new figures yet in this change. The rest is housekeeping: an old to-do item was confirmed as already handled and closed.

prs.title: feat(client): Settings → System → About — identity, version, and the in-app open-source licenses page
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The About page in the desktop app's settings used to be a placeholder and is now real. It shows the app's name, its version, how it is licensed, and a link to the source code. It also has an open-source licenses page listing every bundled third-party package with its full license text, which is a legal requirement. That list is collected automatically at build time, so it stays accurate as dependencies change.

prs.title: Relicense SSPL-1.0 → AGPL-3.0-or-later (with vendor-SDK linking exception)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge changes its license from SSPL to AGPL-3.0-or-later. SSPL kept the project out of Linux distribution package archives, while AGPL still requires companies that modify it and offer it over a network to share their changes. A special exception lets the project keep working with the closed-source hardware vendor libraries it depends on. The code itself does not change: license notices were updated in about 210 files and in the docs. It also documents where each bundled vendor library came from, noting that three of them (QHY, ToupTek, SVBONY) have no written permission to redistribute.

prs.title: feat(client): §3.1 slice 3 — Optimal Sub advisor carries the sequence target into the star-detectability advice
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor's "optimal exposure length" advisor now finds which sky target an exposure belongs to and sends it to the server. It can then advise whether each shot will capture enough stars to line frames up later. When star count is the limiting factor, the advisor says so in its headline. Older servers simply ignore the target and the advisor looks the same as before. The code also skips slew steps set to inherit their target from the surrounding target block, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: feat: §10.6 Switch PR3 — SetSwitchValue targets a specific switch device + editor palette entry
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sequences can now control one specific power/switch box when a rig has several connected, and the "Set Switch Value" step finally shows up in the sequence editor under a new Switch category. Existing sequences and ones imported from NINA behave exactly as before, using the first box. If a sequence names a box that isn't connected, the step is skipped with a log message rather than writing to a different box by mistake. An unused placeholder was also removed and new tests were added. For now the box is picked by typing its number; a friendlier picker is planned.

prs.title: feat: §3.1 slice 3 — star-detectability floor wired into the sub-exposure window + Tonight's Sky
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The exposure-length advisor can now warn when individual shots would contain too few stars to line up and stack, and suggest a longer exposure if that is the real limit. This only kicks in when the user supplies a target's sky position, so older app versions see no change. Tonight's Sky also adds a note like "~N stars/sub — thin for registration" for star-poor setups without changing any target scores. This is advice only and blocks nothing. The part of the app that shows this to users is planned as a separate follow-up change.

prs.title: Complete #100: AsyncConnectable everywhere + #101 TSan stress harness (hardware-validated)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All 26 camera, mount, focuser and power-box drivers now share one well-tested way of connecting and disconnecting, instead of each having its own copy. For 22 of them this fixes rare crashes or ignored disconnects that could happen when connect, disconnect or shutdown overlapped. A new automated check now hammers several drivers with overlapping requests to catch these timing bugs. The change was verified on real hardware across eight devices and six machines. It also includes install-package fixes for one ASIAIR Plus model and a web-page tweak that shows temperature first for ToupTek devices.

prs.title: docs: fold from-zero client setup + remote-daemon guidance into RUNNING.md
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup guide for building the app yourself now covers a fresh computer from start to finish. It adds how to install the exact required Flutter version, which extra packages are needed on Linux and Windows, and how to connect to a daemon running on another machine, including a quick way to check the network first. A new troubleshooting section covers common setup errors. Documentation only.

prs.title: docs: RUNNING.md — run from source on Linux, macOS, and Windows
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new guide for building and running both the daemon and the desktop app from source on Linux, macOS and Windows, linked from the main README. It collects setup steps and known pitfalls that were previously spread across other documents. Running the daemon directly on Windows is marked as untested, with workarounds suggested. Documentation only.

prs.title: chore: remove obsolete .coderabbit.yaml
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Deletes a leftover settings file for an automated code-review service the organization stopped using in May. Nothing reads the file anymore, so there is no change in behavior. Internal cleanup only.

prs.title: feat: multi-target night plans + sequence delete; optimal-sub 500 and OpenNGC membership fixes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adding several targets to a sequence now builds one combined night plan instead of each new target replacing the last. Each target gets its own block, shared start and end steps run once, and a Remove button takes out a single target. Saved sequences can now be deleted, including stopping one that is running first. It also fixes a crash in the exposure-length advisor for profiles with missing camera settings, corrects the NGC/IC sky catalog overlays, and intentionally removes the planetarium's Catalogs drawer until a replacement lands. The visible code goes a bit beyond the description: the settings fix covers every section of a profile, not just camera settings, and saved-sequence lists now count targets correctly for these new multi-target plans.

prs.title: feat: §60.9 frame.complete goes live — capture-driven refresh for library + calibration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Image Library, calibration coverage badges, and dark-library build progress now update on their own while a capture is running, instead of needing a manual refresh. The server now announces each new frame as it is saved, which it was supposed to do but never actually did. The app waits for about two seconds of quiet before refreshing, so a fast burst of frames causes one refresh rather than dozens.

prs.title: perf: streaming frame export — no in-memory tar, prioritized by the #686 review
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Exporting frames no longer builds the whole archive in the server's memory first. Files are now sent to the user as they are read, so large exports won't overwhelm small machines like a Raspberry Pi. The description says every file is opened before sending starts, but the code actually opens them one at a time during the download. As a result, the reported count of exported frames is a best guess: a file that disappears mid-export is quietly skipped. Nothing changes for users of the app.

prs.title: feat: §39.10 bulk export — tar of selected FITS files; the §40.8 bar is complete
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now select frames in the Image Library and export them as a single archive file, saved through the normal save dialog, ready for editing tools like PixInsight or Siril. Missing files are skipped instead of failing the whole export, and files with the same name are renamed so none get overwritten. This completes the library's bulk actions: rate, tag, move, export, and delete. In this first version the server builds the full archive in memory, which the team flagged as a later follow-up.

prs.title: feat(client): §65.9 manual stretch sliders — 200ms debounced server round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The frame viewer has a new "manual" display option with black point, midtone, and white point sliders, so users can adjust how an image is brightened themselves. The image re-renders shortly after the user stops dragging, rather than on every tiny movement, to avoid overloading the server. If a re-render fails, the sliders snap back to match the image still on screen. This is an app-only change; the server already supported these settings.

prs.title: feat: §40.8 bulk move — reassign frames to another session, end to end
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now select frames in the Image Library and move them into a different session using a new session picker. This helps tidy up recovered or stray frames that belong with a real imaging run. The server refuses the move if the chosen session doesn't exist, so frames can't end up lost. Export was still disabled at this point.

prs.title: feat!: temperature_c sentinel pass — nullable end-to-end + schema_version table
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a camera doesn't report its sensor temperature, the app now records it as "unknown" instead of a made-up 0°C, and exports and charts show a blank rather than a fake reading. Existing databases upgrade automatically on the next start, and old readings are kept exactly as they were. Matching dark calibration frames to images from cameras without cooling still works across old and new recordings. The database also now tracks its own version number, which makes future upgrades simpler.

prs.title: feat(client): cursor paging on the library + calibration session lists
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Image Library and Calibration session lists now show a "Load more sessions" button, so people with more than 200 sessions can see all of them instead of having the list cut off silently. If a library search finds nothing yet but more sessions exist on the server, it offers to load them. Long lists also now build only the items on screen, which keeps big catalogs responsive. The frame strips inside each session still show only the first page, and this is intentional.

prs.title: feat(client): §40.5 in-viewer tag editing + full detail metadata
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The frame viewer now shows more of each frame's capture settings, including gain, offset, sensor temperature, focus position and image size. You can also add or remove tags right there without leaving the image. If those extra details fail to load, the viewer still works normally. The description calls tag edits "optimistic," but the code actually waits for the server to confirm before updating the tags on screen, and shows an error message if the change fails.

prs.title: feat(client): §40.5 in-viewer star rating
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: You can now rate a frame from 1 to 5 stars directly in the frame viewer, and tapping the current rating clears it. The stars change right away and go back if saving fails, with an error message. The library behind the viewer refreshes so the new rating shows up immediately. This reuses the existing rating feature on the server, so nothing changed there.

prs.title: feat(client): §65 stretched previews in the live frame viewer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Opening a frame in the viewer now shows a full-resolution, contrast-enhanced version of the image, instead of just the small thumbnail. A picker lets you switch between several display styles. The thumbnail appears instantly while the better version loads. If loading fails, the last good image stays on screen with a short note.

prs.title: feat: §50 Stats CSVs stream the real catalog; demo library data retired
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sessions and Frames CSV export buttons on the Stats dashboard now pull real data from the connected server instead of built-in sample data. The last of that sample data has been removed from the app. The Sessions export now has one row per session with time window, target, frame counts and total light exposure time. It no longer includes the site, average focus quality or guiding columns the old sample-based export had. Users now see clear messages when no server is connected or the export fails.

prs.title: feat(client): 12f.3 library filter/rating/search pills go live
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The filter, rating, and search buttons at the top of the Image Library now work; before this they were only placeholders. You can show only frames taken through one filter, hide frames below a chosen star rating, and search sessions by target name. Active choices are highlighted and a Clear button resets them. When nothing matches, the library says so and offers a one-tap way to clear the filters, so an empty result isn't mistaken for missing data.

prs.title: feat: §40.6 Resume Target — recorded sequence or catalog synthesis, wired to the library
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Resume Target button in the Image Library now works. It builds a ready-to-run capture plan for continuing a target on another night. If the original session's plan was saved, it reuses that plan exactly. Otherwise it rebuilds one from the photos already taken, using the same filters, exposure times, camera settings, focus positions, and frame counts, and then opens it in the Run tab. Pointing the telescope at the target is not included yet, so users still need to add that step themselves before running.

prs.title: feat(client): 12f.3b bulk frame operations — Rate/Tag/Delete live in the library
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the Image Library, users can now select several frames at once and rate them, add or remove tags, or delete them. Deleting asks for confirmation and keeps two choices apart: removing frames from the catalog only (the default), or also deleting the image files from disk. The description only mentions the app side, but the code also makes the server actually delete the image files and their preview images; before this, that checkbox did nothing. The Move to session and Export actions remain disabled.

prs.title: feat(client): 12f.2 Image Library live-wiring — sessions, frame strips, thumbnails + §39.5 flats button
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Image Library now shows the user's real sessions, frames, and thumbnails from the server instead of made-up demo data. It also shows loading, error, and empty states, and supports pull-to-refresh. Tapping a frame opens a new zoomable viewer with that frame's recorded details. Each session card's Capture Matching Flats button now works and uses the same flow as the Calibration screen. Frame editing, bulk actions, search/filters, and Resume Target were left for follow-up work.

prs.title: feat(client): §39.10 Calibration screen — sessions + matching flats + dark library (§39 slice 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds a new Calibration screen, reachable from the bottom status bar. It lists past imaging sessions with a summary per filter and badges showing whether matching flat or dark calibration frames already exist. From there, users can generate a matching-flats capture plan and land straight on it in the Run tab. A second tab shows the dark-frame library and a form for building a new set of dark frames.

prs.title: feat: §39.8 dark library — catalog-backed entries + generated dark-matrix build sequence (§39 slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The dark-frame library on the server now reflects the dark frames users have actually captured, grouped by exposure, gain, and sensor temperature, instead of sample data. Asking to build a dark library now creates a ready-to-run capture plan that cools the camera to each requested temperature and shoots each combination of settings. It can skip combinations that are already covered. Build progress is measured by how many matching frames actually exist in the catalog, and exposures shorter than one second are now supported.

prs.title: feat: §39.5 matching flats — the plan becomes a persisted runnable sequence (§39 slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: "Capture Matching Flats" for a past imaging session now saves a ready-to-run flat sequence instead of just returning a plan. For each filter the session used, the sequence switches to that filter, moves the focuser back to where those images were focused, and shoots flats with the same camera settings, so dust shadows and dark corners calibrate out correctly. Preview-only mode still returns just the plan, and no longer points to a sequence that doesn't exist. The code also quietly adds support for a request key that can prevent duplicate sequences from repeated requests, which the description doesn't mention; controlling a flat panel and matching camera temperature are left for later.

prs.title: feat!: §28 frames-schema widening — REAL exposure_seconds + nullable gain, in-place DB rebuild (§40 prerequisite)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The frame catalog now records exposure times of less than a second accurately. A half-second calibration frame used to be logged as 1 second, or as 0 seconds when rebuilt from image files, and a missing camera gain was stored as a fake number instead of "unknown". Existing databases are upgraded automatically the next time the server starts, and the exported spreadsheets now show sub-second times correctly. One small gap: the dark library listing still expects a gain value, even though the description says unknown gain is supported everywhere.

prs.title: feat(client): Imaging-tab filter picker (PR #71 follow-up) + capture-block entry verified closed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Imaging tab now has a Filter dropdown for manual captures, filled from the filter names in your profile. Until now every manual shot was recorded as using the 'L' filter no matter what was actually in place. Both this picker and the sequence editor's filter picker now handle two slots with the same name without crashing, a fix the description doesn't mention. The PR also closes an old tracking note after confirming that nothing uses the related code.

prs.title: feat!: §60.9 rename frames_* → instructions_* on the wire + document the stream ordering contract
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence progress counters sent from the server to the app were renamed from "frames" to "instructions", because they always counted sequence steps rather than camera exposures. The restart notice now says "was at instruction 5/12" to match. This is a deliberate breaking change, made now because the app is the only consumer and ships alongside the server. The API documentation now also spells out the order in which progress and end-of-run messages can arrive.

prs.title: perf(server): §60.9 sequence.progress back-pressure — single-flight trailing-coalesce pump
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a sequence reports progress very rapidly, such as during fast camera captures, the server no longer piles up an unlimited backlog of progress updates to the app. Only one update is sent at a time, and a burst of updates collapses into a single message with the latest state. Start, pause and finish messages are never held back. Beyond what the description says, the code also makes sure no stray progress update can arrive after a run has ended.

prs.title: feat: §37.4 filter-wheel slot labels daemon round-trip (12h.2b) — profile-authoritative filter picker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Filter wheel slot names are now saved in your profile on the server and load automatically whenever the app connects. The sequence editor's filter picker therefore shows your own filters on every device instead of built-in defaults. Edits in the Filter Wheel settings save as you go, older profiles upgrade with the standard default names, and everything still works offline. Shared profile exports include these names.

prs.title: feat(server): NEXTGEN §3.1 slice 2 — galactic star-count model, validation gate measured + PASSING (unwired)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the second building block for a future warning about exposures too short to capture enough stars: an estimate of how many stars appear per patch of sky, depending on how close the view is to the Milky Way. The estimate was checked against a real star catalog and stayed within the agreed accuracy limit (off by less than a factor of two) everywhere, and that check now runs automatically with every build. Nothing uses it yet, so users see no change; hooking it into the app is a later step that still needs maintainer approval.

prs.title: feat(server): NEXTGEN §3.1 slice 1 — the m_lim(t) limiting-magnitude solver (unwired)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the first building block for a future warning about exposures too short to capture enough stars: a calculation of the faintest star a single exposure can pick up, given the telescope, camera, sky darkness, and seeing. It is not connected to anything yet, so nothing changes for users. It reuses the same sky-brightness math as the existing exposure-length advisor, and a small tidy-up lets both share it.

prs.title: docs(design): NEXTGEN §3.1 star-detectability floor — design proposal for sign-off
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A planning document, with no code, that proposes how to warn users when their exposures are too short to capture enough stars for aligning and stacking images. It recommends a star-count estimate that is only allowed to ship if it matches real catalog data within a factor of two, and asks the maintainer for a yes or no. It also explains why a similar warning about satellite trails is not being proposed for now.

prs.title: feat(server): NEXTGEN §5 Tier-1 sensor QE library — peak-QE auto-fill from the sensor name
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a camera connects, the app now recognizes about 16 common astronomy camera sensors by name and fills in the sensor's light sensitivity rating, a number the exposure-length advisor needs that users previously had to look up themselves. It only fills this in when the field is blank and never overwrites a value the user entered. Unrecognized sensors are left blank so the advisor's standard default applies, and existing profiles pick up the value the next time the camera reconnects.

prs.title: docs(port-todo): track the #652 review's LV dims-vs-maxDim observation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a single note to the project's to-do list about a minor known issue in Live View: the image size the app reports can be larger than the actual preview image, which gets shrunk behind the scenes. It causes no problems today, but it is written down so it isn't forgotten if a future feature relies on those numbers. Documentation only.

prs.title: feat(client): §36.8 Tonight's Sky best-window highlight (slice 4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the Tonight's Sky list, each target's timing line now shows at a glance whether now is a good time to shoot it. It turns green and bold with a "now ·" prefix while the target's best viewing window is open, and fades once that window has passed for the night. This only changes how the list looks, so no targets are hidden or reordered.

prs.title: feat(client): §68.4 — help entries searchable in the command palette + AlpacaBridge troubleshoot article
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's quick-search box (the command palette) now finds help articles as well as settings, so all of the roughly 60 existing help articles can be found by typing what you're trying to do. Choosing a help result opens that article. It also adds a new troubleshooting article for when the equipment hub (AlpacaBridge) isn't detected, triggered by phrases like "equipment hub down," and fixes a search result label that could show the word "null" and long help titles that spilled off the screen. The code also shortens long result descriptions in the search list to a two-line preview, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: docs(port-todo): close the last two review-note hardening entries (#384, #399)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the internal to-do tracker. It marks the last two follow-up hardening items as resolved: one was confirmed already fixed in the code, and the other was closed as not needing a change today. No app behavior changes.

prs.title: feat(client): §68.2 wizard Screen 2 gates Next on AlpacaBridge detection
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The profile setup wizard now checks for the equipment hub (AlpacaBridge) automatically on its connection screen. If the hub isn't found, it shows a clear "not detected" message with the install command and a Retry button, and the user can't move forward until it's found. This means a missing hub is caught right away, instead of showing up later as confusingly empty equipment lists. Users with a non-standard setup can skip the check by entering a custom address. One change the description doesn't mention: the wizard's "Skip — use defaults" button is now also disabled on any screen that has an unresolved problem, not just this one.

prs.title: docs(port-todo): verify + close four stale entries (webview pivot, #390/#425/#349)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the internal to-do tracker. Four entries were checked against the current code and marked done, including the earlier switch to built-in web views and three small reliability fixes. No app behavior changes.

prs.title: feat(client): §25.3 Switch chip busy state — amber while a switch action is in flight
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Switch status indicator in the top bar now turns amber while a switch is being flipped, connected, or disconnected. Before, it stayed green as if nothing was happening. This matches how the other equipment indicators already behave. The amber state also clears correctly if the user changes servers partway through an action.

prs.title: fix: §36 Data Manager delete distinguishes "already gone" from "blocked — retry"
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Deleting a downloaded sky catalog in the Data Manager now tells you when the delete was blocked because files are locked or protected. Before, a blocked delete looked the same as "already removed," so the app acted as if disk space had been freed when the files were still there. Now the user sees a message asking them to close whatever is using the files and try again.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 dumb-cooler support — on/off cooler switch without a TEC set-point
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cameras with a simple on/off cooler, but no way to set a target temperature, now get a cooler on/off switch in the camera settings. Before, these cameras showed no cooler controls at all. The target-temperature field still appears only on cameras that can actually regulate temperature, and cameras that already had full cooler controls look the same as before. It works with older server versions too, which keep the old behaviour.

prs.title: feat(server): §64 Live View debayered colour for OSC cameras
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Live View now shows real colour for one-shot colour cameras. Before, it showed the raw sensor pattern as a grey cross-hatch. Colour only applies when the camera is not binning; binned and mono cameras still show greyscale. Live View and saved-capture previews now share the same colour processing, so the two should always look alike. The colour picture is half the width and height of the raw sensor image.

prs.title: feat: §36.8 Tonight's Sky moon advisory — separation, illumination, moon-up fraction (slice 4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky now shows how the moon affects each suggested target: how far the moon is from it, how bright the moon is tonight, and how much of the target's viewing window has the moon up. A green "Moonless" tag appears when the moon stays down the whole time; otherwise a short readout appears, turning amber when the moon is both close and bright. This is advice only. It does not change how targets are ranked or scored.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 catalog overlay labels — names for the brightest objects in view (Catalogs slice 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The catalog overlays on the sky map (Messier, NGC/IC, and so on) now show object names next to their circle markers when you zoom in past a 45° view. To keep the map readable and fast, only the brightest 60 objects in view are named, and an object in two active catalogs is labelled once. Labels update shortly after you stop panning or zooming.

prs.title: chore: finish the Aladin removal — scrub every remnant of the pre-#611 atlas
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a cleanup that removes the last leftovers of the old Aladin sky viewer, which was replaced by the Stellarium engine earlier. It deletes unused code, a large unshipped Aladin file, and an obsolete setup script. It also fixes the project's licence notices: they wrongly said Aladin was still bundled and never mentioned the Stellarium engine the app actually ships, which is now properly credited. Users should see no change.

prs.title: feat: §59 granular autofocus progress — per-probe job ticks + live client count
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Running autofocus now shows live progress, such as "Autofocusing… (3/9)", instead of a spinner with no information for the whole multi-minute run. Along the way, the server's progress tracking for all background jobs was tightened so a job's count can never go backwards or exceed its total. The PR description only hints at this broader change.

prs.title: Config round-trip tests for every driver + two mountIndex data-loss fixes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where iOptron and SynScan telescope mounts forgot which mount you had selected. A saved choice other than the first one quietly reset to the first mount the next time settings loaded. The PR also adds checks confirming that every supported device's saved settings survive being saved and reloaded. Not mentioned in the description, it also stops the server from crashing when a QHY camera is set up on a machine without working USB, at the cost of the camera's model name only appearing after the first connect.

prs.title: feat(client): §37/NEXTGEN wizard filters feed the planning filter set on Save
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The filters you enter in the setup wizard's filter-wheel step were previously thrown away on Save. They are now saved as your planning filter set, with each filter's type (such as Hα, OIII or red) guessed from its name the same way the Settings screen does. This means a new setup gets filter-aware planning advice right away. Beyond what the description says, the code also merges repeated filter names so they can't make the whole save fail, and uses an entered wavelength to identify filters with generic names like "Filter 1".

prs.title: feat(client): §37/NEXTGEN wizard camera step captures read noise + peak QE
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup wizard's camera step now has two optional fields for read noise and peak efficiency. These are spec-sheet numbers a camera never reports on its own, and they are needed for exposure-length advice, so users no longer have to find them in Settings later. Saving them leaves the details already read from the connected camera untouched. Obviously wrong entries, such as typing 0.8 when you meant 80%, are ignored rather than overwriting good values.

prs.title: feat(client): §59 Run-autofocus button on the Focuser panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Focuser settings panel now has a "Run autofocus" button. It starts an autofocus run, shows "Autofocusing…" while it works, and then displays the result, including the specific reason if it failed. The button is disabled until a focuser is connected. The description calls a vanished job a graceful finish, but the code treats it as the server possibly restarting and tells the user to check the focuser position. The code also rides out brief connection hiccups and only gives up after about 30 seconds of lost contact.

prs.title: feat(server): §59 POST /equipment/focuser/autofocus — on-demand sweep as a background job
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the server side of on-demand autofocus: the app can now ask the server to run an autofocus pass in the background and check on its progress. A failed run reports why it failed. A second request made while one is already running joins the existing run instead of starting a competing one. The client button came in a separate PR.

prs.title: feat(server): §59.8 live autofocus V-curve sweep — RunAutofocus + flip re-focus execute for real
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Autofocus now actually works on the server. It steps the focuser through a range of positions, measures how sharp the stars are at each one, works out the best focus point, and moves there. If anything goes wrong, it restores the starting position according to your settings. Imported plans' autofocus steps and "autofocus every N exposures" now run for real, and a failed autofocus stops the step rather than continuing out of focus. Re-focusing after a meridian flip also runs now, but a failure there only gets logged so it never ends the night's imaging. It has not yet been tested on a real focuser.

prs.title: feat(server): §59 capture-for-analysis seam — probe frames without persistence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for automatic focusing. The camera can now take quick test shots that are measured and then thrown away, instead of being saved as images in the user's library. These test shots wait their turn behind any other camera use, and they stop with a clear error if something goes wrong, so a bad reading can't silently spoil the focus result. The code also checks exposure and binning values more strictly than the description mentions, rejecting invalid or out-of-range settings. Nothing changes for users yet; the actual autofocus routine comes in a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 CenterAndRotate executes its centre half through the §28 loop
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: "Center and Rotate" steps in imported NINA sequences now actually center the telescope on the target. Before, these steps always failed. The app takes a picture, works out where the telescope is pointing, and corrects until it is on target. If centering can't get close enough, the step fails rather than letting the rest of the night's images come out off-target. Rotation is not supported yet: if a rotator is connected the step still stops with an error, and without one the rotation angle is skipped, which matches how NINA behaves.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 Catalogs overlays persist across sessions (epic slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The catalog overlays you turn on in the planetarium, such as Messier objects or galaxies, are now remembered and redrawn the next time you open the app. Turning an overlay off is remembered too. The description says the app side needed no code changes, but the code also changes how these settings are saved. New settings are now combined with the saved ones instead of replacing them, and rapid saves no longer overwrite each other. Both changes come with new tests.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 Catalogs panel — daemon catalog overlays on the planetarium (slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The planetarium has a new Catalogs button that lets you overlay well-known sky objects on the view. You can show catalogs such as Messier, Caldwell, NGC and IC, or filter by type, such as galaxies, star clusters, nebulae and supernova remnants. Each catalog is drawn as small outlines in its own consistent color, brightest objects first. If the deep-sky data package isn't installed, the panel says so and points you to the Data Manager. Object names and saving your choices between sessions were left for later updates, and it has not yet been tested on a real device.

prs.title: chore(client): prune the dead Aladin-era catalog overlay provider
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that removes leftover code from the old sky viewer that nothing was using anymore, along with its test. A planned deletion of the server-side catalog feature was found to be out of date and was not carried out, since Tonight's Sky and the new Catalogs panel depend on it. The planning notes were updated so nobody deletes it by mistake later. No change for users.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 re-surface sequencer Pause/Resume now the daemon pause is real
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequencer toolbar has its Pause button back, and the Run button now changes to Resume while a run is paused. This completes the earlier server-side work that made pausing actually work. A pause takes effect after the current step (such as an exposure) finishes, and the screen shows "Paused" only once the run has really stopped. Tests were updated to cover the paused state.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 real sequencer Pause/Resume — instruction-boundary pause gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Pause and Resume now actually work for running imaging sequences on the server. Before, they did nothing. When you pause, the current step, such as an exposure or a telescope move, finishes first. The run then holds and only reports "Paused" once it has really stopped. Resume picks up where it left off, and checks like a meridian flip are re-checked fresh after a long pause. Abort and Stop still always win over a pause. One limit: steps set to run side by side only pause before they start, not partway through. The app's Pause/Resume buttons come in a separate follow-up.

prs.title: feat(release): generate 3rd-party-licenses.txt + ship license docs in the .deb (§15/§17.2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The project now builds its list of third-party software licenses automatically from the server's actual dependencies (98 packages), instead of keeping it by hand. That list, the main license and the attribution notice now ship inside the server's Linux install package. An automated check fails the build if a dependency changes and the list isn't regenerated, and the packaging script re-runs the same check. The code also makes two changes the description doesn't mention: the install package now requires the system's FITS image library to be installed, and the notice now lists the ASCOM equipment libraries as MIT-licensed.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 sky-data catalogs download from the org's own snapshot repo
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The optional star and deep-sky catalogs that users can download for the sky atlas now come from the organization's own copy of the files. Before, they came from outside projects, one of which is already archived. This protects downloads from breaking if those outside projects disappear. The files are byte-for-byte identical to before, so users see no difference, and the credit notice was updated to match.

prs.title: feat(licensing): WILMA client goes AGPL-3.0-or-later; server stays MPL-2.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop and mobile client app is now licensed under the AGPL. The server and everything else stay under the existing MPL license. The goal is to stop hardware vendors from taking the app, adding their own closed changes, and not sharing them, even if they only serve the app from a device instead of shipping it. This is a licensing and documentation change only: it adds the new license file and updates the readme, notice and changelog. No code changed.

prs.title: docs(client): AGPL §13 satisfied — engine disclosure points at the public open-astro fork
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only change. The notes for the built-in planetarium engine now point to the organization's public copy of its modified source code, marked at the exact version the app uses, plus simpler steps to rebuild it. This meets a license requirement that had to be done before release.

prs.title: Deterministic poll-until-settled decision logic (util::ConsecutiveSettle) + scripted tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The logic that decides when a device has settled after moving is now a shared, tested building block, starting with the ToupTek filter wheel's homing step. The waiting logic is where bugs like settling too early or missing a timeout tend to hide. The filter wheel's behavior is unchanged, and new tests cover tricky cases like a brief bounce while the wheel slows down. The code also makes an unmentioned build change: a library the build needs is now stored inside the repository, because it was removed from its download sites and had been breaking the automated builds.

prs.title: ci: client-build job — compile all three desktop Runners in release mode
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated checks now fully build the desktop app for Mac, Linux and Windows on every pull request, not just test it. An earlier change produced a Mac app that wouldn't build, and nothing caught it until someone tried it on a real machine. This PR also removes an outdated setting, refreshes two version-lock files, updates the to-do notes, and adds a 30-minute time limit to the existing test job (the description doesn't mention the time limit). The new build checks are not yet required to pass before merging.

prs.title: Fault-injectable ToupTek SDK seam + hardware-free driver tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The ToupTek camera, focuser, filter wheel and heater/fan drivers can now be tested with a simulated device instead of real hardware. Five new tests re-create past bugs, such as leftover connections after a failed connect and a filter wheel wrongly deciding it had stopped, so those problems get caught automatically in future. The PR says nothing changes for users, but the code also includes one small unmentioned tweak to the order of steps when the camera hands back an image.

prs.title: scan-build evaluation: advisory RUN_SCAN_BUILD pre-flight knob + dead-store fixes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Developers can now optionally run an extra code-checking tool on their own machines. It only reports possible problems and never blocks a change, and it is not added to the automated checks because it didn't find the kinds of bugs the team was worried about. The PR also removes some unused leftover code the tool flagged. The team says this changes nothing for users.

prs.title: Consolidate Switch get_device_state() into the SwitchDriver base (7 overrides removed)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Seven device drivers, including power and heater switches from several brands, each had their own code for reporting their current on/off state. They now share one version, which works the same way as when an app asks for each value directly. Reported values stay the same but now include a timestamp, and a disconnected switch reports only the timestamp. Not mentioned in the description: the code also locks this shared reporting in place for other device types, and makes the automated build try backup download sites when a required library's usual site is down.

prs.title: feat: §58.9 unattended flip safety — Layer 3 verification gate + Layer 4 safe rest
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This finishes the safety system for automatic overnight meridian flips. With safety on, the telescope must confirm by photographing the sky that it is pointing within 2 degrees of its target, with up to three tries. If it can't, imaging stops instead of continuing to shoot a mis-aimed sky. On any flip failure the mount now parks (or stops tracking if it can't park), guiding stays off, the camera cooler keeps running, and the user gets an alert saying what state the equipment was left in.

prs.title: feat: §58.9 unattended flip safety — Layer 1 pre-flip flight check + Layer 2 in-slew watchdog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the first two safety layers for automatic overnight meridian flips. Before a flip starts, the app checks that the target will be above the horizon limit, that the mount is healthy, and that the needed equipment is connected, trying one reconnect if needed. If a check fails, the flip doesn't start and an alert is sent. During the flip, a watchdog stops the mount if it stalls, loses connection, takes far too long, or ends up on the wrong side. Users get a new on/off switch for this safety system (on by default) and a setting for how long their mount's flip normally takes.

prs.title: AGENTS.md structural cleanup: de-duplicate vendor notes, reorder for driver-authoring flow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Reorganized the internal guide for developers who write device drivers. Rules that were repeated in each camera, filter wheel and power-port vendor section are now stated once in shared sections, and a written policy for choosing version numbers was added. The same change raises the project's version file from 2.2.0 to 3.0.0 to match the changelog, which had already declared the next release a breaking one. No program behavior changed.

prs.title: Add ToupTek AFW-M filter wheel + ATR2600M cooled-camera support
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ToupTek's AFW-M filter wheel and the ATR2600M cooled camera. For the camera, users can now pick its sensitivity modes, adjust the black level, and control its dew heater, fan and tail light, and a hang when shooting at 3×3 binning is fixed. All three devices passed the standard compatibility checker with no errors, and this change marks the 2.2.0 release. The code also includes safety fixes the description doesn't mention in the Player One, ZWO, QHY and SVBONY drivers and the ToupTek focuser, which prevent crashes when a device disconnects mid-operation, plus a long new section of coding rules in the developer guide.
