prs.title: docs(planning): NEXTGEN exposure-intelligence epic — slices 1–4 shipped
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updates the planning notes to mark the four-part exposure-planning project as finished and shipped. It also lists what is still deferred for later, such as runtime exposure adjustment and a built-in sensor database.

prs.title: feat(client): per-filter Optimal Sub advisor in the sequence editor (NEXTGEN §5 slice 4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor now shows an "Optimal Sub" suggestion under each exposure step. It works out which filter is in use at that point and recommends an exposure length, warns when the numbers are based on generic defaults, and credits Dr. Robin Glover as agreed. One click writes the suggested time into the normal exposure field and changes nothing else, so sequences stay compatible with NINA. This completes the four-part exposure-planning project, and it is app-only with no server changes.

prs.title: feat: Tonight's Sky filter/emission-aware advice (NEXTGEN §1 slice 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky now suggests a filter approach for each target: narrowband, dual-band or broadband. The suggestion depends on what kind of light the object gives off, which filters the user owns, and how light-polluted the site is, and it comes with a short explanation. It also shows a suggested exposure length once the camera and telescope details are filled in. The advice is informational only, target rankings are unchanged, and no suggestion is shown when the object type or filter set is unknown.

prs.title: feat: exposure-planning profile setup + GET /api/v1/planning/optimal-sub (NEXTGEN §4 slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the setup the exposure calculator needs. Telescope settings gain an aperture field, and there are new Settings panels for camera electronics and for the user's filter list. Camera details are filled in automatically when a camera connects, and the filter list can be pre-filled from the filter wheel's labels. A new server service calculates a recommended exposure length and says which values were guessed. These new camera and filter details are removed when a profile is shared with someone else.

prs.title: feat(server): Optimal-Sub calculator — Glover read-noise floor + saturation ceiling (NEXTGEN §2/§3 slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the behind-the-scenes math for a new "optimal sub-exposure" helper that will recommend how long each photo should be. It looks at the camera, telescope, sky darkness and filter to find the shortest exposure where camera noise stops mattering, and caps it where the sky background would start to overexpose the image. The method was popularised by Dr. Robin Glover, the author of SharpCap, and is used with his permission. Nothing is visible to users yet; the code matches the description, and a later change will connect it to the app.

prs.title: build: bump the pub group across 1 directory with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine update of four third-party libraries used by the desktop and mobile app, covering networking, app-version info, file locations and the embedded web view used by the planetarium. The networking library update brings several bug fixes from its maintainers, including fixes for requests that could hang. There are no intended changes to how the app itself behaves.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group across 1 directory with 5 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal update to the automated build and review tools, moving five of them to newer versions. This includes the .NET setup, build caching, the Docker image builder and the Claude review bot. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: fix(server): pin Microsoft.OpenApi 2.7.5 over vulnerable transitive 2.0.0 (GHSA-v5pm-xwqc-g5wc)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a security warning that was stopping every build of the server. A library pulled in indirectly had a known high-severity flaw that could make the server hang on certain malformed data, so the project now requires the patched version directly. A note in the code says to remove this once the upstream package includes the fix.

prs.title: ci: bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.154 to 1.0.160 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal update that moves the Claude code-review bot used on AlpacaBridge pull requests to a newer version. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: docs(planning): record Dr. Robin Glover's permission + full sub-exposure bounds
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updates a planning document to record that Dr. Robin Glover, the author of SharpCap, gave permission to use his exposure-length method and endorsed the project's open-source approach. It credits him as the person who popularised the method rather than its inventor, and asks that he be credited in the app wherever the feature appears. The document also expands the planned exposure advice to cover other practical limits, such as overexposed stars, satellite trails and having enough stars to align images. This is a documentation change only, with no code.

prs.title: docs(planning): bookmark next-gen exposure intelligence + sequencer strategy
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only; nothing was built and nothing changes for users. It records ideas for a future version of the planner: recommending filters based on the target and how dark your sky is, suggesting the best length for each photo based on your camera, and possibly moving to the app's own sequence format. It also records the decision to finish the cross-platform release first and to hold back a recent framing improvement until its settings are confirmed.

prs.title: Resolve WandererCover follow-ups #93-#96 (firmware/SDK UI, serial)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The AlpacaBridge web page now shows each connected device's firmware version and, separately, the version of the maker's software it relies on. This information is kept out of what astronomy apps like NINA see. The PR also makes communication with several mounts and focusers more reliable, and Windows users now get a clearer message explaining that automatic device detection isn't supported there, rather than one suggesting their hardware is missing. The updated developer notes also describe a fix for the server hanging when a device is reconnected, which the description doesn't mention; that code wasn't visible in the trimmed diff.

prs.title: Rename Debian package openastro-phd2 → openastro-guider
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The installable Linux package for the headless guider is renamed from "openastro-phd2" to "openastro-guider" to match the project name. The program, background service, and data folder are renamed along with it. Existing installs under either old name should move to the new package automatically on upgrade. The author noted that a full package build on the target Raspberry Pi-class hardware still needed to be run.

prs.title: Fix openastroara-server Recommends to real package names
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the Ara server's install package, which recommended two companion packages under names that don't exist. It now points to the real equipment-bridge package and to the guider's new name. Installing the server should now pull in those companions as intended. The server itself is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(server): Tonight's Sky per-request optics + mosaic overrides (§36.8 slice 4a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server behind Tonight's Sky can now answer "what's worth shooting if I used a different lens, added a reducer, or shot a mosaic?" without the user editing their saved equipment profile. Any settings you don't change fall back to your profile, and mosaics are limited to 20 tiles per side. When no changes are requested, results are the same as before. The on-screen controls to use this are still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): Tonight's Sky slice 3b — dock the panel beside the planetarium + recentre
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky is now visible in the app. A button on the Planning tab opens the ranked target list beside the sky view, which shrinks to make room instead of being covered, and tapping the button again closes it. Each target now has a button that moves the sky view to that object. Checks on real macOS, Windows, and Linux machines were still listed as pending.

prs.title: feat(client): equipment-aware Tonight's Sky — slice 3 (planner panel)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Tonight's Sky list in the app now shows the new planning information for each target. Each target gets a colour-coded 0–100 score, a label saying whether it fits your camera's view ("Fills frame", "Small" or "Too big"), and a short line showing tonight's dark window, hours available and hours left. A "Why?" button explains each score, and low-scoring targets still appear lower in the list. The description says a button to centre the sky view on a target is included, but the changelog added in this same change says that is coming in a later update.

prs.title: feat(planning): equipment-aware Tonight's Sky — slice 2 (worth score + window gate)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now ranks Tonight's Sky targets by a 0–100 "worth shooting tonight" score based on your telescope and camera. The score weighs how well the object fits your camera's view, how many dark hours it has, how high it gets, and how bright it is against your sky. Short reasons come with each score so users can see why a target ranked where it did. The list now includes targets that haven't risen yet but will be up in darkness tonight, and shows how much dark time is left for each.

prs.title: feat(planning): equipment-aware Tonight's Sky — slice 1 (OpenNGC catalog + visibility windows)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tonight's Sky now draws from the full installed deep-sky catalog instead of a fixed list of 20 objects. For each target it works out tonight's viewing window (above the horizon and dark enough), when it is highest in the sky, and how many hours of imaging that allows. If the sky catalog isn't installed, it falls back to the old starter list, so the list is never empty. Ranking is still by current height in the sky; smarter scoring comes in the next update.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 planetarium — drop CEF for native webview on all 3 desktops + framing/Display polish
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The planetarium in the Planning tab now runs on each computer's built-in web browser engine on Mac, Windows and Linux, instead of a bundled copy of Chrome that froze on Mac and broke the whole app on Linux. This also makes the app much smaller to build. Framing got fixes: large multi-panel layouts no longer skew or lock up, the target's sky coordinates are shown live, a centre marker was added, and the sky stops moving while you frame. The row of layer buttons became a tidy "Display" menu whose settings are remembered between launches. One change not mentioned in the description: the old "Catalogs" menu for showing Messier/NGC/IC markers was removed.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 embed Stellarium Web Engine planetarium (offline foundation)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning tab's sky map was replaced with a full interactive planetarium (Stellarium) that works offline. It shows a realistic sky with horizon, planets and constellation art, lets you click any star to identify it, and can point the telescope mount at an object, refusing if the object is below the horizon. The same change also bundles several unrelated fixes: the live connection to the server no longer keeps dropping, equipment no longer shows a false "connected" status when the server is gone, and the connect screen now keeps scanning for servers and has a Rescan button.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 draw the local horizon on the Planning sky atlas
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning sky map now draws your local horizon line, plus a marker for straight overhead and North/East/South/West labels, so you can see at a glance what's above the horizon from your location right now. The line updates each time you open Planning. The description notes it had not yet been checked on a real device at merge time, and this map was replaced soon after by the new planetarium in #610.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 Planning horizon endpoint (RA/Dec horizon overlay for Aladin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now work out where the local horizon sits on the star map for a given time and place, so the planning screen's sky atlas can later draw a line showing what is above or below the horizon. It also returns the point straight overhead and the north, east, south and west markers. This is only the back-end piece; the on-screen overlay and time control come in later changes, and for now the horizon is treated as a flat minimum height rather than following real terrain like trees or buildings.

prs.title: fix(mount): stop a held direction button when it disables mid-hold (#605 follow-up)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Safety fix for the new telescope direction pad: if you were holding a direction button and the mount got busy with something else, such as a sequence step or a GoTo, the button greyed out but the telescope kept moving until you let go. Now the movement stops as soon as the button is disabled. This follows up on an issue flagged in review of the earlier mount-control change, and a test was added to cover it.

prs.title: feat(mount): Park fix + Home + manual control (GoTo, direction pad, speed)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Mount panel is now usable end to end. Park was silently doing nothing and now works, including on mounts like iOptron that need tracking switched on first. The panel also gains a Home button and a manual control section with GoTo to coordinates, a press-and-hold direction pad and a speed picker. Several safeguards make sure a stop command always gets through so the telescope cannot be left moving, and it was tested on a real iOptron mount.

prs.title: feat(client): equipment panel cleanup — dev hints, focuser AF pointer, filter wheel slot numbers/offset/labels
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tidies up the equipment settings screens. Internal reference labels that had leaked into what users see were removed, and the Focuser's non-working autofocus rows were replaced with a link to the real autofocus settings. The Filter Wheel now shows each slot's number, hides the focus offset readout when every slot is zero, and hides the local slot-name editor while a wheel is connected, since the wheel's own names are used then.

prs.title: fix(client): show Reconnect after disconnect — card treats disconnected status like absent
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where, after you disconnected a device, the app showed no Reconnect button and still looked as if the device were connected. The shared connection box now treats a disconnected device the same as having no device, so Reconnect and Connect appear right away on all nine equipment panels. Only the display changed; nothing changed on the server side.

prs.title: fix(client): FLAT chip turns green on connect — flat panel uses the shared connection card
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the FLAT indicator in the top bar staying grey after you connected and switched on a flat panel. The Flat Panel settings screen was using an older connection method that the indicator never heard from, so it now uses the same shared connection box as the other device screens. The screen also shows live cover and light status and gets the standard Reconnect button. It additionally stops tracking one local-only reference document in the repository, which the description mentions.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §52.1 auto + manual reconnect for all devices; live FLAT chip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Switches now reconnect automatically when the rig restarts, like the camera, mount and other gear already did. Setups with several switches are also remembered correctly now. Every device panel gains a one-tap Reconnect button, so a dropped device can be brought back without searching for it again, and the FLAT status light in the top bar now shows the light panel's real status instead of always showing disconnected. The code also reports a separate error when every remembered device fails to reconnect, which the description doesn't mention, and the on-rig testing step is still unchecked.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group across 1 directory with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is an internal update to the automated build tooling: it bumps three GitHub Actions (checkout, caching, and the Claude review bot) to newer versions. There is no change for users. Several notes in the build settings still say the old "v4.x" version even though they now point to v7.

prs.title: fix(client): §36 complete CEF 149 multi-process switch — repair the broken macOS native build
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes the Mac desktop app, which could not be built at all after the previous Sky Atlas update. That update switched to a newer browser engine but left the old engine version in place. This PR brings in the correct engine version and adds all five background helper programs the engine needs on Mac. The automated checks never try to build the Mac app, which is why the break went unnoticed; adding that check is left for a later change.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 Sky Atlas on CEF 149 — software-WebGL OSR + lifecycle fixes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas in the Planning tab now shows the star map on Mac instead of a blank or black screen, and the app closes cleanly without crashing. Tabs are now kept open in the background once visited, so the atlas keeps its position when you switch away and back. The Mac app now requires macOS 12 (Monterey) or newer, and Apple's app sandbox is turned off for it. The description says it bumps the embedded browser engine, but that change isn't in the diff, and the missing engine update is what broke the Mac build until #600 fixed it.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 Skip button on the sequencer toolbar
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequencer toolbar has a new Skip button between Run and Abort. It lets you drop the current target, for example one that has sunk below the horizon, and move on to the next item without stopping the whole night's plan. The button is available whenever Abort is, including while paused, and is greyed out once an abort is already in progress.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 skip-current-target endpoint + deserialize parent-chain wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now has a skip-current command that cancels whatever a running sequence is doing and moves on to the next item. It also fixes a hidden problem where loaded or imported sequences lost track of how their steps fit together. Without that fix, skip would have silently done nothing and other features that rely on tracking the running step could fail. The on-screen Skip button came separately in #597.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 catalog entries for RunAutofocus / CenterAndRotate / AutofocusAfterExposures
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sequences brought in from NINA that contain autofocus steps, center-and-rotate steps, or an "autofocus every N exposures" rule now show up in the sequence editor with proper names and icons, instead of generic placeholder rows. The center-and-rotate step's target position and rotation angle can be edited, as can how often the autofocus rule fires. With this, every commonly used NINA step from real user files now imports and displays correctly. A small test adjustment was also needed because the growing list of steps no longer fit on the test screen.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 import RunAutofocus / CenterAndRotate / AutofocusAfterExposures
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Importing a NINA sequence no longer throws away its autofocus steps, center-and-rotate steps, or "autofocus every N exposures" rules. These appear hundreds of times in real user plans, and they are now kept intact, including the target position and rotation angle. The app cannot actually run the autofocus or center-and-rotate steps yet; for now, running one stops with a clear error rather than quietly skipping it, which would silently ruin the images that follow.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 catalog entries for DSO / SmartExposure / DitherAfterExposures
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imported NINA plans now look right in the sequence editor. Target blocks, NINA's "Smart Exposure" imaging blocks, and "dither every N exposures" rules now show with real names and icons instead of blank generic rows. Target blocks are labelled with the object's name (for example "T Cas") unless the user has given the block its own name, so an imported plan reads target by target. The dither interval can also be edited.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 normalize imported NINA $type names to canonical OpenAstroAra form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sequences imported from NINA were saved using NINA's own internal names for each step, which the editor didn't recognize, so they showed up as rows of unlabeled placeholders. Import now translates those names into the app's own names, so imported plans look the same as ones built in the editor. Steps the app doesn't support yet are left untouched with all their settings kept, and are listed in the import warnings. The original uploaded file is still saved unchanged as a backup copy.

prs.title: Add WandererAstro WandererCover V4 CoverCalibrator driver (release 2.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for the WandererAstro WandererCover V4, a motorized dust cover with a built-in light panel for flat frames. It is the first device of this kind the bridge supports, and it can be picked in the web setup page. It passed the official ASCOM compatibility checker on real hardware with no problems. The device has no true stop command, so a "stop" request only stops the software from reporting the cover as moving while the cover finishes its travel on its own. Released as version 2.1.0.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 import NINA SmartExposure / DeepSkyObjectContainer / DitherAfterExposures
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Importing real NINA imaging plans used to lose most of their content, because the three most common building blocks weren't recognized: per-target blocks, "Smart Exposure" imaging blocks, and "dither every N exposures" rules. A 228-target file came in almost empty. These are now fully supported, so each target keeps its name, sky position and framing angle, each imaging block keeps its filter, exposure count and dither setting, and the plan can be exported back to NINA unchanged. This is server-side only; making them display nicely in the editor came in later changes.

prs.title: fix(client): §36 run macOS CEF/Aladin multi-process — stop the fontations SIGSEGV crash
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a crash that could shut down the whole Mac app when the Planning sky atlas was drawing. The embedded web browser that shows the atlas now runs its heavy work in a separate helper program, so a font-rendering bug no longer takes the app down with it. The trade-off is that the main app's built-in macOS security protections are loosened, and the app can no longer be distributed through the Mac App Store; the PR explains both. The final check, opening the atlas on a real Mac and confirming it no longer crashes, was still pending when this merged.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal maintenance only: updates two third-party tools used by the project's automated build and review pipelines to newer versions. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: chore(build): remove the dead VVVV.FreeImage dependency — eliminate the NU1701 warnings
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup: removes an old image-processing library that nothing in the app used anymore, which also gets rid of a warning that appeared on every build. The app package gets slightly smaller, and the third-party license list is updated to match. Any similar outdated library added in the future will now stop the build instead of only producing a warning.

prs.title: fix(server): §26 InvariantGlobalization in all configs — fix clean Debug build on 10.0.3xx SDKs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a problem where developers on newer versions of the .NET tools could not build the server in its development mode, even though the official release build worked. The server now uses the same language- and region-neutral settings for dates and numbers in every build type, so development builds behave exactly like the shipped version. Users see no change.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 draw installed star/DSO catalogs as markers on the Planning atlas
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning sky atlas now shows the star and deep-sky object catalogs that users have downloaded, drawn as markers over the background sky images. Installing a catalog adds its markers and deleting it removes them, with no refresh needed. To keep the view readable, stars are limited to the brighter ones (roughly 9,000, a bit more than the description suggests) and deep-sky objects are capped at 5,000. The on-screen appearance has not yet been checked on a real device.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 serve an installed catalog as JSON for the Sky Atlas overlay
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the server-side piece that lets the app read a downloaded star or deep-sky catalog and send its objects to the sky atlas in one consistent format, even though the two catalogs are stored very differently. Callers can ask for only the brighter objects or a maximum number of objects, which keeps the data small. The code also does two things the description doesn't mention: it rejects nonsensical filter values with an error, and when a brightness filter is used, objects with no recorded brightness (common for deep-sky objects) are left out.

prs.title: fix(server): §36 remove the broken horizon-default download; injectable catalog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes the default horizon download from the Data Manager. It pointed at a website that no longer exists, so every attempt to download it failed. Horizon data will instead be generated on the device when the Tonight's Sky horizon feature is built, so users no longer see a broken download option. The change also lets the automated tests use their own made-up package list instead of the real one.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 Data Manager downloads real HYG + OpenNGC catalogs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Data Manager can now download real sky catalogs. Previously every download failed because the packages pointed at a website that doesn't exist. The two packages are now the HYG named-star database and the OpenNGC deep-sky object catalog, fetched from fixed versions of their original sources, with credit added to the project's notices. Beyond what the description says, the code also checks each download against a known fingerprint and rejects a corrupted or wrong file before it can replace a good install. Showing these catalogs on the sky map is still to come.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 sky-data installer accepts bare CSV / CSV.gz files
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork so the sky-data installer can install a single catalog file, optionally compressed, instead of only bundled archives. It reuses the same safe install steps as before, including rolling back if something fails, a size limit, and a check that blocks unsafe file names. There is no visible change for users yet. The follow-up change that actually downloads the real catalogs relies on this.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 sky-imagery survey picker in the Planning atlas
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning tab's sky map now has a dropdown for choosing which set of sky photographs forms its background. The options are the default full-sky color images, two deeper color surveys that cover only part of the sky, and a full-sky infrared survey. Each option says how much of the sky it covers, so blank areas in the partial surveys don't look like a bug. This is the first step toward making the atlas look as realistic as possible.

prs.title: Fix per-vendor camera/focuser index collision and auto-increment
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes two bugs in AlpacaBridge's web setup page for cameras and focusers from brands other than ZWO. Before, any device number you typed for these brands was silently thrown away and saved as 0. Adding a second device of the same brand also didn't pick the next free number, so it clashed with the first. Both now work for every supported brand, and the developer guides explain how to keep new brands from bringing these bugs back.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 add a Planning target to a new sequence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each object in the Planning tab's Tonight's Sky list now has an "Add to a new sequence" button. It creates a new observing sequence named after the object that points the telescope at it, shows a confirmation, and the new sequence appears in the Sequencer tab. The button is turned off when no server is connected, and it can't create duplicates if tapped twice. The same button on the Framing panel is still disabled and is planned for later.

prs.title: fix(client): §36/§25.5 hydrate optics in Planning so the framing FOV box draws
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When framing a target in the Planning tab, the box showing how much sky your camera and telescope will capture now appears. It was blank before because Planning never loaded the user's camera and telescope settings; only the Settings screen did. Planning now loads them when it opens. The code notes one gap: if you switch profiles while Planning is already open, the box keeps the old size until the tab is reopened.

prs.title: feat(client): §37 wizard "Refresh from connected device" — telescope, camera + filter wheel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup wizard now has "Refresh from connected device" buttons that fill in settings read from the user's connected gear, so they don't have to type them. It pulls focal length and aperture from the telescope mount, pixel size from the camera, and filter names and focus offsets from the filter wheel. When a device isn't connected or doesn't report a value, the wizard shows a clear message. The description calls the filter wheel a later step, but this change already includes it.

prs.title: feat(client): §25.3 wire the top-bar equipment icons live + clickable
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The row of equipment icons at the top of the app is now live. Each icon (camera, filter wheel, focuser, mount, dome and the rest) shows green when connected, amber when busy, blue while connecting and red on error. Clicking an icon opens that device's settings page. Before this, only the guider icon worked; the others were always grey and did nothing when clicked. The flat panel icon still stays grey because it has no live status yet, but it can be clicked.

prs.title: feat(server): §25.5.5/§37 expose telescope focal length + aperture in caps
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now reports a connected telescope mount's focal length and aperture, when the mount provides them. This groundwork lets the setup wizard fill those values in automatically. Many mounts don't report these values, and blank or zero values are treated as missing so the wizard never fills in a useless zero.

prs.title: fix(client): §37 wizard save now refreshes the profile list (new profile appears)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where finishing the setup wizard seemed to save nothing: the new profile was saved but did not show up in the profile list. The list only refreshed when the wizard was opened from the profile management screen. The wizard now refreshes the list itself after a successful save, so the new profile appears no matter where the wizard was opened from.

prs.title: fix(client): §6.4/§37.2 enable Switch discovery in the wizard equipment screen
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now pick a power or accessory switch device during the setup wizard's equipment step. Before, that option was greyed out with an "in progress" note. The wizard sets one switch as the profile's default, and more switches can be added later in Settings.

prs.title: docs: refresh README + client description (WILMA acronym, Alpaca-only, status)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's front page and the app's short description. It now explains that WILMA is shorthand for the five systems the app runs on (Windows, iOS, Linux, macOS, Android) rather than the app's name. It also explains that the server talks to equipment only through a network standard, which is why it can run without a screen on Linux, and that the app finds the server automatically on the local network. The status now says the first version is feature-complete and work on the next one has started; no code changed.

prs.title: feat(client): §70.5 export a sequence to a shareable .araseq.json file
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now export a saved imaging sequence to a file and share it with someone else, who can load it on their own setup. The sequence picker gains an Export button on each row that opens a normal save dialog, and you can export several sequences in a row without the window closing. If the server sends back nothing usable, the app shows an error instead of quietly saving an empty file. The save dialog itself has not yet been checked on a real device, although it works the same way as the existing profile export.

prs.title: fix(server): §70.5 sequence share-export — 404 on unknown id, mirror profile-share DTO
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the server side of sequence sharing so it behaves the same way as profile sharing. Before, asking to export a sequence that no longer existed returned an empty placeholder that looked like a success; now it clearly reports that the sequence was not found. It also stops pointing to a download location that was never built, since the shared content is already included directly in the reply. This prepared the ground for the export button added in the app.

prs.title: feat(client): §36.1 bundle Aladin Lite engine for offline use (drop CDS CDN)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas map engine now ships inside the app instead of being downloaded from an outside astronomy server each time it opens. This means an outage or an unannounced update on that server can no longer blank out or change the atlas. The actual sky images are still downloaded from that server, so an internet connection is still needed to see imagery. The required license notices were added, and the atlas still needs a manual check on a real machine to confirm it draws correctly.

prs.title: feat(client): §64 Live View viewer — Imaging-tab loop (LV-2, closes the epic)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Live View switch on the Imaging screen now works: turning it on shows a continuously updating picture from the camera, with a LIVE badge, to help with framing and focusing. Before this, the switch did nothing. Turning it off returns to the last captured image, and if Live View fails to start, the switch turns itself back off and a message explains why. This completes the Live View feature, together with the server work in #569.

prs.title: feat(server): §64 Live View daemon loop — short-exposure render (LV-1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now run a Live View: it takes a stream of short camera exposures and makes the latest one available as a quick preview image for framing and focusing. These preview frames are temporary and are never saved as real image files or added to the image library. A normal photo can still be taken while Live View is running, because the two take turns so they never use the camera at the same time. The on-screen viewer came in the follow-up PR (#570).

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 live Mount panel + /telescope/tracking endpoint — slice 8 (closes equipment epic)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Mount settings panel is now live instead of a placeholder. It shows where the telescope is pointing, whether it is parked or at its home position, and whether it is currently moving. Users can turn tracking on or off, park or unpark the mount, and hit a Stop button to halt a movement in progress. The server gained the missing command for switching tracking on and off. This is the last of the eight single-device equipment panels, which completes that body of work.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 live Camera panel + /camera/cooler endpoint — slice 7
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Camera settings panel now shows live information instead of a placeholder: sensor temperature, how hard the cooler is working, and exposure progress. It also adds a cooler on/off switch with a target temperature, plus a read-only summary of the sensor's specs. The server gained the command needed to control the cooler. This change also quietly fixes a gap from the earlier Rotator update, where the new reverse and sync commands could fail in optimized server builds. A few less important camera details are listed as future work, including showing the cooler's target temperature back to the user.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 live Dome panel + daemon caps-in-DTO — slice 6
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Dome settings panel is now live instead of a placeholder. It shows whether the shutter is open, which direction the dome faces, whether it is parked or at home, and whether it is moving. Users get buttons to open or close the shutter, turn the dome to a direction, and park it. Each button only appears if the dome supports it and is disabled while the dome is moving. The server now tells the app what the dome can do, information it already had but was not sharing.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 live Rotator panel + daemon caps/reverse/sync — slice 5
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Rotator settings panel is now live instead of a placeholder. It shows the rotator's current angle and whether it is moving, and lets users rotate to a chosen angle, reverse its direction if the device supports that, and sync its angle to a known reference. The server gained the reverse and sync commands and now reports what the rotator can do. These two new commands were missing a small registration step, so they could fail in optimized server builds until the next update fixed it.

prs.title: feat(client): §25.5.5 live Filter Wheel panel (slots + select) — slice 4
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Filter Wheel settings panel now shows the connected wheel's real filter names and focus adjustments, and marks which filter is currently in place. Users can select any filter, and selection is disabled while the wheel is turning. The separate list of user-defined filter labels used for planning sequences is kept as its own section. This was an app-only change, since the server already provided this information.

prs.title: feat(client): §25.5.5 live Focuser panel (position/move/temp) — slice 3
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Focuser settings panel is now live instead of a placeholder. It shows the focuser's position, temperature, and temperature-compensation setting, and indicates when it is moving. A new Move control lets users send the focuser to a position, keeps the value within the device's allowed range, and is disabled while it moves. Behind the scenes, this adds a shared way for panels to send device commands, and the app now checks status more often while a device is moving. The later equipment panels build on this.

prs.title: feat: §25.5.5 live Weather panel + shared EquipmentConnectionCard (slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Weather panel in Settings now shows live readings from the connected weather station instead of placeholder text. It covers temperature, humidity, dew point, pressure, cloud cover, wind speed, wind gust, wind direction and rain rate, hides any reading the station doesn't provide, and shows when the data was last updated (in UTC) along with Connect and Disconnect buttons. The server was updated to send dew point and wind gust, which it wasn't reporting before. The Safety Monitor panel was also moved onto a new shared connection layout, so the remaining equipment panels can reuse it instead of each building their own.

prs.title: feat(client): §25.5.5 live Safety Monitor panel + generic equipment-status core
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Safety Monitor panel in Settings now shows the real, connected device instead of a static placeholder. Users can see a clear Safe or Unsafe indicator, the connection status, when the safe/unsafe status last changed, and Connect and Disconnect buttons. The PR also adds shared behind-the-scenes plumbing that the other equipment panels (weather, focuser, camera, mount and others) will use to show live data the same way. As a small side fix, long labels in settings rows now get cut off with an ellipsis instead of spilling out of their column.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §68.1 remove the AlpacaBridge version gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Connecting equipment no longer goes through a version check on the AlpacaBridge. That check never worked: the Alpaca standard has no version handshake, so it always failed and only got in the way. Connections, including automatic reconnects when the server starts, now go straight to the device. The related warning banner in the app and the matching server alert were also removed. A design document that still describes the old check was deliberately left unchanged and flagged for the maintainer to reconcile.

prs.title: fix(client): §6 Switch panel stuck on "Connecting" — poll while connecting
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes the Switch panel getting stuck on "Connecting" after a user added a switch, which looked like a failed connection even though it had actually worked. The server finishes connecting a moment later in the background, but the panel only checked once and never looked again. The panel now rechecks every 1.5 seconds while any switch is still connecting, so each card updates to its real status on its own.

prs.title: feat(client): §6 Switch settings panel — connect + control multiple switches (PR2b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new Switch page under Settings → Equipment, where users can connect several power or relay boxes at once and control them. Each connected switch appears as a card with its status and its outputs: on/off outputs get a toggle, adjustable outputs get a slider, and read-only outputs just show their value. An "Add switch" button finds and connects another box without disconnecting the existing ones. Errors appear as a short pop-up message and don't clear the list; managing multiple switches from the setup wizard is left for later.

prs.title: feat(client): §6 multi-switch data layer — SwitchApi + models + provider (PR2a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork in the app for talking to multiple switch devices (power and relay boxes): listing them, connecting more, disconnecting one, and setting output values. Switches can also now be found by the app's device search like other equipment types. There is no visible change yet, since the screen for this came in a later update. The description says the switch list refreshes on a regular schedule, but the change itself only refreshes it when asked.

prs.title: fix(client): §6 equipment discovery parsed every device to blanks (snake_case)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixed a bug in the app that made every device found during equipment discovery show up with no name and no real details, so picking one tried to connect to a blank device. It affected all equipment types and was blocking connecting power/relay switch boxes from the app. The app now reads device details in the format the server actually sends, still accepts the older format as a fallback, and a new test locks in the correct behavior.

prs.title: feat(server): §6 connect to multiple Switch devices (multi-instance, PR1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now stay connected to several power/relay switch boxes at once. Before, connecting a second one quietly disconnected the first, so a rig with two boxes could only control one. Each switch is now addressed by its device number, and the server can list all switches, control one specifically, or disconnect one without touching the others. The app screen for multiple switches and letting automated sequences pick a specific switch come in later changes; for now sequences keep using the lowest-numbered switch, and two switches with the same number on different machines will clash, with the later one winning and a warning logged.

prs.title: fix: daemon-log download + mDNS discovery + equipment auto-connect on boot (redo of #552, with per-device connect timeout)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Re-applies the bundle of fixes that was pulled back earlier: downloading the server's log file works again instead of failing, the in-app log viewer lets you select and copy text, the Mac app can save downloaded files again, the app's "scan for servers" can now find the server automatically on the local network, and equipment set to auto-connect reconnects by itself after the server restarts. New this time, each device's automatic reconnect gives up after 30 seconds, so one unresponsive device can no longer hold up the rest at startup. This adds one outside library, used for the network announcement.

prs.title: Revert "daemon-log download + mDNS + equipment auto-connect on boot (#552)"
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Undid the previous bundle of log-download, server-discovery and auto-reconnect fixes, because it was merged before an outstanding review concern was resolved. That concern was that a hung device could stall startup. The work was redone and merged again separately with that concern addressed.

prs.title: fix: daemon-log download + server mDNS discovery + equipment auto-connect on boot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A bundle of fixes from chasing why the camera stopped taking pictures. Downloading the server's log file no longer fails, the in-app log viewer lets you select and copy text, and the Mac app can save downloaded files again. The server now announces itself on the local network so the app's "scan for servers" finds it, and equipment set to auto-connect reconnects by itself after a server restart. This change was later reverted and re-merged with an added per-device timeout.

prs.title: fix(client): §38 remove the inoperative sequencer Pause control
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removed the Pause button, and its matching Resume option, from the sequence runner's toolbar. The server can't actually pause a running sequence yet, so clicking it did nothing while giving the impression the run had paused. Run and Abort work as before, and Pause can be brought back once the server supports real pausing.

prs.title: feat(server): §70 friendlier names for imported profiles
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imported profile templates now get a more useful name based on the telescope's focal length, such as "Imported — 1626 mm rig", instead of always being called "Imported profile". If that name is already taken, a number like " (2)" is added so repeated imports stay distinct. The name the user sees in the preview is the exact name used when the profile is created. The description suggests the name is checked again for duplicates at creation time, but the code reuses the preview name without re-checking, so two imports at the same moment could still end up with the same name.

prs.title: feat(client): §37 wizard per-screen validity gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup wizard now greys out the Next and Save Profile buttons while a field on the current screen shows a red error, such as an out-of-range value. Hovering over the disabled button explains that the highlighted field needs fixing. Back and Skip still work, so users are never stuck. Invalid values were already never saved, so this mainly stops the wizard from looking like it accepted bad input.

prs.title: feat(client): §54 bug-report bundle action (prepare + PII disclosure + download)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Support tab gains a "Send me a bug report" option in the app. Before anything is downloaded, it shows a clear warning that the report contains logs, the full profile (which may include passwords, tokens and precise location), and system details, along with the file's approximate size. The report is saved only if the user explicitly confirms. This completes the privacy disclosure that the server now requires before it will hand over a bug report.

prs.title: feat(client): §54 Support tab — daemon log viewer + download
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app gets a new Support tab that shows the server's recent log messages. Users can filter by severity or search text, refresh the list, and save the full log file to their computer. It shows a "connect to a server" message when no server is connected, and it reloads automatically when the user switches servers. The code shows a manual refresh button rather than a continuously updating feed, even though the description calls it a live view.

prs.title: feat(server): §54 real bug-report bundle (ZIP prepare + download)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: "Send me a bug report" on the server now produces a real downloadable file containing recent logs, the active profile, and basic system information, replacing a stand-in that produced nothing. The code also does several things the description doesn't mention. It refuses the download unless the request explicitly acknowledges that the file contains personal data. It keeps only the newest 10 reports and limits each report to the 3 newest log files. It also cleans up half-finished report files when the server starts.

prs.title: feat(server): §29.9 real daemon logs (Serilog CLEF sink + LogService)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now keeps its own log files on disk, rotating daily or at 50 MB and keeping the last 14. Users can view recent entries with severity and text filters, or download a whole log file, instead of seeing sample data. The "rotate logs" action only writes a marker line in the log; it does not start a new file immediately. The server also now makes sure its final log lines are saved even if it crashes.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 TimeCondition "Until a time" (clock time or sky-event provider)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor gains a new "Until a time" loop condition, so a block of steps can keep running until a set clock time or a sky event such as sunset, sunrise, civil, nautical or astronomical dusk and dawn, or when the target crosses the meridian. When a sky event is chosen, you can also shift it by a number of minutes, for example 15 minutes before sunset. The hour, minute and second boxes only accept valid values. Beyond what the description says, the editor also greys out whichever settings don't apply: the clock-time boxes when a sky event is picked, and the minutes shift when a custom time is picked.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 altitude conditions (Until altitude / Until above horizon)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor gains two new loop conditions: "Until altitude" and "Until above horizon." These let a block of steps repeat until a target in the sky drops below, or rises above, a chosen height. Each has a small editor for the target's sky position, the height threshold, and whether to wait for "less than" or "greater than." Defaults match what the observatory software expects (30° and falling for altitude, 0° and rising for the horizon), and the position editor is now shared with the existing slew step.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 SwitchFilter filter picker (over configured slot labels)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "Switch Filter" step in the sequence editor now has a working dropdown to choose a filter, replacing a placeholder. The dropdown lists the filter names set up in Settings → Filter Wheel. If a sequence imported from another setup refers to a filter not in that list, it still shows up instead of disappearing. If no filters have been named, the editor asks the user to set them up. For now the names come from the app's own settings rather than the connected filter wheel; that change is planned for later.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer positional drag (drop between rows to reorder/insert)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Drag-and-drop in the sequence editor is now more precise: you can drop a step into the thin gap above any row to place it exactly there. This lets you reorder steps within a group or insert them at a specific spot, not just drop them onto a group. The code also adds a gap below the last item of each group so you can drop a step at the end of that group, which the description doesn't mention. A highlight line shows where the item will land, and the existing move up/down buttons still work.

prs.title: feat: §38 sequence Validate (server dry-run endpoint + toolbar button)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Validate button in the sequencer toolbar, which was previously disabled, now works. It sends the sequence being edited to the server to be checked, without saving anything. It then shows either a green "Sequence is valid" message or the first problem found, so mistakes can be caught before saving or running. The server-side piece is a thin wrapper around the existing checker and has no dedicated test of its own.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 numeric field bounds (clamped entry) for sequence fields
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Number fields in the sequence editor can now enforce allowed ranges, so values outside the range snap back automatically. This is applied to the loop conditions: in "For a duration," minutes and seconds stay between 0 and 59 and hours can't go negative, and a loop count can't go below 1. This stops users from entering values the observatory software would reject.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 ReconnectTrigger (Reconnect Device) in the trigger catalog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor has a new "Reconnect Device" trigger. It automatically reconnects a piece of equipment that drops out partway through a run. Users choose the device from a dropdown (camera, filter wheel, focuser, mount, dome and others), and it defaults to the camera. It uses the existing trigger editing screen, so nothing else in the interface changed.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer drag-and-drop reparent (tree drop-into-container)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now rearrange a sequence by dragging. Press and hold a step, then drop it onto a group to move it inside that group, including nesting one group inside another. Invalid drops are refused, such as dropping onto a single step or into a group's own contents, and a highlight shows only on valid drop spots. Reordering steps within the same group still uses the existing up and down buttons.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer move/reparent engine (drag-and-drop core)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes logic for moving a step or group of steps to a different place in a sequence. It prevents impossible moves, like putting a group inside itself, and marks the sequence as having unsaved changes. There is no visible change yet; it is groundwork for the drag-and-drop editing that arrived in a later update.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer triggers UI (field-panel Triggers editor)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a group of steps is selected in the sequence editor, a new "Triggers" section now appears below its loop settings. Users can add, edit and remove automatic actions there, starting with the meridian flip. Changes are included when the sequence is saved. This completes the main structure needed to build sequences the same way as in NINA, the astronomy software many users are coming from.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer triggers engine + controller methods
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes logic for adding, removing and editing triggers (automatic actions such as a meridian flip) on a group of steps. It follows the same pattern already used for loop settings. There is no visible change yet; it supports the Triggers editor that came in a follow-up update.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 surface NINA "Import" as a first-class toolbar button
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequencer toolbar now has an "Import" button next to New and Load, so users can browse to a sequence file exported from NINA and bring it in with one click. The import feature already existed but was hidden inside the Load window, and users reported they could not find it. Beyond what the description says, the button is also greyed out while another toolbar action is running, and other toolbar actions pause while an import is in progress.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer trigger catalog (data model)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This lays the groundwork for triggers, which are automatic actions a group of steps can run partway through a sequence. It starts with the meridian flip, which turns the telescope over as a target crosses the sky. It is behind-the-scenes groundwork only: nothing is visible in the editor yet, and the reconnect trigger is postponed. The code also adds an unmentioned safety check to the existing step and loop-condition lists that stops a setting from accidentally overwriting a built-in value.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer loop conditions UI (field-panel Conditions editor)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now make a group of steps in the sequence editor repeat, either a set number of times or for a set length of time. When a group is selected, a new Conditions section lets users add these rules, adjust them, and remove them. Changes are saved like any other edit. Time-of-day and altitude-based rules are still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer conditions engine + controller methods
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes logic for adding, editing, and removing repeat rules on a group of steps in the sequence editor, and marks the sequence as having unsaved changes when this happens. There is no visible change yet; the editor screen for it followed in a later update. The description says every action refuses to run on a single step, but the code only enforces this when adding. Editing and removing just check that the target exists and simply do nothing when there is no rule to change.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer loop-condition catalog (data model)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This defines the two kinds of repeat rules a group of steps can use: 'repeat N times' (default 2) and 'run for a duration' (default 1 minute). It is groundwork only, with no visible change in the editor yet, and more complex rules such as time-of-day and altitude are postponed. The description says the code blocks non-simple default values, but it actually copies them safely instead, which achieves the same protection.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer container rename (field-panel Name editor)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now rename a group of steps in the sequence editor. Selecting a group shows a Name box, and the new name appears in the sequence outline as they type. The change counts as an unsaved edit until saved. Individual steps are unaffected because they do not have names.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer containers (Sequential/Parallel) in the editor palette
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor's list of building blocks now includes 'Sequential' and 'Parallel' groups, so users can nest steps inside groups to build structured observing plans. New groups are saved in exactly the format the observatory software expects, so sequences stay compatible with NINA. The outline now shows a group's own name instead of a generic label. Renaming groups and adding repeat rules and triggers were left for later updates.

prs.title: refactor(client): §38 remove the superseded read-only sequence display tree
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cleanup only: removes the old view-only sequence display from the app, about 880 lines of code and its test. The new editable sequence editor replaced it in the Sequencer tab, so nothing used the old version anymore. Users will see no change.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor coordinates (RA/Dec) field editor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now edit the sky position for a "Slew to RA/Dec" step directly in the sequence editor. Right ascension is entered as hours, minutes and seconds, and declination as degrees, minutes and seconds with a plus/minus toggle. Values outside the valid range snap to the nearest allowed value, and the box updates to show the corrected number. The code also does one thing the description leaves out: at the pole (90°), declination minutes and seconds are set to zero and their boxes are greyed out. Filter selection is now the last setting that still has no editor.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor binning (X × Y) field editor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor now lets users set the binning for a "Take Exposure" step with two number boxes (X × Y). Before, this setting only showed a placeholder. Entering 0 is automatically corrected to 1, the lowest valid value. Coordinates and filter still showed placeholders at this point.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor reorder — move up/down on the selected row
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now move a step up or down within its group in the sequence editor, using arrow buttons next to the delete button on the selected row. The buttons are greyed out when a step is already first or last, and the step stays selected as it moves. Moving a step marks the sequence as having unsaved changes. This completes the basic editing actions: add, edit, delete and reorder. Drag-and-drop reordering is planned next.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor delete node (CRUD complete)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now delete a step from a sequence: selecting a step in the editor shows a delete button that removes it. The top-level sequence itself can't be deleted this way. The removal is saved when the user clicks Save.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 wire Save — PATCH the edited body (editor phase 3a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Save button in the sequence editor now works; before, it was always disabled. It turns on only when there are unsaved changes and sends the edited sequence to the server, then shows a "Sequence saved" message. If the server rejects the sequence as invalid, the user sees the server's reason. Other failures show a connection error and keep the changes so the user can try again. The code also handles a case the description doesn't mention: edits made while a save is still in progress stay marked as unsaved instead of being lost.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 wire the sequence editor into the Sequencer tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer tab now shows the new sequence editor: a list of instructions to add on one side, the sequence's steps in the middle, and a settings panel for the selected step on the other. Picking a sequence loads its real contents, so users can add instructions and change their settings, replacing the old view-only display. Saving, checking, reordering, and deleting steps are not wired up yet. The instruction list was also reshaped into full-width rows so it fits the narrower side panel.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor field panel (editor phase 2e)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a settings panel for the step selected in the sequence editor, so users can change things like exposure time, gain, tracking rate, or wait duration using text boxes, on/off switches, and dropdowns. Changes go straight into the actual sequence so they will be kept when saving. More complex settings such as binning, sky coordinates, and filter choice only show a placeholder for now. The panel was not yet visible in the app when this merged; the code also tightens a couple of internal consistency checks and moves some shared labeling logic.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor instruction palette + tap-to-add (editor phase 2c)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the instruction list for the sequence editor, grouped by equipment type (camera, filter wheel, focuser, telescope, guider, utility). Tapping an instruction adds it to the sequence at a sensible spot based on what is selected: at the end, inside a selected group, or right after a selected step. The new step is then selected. Dragging to a specific spot comes later, and the list was not yet shown in the app when this merged.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor tree view (editor phase 2b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the middle panel of the new sequence editor, which shows a sequence's steps as an indented list that users can click to select. Steps are labeled with friendly names and icons, and unfamiliar steps (for example, ones imported from NINA) still get a readable name. It only displays and selects for now; moving steps comes later, and it was not yet shown in the app when this merged.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor working-state controller (editor phase 2a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for the sequence editor: it keeps track of the sequence being edited, which step is selected, and whether there are unsaved changes. Edits are applied to the original sequence data rather than a simplified copy, so saving should keep everything exactly as it was apart from the user's changes. There is nothing new on screen yet.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor instruction catalog (editor phase 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the list of instructions users will be able to add in the upcoming sequence editor: taking exposures, cooling or warming the camera, switching filters, moving the focuser, slewing, tracking, parking, guiding, dithering, waiting, and notes. Each one is built to match exactly what the server expects, so added steps will run correctly. Autofocus and centering are left out on purpose because the server does not support them yet. There is no visible change on screen yet.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequence-editor DOM mutation engine (editor phase 0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Lays the hidden groundwork for an upcoming drag-and-drop sequence editor. It adds the behind-the-scenes logic for adding, removing, reordering and editing steps directly on the original saved sequence, rather than on the simplified version shown on screen. This keeps edits from losing anything. Nothing changes for users yet; the editor screens and Save come in later steps. The team noted one open question to check before Save is wired up: whether the server accepts a slightly reshaped step list in a rare case.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.4 Export a sequence back to a NINA .json file
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer toolbar now has an Export button that saves the selected sequence as a file that opens directly in NINA, the imaging program many users are moving from. The file is an exact copy of the stored sequence with ARA's own internal marker removed, so nothing is lost when moving a sequence back to NINA. Cancelling the save does nothing, and errors show a short message.

prs.title: fix(deps): patch CVE-2025-6965 — pin SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 3.50.3
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a known security flaw (CVE-2025-6965, rated fairly serious) in the built-in database engine the server uses, by switching to a patched version. The change does not affect how the app stores data. It also unblocks every other pull request, because the automated security check had been failing all builds.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.5 keep raw sequence body + update API (save-a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork so sequences can be saved and exported without losing any detail. The app now keeps the complete original copy of a sequence as the server stores it, and it can send changes such as a new name, description or content back to the server. There is no visible change yet; the Save and Export buttons are built on this in follow-up work.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.7 New-sequence dialog (create from template) + wire New (new-b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer's New button now works. Once connected, it opens a list of ready-made starting templates. You pick one, name your sequence, and it is created and opened right away. The name fills in from the template unless you have already typed one, and the button guards against creating the same sequence twice. Editing and saving the new sequence are still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.6/§38.7 sequencer template API + model + provider (new-a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for the Sequencer's New button. The app can now ask the server for its list of starting templates and create a new sequence from one of them. There is no visible change on its own; the picker screen that uses this arrived in a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(client): §38/§28.12 live sequence run-state via sequence.* WS
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer screen now follows a running sequence live, so its status line (for example "Running — 18/60 frames") and its Run/Pause/Abort buttons update as the run progresses. Before, they only refreshed after you pressed a control. Updates meant for other sequences are ignored, and details like the target name and start time are kept rather than blanked by each update. The code also changes something the description doesn't mention: if a background refresh of the run status fails, the last known status stays on screen and the error is only logged, instead of being shown as a failure.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.4 import a NINA sequence file from the Sequencer (slice import-b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer's Load window now has an "Import NINA…" button. You pick a sequence file exported from NINA (another astronomy imaging program), it is uploaded, and it opens straight into the editor. If parts of the file couldn't be carried over, a dialog lists what was dropped so you can review it before running. Cancelling does nothing, and a bad or unreadable file shows a clear message instead of being uploaded; the code also rejects files over 32 MB, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: Headless connect fix, web app polish from live ASI290 testing, faster .deb builds
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This PR came out of testing with a real camera. Its biggest fix: the guider's web page showed no camera image when opened from another computer, because large images were silently cut off in transit; they are now delivered in full. The web app also gains a version label, a Shut down button with a confirmation, a progress bar and exposure range choices for building dark calibration frames (previously it quietly captured all 22 exposure lengths), a live view that is much closer to real time, and a fix so discovered servers show correctly instead of "undefined". Behind the scenes, the headless guider no longer tries to open pop-up windows when connecting remotely, package builds are much faster (about 70 seconds down to 19 on a repeat build), and the Debian changelog is now generated automatically from the main changelog. The code also fixes a live-view glitch that could briefly show an older frame, which the description doesn't list.

prs.title: feat(client): §38.4 SequenceApi.importNina + import-result model (slice import-a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes piece the app needs to send a NINA sequence file to the server and read back what was imported, including any warnings about parts that couldn't be translated. There is no visible change yet; the import button arrived in a follow-up PR.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 load selected sequence body into the editor tree (slice 3c-b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Picking a sequence in the Sequencer's Load window now shows the actual saved sequence in the editor tree (areas, targets, and steps) instead of a demo placeholder. The description says a failed load is only logged and leaves the current view unchanged. The code goes further: it also shows an error message and clears the selection, so you can simply pick the same sequence again to retry.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 NINA sequence-body → editor tree parser (slice 3c-a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds groundwork for reading sequence files saved in NINA's format and turning them into the step-by-step tree the Sequencer editor displays. It has been tested against a real, complex NINA sequence. Nothing changes for users yet; showing the result on screen came in a follow-up PR.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 wire Sequencer Run/Pause/Resume/Abort controls (slice 3b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer's Run, Pause, Resume, and Abort buttons now work for the sequence you've picked. Only the buttons that make sense are enabled: for example, Run turns into Resume when paused, and Pause only works while running. The status line shows progress such as "Running — 12/60 frames", and a failed command shows an error message instead of failing silently. Not mentioned in the description, the change also briefly locks the buttons while a command is being sent, so a double-click can't send two commands at once.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 SequenceApi.getRunState + run-state model (slice 3a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork that lets the app ask the server what a sequence is currently doing: its run status, current target, and how many frames are done. There is no visible change yet; the next change uses this for the run buttons and status line. If the server reports a status the app doesn't recognize, the app treats it as unknown rather than assuming the sequence is idle, so it won't wrongly offer to start one that is already running.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 wire Sequencer Load to the saved-sequence picker (slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer's Load button now works once you're connected to a server. It opens a list of your saved sequences, newest first, showing each one's size and a colored badge if it is running or paused, and lets you pick one. Picking a sequence only selects it; its contents don't appear in the editor yet, and Save, Validate, and the run buttons stayed disabled in this change. Not mentioned in the description, the selection also clears automatically when you switch or disconnect servers, so it can't accidentally act on the wrong server.

prs.title: feat(client): §38 sequencer client API — list + lifecycle (slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Behind-the-scenes groundwork for making the Sequencer tab real. It lets the app fetch the server's list of saved sequences and send start, pause, resume, abort, and stop commands, with no visible change yet. For now only the first page of saved sequences (up to 50) is fetched. Longer lists are cut off with only an internal log note until paging is added.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.7 wizard screen 18 (review + Save) — wizard complete
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The last step of the setup wizard is now a real review page, which makes the whole 18-step wizard complete. It shows a read-only summary of everything entered, grouped by section, each with an Edit button that jumps back to that screen. Anything left blank reads "Not set" so it's clear the default will be used, and skipped screens are flagged. Saving still uses the existing Save Profile button.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.6 wizard screen 17 (sky data) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The setup wizard's sky-data step is now a real screen. It lists star catalogs and target lists that aren't installed yet, with their sizes, and lets you tick which ones to download (with Select all and Clear). The chosen packages start downloading in the background only after the profile saves successfully, and a download problem never causes the save to fail. The originally planned pre-ticked "recommended" set isn't possible yet because the server doesn't provide that information, so you pick packages yourself.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.5 wizard screen 16 (site & altitude) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 16 of the new-profile setup wizard, covering site and altitude, is now a working form. It lets users set the lowest altitude a target must reach before it is imaged (0 to 90 degrees, with an error message for anything outside that range) and how dark the sky must be before imaging starts: civil, nautical or astronomical twilight. Both choices are saved into the profile's site settings, and blank fields keep the existing defaults. A separate early-warning altitude and a cap on how long a sequence can run were planned but postponed, because the server has nowhere to store them yet.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.5 wizard screen 15 (safety) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 15 of the setup wizard, covering safety, is now a working form. Users choose what happens when conditions turn unsafe (pause and park, park only, abort and park, or ignore), whether imaging restarts automatically once it is safe again, and how many minutes to wait first. These choices are saved into the profile's safety settings. One detail not in the description: choosing "Ignore" hides and clears the auto-restart options. Separate rules for clouds, wind and rain, and the alarm sound and vibration options, were postponed and remain in the main Safety settings.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.4 wizard screen 14 (imaging defaults) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 14 of the setup wizard, covering imaging defaults, is now a working form. It sets the default exposure length in seconds (must be greater than zero) and the default frame type: light, dark, flat or bias. These are saved alongside the camera settings collected earlier in the wizard. Duplicate gain and offset fields were removed from this step because the camera step already handles them.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.4 wizard screen 13 (file saving) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 13 of the setup wizard, covering file saving, is now a working form. Users can set where captured images are saved, the file format (FITS or XISF), whether files are compressed without quality loss, and how files are named. These are saved into the profile's storage settings, and blank fields keep the existing defaults. The wizard offers only on or off for compression; the other compression option and the disk-space limits are still set in the main Storage settings.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.4 wizard screen 12 (autofocus) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 12 of the setup wizard, covering autofocus, is now a working form. It collects the exposure used for each focus sample, the number of focus points to test, how far the focuser moves between points, and whether to refocus after a filter change.
