These are saved into the profile's autofocus settings. Invalid numbers show an error and are not saved. The number of focus points is limited to between 3 and 31, which is slightly stricter than the "greater than zero" rule the description mentions.

prs.title: feat(client): §37.4 wizard screen 11 (plate solving) — real form
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Step 11 of the setup wizard, covering plate solving, is now a working form and the first of the remaining placeholder steps to be finished. Users can point the app at the ASTAP plate-solving program and its star database, and set the search radius and image downsampling. These are saved into the profile's plate-solving settings, and blank fields keep the existing defaults. This PR also added the ability for wizard text fields to show inline error messages, which the later wizard steps reuse.

prs.title: feat(client): §70 profile-share export UI (Profiles → Export…)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each saved profile on the Profiles screen now has an Export option that saves a shareable copy of the profile to a file you choose. The copy has personal and machine-specific details removed, such as folder locations, passwords and tokens, your observing location, and network settings. Someone else can then use the Import option to start from it, so sharing now works entirely inside the app. The code only shows Export on Mac, Windows and Linux, which the description does not mention, and the full export-then-import test had not been done by hand at merge time.

prs.title: feat(client): §70 profile-share import UI (Profiles → Import)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Profiles screen now has an Import button for loading a profile file someone has shared. Before anything is created, it shows a preview: the new profile's name, notes about the template, and the things you will need to fill in yourself, such as equipment, folder locations, observing site, guiding setup and notification tokens. Confirming creates a new profile that is not switched on until you choose it, and files that are too large or not valid are refused with a clear message. Testing a real exported file by hand was still pending when this merged.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group in /client/openastroara_client with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of two building blocks the desktop app depends on: the file-picker component and the component that reads the app's version information. Both are major version jumps. The file-picker update is a pre-release (beta) version, which carries somewhat more risk than a stable release.

prs.title: ci: Bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.142 to 1.0.151 in the github-actions group across 1 directory
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal update to the automated code-review tool that runs on pull requests, moving it to a newer version with bug fixes. It has no effect on the product itself.

prs.title: feat(server): §70 profile-share import — preview + commit (D-2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now accept shared profile files. Before, this feature only replied "not available yet." A shared file is first checked and previewed, showing what will be created and what the recipient must re-enter. Confirming within 15 minutes then creates a new profile that is not switched on until the user chooses it. The code also limits how many unconfirmed previews can pile up, which the description does not mention. For now, every imported profile is named "Imported profile" and has to be renamed by hand, which is noted as a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(client): §37/§30 profile management UI — list/select/rename/delete (epic PR C)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app gets a new Profiles screen that lists all saved equipment profiles and marks which one is currently in use. From there users can switch to another profile, rename or delete one, or add a new one through the setup wizard. Deleting the profile in use, or the only remaining one, is blocked, and the reason is shown on screen. This finishes the user-facing part of the multiple-profiles work.

prs.title: feat(client): §37 wizard Save → create a profile (epic PR B)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Finishing the setup wizard, or choosing Save & Exit partway through, now creates a new active profile. It stores the name, site location, telescope and camera basics, camera imaging defaults, and guider settings the user entered. A spinner shows while saving. If saving fails, the wizard stays open with everything still filled in and shows the error. Beyond what the description says, the code also makes a retry after a partial failure reuse the profile it already created instead of making a duplicate. Equipment device assignments and the later wizard screens are not saved yet.

prs.title: feat(server): §70 profile-share export — real profile-share-v1 template (epic PR D)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now export a profile as a shareable template for another person to use as a starting point for their own setup. The export removes anything personal or machine-specific: file paths, notification passwords and tokens, the owner's location, and guider network details. It keeps the owner's tuning choices, and it describes the telescope and camera the template was built for rather than applying them. The description says importing a shared profile keeps its placeholder behavior, but the code actually makes both import steps return a clear "not available yet" error.

prs.title: fix(server): audit hardening — guider build cancellation (#384) + preview size cap (#349)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Two small server fixes from a recent quality audit. Long-running guider calibration jobs now get a proper stop signal when the server shuts down, so they are no longer left running with nothing tracking them. Full-size image previews are now capped at 2048 pixels on their longest side, so very large camera frames no longer produce huge preview files. The original image files are not affected.

prs.title: fix(client): audit hardening — WS teardown + dropped-snapshot logging (#390/#425/#399)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Three small app-side cleanups from the same audit. Errors that happen while closing a live server connection are now logged instead of silently ignored. The backup list now logs when it skips damaged entries. A confusingly named setting in the guider calibration dialog was renamed. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: fix(server): §37 multi-profile review follow-ups (PR #479)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Follow-up fixes to the earlier multiple-profiles server work. Reading a single profile no longer holds up other profile operations while it reads from disk. On startup, the server now ignores stray or mismatched files in the profiles folder instead of partly loading them. A debug-only safety check and clearer internal documentation were also added, along with tests for the stray-file handling.

prs.title: refactor(client): clear discovery-sheet height helper (PR #478 follow-up)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup only. A confusing calculation that sets the height of the device list in the wizard's equipment discovery sheet was rewritten more clearly. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: feat(server): §37/§30 file-based multi-profile store + CRUD
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now store several named equipment profiles instead of just one, and you can list, create, rename, delete, and switch between them. On first start, the existing single profile is automatically carried over as a profile called "Default", so nobody loses their settings. The server refuses to delete the profile currently in use or the last one left. This is the behind-the-scenes groundwork only; the app screens for managing profiles will come in later changes.

prs.title: feat(client): §37 wizard gear screens — real forms for stages 1-3 (screens 1-10)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The first ten screens of the new-profile setup wizard are now working forms instead of placeholders. Users can enter their profile name and location, test the connection to their equipment bridge, scan for and assign devices, and fill in details for the telescope, camera, filter wheel, focuser, mount, rotator, and guider. The telescope and camera screens work out key numbers such as focal ratio and image scale as you type. The last eight screens are still placeholders, and the wizard does not yet save the finished profile.

prs.title: Fix Configure tab retaining a previous device's settings (Release 2.0.2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug in the AlpacaBridge web page where opening the Configure tab to add a new device could still show an earlier device's settings. Submitting that form could remove and re-add the wrong device. The form now starts clean each time the tab is opened, but still keeps its contents when you choose to edit an existing device. This change also publishes version 2.0.2.

prs.title: Keep docs/architecture.md vendor table current via /commit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation and tooling only, with no change to how the software works. The architecture guide's list of supported equipment brands and device types had fallen out of date and has been corrected, for example to add Player One filter wheels and several power-switch devices. The automated commit helper will now keep that list updated as new drivers are added.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 vendor webview_cef CEF 130 + SwiftPM fork as submodule (macOS Aladin renders)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The built-in sky atlas in the Planning tab now displays on Mac computers; before, it appeared as a black rectangle. The embedded web-browser component was upgraded to a newer version, and it now lives inside the project as a linked copy, which also removes a build warning on Mac. Mac developers need to run a one-time setup step after checkout, and Windows still uses the older browser version for now. The description confirms this was tested on a Mac but does not confirm that the automated checks passed on all systems.

prs.title: ci: bump anthropics/claude-code-action from 1.0.141 to 1.0.149 in the github-actions group
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Internal maintenance: the automated code-review tool used in this repository was updated to a newer version. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: docs: reconcile §36/§47/§25.5/§61 prose with the shipped Planning tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update so the project's design notes match what actually shipped. The old separate "Sky Atlas" and "Framing Assistant" screens are now described as the single Planning tab. The notes also record what is still unfinished: turning a mosaic into a runnable imaging plan, and the full planetarium-style extras for Tonight's Sky (horizon, planets, time slider).

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 Tonight's Sky list in the Planning tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning tab's Tonight's Sky mode now shows a ranked side list of well-placed deep-sky objects. Each entry shows its type, brightness, current height above the horizon, and highest possible height. Tapping an entry moves the sky map to that object, and a refresh button re-ranks the list for the current time. This finishes the Tonight's Sky feature end to end, though the description's note about bad numbers becoming zero is slightly off: in the code, entries with bad position or height data are dropped, and a bad brightness value is simply left blank.

prs.title: feat(server): §36/§25.5 Tonight's Sky ranking endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now rank a built-in list of about 20 popular deep-sky objects by how high each one is above the user's local horizon right now, highest first. It uses the site location saved in the profile and does its own sky-position math with no outside data. It also politely rejects a malformed time or a requested count below one. This supplies the data behind the new Tonight's Sky list; a larger, smarter catalog is planned later.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 "Refresh from connected camera" on the Optics panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Optics settings screen now has a "Refresh from connected camera" button that fills in and saves the camera's sensor size and pixel size in one click. This is handy after swapping cameras. If no camera is connected, or it doesn't report its sensor details, the user gets a clear message instead of bad values being saved. Focal length and reducer settings are never touched.

prs.title: feat(server): §36/§25.5 auto-populate optics from the camera on connect
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a camera connects, the server now automatically saves its sensor size and pixel size into the user's optics settings, so the Planning tab's field-of-view box works without typing those numbers in. It updates them again if a different camera is connected later, and never changes focal length or reducer. Beyond what the description mentions, it also adds a safer way of saving these settings, so an edit the user makes at the same moment isn't accidentally overwritten.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5/§47 Planning Frame mode draws a mosaic panel grid
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Planning tab's Frame mode can now draw a full mosaic on the sky map: a grid of camera-sized rectangles, with the number of columns, rows, and overlap set by the user. The whole grid rotates to the chosen angle and follows the map as you move and zoom, and a 1×1 grid is just the single frame as before. Turning the mosaic into an actual imaging plan is still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 Optics settings panel — enter rig, FOV box appears
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a new Optics settings page where users enter their telescope and camera details: focal length, reducer or barlow, sensor size, and pixel size. As you type, it shows the field of view and image scale the rig will produce. Saving makes the framing rectangle show up on the Planning tab's sky map right away. The settings are also searchable. Confirming that the rectangle actually appears on a real device is still an open checklist item.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 Frame-mode FOV overlay on the Aladin atlas
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Builds the drawing logic that puts a field-of-view rectangle on the Planning tab's sky map when Frame mode is on. The rectangle is sized from the saved telescope and camera details, turned to match the chosen rotation, and follows the view as you pan and zoom. Users won't see anything yet because there was no way to enter those details until a follow-up change.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 optics client data layer + FOV geometry
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds behind-the-scenes groundwork in the app for storing a user's telescope and camera details, loading and saving them with the server, and working out the field of view they produce. If any detail is missing, no field of view is calculated, so the app won't draw a made-up box. There is no visible change yet.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 optics profile section (FOV geometry foundation)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a place on the server to store each profile's telescope and camera details (focal length, reducer or barlow, sensor size, pixel size), plus a way for the app to read and update them. It rejects impossible values, and older saved profiles get sensible defaults instead of breaking. This is storage only; filling these in automatically when a camera first connects is planned for later.

prs.title: feat(client): §36/§25.5 merge Sky Atlas + Framing into one Planning tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Replaces the separate Framing and Sky Atlas tabs with a single Planning tab, so the app now has four main tabs instead of five. The new tab keeps the sky map and target search, and adds a Frame switch that slides in the rotation and mosaic controls. Doing this now avoids running two copies of the built-in browser, which would double memory use. The "Add to Sequence" button stays turned off for now, and a layout glitch on narrow windows was fixed along the way.

prs.title: design(§36/§25.5): merge Sky Atlas + Framing into one "Planning" tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only: records the decision to combine the Sky Atlas and Framing tabs into one Planning tab and updates the planning documents to match. It explains that running both tabs would have meant two memory-heavy copies of the same sky map. It also lays out the plan to remember each user's camera and telescope details so framing works even when the camera is not connected.

prs.title: fix(client): §36 re-pin webview_cef fork — Aladin createWebView null crash
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas tab on Mac now actually shows the sky map instead of a misleading "Sky atlas unavailable / Chromium required" message. The real cause was a small bug in the team's own copy of the third-party web-view component, which crashed when opening the map; this PR points the app at the fixed version. It also makes the Mac setup script reliably pick the right copy of that component after an update, and updates the notes to record that sky images now load correctly on a real machine.

prs.title: build(client): §36 provision macOS CEF for webview_cef (script + Podfile fix)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app can now be built and run on a Mac with the embedded sky map. This PR adds a setup script that downloads and checks the built-in browser engine the map needs and rearranges it into the layout Mac builds expect. It also includes a fix for a build-tool quirk that broke the build because the engine's name contains spaces, and it commits some Mac project setup files that were missing before. Windows still needs a similar step later.

prs.title: feat(server): §55.1 reclaim orphaned client-settings temp files at boot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the server starts up, it now cleans up leftover temporary files from saving app settings that were cut off by a sudden shutdown or crash. The real settings file is never touched, and a warning is logged whenever something is cleaned up. This stops junk files from slowly piling up and matches the cleanup already done for backups.

prs.title: fix(server): §28/§50 parse FITS DATE-OBS as UTC, not local
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes wrong capture times for image files the server finds on disk and adds back into its catalog. The time stored in those files is meant to be in universal time, but it was being read as the computer's local time. That shifted it by the local time-zone difference and could put frames out of order in the statistics views. Photos captured normally during a session were not affected.

prs.title: feat(server): §43-2 reclaim crash-only orphan backup archives at boot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the server starts up, it now removes half-finished backup files left behind if it was shut down abruptly in the middle of making a backup. These files were already hidden from the backup list but kept using disk space forever. Complete backups and unrelated files are left alone, and a warning is logged whenever something is cleaned up so an unexpected shutdown doesn't go unnoticed.

prs.title: feat(client): §43-2b(d) poll clone-status for the real restore outcome
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Backup & Restore screen now waits for a restore to really finish before telling the user it's done. Previously it said "Restore complete" as soon as the server accepted the request, even though the work continues in the background. It now checks back with the server until the restore succeeds or fails, shows the actual error if something goes wrong, and gives up cleanly if the restore takes more than about five minutes.

prs.title: feat(server): §43-2b(a) backup restore on a background worker + live clone-status
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Restoring a backup now runs in the background: the server confirms the request right away and the app can check a live status (idle, running, done, or failed) instead of a status that always said idle. Obvious problems, like a missing or damaged backup, are still reported immediately, and starting a second restore while one is already running is refused. The safety behavior that undoes a restore if anything goes wrong is unchanged. The app does not yet wait for the restore to finish by checking that status; that is planned as later work.

prs.title: docs(port): track captured_utc mixed-format inconsistency (#456 follow-up)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Notes only, with no code change. It adds an entry to the internal to-do list about capture times being saved in two slightly different formats. This causes no known problem today but could matter for sorting or matching later, and the entry is marked low priority.

prs.title: fix(server): §50 normalize stats since-cutoffs to UTC
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Stats features that look at a recent time window (Focus & Temperature, Guiding, and the Calendar's 30-day view) now convert the start time to universal time before filtering. Without this, a start time given in a local time zone could pick the wrong set of frames. No current caller is affected, but it closes off a hidden bug and adds a test for it.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50.19 Achievements onto StatsRefreshMixin (fixes latent stale-error)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Achievements section of the Stats dashboard now uses the same shared refresh logic as the other Stats sections. This fixes a rare glitch where an error could briefly flash on screen if a refresh failed at the exact moment you switched servers. New tests cover this case.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50 unify stats timestamp parsing into parseStatsUtc
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup in the app: the six Stats sections now share one routine for reading dates and times from the server, replacing six separate copies. Four of those copies could have shown times shifted by your local time zone if the server ever sent a time without a zone marker. The server always includes one today, so nothing visibly changes.

prs.title: perf(server): §50 partial light-frame index for stats queries
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Stats pages that list or chart your light frames over time should load faster as your image catalog grows, because the database now keeps a dedicated lookup for those frames. Existing databases pick this up automatically the next time the server starts, and nothing else changes in behavior.

prs.title: docs(port): refresh PORT_PROGRESS to v0.1.0 + §36 fork-maintenance follow-ups
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This updates internal planning notes only. The progress tracker now reflects the current release work: the stats dashboard, focus-versus-temperature tracking, backups, and the Sky Atlas. It also adds a reminder to keep the project's copy of the web browser add-on working after Flutter (the app framework) upgrades, plus a warning comment for developers. The app itself does not change.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 Aladin search-goto + fork webview_cef for Flutter 3.44
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Typing a target name or sky coordinates into the Sky Atlas search bar now moves the sky map to that spot. A search made before the map finishes loading is applied once it is ready, and repeating the same search recenters the map again. The change also fixes a problem that stopped the app from building on newer versions of Flutter (the app framework): the project now uses its own patched copy of the add-on that shows the map. The code also restores your last search when you come back to the Sky Atlas tab, which the description does not mention. Checking on a real Mac is still listed as not done.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 embed Aladin Lite sky atlas via webview_cef
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas tab now shows a real, interactive sky map (Aladin Lite) inside the app, replacing the placeholder, and it works the same way on Mac, Windows, and Linux. If the map cannot start on a computer, the tab shows an 'atlas unavailable' message instead of crashing. For now the map is downloaded from an online source, so it needs an internet connection until offline support is added. Searching the map comes in a later change, and checking it on a real device was still pending at merge.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.4 Focus & Temperature scatter — live /stats/focus-temp
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Focus & Temperature chart on the Stats dashboard now shows real data from the telescope server instead of demo points. It plots each captured image's camera temperature against where the focuser was set, and shows a score for how closely the two move together. This helps with setting up automatic focus adjustment as the temperature changes. It also has loading, error-and-retry, and empty states, plus a refresh button. This was the last of the six Stats charts still using demo data.

prs.title: feat(server): §50.4 implement GetFocusTempAsync (focuser position vs temperature + r²)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The telescope server can now supply real focus-versus-temperature data. It lists every captured image that has a focuser position, and it works out how closely the focus setting follows the temperature. When that cannot be measured, such as when the temperature never changed, it reports nothing instead of giving a misleading number. The tests also check filtering by date, which is one more case than the description lists.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 capture stamps the focuser position (FOCUSPOS + catalog)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a focuser is connected, each captured image now records where the focuser was set. The setting is saved both in the image file and in the app's image catalog, which gives the Focus & Temperature chart real data. If no focuser is connected, or reading it fails, the image is still saved without that detail rather than the capture failing. Based on the code, this applies to single manual captures.

prs.title: feat(server): §38 add focuser_position to the frame catalog (Focus-Temp slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The frame catalog can now store the focuser's position for each captured image. This is the groundwork for a future Focus & Temperature chart showing how focus drifts as the night cools. Existing databases gain the new field automatically at startup, and images recovered from disk now fill it in when their files already carry that information. Normal captures don't record the position yet; that part, the data query, and the chart itself are planned follow-ups, so the chart remains empty for now.

prs.title: Fix GPIO Switch permission under systemd, release 2.0.1
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes power-switch devices failing to connect when AlpacaBridge runs as the installed background service, which affected the iOptron iMate PowerBox, ToupTek StellaVita, and ZWO ASIAIR Pro/Plus. The installer never gave the service permission to use the hardware pins those switches rely on, and it now does. Upgrading restarts the service so the fix takes effect right away. This also publishes version 2.0.1, which bundles some earlier documentation and tooling updates.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50.6 persist-through-refresh for Calendar chart (mixin) — completes the migration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Calendar heatmap on the Stats dashboard now keeps showing its last data while you refresh it, instead of flashing to a loading screen. If a refresh fails, the old heatmap stays up with a small "Stale" tag rather than being replaced by an error screen. This was the last of the six Stats sections to get this treatment, so the whole dashboard now behaves the same way when refreshed.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50.7 persist-through-refresh for Guiding RMS chart (mixin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Guiding RMS chart on the Stats dashboard now keeps its last data on screen during a refresh, and shows a small "Stale" tag if the refresh fails. The "Stale" tag is now a single shared piece reused by the Frame Quality chart. The change also quietly fixes an edge case not called out in the summary: if you switch servers while a refresh is failing, the new server's data no longer gets a misleading "Stale" tag.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50.10 persist-through-refresh for Frame Quality chart (mixin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Frame Quality chart on the Stats dashboard no longer blanks out to a loading screen when you refresh it. Its last histogram stays visible, and if the refresh fails, a small "Stale" tag appears over the chart instead of an error screen. A new test covers the failed-refresh case.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50 persist-through-refresh for Stats Best Frames (shared mixin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Best Frames list on the Stats dashboard now stays on screen while you refresh it, instead of flashing to a loading placeholder. If the refresh fails, the list remains visible with a small "Couldn't refresh — showing the last loaded frames" note instead of switching to an error screen. This matches how the Overview and Targets sections already behave, and new tests cover it.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50 persist-through-refresh for Stats Targets (shared mixin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When you hit refresh on the Targets part of the Stats screen, your list of targets now stays visible instead of briefly disappearing behind a loading message. If the refresh fails, the old list stays up with a small "Couldn't refresh" note, rather than being replaced by an error screen. This uses the same shared behavior introduced for the Overview section. It is the second of several sections to get this treatment.

prs.title: refactor(client): §50 persist-through-refresh for Stats Overview (shared mixin)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Refreshing the Overview totals on the Stats screen no longer blanks the numbers to a loading placeholder. The previous numbers stay visible while it reloads, and if the reload fails a small "Couldn't refresh" note appears instead of a full error screen. The behavior is built as a reusable piece so the other Stats sections can adopt it one at a time. It also safely ignores results that arrive after you've switched to a different server.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.6 wire Calendar heatmap to the live calendar endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Calendar heatmap on the Stats screen now shows real data from the imaging server instead of demo numbers. Each day in the last 49 days is shaded by how many minutes of imaging actually happened that night. It includes loading, error-with-retry, and no-server states plus a refresh button. The last remaining demo chart, Focus & Temperature, is intentionally on hold because the server doesn't record focuser position yet.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.7 wire Guiding RMS chart to the live guiding endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Guiding RMS chart on the Stats screen now shows real guiding accuracy for each captured frame over time, instead of demo data. The subtitle shows the average and a near-worst-case (95th percentile) value, and the chart has dates along the bottom and a refresh button. For now it shows a single combined line, because the server doesn't yet split guiding error into its two directions. It is ready to show that split once the server provides it.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.10 wire Frame Quality chart to the live frame-quality endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Frame Quality chart on the Stats screen now uses real data from the server instead of a demo estimate. It shows how frames are spread across ten quality levels from 0 to 1, where the score combines star sharpness, star count, and background. The average score appears in the subtitle, and the chart includes empty, error, and refresh handling. This is the first of the Stats charts to switch from demo data to live data.

prs.title: feat(client): §50 wire Stats Best Frames to the live best-frames endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Best Frames list on the Stats screen now shows the top frames from the server, ranked by an overall quality score, instead of a demo list ranked only by star sharpness. Each entry shows the target, score, filter, and capture date. The old list's file names, star counts, and star ratings are no longer shown. With this change, all the main Stats sections use live data, though some charts were still on demo data at the time.

prs.title: feat(client): §50 wire Stats Targets to the live targets endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Targets part of the Stats dashboard now shows real data from the connected observatory computer instead of sample numbers. Each target lists how many frames were taken, total imaging time, an average quality score (when available), and when it was last imaged, with the busiest targets first and a refresh button. The old per-target session count and average star-sharpness figure from the sample version are no longer shown. Best Frames is now the only Stats section still using sample data.

prs.title: feat(client): §50 wire Stats Overview to the live overview endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Overview part of the Stats dashboard now shows real totals from the connected observatory computer instead of sample numbers: sessions, frames, light frames, total imaging time, number of targets, and last-imaged date. It handles loading, errors, no server, and an empty catalog, and has a refresh button. The old Nights and average star-sharpness tiles were removed from this section because that information lives elsewhere on the dashboard.

prs.title: Make CHANGELOG versions collapsible (keep deb generation working)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The project's change history file now folds each past release into a collapsible section, so it reads as a short list of versions, while the current in-progress version stays open. The script that builds the Linux package's change history was updated to understand the new layout, so packaging keeps working. The internal instructions for writing commits now describe this convention. Documentation and tooling only; nothing changes for users of the software.

prs.title: feat(client): §55.1 settings-sync client data layer (model + api + provider)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the app-side groundwork for syncing display preferences across a user's devices: the app can now load saved preferences from the observatory computer when it connects and save changes back to it. There is nothing visible to users yet; individual features will start using it later. It includes a safeguard that refuses to save a partial update before the existing preferences have loaded, so other saved settings aren't accidentally wiped.

prs.title: feat(server): §55.1 multi-device WILMA settings sync (server store)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The observatory computer can now store a user's app display preferences, such as layout and theme, so other devices can pick up the same setup when they connect. The newest save always wins. Saves are protected against file corruption, very large or malformed submissions are rejected, and a damaged preferences file falls back to empty instead of breaking the app. This is the server half only; the app does not use it yet.

prs.title: Vendor ASCOM Alpaca API spec and codify versioning policy in skills
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The official ASCOM Alpaca device standard is now saved inside the project, so new device drivers are built against a fixed, known copy of the standard. The internal driver-building instructions now check that copy against the published version each time. The commit and pull-request instructions also spell out a consistent version-numbering policy. Documentation and tooling only; nothing changes in the software itself.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 sky-data conditional updates — skip re-download of an unchanged package
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When you re-download a sky-data package you already have (for example, to check for updates), the app now first asks the download server whether the package has changed since your last install. If nothing has changed, it keeps what you have and reports the download as complete and up to date, instead of pulling down a multi-gigabyte file again. Fresh installs work the same as before. Older installs made before this change will do one full re-download, after which later checks can be skipped.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.19 AstroBin export — target picker + download
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Stats dashboard's Export menu has a new "AstroBin (per target)…" option. It opens a list of the targets you have imaged, busiest first, with frame counts and hours. Picking one downloads that target's AstroBin-ready capture log. It only opens normal web links, which guards against a misbehaving server sending the user somewhere unsafe. The description notes this has not yet been checked by hand against a live system.

prs.title: feat(server): §50.19 AstroBin acquisition CSV export
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now produce an AstroBin-ready spreadsheet for a single target, built from the photos it has already recorded. Photos are grouped into one row per combination of night, filter, exposure length, gain and camera temperature, with a count of shots in each row. Calibration and site details are left blank for users to fill in on AstroBin. The PDF report version was deliberately left for later.

prs.title: feat(client): §50.19 Stats Achievements view — records + milestone badges
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Stats dashboard now has an Achievements section showing your imaging records and milestone badges. Records include night streaks, total nights, your biggest night, total hours, targets and frames. Earned badges are highlighted, and locked ones show a progress bar. This is the first part of the Stats screen that uses real data from the server; the other sections still show demo data. The change also stops long tile labels from overflowing by cutting them off with "…".

prs.title: feat(server): §50.19 stats achievements — milestones + night streaks
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now works out imaging achievements from photos it has already recorded. These include total nights imaged, longest and current streaks of consecutive nights, your biggest single night, total hours, number of targets, and first-light date. It also tracks milestone badges, such as 10, 50 and 100 hours or 10 and 25 targets. Calibration frames are left out, and a current streak resets to zero if you haven't imaged since the day before yesterday. The app screen that displays these arrived in a separate change.

prs.title: feat(client): §43 Backup & Restore screen + Storage launcher
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Settings → Storage now has an "Open Backup & Restore" button that opens a full-screen manager for saved copies of your profile settings and sequences. From there you can create a new backup, download one, or restore one. Restoring first shows a warning and asks which parts to overwrite, and it can't go ahead until at least one part is chosen. This completes the backup feature from start to finish, though restoring from cloud storage and a live progress display are still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §43 backup client data layer (model + api + provider)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Lays the behind-the-scenes groundwork in the app for the upcoming Backup & Restore screen: it can now ask the server for the list of saved backups, create a new backup, restore chosen parts of a backup, and build a link to download one. There is no visible screen yet; that comes in the next change. When the server refuses a request, for example because there is nothing to back up or the file is damaged, the reason is passed along so the future screen can show it to the user.

prs.title: feat(server): §43-2a backup restore — atomic staged-swap from a local snapshot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now actually restore a saved backup, bringing the observing profile settings and/or saved sequences back to how they were in that backup. Before changing anything it checks that the backup file is intact. The swap is all-or-nothing, so a failed restore never leaves settings half old and half new. For now it only restores from backups stored on the same machine, and it finishes in one step with no progress reporting; restoring from cloud copies and live progress are planned for later.

prs.title: feat(server): §43-1 backup — real ZIP snapshots (create + list + download)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Backups on the server are now real: creating a backup packages the profile settings and saved sequences into a zip file stored alongside the profile, and the list shows actual backups, newest first, instead of a fake sample. A new download link lets users fetch a backup file. Backups are written safely so a crash mid-save never leaves a broken file, and asking to back up when there is nothing to save now returns a clear error. Restoring is not available yet; the server openly says so rather than pretending it worked.

prs.title: feat(server): §36-2c sweep stale sky-data scratch dirs on startup (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the server starts, it now cleans up leftover temporary folders that can be left behind if it crashed in the middle of installing a sky-data download. This frees wasted disk space, and installed sky-data packages are never touched. It is a small reliability and housekeeping improvement with no visible change for users.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 functional Data Manager modal — Sky Atlas (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas "Data Manager" window now works for real. It replaces the old placeholder, which showed made-up survey names with buttons that did nothing. It lists the sky-data packages the connected server offers, grouped by type, with each package's size and a total of what is installed. Users can download a package and watch a live progress bar, cancel a download in progress, or remove an installed package, and problems are shown on screen. The embedded sky-image viewer is still to come.

prs.title: feat(client): §36 Data Manager client data layer — model + API + state (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the behind-the-scenes plumbing in the app for the Sky Atlas Data Manager: fetching the list of sky-data packages from the server, starting, cancelling and deleting downloads, and tracking live download progress as the server reports it. There is no visible screen in this change; the Data Manager window was hooked up to this in a follow-up change.

prs.title: feat(server): §36-2b-2 sentinel-aware Data Manager inventory (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Data Manager now counts a sky-data package as installed only if its install actually finished. A download that was interrupted partway no longer shows up as a complete package. The install date now reflects when the install finished rather than the last time any file changed, and the reported size covers only the package's own data. This completes the server side of the Data Manager; the app screen for it comes next.

prs.title: feat(server): §36-2b Data Manager download engine (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Data Manager can now actually download sky-data packages such as star catalogs. Downloads run in the background, report live progress, can be cancelled, and send notifications when they finish or fail, including a distinct warning if an existing install may have been lost. Only one download per package runs at a time, and oversized archives are stopped as a safety measure. Not mentioned in the description: asking to download a package that is already installed now returns a clear 'already installed' response unless a reinstall is forced, and downloads refuse to follow web redirects so they cannot be quietly switched to an insecure connection.

prs.title: feat(server): §36-2a safe + atomic sky-data tar.gz install engine (v0.1.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes machinery that safely unpacks a downloaded sky-data package onto the device. It blocks archives that try to write files outside their own folder, and it only replaces an existing package once the new one has fully unpacked, so a failed or cancelled install leaves the old data untouched. It also leaves a marker showing that an install finished. Nothing uses it yet; the download feature that relies on it arrives in a later change.

prs.title: feat(server): §36 Data Manager real package inventory (v0.1.0, §36-1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Data Manager now shows which sky-data packages are really on the device, with their actual size and install date, instead of a fixed sample list. Users can delete an installed package to free up disk space, and requests are checked so they can never touch files outside the data folder. Download and cancel requests are accepted but do not do anything yet; that work comes in follow-up changes.

prs.title: docs(port): record §68 completion + architectural findings; reconcile queue status
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This updates the planning notes only; no code changed. It records that the AlpacaBridge version check is finished and confirms it sits at the right point, since the connect request is currently the only way to connect equipment. It also notes that the remaining related work and the next tasks need decisions from the team before anyone can build them.

prs.title: feat(client): §68.2 AlpacaBridge "newer recommended" advisory banner
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now shows a dismissible notice on the Equipment settings screens when a device connects through an older AlpacaBridge hub that still works but should be upgraded. The notice reads, for example, 'AlpacaBridge 1.3 detected, 1.5+ recommended'. Dismissing it hides it for that bridge version only, so it reappears if a different version is later reported. The pop-up for a bridge too old to connect at all is still to come.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §68.1 warn-band WS event for a 1.2–1.5 AlpacaBridge (§68-b-3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a device connects through an AlpacaBridge that works but is older than recommended (versions 1.2 to 1.5), the connection now goes ahead as normal and the server also sends a notice so the app can show a dismissible "newer AlpacaBridge recommended" banner. If that notice fails to send, the connection still succeeds. This finishes the server-side part of the bridge version checks; the banner itself and related setup-wizard screens still need to be built in the app.

prs.title: Release 2.0.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge version 2.0.0 is now officially released and dated June 13, 2026. It is a major version because this release cycle drops support for regular PC (Intel/AMD) Linux machines, so it now runs only on ARM-based Linux like the Raspberry Pi, and it brings every device driver up to the latest ASCOM standard. This PR only changes the version number and release notes; it also updates those notes to say all device types have now passed the ASCOM compatibility tests and removes a "pending validation" note from the Player One filter wheel entry.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §68.1 refuse equipment connect through an outdated AlpacaBridge (§68-b-2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: ARA now refuses to connect any piece of equipment (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, and the other six Alpaca device types) through an AlpacaBridge older than version 1.2.0, returning a clear "bridge outdated" error instead. This keeps the software from driving expensive gear through an untrusted, too-old hub. Newer bridges connect normally, and if the bridge's version can't be read the connection still goes ahead. The guider is not affected because it doesn't go through the bridge.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §68.1 AlpacaBridge handshake cache (§68-b-1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a short 30-second memory of each AlpacaBridge's version check, so connecting several devices on the same bridge in quick succession doesn't re-ask the bridge its version every time. If a bridge couldn't be reached, that result is not remembered, so a bridge that comes back online is noticed right away. This is behind-the-scenes groundwork and was not yet switched on when merged; a later PR connects it to device connections.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §68.1 AlpacaBridge version-gate core — classifier + /version probe (§68-a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Lays the groundwork for checking the AlpacaBridge version: new code asks the bridge for its version and sorts it into fine (1.5 or newer), usable but outdated (1.2 to 1.5), too old (below 1.2), or unknown if the version can't be read. It copes with version text in slightly different formats and treats an unreachable bridge as unknown rather than too old. This PR adds the logic and tests only and does not change how ARA behaves yet; later PRs turn it on.

prs.title: test(bench): select the bench suite by [Category("bench")], not a substring filter (bench-6)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal test cleanup with no change to the product. The simulated-observatory test suite is now picked out by a simple label on each test group instead of matching name fragments, which could accidentally include unrelated tests and had to be kept in sync in two places. The same 29 tests still run and pass. It also gives the test container a fixed name so repeated builds stop leaving leftover copies behind, and updates the project's progress notes.

prs.title: test(bench): bench-5 hermetic Linux/arm64 lane for the §42.2 bench
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a one-command way to run the simulated-observatory tests inside a Linux container built for the same kind of processor as the Raspberry Pi, not only on a developer's Mac. The main goal is to keep checking a simulated 'connection suddenly dropped' fault, which can behave differently depending on the operating system. It is not part of any automated build yet, because the hosted build machines use a different processor type. One difference from the description: the list of files to leave out of the container sits at the top level of the project rather than next to the bench setup, so it also trims other container builds.

prs.title: test(bench): bench-4 guider fault scenarios — star-lost + link-drop (§42.2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds two simulated guiding-problem tests that need no hardware. In the first, the guide star is lost mid-session, and the software reports 'star lost' while staying connected. In the second, the guider connection is cut, and the software switches to an error state and starts its recovery process. Test-only change, plus a small helper that lets the fake guider drop its connections on demand.

prs.title: test(bench): bench-3 full guider lifecycle (connect→guiding→RMS→disconnect)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Extends the simulated guider test so it covers the whole session, not just the initial handshake. It connects, sees guiding start, collects guiding-accuracy numbers, and disconnects. This confirms the three recent guider connection fixes work together from start to finish. Test-only change.

prs.title: fix(guider): bound SendMessage's async read by receiveTimeout (§63, bench finding)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where connecting to a guider that is silent or misbehaving could freeze forever, because one of its replies was waited on with no time limit. That wait is now capped, so a bad guider causes a failed step instead of a permanent hang. Each step can still wait up to about a minute before giving up, so connecting to a misbehaving guider can remain slow; this is noted as follow-up work.

prs.title: fix(guider): read-driven event listener — drop the macOS-fragile TCP-table poll (§63)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Changes how the software listens for messages from the guider. It no longer repeatedly checks the computer's network connection list, a method that could crash on Macs and wasted effort. It now simply reads messages as they arrive and treats a closed connection as the signal to start recovery, so disconnects are noticed sooner. The code also does two things the description doesn't mention: it detects a silently dead connection, such as a pulled cable, within about 45 seconds, and it skips garbled messages instead of stopping the listener.

prs.title: feat(guider): connect to the guider as a service, not by launching it (§63.1 + bench-3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The software no longer tries to launch the guiding program itself, which was a leftover from the desktop version. That approach cannot work on a headless Raspberry Pi, and it blocked connecting to a guider running on the same machine. Now it connects to the guider service that is already running, and if the guider isn't up yet, it asks the system to start it and waits briefly. Outside a standard Linux setup, it simply connects to whatever guider is already running. The problem was found by the new simulated guider test, which is also added here.

prs.title: test(bench): scriptable fake PHD2 guider for the virtual-observatory bench (§42.2 bench-2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a pretend version of the telescope guiding program for the team's simulated observatory test setup. Tests can now walk the app through calibrating, guiding, small deliberate pointing shifts between photos, and losing the guide star, all without the real guiding software. This is test-only and ships to no users. The code also makes sure a failing scripted reply comes back as a clear error rather than a dropped connection, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: test(bench): Alpaca fault proxy for the virtual-observatory bench (§42.2 bench-1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Starts a simulated observatory for testing, with no physical hardware needed. The first piece sits between the app's background service and simulated equipment and can make that equipment misbehave on demand. It can return errors, cut the connection, freeze, or report a move that never finishes. This lets the team check how the app recovers from equipment problems. It is test-only and ships to no users.

prs.title: docs(release): complete client dependency license inventory (Phase 15 close-out)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Completes the list of third-party components and their licenses for the upcoming first release by adding five components the app uses but that were missing. The file also now records the exact version and copyright holder for the components that were already listed, and drops one older entry name, which the description doesn't mention. This is a documentation change only, with no change to how the app behaves.

prs.title: feat(client): guider calibration dialog — dark-library/defect-map build + enable UI (slice 3b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now prepare the guide camera's calibration files from inside the app. These are a set of reference dark frames and a map of faulty pixels. When the guider is connected, a new Calibration… button shows whether each file exists and is loaded, and lets users build or rebuild each one and turn it on or off. Previously this was only possible through the service's behind-the-scenes interface. Builds run in the background, and users must tap Refresh to see the result because live progress isn't shown yet.

prs.title: feat(client): guider calibration API + status model + provider (slice 3a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the behind-the-scenes groundwork the app needs to check, build, and switch on or off the guide camera's calibration files (dark frames and a faulty-pixel map). There is nothing visible to users yet; the screen that uses it arrives in a later change. It is designed to cope gracefully with incomplete or odd data from the server.

prs.title: feat(client): live GUIDE chip + connect/disconnect dialog (guider control slice 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The GUIDE button in the app's top bar now works. Its colored dot shows the guider's real state: grey when off, blue when connecting, green when guiding, amber when busy, and red when the star is lost or there's an error. Tapping it opens a window to connect, disconnect, or refresh the guider on the same computer. The code also shows amber while guiding is paused, which the description doesn't mention. It also quietly prevents rapid repeated refreshes, and stops out-of-date status from appearing after switching servers.

prs.title: feat(client): guider control service — GuiderApi + status model + provider (slice 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the behind-the-scenes groundwork for controlling the guider (the device that keeps the telescope tracking a star) from the app. The app can now ask the server whether a guider is set up, connect or disconnect it, and read its current status, such as whether it is guiding and how steady the tracking is. Nothing is visible to users yet; the on-screen controls and the dark-library build screen are planned for later steps.

prs.title: feat(client): §51/§60.9 — route diagnostics.* WS events into the §51 panel (WS slice 5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The health light on the Imaging tab and the diagnostics panel now show live problems reported by the server, replacing the fixed "not connected" placeholder. When the server raises an issue, the light turns amber or red, shows how many issues are open, and adds a short entry to the log. It returns to normal once every issue is cleared. One known gap is noted in the team's to-do list: if the connection drops while an issue is being cleared, the light can stay stuck on amber or red until the user switches servers.

prs.title: feat(server): §51/§60.9 — emit diagnostics.* WS events on raise/clear (WS slice 4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now sends live notices to connected apps whenever it detects a problem, takes an automatic fix, or clears an issue. The low-disk-space warning is one example. A clear that doesn't actually close anything sends no notice. If a notice fails to send, the problem is logged and the diagnostic is still recorded normally. This is the server half of making the app's health panel update in real time.

prs.title: feat(client): live WS connection indicator in the status bar (WS slice 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The status bar at the bottom of the app now shows the real state of the live link to the server: Connecting, Connected, Reconnecting, or Disconnected. Before this change it always said "Disconnected." This lets users see at a glance whether the app is receiving live updates.

prs.title: Show hostname and LAN IPv4 URLs in build_and_run.sh startup banner
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the developer start-up script launches the web interface, it now lists the device's network name and its local network addresses, not just "localhost." This makes it easy to open the interface from another computer when AlpacaBridge runs on a small screenless device. Only the familiar number-style addresses are shown; the longer newer-style ones are left out.

prs.title: feat(client): §60.9 WS event-stream Riverpod providers (slice 2b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal plumbing that connects the app's new live-update channel to the rest of the app. Features can now watch the server's connection status and incoming live events. Nothing changes for users yet; later updates build the visible indicators and panels on top of this.

prs.title: feat(client): §60.9 WS event-stream — connection-state signal (slice 2a)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's live connection to the server can now report whether it is connecting, connected, reconnecting, or disconnected. Before, a quiet connection looked the same as a broken one. It only counts as connected once real data arrives from the server, not just when the connection opens. Nothing on screen uses this yet; a follow-up will add a disconnected indicator to the diagnostics panel and the dark-library build screen.

prs.title: Add Player One thermal switch: dew heater + fan (Uranus-C PRO validated)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cooled Player One cameras now have adjustable dew heater and cooling fan controls, set from 0 to 100%. Astronomy apps like NINA show these as sliders on a new "Thermal Switch" device, and the same controls are also available as camera commands. The settings deliberately reset each session, so a heater left on months ago can't silently turn itself back on. The work was tested on a real Uranus-C PRO camera, confirming for the first time that its cooling holds the target temperature and that the heater really works; both devices passed the standard compatibility checks with no errors.

prs.title: feat(client): §60.9 WS event-stream client — transport slice (Phase 12c.3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now has the groundwork to receive live updates from the server, such as guider calibration progress, health changes, and sequence events. If the connection drops, it reconnects automatically after a growing wait and asks the server to replay anything it missed. Garbled messages are skipped without breaking the connection. Nothing uses this on screen yet, and it doesn't work in the web version for now; hooking it into the app is the next step.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.6 guider-e-4c-c — enable/disable calibration artifacts over REST
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now switch the guider's dark-frame correction and bad-pixel correction on or off without deleting the calibration files. Each toggle takes effect immediately and returns the updated calibration status. It returns a clear error if no guider is connected or if the guider refuses, for example when turning a correction on with no camera attached. The app screen for this is still to come.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.6 guider-e-4c-b-2 — defect-map build over REST + WS events
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now build the guider's bad-pixel map on request. The build runs in the background and sends started, finished, and failed updates over the live event stream. Bad settings are rejected, and so are builds with no guider connected. Only one calibration build can run at a time, so starting a bad-pixel map while a dark library is being built (or the other way round) is turned away. The on-screen build button is still a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.6 guider-e-4c-b-1 — defect-map build on the guider client
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The part of the program that talks to the guider can now ask it to build a bad-pixel map. Settings like frame count, exposure time, and note length are checked first, so mistakes give a clear message instead of an obscure guider error. The same checks are now shared with the existing dark-library build rather than copied. Users can't reach this yet; the server endpoint comes in a follow-up. The description says five new tests were added, but the visible changes show four.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.6 guider-e-4c-a — defect-map RPC request/response classes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds groundwork for building and turning on a guide camera 'bad pixel map', which helps guiding ignore faulty pixels on the sensor. The app can now describe these requests to the guiding software and understand its replies, but nothing uses them yet, so users won't see any change. The button and server wiring come in a later change. The code adds five tests, although an internal planning note says four.

prs.title: refactor(equipment): thread CancellationToken through IDomeFollower.TriggerTelescopeSync (§58)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that lets the 'move the dome to match the telescope' step be cancelled in the three places that use it: meridian flips, centering on a target, and the sequence step. Nothing changes for users today, because real dome control hasn't been brought over yet and the current placeholder ignores the cancel signal. It also corrects two outdated entries in the project's to-do notes.

prs.title: feat(server): §63.6 guider-e-4b-2 — dark-library build over REST + WS events
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now build the guide camera's library of dark calibration frames on request and report whether one exists and is loaded. A build runs in the background and announces when it starts and when it finishes or fails. There's no percentage progress bar, because the guiding software doesn't report progress. Bad settings are rejected up front, as is trying to build with no guider connected. Not mentioned in the description: the code also limits the optional build note to 500 characters, and the status check always answers normally with a connected yes/no flag rather than an error when no guider is connected.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.6 guider-e-4b-1 — dark-library build on the guider client
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Teaches the app's guider connection how to build a guide-camera dark-frame library and read back the calibration-file status, with sensible settings checked before anything is sent. It isn't reachable from the app yet; the server endpoint and the on-screen build flow follow in later changes. The work showed the guiding software gives no progress updates during a build, so the plan changed to showing only 'started' and 'done'. Not stated in the description: the code notes that once a build starts it can't be cancelled and runs until it finishes or hits a two-hour limit.

prs.title: Add Player One Phoenix Wheel filter wheel driver (ConformU validated)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for Player One Phoenix Wheel filter wheels (5, 7 and 8-slot models), tested with the standard compatibility checker with no errors, though only on 64-bit ARM Linux. The web setup page gains a shared slot-count and filter-name picker for filter wheels, plus buttons to download all logs as one archive or delete them all. It also fixes the automated code-quality check for vendor drivers. Not mentioned in the description: the change also makes disconnecting ZWO filter wheels, focusers and rotators more robust, so an unplugged device can't leave the driver stuck half-connected.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.6 guider-e-4a — dark-library RPC request classes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the basic building blocks for talking to the guiding software about dark-frame libraries. These cover building one, switching it on or off, checking its status, and deleting stored calibration files. Nothing uses them yet, so there is no change for users. The actual build flow is planned for follow-up work.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.4 guider-e-3c — collision-free ara-<slug>-<id> profile names
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each profile in the app now always gets its own separate profile in the guiding software, even when two profile names are nearly identical (like "C-14" and "C 14"). Before this, such profiles could end up sharing one guider profile, which meant sharing its calibration and dark library. The fix adds a short unique code to the end of each guider profile name. Side effect not mentioned in the description: guider profiles created under the old naming won't be picked up, so each rig gets a fresh guider profile on its next connect.

prs.title: feat: §29 hard-stop policy — abort the sequence on critically-low disk
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds an optional safety setting that stops a running imaging sequence when the disk becomes critically full, instead of only warning. When it triggers, the team also gets a critical "Sequence halted" alert. The default is still warn-only, and nothing is ever deleted. A "pause" option was deliberately left out because pausing doesn't actually work yet.

prs.title: feat: §29 configurable disk-space thresholds
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now set their own low-disk warning and critical levels in the storage settings, instead of being stuck with the fixed 10 GB and 2 GB defaults. Changes take effect within about a minute. Older saved settings keep working with the defaults. Beyond what the description says, the server now also refuses to save an invalid pair (for example, a critical level that isn't below the warning level) and returns an error, rather than only quietly falling back to the defaults.

prs.title: feat(server): §29 low-disk-space warning monitor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a background check, run every minute, of free space on the drive where images are saved. It raises a yellow warning below about 10 GB and a red one below about 2 GB, plus an inbox alert if the user has that notification turned on. This helps an unattended night session avoid silently failing on a full disk. It only warns and never stops captures or deletes files, and the warning clears itself once space is freed.

prs.title: feat(server): §39 dark matching considers set-point temperature
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app checks whether you already have matching dark calibration frames, it now also requires the camera temperature to match, to the nearest whole degree. Previously, darks shot at the wrong temperature on a cooled camera were wrongly counted as a match. Cameras without cooling are unaffected, and new tests cover these cases.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.4 guider-e-3b — select/create the ara-<slug> guider profile on connect
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the guider connects, the app now automatically switches the guiding software to a profile named after the user's active app profile, creating it the first time. This keeps each rig's guider calibration separate, and makes sure guider settings pushed on connect land in the right place. Users who manually picked a specific guider profile keep that choice, and a failure here never blocks the connection. The code also quietly fixes a check that looked at the wrong reply when loading the guider's list of profiles, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.4 guider-e-3a — profile-name RPC classes + ara-<slug> mapping
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the building blocks for giving each app profile its own matching profile in the PHD2 guiding program, so every telescope setup can keep separate guiding tuning and calibration. It includes a rule that turns a profile name into a simple guider-friendly name (for example "RedCat on HEQ5" becomes "ara-redcat-on-heq5"), plus the commands to select or create that guider profile. Nothing uses this yet, so there is no change for users. Automatically switching or creating the guider profile on connect comes in a later change.

prs.title: feat(equipment): §63.5 guider-push observability + guider-e-2 tracking reconciliation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The step that sends guiding settings to PHD2 when the guider connects now writes a short summary to the log. Before, a successful send left no trace in the log at all. The summary also calls out partial failures, and quieter notes explain when nothing was sent or when the Dec mode was deliberately left alone. The rest is project-tracking paperwork: it marks this guider work as done and records two small follow-ups. Guiding behavior itself is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(client): §63.5 Guider-engine settings editor (panel + help + search)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Settings → Equipment → Guider now has a "Guider engine" section where you can set guide scope focal length, guide camera pixel size, RA and Dec aggressiveness, minimum move, and Dec guide mode. These are the values sent to PHD2 when the guider connects. Each setting has built-in help text and can be found through quick search. Out-of-range values are rejected to match what the server accepts, and this completes the chain of saving these settings, sending them, and editing them in the app.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63.5 push guider-engine config to PHD2 on connect (guider-e-2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the guider connects, the app now sends your saved guiding settings to PHD2 automatically: scope focal length, camera pixel size, aggressiveness, minimum move, and Dec guide mode. A fresh PHD2 setup therefore starts with your values instead of its own defaults. Each setting is sent separately and on a best-effort basis, so one that PHD2 rejects is logged and skipped without blocking the connection. Values left at zero are not sent, so PHD2 keeps its own setting for them. This has not yet been tested against real guiding hardware.

prs.title: feat(profile): §63.5 guider-engine config on the PHD2 profile section
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Your profile can now store the core guiding settings: guide scope focal length, guide camera pixel size, RA and Dec aggressiveness, minimum move, and Dec guide mode. They default to sensible PHD2 values, and older saved profiles upgrade to those defaults cleanly instead of ending up with broken zeros. Invalid values are corrected when the profile is loaded. This was the groundwork that let later changes send these settings to PHD2 and edit them in the app.

prs.title: feat(calibration): §39 catalog-backed sessions + matching flats/darks
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The calibration view now shows your real imaging sessions instead of fixed sample data. For each night it lists which filters were used, with frame counts and average exposure, and tells you whether you already have matching flats (by filter) and darks (by exposure and gain). Asking for matching flats produces a per-filter capture plan, defaulting to 20 frames each. That plan is not yet turned into a runnable sequence, and dark matching does not yet account for camera temperature.

prs.title: feat(client): §18.I Solve-frame action + result panel on the Imaging tab
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Imaging tab now has a Solve frame button under the image viewer. After you take a picture, one tap works out exactly where in the sky the camera was pointing and shows the position, rotation, and image scale, or a clear message if no match was found or the solver isn't set up. Before this, the feature was only reachable through hand-typed technical commands. Taking a new picture clears the old result, and a slow solve that finishes after a new picture is taken is thrown away so the panel never shows a mismatched answer.

prs.title: fix(platesolve): explicit ASTAP fallback + log for removed AstrometryNet blind solver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Some users' settings still point to an online sky-matching service that the app no longer supports. The app used to quietly swap in the built-in local solver instead, and now it makes that swap on purpose and writes a note in the log. The code goes a bit further than the description: it logs a warning rather than an informational note, logs it only once per run, and covers the main solver setting as well as the backup one. Other solver choices are unchanged.

prs.title: test(astrometry): §58 side-of-pier projection + flip-timing matrix
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds tests only, with no change to how the app behaves. The tests check the math that predicts when the telescope mount needs to turn itself around as a target crosses overhead. Getting this wrong could swing the telescope into its own mount, and the math previously had no tests at all.

prs.title: feat(sequencer): §58.4 meridian-flip orchestration executor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When a target crosses overhead during an automated imaging session, the app can now flip the telescope mount on its own and recover. It pauses guiding, turns the mount, re-aims precisely at the target, restarts guiding, and checks that the mount ended up on the correct side. If the flip fails, the session stops safely instead of continuing to image with a mis-aimed telescope. Saved sessions that include a flip step now actually run it, though refocusing after the flip is not done yet and this hasn't been tested on a real mount.

prs.title: feat(platesolve): §28 CenteringService (slew → solve → sync → re-slew)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now point the telescope precisely at a target. It takes a picture, works out where it's actually pointing, corrects the mount, and repeats until it is close enough to the target. This is the building block for automatic framing and for re-aiming after a mount flip. Only one aiming job can run at a time, and there is no button or web address for it yet.

prs.title: feat(platesolve): §18.I solve-a-frame REST endpoint
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: There is now a server web address that takes a saved picture, works out exactly where in the sky it was taken, and returns the position, rotation, and scale. It also returns clear, readable errors when the picture is missing or the solver isn't set up, such as a missing lens length or solver program. This is what later made the Solve frame button in the app possible.

prs.title: feat(platesolve): §18.I PlateSolveService — image → astrometric solution
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The system can now plate-solve a captured image, which means working out exactly where in the sky the telescope was pointing by matching the stars in the picture. The solving tools were already in the codebase but nothing could actually use them; this connects them using the settings in your profile, and can take a rough starting position to speed things up. It is the groundwork for automatic re-centering on a target and for re-centering after a meridian flip. Not mentioned in the description: the code refuses to solve, with a clear error, if the telescope's focal length or the camera's pixel size hasn't been set in the profile.

prs.title: feat(sequencer): re-port MeridianFlipTrigger decision logic (§58, sub-PR 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: An imaging sequence can once again decide when the telescope mount needs to do a meridian flip, the maneuver where it swings to the other side as a target crosses overhead. It checks the mount's timing, the user's configured wait windows and the length of the next exposure, and skips cleanly if the mount is disconnected, parked or not tracking. The flip itself isn't built yet. Until it is, a sequence that reaches a real flip deliberately stops with an error rather than carrying on, because skipping a flip can drive the telescope into its mount.

prs.title: feat(autofocus): §59.8 trendline curve fit + #360 review nits
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the third and final classic method for working out the best focus point from a series of test images. It fits a straight line to each side of the focus curve and finds where they meet, which works better when the bottom of the curve is flat or rounded. It also includes small efficiency and safety cleanups to the method added in the previous autofocus change.

prs.title: feat(autofocus): §59.8 hyperbolic fit + FitBest fallback selector
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a second way to calculate the best focus point, using a curve shape that often matches real focus data more closely than the basic one. It also adds a simple rule for choosing between the two: keep the basic method's answer when it fits well, and otherwise try the new one.
