Testing showed that clean data almost always stays with the basic method, so the new method acts mainly as a backup.

prs.title: feat(autofocus): §59.8 Classic AF parabolic curve fit + best-focus solver
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the first piece of autofocus. Given measurements of star sharpness at different focuser positions, the system can now calculate the likely best focus position and report how well the data fit. It clearly flags results that can't be trusted, such as data with no real best point or a best point that lies outside the tested range. It is calculation only for now; nothing moves the focuser yet.

prs.title: feat(image): un-stub RenderedImage.DetectStars + UpdateAnalysis (§2105 PR5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The system can now find the stars in a captured image and measure how sharp they are, and it records the star count and sharpness in the saved image file. The detector was built from scratch so it works the same on every platform without an extra outside library. This is the prerequisite for autofocus. Marking the detected stars on the image is not done yet and is currently skipped.

prs.title: feat(image): full-resolution bilinear Debayer (§2105 PR4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Color camera images can now be turned into full-size color pictures inside the app. Before, this step was just a placeholder that failed. Common color sensor layouts are supported, and rarer ones give a clear error. The description says image edges are handled by repeating the nearest pixel, but the code and tests use a mirroring approach at the edges instead.

prs.title: feat(image): un-stub RenderedImage.Stretch via parameterized §65 STF (§2105 PR3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Images can now be re-brightened with custom settings for how bright the background should look and how much of the dark shadows to cut off. Before, this option was a placeholder that failed. The option to adjust each color separately is accepted but has no effect yet, because color processing had not landed when this merged. The default automatic brightening looks the same as before.

prs.title: feat(image): un-stub RenderedImage GetThumbnail + ReRender on §65 (§2105 PR2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now make small preview thumbnails (up to 320 pixels wide) of camera images and refresh an image's display from the original data. Both were placeholders that failed before. A refresh starts over from the original data, so it drops any custom brightening. Nothing uses these yet; they are groundwork for a future Live View feature.

prs.title: feat(image): un-stub RenderBitmapSource on the §65 Stretcher (§2105 PR1, SkiaSharp)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Raw camera images can now be turned into a viewable, automatically brightened picture instead of failing. The team chose a graphics library that works on all the computers the app supports over one that did not. Beyond what the title says, this also fixes the automatic brightening, which was making the sky background far too bright. That fix likely changes how existing image previews look as well. The new display path is groundwork for Live View and is not used yet.

prs.title: feat(guider): named-object RPC request classes for §63.5 profile-push setters (guider-e-1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the message formats the app will use to send setup details to the guiding software, such as focal length, pixel size, calibration settings, which camera to use, and network device settings. Only the settings that are actually filled in get sent, so the guider's other settings are not overwritten. Nothing uses these messages yet; the automatic setup push when connecting comes in a follow-up, and it has not been tested against a live guider.

prs.title: fix(stretch): harden §65 SkiaSharp encode paths (GetPixels/Resize guards)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes image and thumbnail saving fail safely with a clear error when the computer runs low on memory, instead of risking a crash or corrupted memory. Nothing changes when things work normally.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63.3 crash detection + auto-restart of the guider daemon (guider-d)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the guiding program crashes mid-session, the app now tries to bring it back instead of silently sitting in an error state. It checks on the guider repeatedly over about four minutes and asks the system to restart it if needed. If the guider never comes back, it shows a critical alert so the user knows guiding is unavailable. This only works on the Linux devices the app ships on; the app does not yet reconnect to the guider by itself after it recovers, and that is planned as follow-up work.

prs.title: feat(client): manual capture + frame display in the Imaging tab (§25.5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Imaging tab's "Take One" button now takes a real picture with the connected camera and shows the result in the main viewer, where you can zoom and pan. Before this, both the button and the viewer were placeholders. The app waits for the picture to finish saving and shows a message if something goes wrong. The change also makes local testing on Apple Silicon Macs easier. One detail: the app sends the shot to the most recently saved server rather than checking which one is actually connected.

prs.title: Unify web UI header with guider; generate debian/changelog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This finishes making AlpacaBridge's web page header look like the OpenAstro Guider's. The header is now the same height, the version tag reads like "v1.0.3" in a muted style, and the tagline is gone. Behind the scenes, the installer package's release history is now built automatically from the main changelog, fixing a copy that was stuck at version 1.0.0. The package build also now accepts either of two common versions of a required networking library.

prs.title: Restyle web UI to the OpenAstro dark astro theme
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge's web page has been redesigned with the same dark astronomy look as OpenAstro Guider, so the two tools look like one family. The header is now a compact bar with a small logo and a badge showing the server's version. Device controls work the same as before. The changelog says the page's script was untouched, but it did get a small addition to fill in the version badge. The tagline stayed in this change and was removed later.

prs.title: feat(image): debayered color previews for OSC cameras (§65)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Previews and thumbnails from color cameras now show in actual color instead of a gray checkerboard pattern. The saved image files stay unchanged and raw, with a small tag added so stacking software can process the color itself. Black-and-white cameras are not affected. The code only enables color when the camera is not binning pixels together, a limit the description doesn't mention, so binned color shots will still preview in gray.

prs.title: Add ASCOM Platform 7 interface versions and compliant DeviceState
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All AlpacaBridge device drivers now identify themselves as supporting the newest version of the ASCOM astronomy standard. Each device type now reports its live status in one standard, consistent way instead of every brand doing it separately. One ZWO camera passed the official compliance checker with no problems. The mounts, focusers, rotators, filter wheels, and weather drivers still need the same real-hardware check before the 2.0.0 release. The new status report is also no longer taken all at once, so values can occasionally be from slightly different moments.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group in /client/openastroara_client with 4 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of four outside libraries used by the ARA client app. The visible change only raises the required version for one of them, a small patch update. The description also lists a jump to a beta version of the file-picking library, but the main settings file still asks for the old version, so that upgrade may not fully take effect. No new features for users.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of three tools used by the project's automatic build and check system: build caching, the automated code reviewer, and security scanning. The caching tool moves up a major version, which needs a newer build machine. Nothing changes in the app itself.

prs.title: ci: skip Claude review on Dependabot and fork PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated AI code review now skips pull requests from Dependabot and from outside contributors' copies of the project, instead of failing on them. GitHub doesn't share the reviewer's login key with those runs, so every such PR showed a misleading red failure mark. This check never blocked merging, so the change just removes noise. Outside contributions will now be reviewed by hand only.

prs.title: ci: bump the github-actions group with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: Routine automated update of two tools used by the project's build and check system: the step that downloads the code, which jumps two major versions, and the automated AI code reviewer. The app itself is unaffected. One of the updated lines still carries an old note saying it is the older version, a harmless labeling slip.

prs.title: feat(webui): profile New/Rename/Delete; fix create_profile select
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider's web app now has New, Rename and Delete buttons for equipment profiles on the Equipment tab. This came from early user feedback, for example wanting a separate profile for taking darks. New profiles can copy the current profile's settings, and deleting a profile can optionally remove its saved dark and bad-pixel files. The work also fixed a long-standing server bug: a profile created remotely could never be switched to straight away and always gave an "invalid profile id" error.

prs.title: Fix Alpaca conformance: casing, HTTP 400, error codes, drop Shutter
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now follows the official Alpaca standard more closely, which should help astronomy apps like NINA work smoothly with it. Setting names in requests are now accepted in any capitalization for every app, not just the official test tool. Requests for an unknown device or command now get the standard "bad request" response instead of "not found". An unused, non-standard "Shutter" device type was removed, since shutter control belongs to domes; the internal error codes were tidied up without changing the numbers apps see, and new tests and documentation cover the rules.

prs.title: feat(webui): real PHD2-like web app + get_guide_history + /api/frame.jpg
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider's built-in web page has been rebuilt from a basic setup wizard into a full control app that works like the desktop PHD2 program, and it runs offline on the Pi. From a browser you can now watch the live camera view and guiding graph, start and stop guiding, run all three polar-alignment tools, manage equipment and settings, and handle dark frames and bad-pixel maps. Two small server additions support it: a way to fetch recent guiding history and the current camera image. Not mentioned in the description, the change also blocks other websites from secretly controlling the guider through your browser and fixes a latent memory-safety bug in the image brightness code.

prs.title: feat(api): drive the Drift Align tool over RPC; fix Alpaca coordinate units
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The classic Drift Align polar-alignment tool can now be run remotely without the desktop screen, so all three of the guider's polar-alignment tools are now available to outside apps. The work also fixed a real bug: when a mount was connected, telescope position was being read and sent in the wrong units, which threw off every alignment and slew calculation that relied on it. The simulated test equipment now includes a fake mount, so calibration, guiding and alignment can all be tested without real hardware.

prs.title: feat(api): drive the Static PA + Polar Drift alignment tools over RPC
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Two of the guider's built-in polar-alignment tools, Static Polar Alignment and Polar Drift Alignment, can now be run remotely without the desktop screen. Outside apps can start them, check progress, and get live guidance on how to adjust the mount's alignment knobs. The remote version reuses the same logic as the desktop tools rather than copying it. The simulated test camera can now rotate its star field to mimic polar alignment, and tests against it recovered the expected results closely.

prs.title: feat(api): polar-alignment guider-side enablers — centroid report + PA session lease
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the guider's part of the upcoming polar-alignment feature, which the companion ARA app will run. Outside apps can now get a list of star positions from the current image without disturbing guiding. They can also temporarily reserve the camera so nothing else starts guiding or looping mid-alignment, and the reservation expires on its own if the app crashes. The team also confirmed that saved images contain everything needed for star-field solving, and added a simulated camera for testing without hardware.

prs.title: feat(api): dark/bad-pixel-map tail — rebuild_defect_map, add_bad_pixel, set_dark_auto_load
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Outside apps can now fine-tune the bad-pixel map remotely. They can rebuild it with different sensitivity settings, preview the result before saving, add individual bad pixels by hand, and choose whether darks and bad-pixel maps load automatically when the camera connects. This matches what the desktop app's dark-frame tools already offered and completes the planned effort to expose every setting to remote control. A guard was added to require a connected camera, after testing revealed a crash without one.

prs.title: cleanup(api): remove dead *_indi_* JSON-RPC methods left from the Phase 3 INDI drop
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal cleanup that removes six leftover remote commands for INDI, an equipment system dropped earlier, along with the unused code behind them. Nobody was using them. Not mentioned in the description, the change also adds two safety limits: manual guide pulses are now capped at 60 seconds to avoid a runaway movement that could damage hardware, and bulk command requests are capped at 100 at a time to prevent overload.

prs.title: feat(headless): sandbox the systemd unit; drop vestigial plugdev/dialout grants
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider's background service is now locked down so it can only reach the network and write to its own data folder. It can no longer gain extra privileges or touch the rest of the system or users' home folders. Installs also stop giving the service access to local USB and serial devices, and upgrades remove that access where older versions granted it. The guider only talks to equipment over the network now, so those permissions had no purpose.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63 guider-c — IGuiderMediator unification (sequencer drives live guider)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved sequences can now actually start guiding, stop guiding and dither using the connected guider; before, those steps did nothing. If the guider isn't connected, the steps report a failure and the sequence's normal retry handling takes over, rather than crashing. A few less-used guider functions in this path are still placeholders, such as reading the lock position and per-sequence accuracy recording. This hasn't yet been tested against a real guider.

prs.title: feat(guider): §63 guider-a — re-port PHD2Guider + real GuiderService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider controls now talk to a real guiding program (PHD2) instead of a placeholder. Users can connect using the address in their profile, see whether it is guiding, calibrating or has lost the star, and start guiding, stop guiding or dither. The description says guiding accuracy (RMS) figures would come later, but the code already calculates and reports them from recent guide steps. Only basic automated checks were run; a live test with real equipment is still to come.

prs.title: feat(sequencer): re-port TakeExposure + camera/imaging mediator unification (§14e capture-path PRb)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved sequences can now take real pictures again. This includes sequences imported from NINA and the built-in starter templates. Frames are saved and catalogued with the right frame type, filter and target name, through the same process as manual captures. If a sequence tries to capture while a manual shot is running, it waits its turn instead of failing. Not mentioned in the description, the change also adds a camera offset setting and reports the camera's allowed offset range.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real CameraService — capture to FITS + frame catalog (§14e capture-path PRa)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now take real photos with a connected camera. It saves each image as a standard astronomy (FITS) file in the user's save folder and adds it to the frame library. This means the existing list, preview, thumbnail and download features show new shots right away. Cooler control and cancelling an exposure also work on the real device. Color cameras are not supported yet in this first version, and images fall back to a local folder if the configured save location isn't available.

prs.title: feat(astrometry): build + resolve SOFA/NOVAS natives off-Windows (§14e)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The math that corrects star positions for the slow drift of the sky over the years now works on Linux and macOS, not just Windows. This means slews to catalog targets are corrected properly instead of using uncorrected positions. The automated checks now build and verify this on every run. Installer and Docker packaging of the new pieces is still a separate follow-up, so shipped builds won't get this until that lands.

prs.title: feat(sequencer): ship §38.7 starter sequence templates + first-run seeding
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app now comes with three ready-made imaging plans (a standard color deep-sky plan, a narrowband plan, and a comet plan), which are copied into each user's plan library the first time it starts. Copies the user has edited are never overwritten, and deleting one brings back a fresh copy on the next start. The actual 'take a picture' steps inside these plans do nothing yet because camera capture isn't built; they will start working automatically once it is. Automated checks now confirm the shipped plans stay valid.

prs.title: feat(server): profile source-of-truth — hydrate ActiveProfile from IProfileStore (§14e PR20)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automated imaging runs now use the settings people actually enter in the app, such as site location, guiding options, autofocus, where images are saved, plate-solving tuning and meridian-pause rules, instead of built-in defaults. Settings are loaded at startup and refreshed every time the user saves a change. Some settings, like notifications and display defaults, are still only stored and not yet used by automated runs, and a failed settings refresh keeps the previous values rather than breaking the save.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify FilterWheelService with IFilterWheelMediator + profile filter import (§14e PR19)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 'change filter' step in an automated imaging run now actually turns the real filter wheel, instead of doing nothing. When a filter wheel connects, its list of filters is copied into the user's profile so runs can pick filters by name or slot. Any per-filter settings the user already edited are kept. The step waits up to about a minute for the wheel to report it has reached the requested filter.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify SwitchService with ISwitchMediator (§14e PR18)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 'set switch value' step in an automated imaging run now controls the real power or switch box, instead of doing nothing. Before running, it checks each value against the device's real allowed range. If the device drops out or a write fails, the problem is logged and the run keeps going. The settings screens work the same as before.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify TelescopeService with ITelescopeMediator (§14e PR17)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automated imaging runs can now really control the telescope mount: turn tracking on or off, park and unpark it, send it home, and point it at a target. Target positions are converted to the coordinate system the mount expects, so it points accurately. Each step waits until the mount actually finishes, with time limits so a stuck mount can't hang the run. Less common mount actions, such as guiding pulses and meridian flips, are still not hooked up.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify DomeService with IDomeMediator (§14e PR16)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automated imaging runs can now really control the observatory dome: open and close the shutter, park it, send it home, and turn it to a set direction. Each step waits, with time limits, until the dome actually finishes, so the run knows whether it worked. Having the dome automatically follow the telescope is still not hooked up.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify RotatorService with IRotatorMediator (§14e PR15)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automated observing sequences can now actually turn the real camera rotator. Before this, the rotator step in a sequence was a do-nothing placeholder. It reuses the safeguards built for the focuser: a move can't hang the sequence forever, and it reports the angle the rotator really ended up at rather than the one it was asked for. Some secondary rotator details, such as whether it can reverse direction or its step size, are still left blank because no current sequence step uses them.

prs.title: feat(equipment): unify FocuserService with IFocuserMediator (§14e PR14)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Automated observing sequences can now actually move the real focuser. Before this, the focus steps in a sequence were do-nothing placeholders. A move waits for the focuser to finish and then reports where it really stopped. If the device misbehaves, the sequence logs the problem and carries on instead of crashing. The description says the code waits by checking stored readings, but it actually asks the device directly, and it also adds an unmentioned 5-minute limit so a silent focuser can't stall a run indefinitely.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca Telescope REST service (§14e PR13)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now connect to and control a real telescope mount instead of a placeholder. It shows where the mount is pointing and whether it is tracking, parked, or at home. It can slew to or sync on sky coordinates, park and unpark, turn tracking on or off, and emergency-stop a slew immediately. Coordinates outside valid sky ranges are rejected, and sequences cannot drive the mount yet; that is planned next.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca Dome REST service (§14e PR12)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now connect to and control a real observatory dome instead of a placeholder. It shows the dome's direction and whether the shutter is open, parked, or at home. It can turn the dome to a given direction, park it, and open or close the shutter. Any in-progress turn is stopped before disconnecting, and sequences cannot control the dome yet.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca FlatDevice (CoverCalibrator) service (§14e PR11)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now connect to and control a real flat-field panel (the dust cover and light panel used to take calibration images) instead of a placeholder. It can open or close the cover, switch the light on or off, and set its brightness. The app shows the panel's current state, and brightness values outside what the device supports are rejected. Sequences cannot use it yet.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca FilterWheel service with change-slot (§14e PR10)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app can now connect to a real filter wheel instead of a placeholder. It lists the wheel's filters with their names and focus adjustments and shows which filter is currently in place. It can also switch to a different filter, and it rejects filter numbers that don't exist on the wheel. Automated sequences cannot change filters yet; that is planned as a follow-up.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca Rotator service with Move (§14e PR9)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now connect to a real telescope rotator, the device that turns the camera to a chosen angle. It shows the rotator's current angle and can turn it to a new angle between 0 and 360 degrees, rejecting anything outside that range. For now this works only through the server's web interface; automated observing sequences cannot drive the rotator yet. Tests include one that turns a simulated rotator to 90 degrees and checks that it gets there.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca Focuser service with Move (§14e PR8)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now connect to a real focuser, the motor that adjusts telescope focus. It reports the focuser's limits, current position and temperature, and can move it to a new position. Readings a particular focuser doesn't support, such as temperature on a unit without a sensor, show as blank instead of causing an error. For now this works only through the server's web interface, not from automated sequences or autofocus.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca Switch service with SetValue (§14e PR7)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now connect to a real switch box, the kind used to power equipment or dew heaters on and off. It lists each switch and its current setting, and can change a setting. This is the first device the server can actually control rather than just read. For now this works only through the server's web interface; the switch step in automated sequences still doesn't drive the real hardware.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca ObservingConditions service (§14e PR6)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now connect to a real weather station and show live readings such as temperature, humidity, pressure, cloud cover, wind and rain, refreshed every two seconds. Any sensor the station doesn't have shows as blank instead of breaking the display. The station never reports conditions as "safe"; that judgment is left to the separate safety monitor. The code also includes a small fix the description doesn't mention: when switching to a different safety monitor, the old device's "safe" reading is cleared so it can't briefly appear under the new one.

prs.title: perf(equipment): §32.4 cache for SafetyMonitor IsSafe — no per-poll HTTP read (§14e PR5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The safety monitor, which tells the system whether it's safe to observe, is now checked in the background every two seconds. Before this, every status request waited on the device directly, which could take up to about three seconds and pile up under frequent requests. As a result, the reported safe/unsafe status can now be up to two seconds old. This speed fix was the prerequisite for connecting the other types of equipment the same way.

prs.title: feat(equipment): SafetyMonitorService also serves ISafetyMonitorMediator (§14e PR4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "wait until safe" step in automated observing sequences now reads the real, connected safety monitor. Previously it used a stand-in that always reported "not connected". The screens and the sequence now share a single connection to the device. If the server is shutting down while a sequence is still running, the step simply sees "not connected" instead of crashing.

prs.title: feat(equipment): real Alpaca SafetyMonitor service (§14e PR3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now actually connect to a real safety monitor, the device that reports whether conditions are safe for observing, and show its live connection status and safe/unsafe reading. Until now, every piece of equipment was only a stand-in; this is the first real one, and the other eleven device types are still stand-ins. Sequences that wait for safe conditions do not use this live reading yet; that is planned next. The description mentions three quick checks, but the code adds six, including checks that the service refuses to work after it has been shut down.

prs.title: test(equipment): live Alpaca discovery integration test (§14e PR2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal testing change. It adds an automated check that the server can find simulated equipment (a camera and a telescope) on the network the same way it would find real gear. That check runs as a separate, optional step in the automated build and is left out of the regular test run. The code also makes an existing simulator check wait for basic build checks to pass first, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(§14e): pin the Alpaca simulators + CI smoke harness
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal test infrastructure. The automated build now downloads a fixed, verified version of a free equipment simulator and confirms it starts up and shows a simulated camera. This gives future equipment work something realistic to test against without needing real hardware. It also adds a small check that the simulator's version details are recorded correctly.

prs.title: port(§38): precise frames_completed + current_instruction_index
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A running sequence now reports real progress: how many steps are done out of the total, and which step is running right now. Previously these always showed zero or blank. Unlike what the description lists, the code also counts turned-off steps as done, so a successful run with a disabled step still shows as fully complete. For sequences that loop, the count only reflects the current pass through the loop.

prs.title: port(§38): real sequence execution engine (SequencerService)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved sequences now actually run on the server instead of just pretending with a timer, keeping support for loops, conditions, triggers, and nested steps. Because equipment is still simulated, only steps that need no hardware (such as waits and notes) really do anything; hardware steps fail or do nothing without crashing. Pause and resume are accepted but have no effect yet. Not mentioned in the description, the code also stops the server from crashing at startup when language settings are unavailable, by falling back to a neutral default.

prs.title: port(§38k-22): HeadlessProfileService + register all profile-bound instructions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved sequences can now include the last seven types of steps that were missing, such as dithering, changing filters, connecting or disconnecting equipment, and switching profiles. To make this possible, the server uses a placeholder profile with default settings. It does not yet read the settings the user has actually edited, and connecting that is planned for later.

prs.title: port(§38k-21): HeadlessDomeFollower + register SynchronizeDome
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now include the "synchronize dome" step in observing sequences, which completes the full set of dome steps. To make this possible, the PR adds a placeholder for the part that keeps the dome lined up with the telescope. For now it does nothing and always reports that the dome is not following. Real dome-following behavior will come later, once actual dome hardware support is connected.

prs.title: port(§38k-19/20): complete the device-mediator stub set
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the last two placeholder devices on the server, a flat panel and a weather station, so the server now has stand-ins for all 11 equipment types. It does not add any new sequence steps that use them. The goal is to unblock the later "connect/disconnect all equipment" steps, which need every device type to exist. Those steps are still waiting on the server getting access to user profile settings.

prs.title: port(§38k-13…18): complete the equipment-mediator stub layer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server gains placeholder devices for the camera, filter wheel, rotator, power switches and dome. It also registers about fifteen new sequence steps that rely on them, including cooling and warming the camera, starting and stopping guiding, moving the rotator, and opening, parking or turning the dome. Taking actual pictures deliberately reports "not supported" for now, because the image pipeline isn't built yet. Dithering, filter changes and dome synchronization are also left for later, and the code confirms these gaps.

prs.title: port(tracking): PORT_PROGRESS.md refresh — §38k-9..12 landed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update that brings the porting progress tracker up to date. The tracker had fallen behind four already-merged steps, covering the safety monitor, telescope, guider and focuser placeholders. It also corrects the test counts and the status of the CI work, and names the camera as the next piece of work.

prs.title: Whole-solution analyzer compliance → zero warnings + TreatWarningsAsErrors
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a large internal cleanup. It fixes every code-quality warning across the whole server solution and then makes any new warning block the build, with a new CI check that builds and tests everything on every PR. According to the description, it also removes some unused code, such as an unwired GPS driver interface. No code diff was available, so these changes couldn't be confirmed against the actual code.

prs.title: Add ToupTek StellaVita switch driver (ConformU 4.3.0 validated)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now supports the ToupTek StellaVita power box. Astronomy software can switch its four 12V ports on and off, or dim them from 0 to 100% for dew heaters and flat panels. The ports it controls that power the board's own USB hub are deliberately left out, and connecting or disconnecting never cuts power to attached gear. The code also quietly tightens the existing iOptron and ZWO power switch drivers (for example, rejecting invalid numeric values), which the description doesn't mention; the docs also give slightly inconsistent test counts and still list ConformU validation as "pending" in one table despite the passing result.

prs.title: docs: polar-alignment design (plate-solve, FOV-adaptive, bolt-disambiguation)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a design proposal, with no code yet, for a future polar-alignment feature, the step where users line up their telescope mount with the sky's pole. The plan works from any part of the sky and with any camera setup, not only when the pole is in view. Its main goal is to tell users exactly which adjustment knob to turn, which way, and how far, using on-screen arrows and a short calibration nudge. The document also sets out which work belongs in the guider and which in the separate control app, lists the known risks, and lays out a five-step rollout.

prs.title: feat(api): Phase 5 Batch C2 — camera extras, rotator, guider options
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The external control app can now change a final set of camera, rotator and guiding settings remotely. These include partial-frame capture, the cooler's target temperature, how the camera detects overexposed stars, rotator direction, and a few niche guiding options. This completes the planned three batches of remote-control additions, leaving only dark-frame library management as a known gap. The PR also tightens the written rules for the backlash settings added in the previous batch. The code builds, but the new commands were not tested against a running app.

prs.title: feat(api): Phase 5 Batch C1 — mount options, backlash, auto-exposure, noise reduction
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The external control app can now remotely adjust four more groups of settings: mount behaviour switches, correction for slack in the mount's gears (backlash), the limits for automatic exposure, and image noise reduction. Each change is fully checked before anything is applied, so a bad value cannot leave settings half-updated. The docs describe a slightly stricter backlash rule than the description gives: the minimum pulse must not exceed the main pulse, and the main pulse must not exceed the maximum. The code builds, but the new commands were not tested against a running app.

prs.title: feat(api): Phase 5 Batch B — star-detection + camera settings
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The external control app can now remotely read and change how the guider decides what counts as a usable star. It can also adjust the camera's gain and how long the guider waits for a camera image. Changes are checked in full before any are applied, so a bad request cannot partly change settings. There is one small mismatch: the description says timeouts under 5 seconds are quietly raised to 5 seconds, but the docs in this change say such values are rejected. The code builds, but the new commands were not tested against a running app.

prs.title: feat(api): Phase 5 Batch A guiding-control methods + full API reference
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The external control app can now switch which guiding method is used on each axis, not just tune its settings. It can also set limits on how hard the guider corrects, turn declination compensation on or off, and set default dithering behaviour. The PR also adds a complete plain-language reference for all ~104 remote commands. It records a team decision to keep the remote interface unauthenticated, since it is meant for trusted local networks only. The description says choosing "None" as the guiding method is allowed as a do-nothing option, but the docs in this change say that choice is rejected, and the new commands were not tested against a running app.

prs.title: docs: Phase 5 API gap audit (Advanced settings → JSON-RPC)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only, with no code change: this adds an audit comparing the app's Advanced Settings screen with what the external control app can currently change remotely. The audit ranks the missing settings by priority and suggests grouping them into a few combined commands delivered in three batches. It became the roadmap for the follow-up feature PRs.

prs.title: feat(headless): headless-by-default run mode + finish systemd packaging (Phase 4)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guiding program now starts in background (no-window) mode by default, which suits its job as a service running on a Raspberry Pi. Showing the window is now opt-in for local troubleshooting, and a new option connects the chosen equipment automatically at startup. The old startup options still work, so existing setups and NINA keep working. The background service settings were updated to use the new options, a wrong documentation link was fixed, and an outdated duplicate service file was removed.

prs.title: fix(alpaca): handle ROI-sized subframe responses; guard pGuider; atomic refcnt
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a problem where guiding images could come out black when the camera was asked for only a small area around the guide star, which is the normal mode once a star is selected. The program now works out whether the camera sent back just that small area or the whole picture, and places the pixels correctly either way. Cameras that send the whole picture behave exactly as before. The team could not test the new path on a real camera. The change also prevents a possible crash when a client connects while guiding is shutting down, and adds a small safety change for future multi-threaded use.

prs.title: fix(alpaca): correct PUT body, drop per-PUT 100ms sleep, fix m_response data race
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes the way the guider sends commands to network (Alpaca) equipment follow the official standard, so stricter devices should no longer reject them. It also removes a fixed 100-millisecond pause after every command, including guide corrections, which makes the guider more responsive. It also fixes a rare issue where two tasks talking to the same device at once could corrupt the log messages.

prs.title: cleanup: scrub historical Windows/macOS comments + strip _WIN64 blocks
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that rewords code comments still referring to Windows and macOS, which the project no longer supports. It also removes two leftover sections of Windows-only code that had been missed earlier. The guider should behave the same.

prs.title: cleanup: strip last _WINDOWS ifdef in phd.h; fix wizard ASCOM/Windows text
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes one last piece of leftover Windows-only code. It also updates the setup wizard's mount help text, which used to recommend a Windows-only connection option. The text now says equipment is reached over the local network using the standard the project supports. Otherwise this is cleanup with no change in behavior.

prs.title: cleanup: remove orphaned build/get_phd_version Perl script
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that deletes an old helper script for working out the version number. Nothing uses it anymore since the build gets the version another way. No effect on users.

prs.title: cleanup: remove GUI help system and all translations (headless build)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removes the program's built-in help pages and all translations into other languages, about 49 MB across 629 files. The guider now runs in the background without a screen, so it never shows these. The English interface is unchanged, and the few remaining Help buttons now open the online help website instead of a bundled help file. No code changes were available to check, so this summary relies on the description alone.

prs.title: cleanup: strip remaining macOS #if blocks in serialport_posix
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that finishes the previous pass by removing a few leftover Mac-only bits from the code that talks to serial-port devices. An earlier search missed them because of a small formatting difference. This code never ran on Linux, so nothing changes for users, and the code now has no Windows- or Mac-specific sections left.

prs.title: cleanup: strip dead Windows/macOS inline #ifdefs from src
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that removes about 56 leftover Windows- and Mac-only code sections spread across roughly 20 files, keeping only the Linux versions. For example, the code that finds devices on the network now uses only the standard Linux approach. None of the removed code ever ran on Linux, so behavior is unchanged. It also corrects a planning note that had claimed this cleanup was already finished.

prs.title: cleanup: remove dead vendor-SDK and Windows build scripts
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that deletes old helper scripts for unpacking camera-maker software kits and for Windows builds. These stopped being used once the project switched to connecting equipment only through the Alpaca standard and dropped Windows. The shortened code changes only show the changelog entry, so the file deletions themselves could not be checked there.

prs.title: fix: AlpacaClient::Get() logged its error as "PUT"
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a mislabeled debug message: when reading data from a device failed, the log said it was a write ("PUT") instead of a read ("GET"). This only affects log text, but it makes troubleshooting device communication less confusing.

prs.title: cleanup: remove macOS/Windows vendor cruft, focus repo on Debian/arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup that removes about 4 MB of leftover Mac and Windows files, such as old camera-maker software kits, Windows translation tools, and Mac and Windows icon and cursor files. Nothing used any of them anymore. This leaves the project focused purely on Debian Linux on ARM hardware, and the program still builds and passes its tests.

prs.title: fix: review guard used unsupported gh --jq --arg (false-red)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a mistake in the automated code-review check added in #27. A command-option error made the check fail on every pull request, even when the review had actually run. The check now reads the commit identifier in a way the tool supports, so it passes when a real review was posted and fails only when one is missing.

prs.title: ci: harden review workflow against false-greens
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes the automated AI code-review check much harder to fool. Before, it could show a green 'passed' result even when no review had happened, for example if its login key was missing or it hit an internal error. It now fails straight away if the key is missing, asks the reviewer to tag its comment with the exact version of the code it looked at, and fails unless a matching review with a clear verdict was posted. The final verification step shipped with a bug that made it fail every time, which was fixed in #29.

prs.title: build: target arm64 only, drop amd64 and 32-bit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider is now officially built and supported only on 64-bit Raspberry Pi hardware (Pi 4/5, or a Pi 3 running a 64-bit OS). Regular 64-bit PCs are no longer supported, and 32-bit systems remain unsupported. The packaging settings and build scripts now refuse to build on other machines and show a clear message explaining why. The README was updated to match.

prs.title: docs: track peak-mode saturation gap in star detection (PR #24 follow-up)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only, with no change to how the software behaves. It records a known, long-standing gap inherited from the original PHD2 code: in one of the two star-finding modes ('peak' mode), the software never warns when a star image is overexposed. The gap is noted in the code and in the project's to-do list rather than fixed, because the team's current rule is not to change guiding behaviour during the port.

prs.title: test: extract star-detection pixel math and golden-test it on a fixture
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the math that finds a guide star in a camera image into its own self-contained piece, so it can be tested quickly on its own. New tests use a real sample star image to confirm that the detected star position, brightness, sharpness and signal quality stay the same. The description calls the change behaviour-neutral, but the changelog also records one small fix: a star at the very edge of a tiny image could previously be reported as found with an invalid quality score, and is now correctly reported as not found. The new tests are skipped automatically if the image-file library is not installed.

prs.title: test: extract calibration camera<->mount transforms and unit test them
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the math that converts movements seen by the camera into telescope-mount movements (and back) into its own self-contained piece, and adds seven automated tests for it. The tests check basic properties, such as a pure rotation keeping distances the same and a conversion followed by its reverse returning the original values. The math itself is copied over unchanged, so guiding behaviour should be the same.

prs.title: test: extract Lowpass/Lowpass2 decision math and unit test it
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal groundwork with no change in how guiding behaves. The number-crunching behind two of the guiding methods (the "lowpass" styles) was moved out of the code tied to the settings screens into a standalone piece. That lets it be tested on its own. Ten new automated checks confirm it handles startup, small movements, sudden jumps, and steady drift correctly, and the existing diagnostic log messages were kept.

prs.title: cleanup: resolve PR #20 follow-ups (GetVariance semantics, exit(1)->throw)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a small tidy-up following review comments on #20. A statistics helper that claimed to report "variance" was actually returning an unfinished intermediate number. It now returns the real value, which is safe because nothing in the running program used it. The filter-design code also now reports an internal error in a way the program can catch, instead of abruptly shutting the whole program down, though that error should never happen with the filter types in use.

prs.title: test: guiding-stats, zfilter & polar-alignment unit tests; README pivot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds a large batch of automated checks for the guiding statistics, the smoothing filters, and the polar-alignment calculations, and fixes a bug found along the way where a spread calculation gave a nonsense result for a single data point. The polar-alignment math was moved into its own standalone piece so it could be tested, and the README was rewritten to describe the project as Linux-only and Alpaca-only. The change log shows more than the description mentions. It also removes an unused filter type that could have produced garbage if ever selected, and makes polar alignment show a message and stop, rather than silently producing broken numbers, when the input images are unusable (for example, when there was no rotation between captures).

prs.title: cleanup: remove dead CPack NSIS (Windows) + vestigial CPack DEB path
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is internal build cleanup. It removes an old, unused way of producing installers, including a Windows installer section that was already switched off and Debian package settings that still referred to dropped components. The project's real Debian package process is untouched and was confirmed to still build.

prs.title: cleanup: strip dead platform/backend ifdefs, drop FreeBSD + direct-ST4
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This clears out leftover code for Windows, macOS, and INDI now that those have been dropped, so the code reflects what the project is: a Linux program that talks to equipment only over Alpaca. It also formally drops FreeBSD support and several older direct-cable guiding hardware options, which could no longer be reached in this setup. The author says everything removed was already inactive on Linux, so behavior should not change. A few small latent code mistakes surfaced by the code checker were fixed along the way, and the project's progress notes were updated.

prs.title: strip(indi): drop INDI — Alpaca-only equipment (Phase 3)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider no longer supports INDI equipment: cameras, mounts, and rotators can now only be connected over ASCOM Alpaca. Anyone who relied on INDI devices will need an Alpaca route instead. The big payoff is simpler, faster builds, since the slow from-scratch build of the INDI library and its extra dependencies are gone from both the build scripts and the Debian package. The package description and homepage link were updated to match, and a few leftover INDI references in the code were left for a later cleanup.

prs.title: strip(macos): drop macOS build system, mac backends, and CMake (Phase 2)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider no longer supports macOS. This PR removes the Mac app packaging, the bundled Mac camera driver files, and three Mac-only telescope connection options, continuing the move to a Linux-only program that talks to equipment over the Alpaca network standard. None of the removed code ran on Linux, so Linux users should see no difference. Some small leftover Mac-specific pieces remain and are tracked for a later cleanup.

prs.title: fix(cppcheck): clear remaining perf/portability/style findings (#9)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the last batch of the code-quality cleanup flagged by an automated code checker, which now reports zero problems across the project. Most of the changes are internal tidying, including fixing many log messages that were passing values in the wrong format. There is one fix users can see: the calibration assistant was rounding the telescope's distance from the meridian down to a whole number, and it now shows the precise value.

prs.title: fix(cppcheck): mark intentionally-ignored return values with (void) (#8)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This internal cleanup marks 38 places where the program deliberately ignores a result, such as saving settings or adding menu separators. Each case was checked and confirmed safe, and these markings change nothing at runtime. The code also does something the description leaves out: when settings are copied, for example between profiles, the temporary values now start at a known default. Before, a failed read could have copied unpredictable data.

prs.title: fix(cppcheck): make 18 resource-owning classes non-copyable (#7)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal safety change. Eighteen parts of the program that manage their own memory or screen controls can no longer be accidentally duplicated. An accidental copy of one of these could have caused crashes, and any such copy will now be caught when the program is built instead of at runtime. None of them were being copied, so nothing changes for users.

prs.title: fix(cppcheck): initialize uninitialized member variables (#6)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: About 80 internal values that could previously start out with random leftover data now start at sensible defaults, such as "unknown" for calibration details. This is mainly a safety cleanup with no intended change in behavior. The code also includes a real bug fix that the description doesn't mention: clearing the guiding statistics didn't fully reset them, which could leave the displayed largest star movement values wrong until something else forced a recalculation.

prs.title: fix(cppcheck): real bugs from the static-analysis audit (#5)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes five problems found by an automated code checker. The only one that changes how the program runs was a debug log message in the static polar alignment tool that tried to print more values than it was given, which could produce garbage output or worse. The other four are small cleanups that make the code clearer without changing behavior.

prs.title: strip(windows): drop Windows build system, ASCOM/win32 backends, CMake (Phase 1)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider project no longer supports Windows. The Windows build and installer files, bundled Windows system libraries, and Windows-only hardware connections have been removed, since equipment will now be reached only over the network through AlpacaBridge. The removed code never ran on Linux, so Linux users should see no change in behavior, and some leftover Windows-only code remains for a follow-up. The PR also quietly changes an automated code checker so it only fails on problems in lines the PR actually touched, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: Add iOptron iMate PowerBox Switch driver (PWM, ConformU validated)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge can now control the power outlets on iOptron's iMate PowerBox. Two of the three outlets can be switched on and off, and each can optionally be dimmed from 0 to 100%, which is useful for dew heaters and flat panels. The third outlet is always on and shown as read-only. Power is never cut when the software disconnects. It passed the standard compatibility test with no errors on real hardware, and it can be set up from the web page. The PR also tightens the automated build checks by verifying a downloaded library against a known fingerprint, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: Fix Alpaca Value typing, NDEBUG tests, ASIAIR Plus naming + JS/cppcheck CI gates
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes a bug where AlpacaBridge could send some device information in the wrong form. Text that looked like a number or true/false could come out as a number, and lists such as a camera's gain options were sent as plain text, which compatibility testing rejected. The ASIAIR Plus (Pi CM4) now reports its real model name instead of calling itself a "Pro". Some tests that were silently skipped in release builds now actually run, and a new automated check catches typos in the web page code. The description says it also pins the version of a code-checking tool, but that change appears to have landed separately in #70.

prs.title: Pin CI cppcheck to 2.17.1 (built from source) to match dev environment
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a behind-the-scenes change so that the automated build checks and developers' own machines use the same version of a code-checking tool. Before this, a change could pass locally and still fail on the build server. The PR also edits the README in ways the description does not mention: the iMate is dropped from the supported-platforms list, and the two separate links for the management page and device API are replaced with a single "Driver Setup" link.

prs.title: Source DriverVersion from VERSION file; add CI pre-flight tooling
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All 19 device drivers now report AlpacaBridge's real release version instead of a fixed "1.0.0", and future version bumps only need one file edited. A new script lets developers run all the automated checks on their own machine before opening a PR, and the PR submission process now requires it to pass. Beyond what the description says, the automated checker is also told to ignore a warning about a shutdown pattern used in every driver, and many files had their include lines reordered with no effect on behavior.

prs.title: platesolve: surface hint on blind failover + ASTAP/workflow docs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When finding the telescope's position from a photo fails because the mount reported the wrong location, the log now says so clearly. It shows the position it searched around, instead of looking like a silent, slow retry. Recovery is unchanged: the software still searches the whole sky and then corrects the mount. The rest is documentation. A misleading code comment was fixed, the team's branching process was simplified so every change goes straight to the main branch (with the old integration branch removed from the automated build triggers), and a future feature was written up for picking star databases based on field of view.

prs.title: build: Bump the pub group across 1 directory with 2 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is a routine, automated update to two outside building blocks used by the desktop/mobile app: the one that opens a file-picker dialog and the one that reports the app's version. The file-picker update is a very large jump, from version 3 to version 11, and includes upstream security and platform fixes. Only the dependency list and its lock file changed, with no adjustments to the app's own code, so it may be worth checking that file selection still works.

prs.title: ci: Bump the github-actions group across 1 directory with 9 updates
prs.author: app/dependabot
prs.summary: This is an internal, automated update to the tools that run the project's automatic checks, builds, security scans and AI reviews. Several of these tools moved up a major version. The notes next to many of them still name the old versions, so those labels are now out of date. Nothing in the product itself changed.

prs.title: ci: skip Claude Code Review on Dependabot PRs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automatic AI code review no longer runs on dependency-update requests opened by the Dependabot bot. Those runs could never reach the login secret they need, so every such request showed a misleading red failed check. Normal pull requests are still reviewed exactly as before. This is an internal CI change only.

prs.title: ci: harden CI (format set -e, zizmor checksum, unicode scanner)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This tightens the project's automatic checks in three ways, bringing them in line with the sibling repos. The code-formatting check now shows what is wrong and how to fix it instead of failing with a bare error. The workflow security scanner is verified against a known fingerprint before it is allowed to run. The scan for hidden or trick characters in source files no longer lets files in unusual text encodings slip through unchecked. These are internal CI changes with no effect on the product itself.

prs.title: ci: Debian-focused non-compiling check suite, drop build jobs for now
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider project's automatic checks were rebuilt around its new direction as a Linux-only background guiding service. The Mac, Windows and Linux build jobs were dropped for now, because the code is still being stripped down and a build would fail. They are replaced by checks that don't require building: required planning documents must exist, style and code-quality checks cover only lines a pull request changes, and there are scans for hidden trick characters, shell script problems and workflow security issues. Translation files are exempt from the hidden-character scan because right-to-left languages legitimately use those characters, and a stray invisible marker was removed from a settings file. The change also touches the changelog, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: ci: add Claude Code automated PR review workflow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider project now gets an automatic AI review on every pull request. The AI posts a single short comment, updated with each new push, that flags likely bugs, security problems or performance concerns and ends with an approve-or-issues-found verdict. Formatting nitpicks are skipped because other tools handle those. The reviewer only becomes active once this is on the main branch, and it is an internal tooling change with no effect on the product.

prs.title: Fix cppcheck findings and remove dead Beast/vcpkg scaffolding (#64)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Mostly a cleanup pass that clears every warning from a code-checking tool, plus one real crash fix. If disconnecting an iOptron mount failed while the driver was shutting down, the whole program could abort; now it logs a warning and carries on. The code also makes the same shutdown change to the Celestron driver, which the description doesn't mention; that driver already caught such errors quietly and now logs them too. The rest removes leftover build options for Windows and other unused setups, and updates the docs to say the project only runs on 64-bit ARM Linux, with no change in how the software behaves there.

prs.title: ci: add Claude Code automated PR review workflow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds an automated AI reviewer that posts one summary comment on each pull request, flagging likely bugs, security issues, and performance problems rather than style nitpicks. It only starts working once it is on the main branch. No code changes were available to check this against, and the reported size (about 460 files changed) is far larger than a single review setup would need, so this merge probably includes more than the description covers.

prs.title: Add CI verification jobs, CodeQL, and dependabot
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Greatly expands the automatic checks that must pass before changes can be merged: a full build with every camera and mount vendor included, memory-safety testing, formatting and code-quality checks on changed lines, security scanning, and weekly automatic updates for the build tools. It replaces a third-party review service that is no longer used. The code also adds several checks the description doesn't list: a scan for hidden or misleading text characters, a check of the shell scripts, a second code-analysis tool, a security audit of the build setup, and an AI reviewer. Internal only; nothing changes for users.

prs.title: docs: headless-port playbook + tracking files (Phase 0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Starts the new openastro-guider project, a behind-the-scenes version of the PHD2 guiding software that runs on the Pi without its own screen and is controlled entirely by ARA. This PR adds only planning documents: an overview of how the pieces fit together, a six-phase plan, and files for tracking progress, decisions, open tasks, and the controls ARA will use. The plan drops Mac, Windows, and INDI support, and flags managing dark frames as the biggest missing piece to build. No code changes.

prs.title: ci: add build + test workflow (arm64)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sets up AlpacaBridge's first automatic build-and-test check, which runs on every pull request on a 64-bit ARM machine to match the project's only supported platform. For now it builds the core without the vendor camera and mount libraries, and style checks are postponed until a formatting standard is agreed. Internal only.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-12 focuser mediator (#305)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: ARA's background server now recognizes three focuser steps in imaging sequences: move to an exact position, move by a relative amount, and adjust for temperature. These are placeholders for now. No real focuser is connected yet, so the steps don't move anything and always report position 0 until real equipment support is added. Nine new tests cover the placeholder and confirm the new steps are available.

prs.title: Add ZWO ASIAIR Plus (Pi CM4) switch support + 50 Hz RK3568 default
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge can now control the four 12V power ports on the Raspberry Pi CM4 version of the ZWO ASIAIR Plus. That model is wired the same way as the ASIAIR Pro, so it reuses the existing Pro controls, and the description says it passed the standard compatibility test on real hardware. The PR also changes the product name to ZWO's official 'ASIAIR' spelling and lowers the default dew-heater and flat-panel pulse rate on the other ASIAIR Plus model (RK3568) from 200 to 50 Hz to match ZWO's own software. The new setup guide in the visible diff disagrees with the description in two places: it tells users to pick the existing 'ASIair Pro' option rather than a new CM4 option, and it still labels the compatibility test as pending and uses the old spelling. The docs may need a follow-up.

prs.title: port(§38k-12): HeadlessFocuserMediator + 3 focuser instructions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds three focuser steps to the list of steps the server can build into an observing sequence: move to an exact position, move by an amount, and adjust for temperature. No real focuser is connected yet. A placeholder answers every request by reporting 'not connected' and a position of zero, so these steps can be added to sequences but will not move anything until real hardware support arrives. Includes new tests.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-11 guider mediator + 4 telescope prototypes (#303)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the changes from #303 into the main line of development. It adds four telescope steps to the sequence builder: unpark, park, find home, and slew to a sky position. It also adds a placeholder for the guiding camera system. As with earlier steps, nothing talks to real hardware yet, and every guiding or telescope action simply reports that it did not succeed.

prs.title: port(§38k-11): HeadlessGuiderMediator + 4 telescope-bound prototypes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds four telescope steps to the list of steps available in observing sequences: unpark, park, find home, and slew to a sky position. Several of these also need to pause guiding, so a placeholder for the guiding system was added too. That placeholder reports 'not connected' and fails every action until real guiding support (PHD2) is built. This PR adds four steps at once instead of the previous one at a time, and includes new tests.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-10 telescope mediator (#301)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the changes from #301 into the main line of development. It adds a placeholder telescope connection and makes the 'set tracking' step available in observing sequences. The placeholder does not control a real telescope yet; every action reports failure.

prs.title: port(§38k-10): HeadlessTelescopeMediator + SetTracking prototype
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a stand-in telescope connection so that telescope-related steps can start appearing in observing sequences. The first such step is 'set tracking'. The stand-in always reports that it is not connected, that it is pointing at position zero, and that any slew, park, or tracking change did not succeed. Real telescope control will replace it later. Includes new tests.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-9 first equipment-mediator (SafetyMonitor) (#299)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings the safety-monitor work from #299 into the main branch. Sequences can now include a "wait until safe" step, which is the first step that depends on real observatory equipment. For now there is no actual safety monitor behind it, only a stand-in that always reports "not connected, not safe." So the step can be saved and loaded but would not finish if run. It also sets the pattern for adding other equipment, such as the telescope and camera.

prs.title: port(§38k-9): HeadlessSafetyMonitorMediator + WaitUntilSafe prototype
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a "wait until safe" step to sequences, the first step that depends on observatory equipment (a safety monitor, such as a weather or roof sensor). Real hardware support isn't connected yet. A placeholder stands in that always reports "not connected, not safe," so sequences with this step can be saved, loaded and checked, but the step would never finish if actually run. The work also sets the template for adding the telescope, camera and other equipment next, and includes new tests.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: PORT_PROGRESS.md refresh — §38j-9 + §38k-1…§38k-8
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It records the recently finished sequence-engine work and rewrites the "what's next" section to focus on equipment-dependent sequence steps. It also marks the equipment simulator work as no longer blocked, since the needed simulator release is now available.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-8 conditions round-trip test (#296)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings the new tests from #296 into the main branch. They check that loop and time-limit rules on a sequence survive being saved and reloaded. Tests only; the app's behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: port(§38k-8): conditions round-trip test
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds tests that save and reload sequences containing "repeat N times" and "run for a set time" rules. The tests confirm the rules come back in the same order with their settings intact, including when mixed with regular steps. Tests only; the app's behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-7 condition prototypes (#294)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Sequences can now use two kinds of stopping rules, "repeat a set number of times" and "run for a set length of time." When a saved sequence contains these rules, they now load correctly instead of being treated as unknown entries. The change includes tests confirming both rules are recognized.

prs.title: port(§38k-7): register LoopCondition + TimeSpanCondition prototypes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence engine now recognizes two basic stopping rules for a group of steps: "repeat this a set number of times" and "keep going for a set amount of time." Saved sequences that use either rule will now load as the real rule instead of a placeholder. Rules that depend on telescope equipment still show up as unrecognized placeholders until later work connects them. Three new tests confirm the two rules are available.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-6 NINA type-name remap fix (#292)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merge brings the fix from #292 into the main line. Sequences imported from N.I.N.A., the app this project was forked from, can now be read correctly instead of every step coming through as an unrecognized placeholder. The old conversion only renamed part of each saved step's label, so nothing matched. It is identical to #292 and adds the same six tests.

prs.title: port(§38k-6): fix NINA → OpenAstroAra type-name remap in JsonCreationConverter
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where any sequence imported from N.I.N.A., the app this project was forked from, loaded with every step as an unrecognized placeholder. When the project was renamed, the code that translates old N.I.N.A. step names to the new ones only updated part of each name, so nothing ever matched. It now translates the full name, while keeping the older fallback for very old files. This unblocks the N.I.N.A. import feature working end to end, and six new tests cover the fix.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-5 end-to-end round-trip test (#290)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merge brings the test-only work from #290 into the main line, with no change to how the app behaves. It adds five checks confirming that simple sequences can be saved and loaded back without losing anything.

prs.title: port(§38k-5): end-to-end Serialize → Deserialize round-trip test
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Test-only change with no effect on how the app behaves. It adds five checks that save a simple sequence and load it back, confirming the step types, their order, names, and settings like wait times all come through unchanged. This confirms the earlier engine groundwork fits together for simple sequences that don't involve equipment.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-4 utility instruction prototypes (#288)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merge brings the work from #288 into the main line. The sequence engine now recognizes two basic steps that don't need any telescope equipment: adding a text note and waiting for a set amount of time. Sequences that use these steps will load as real steps instead of placeholders, and equipment-based steps such as taking an exposure will come in later work. Three new tests confirm both steps are available.

prs.title: port(§38k-4): register Annotation + WaitForTimeSpan instruction prototypes
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now recognize two simple sequence steps that don't need any telescope equipment: a comment-style note and a fixed-length wait. Before this, these steps in a saved sequence were treated as unrecognized placeholders. The tests confirm the server knows about both steps, but not yet that they load correctly from inside a real saved sequence; the description says that check will come once a real sample sequence is available. Steps that control equipment, such as taking an exposure or changing a filter, are still not recognized.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-3 structural container prototypes (#286)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the change from #286 into the main porting branch. The server now recognizes the three basic 'grouping' blocks that every saved sequence starts with, so it no longer treats the whole sequence as unrecognized. The actual steps inside those groups are still loaded as placeholders for now.

prs.title: port(§38k-3): register structural container prototypes in HeadlessSequencerFactory
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the server reads a saved imaging sequence, it now recognizes the three basic 'grouping' blocks that every sequence starts with: the top-level block, a run-in-order block, and a run-side-by-side block. Before this, the server gave up at the very top of every sequence and treated it as unrecognized. Individual steps like taking exposures are still loaded as placeholders until later updates add them. Anything the server doesn't recognize is still handled safely without crashing.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-2 HeadlessSequencerFactory wired into DI (#284)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the change from #284 into the main porting branch. The server gets a lightweight 'catalog' of sequence building blocks that works without the desktop app's user interface and settings. The catalog starts out empty, so for now every saved sequence still loads as an unrecognized placeholder.

prs.title: port(§38k-2): HeadlessSequencerFactory wired into DI
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds a lightweight 'catalog' of sequence building blocks to the server, which lets the server read saved sequences without depending on the old desktop app's screens and settings. It also turns on the sequence reader from #282 inside the running server. The catalog starts out empty, so for now every saved sequence still loads as an unrecognized placeholder, and nothing in this change actually uses the reader yet. This is groundwork for the real sequence engine.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38k-1 SequenceBodyDeserializer (#282)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the change from #282 into the main porting branch. It adds the first piece of the real sequence engine: a reader that turns a saved sequence file into something the server can work with. If the file contains steps the server doesn't recognize, the reader keeps them as placeholders instead of crashing. If the file is broken, it reports a clear error. The reader is not switched on in the running server yet; that happens in a later change.

prs.title: port(§38k-1): SequenceBodyDeserializer wraps SequenceJsonConverter
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the first piece of the real sequence engine: a component that reads a saved imaging sequence and turns it into the internal structure the engine will run. It handles unexpected input without crashing. Unrecognized step types become an "unknown" placeholder, and badly formed files produce an error message. It is not switched on in the app yet, and nothing actually runs sequences so far. That depends on equipment connections that will come in later changes.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-9 §51 startup diagnostic (#280)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings the change from #280 into the main branch. When the app starts and finds that the saved record of a running sequence was damaged, it now also logs a red, already-resolved entry in the diagnostics history. This is in addition to the inbox notification. The code is identical to #280.

prs.title: port(§38j-9): emit §51 diagnostic event on reconciler Corrupt outcome
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app starts and finds that the saved record of a previously running sequence is damaged, it now adds an entry to the diagnostics history as well as the inbox notification. The entry is marked red but already resolved, because the damaged file was already moved aside or deleted automatically. It therefore shows up in history rather than as an open problem. A sequence that was simply interrupted still produces only the inbox notification.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: PORT_PROGRESS.md refresh through §38j-8
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It lists the recent batch of sequence-library and startup-recovery work and marks startup recovery as done. It also notes that the next major step is wiring up the real sequence engine. No code changed.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-7 + §38j-8 startup reconciliation (#276 + #278)
prs.author: joeytroy
