prs.summary: Brings two related changes into the main branch. The first is a startup check that detects whether a sequence was cut off by a crash or shutdown. If so, it clears the leftover record so the sequence is never resumed automatically, and it sets aside a damaged record for later inspection. The second posts an inbox notification about what happened: a warning for an interrupted sequence, or a critical alert for a damaged record. Users therefore learn about the interruption instead of it being noted only in logs.

prs.title: port(§38j-8): emit §46 notification on reconciler Interrupted/Corrupt
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app starts and finds that a sequence was cut off last time, users now get an inbox notification instead of the event only appearing in internal logs. An interrupted sequence produces a warning that includes how far it got. A damaged saved record produces a critical alert explaining that the record was set aside and the progress is lost. In both cases the sequence is not resumed automatically, and the user must restart it themselves.

prs.title: port(§38j-7): SequenceStartupReconciler — §28.2 daemon-startup reconciliation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the server starts up, it now checks whether an imaging sequence was still running when it last shut down. If so, it logs a warning and clears the leftover record so the warning doesn't repeat on every restart. The sequence is deliberately not resumed automatically; the user has to restart it. If the leftover record is damaged, it is set aside with a timestamped name for later inspection, or deleted if that fails, so startup is never blocked. Users are not notified yet: the result only goes to the server log, and on-screen notifications are planned for later.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-6 ActiveSequenceCheckpoint (#274)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the work from #274 into the main line. While an imaging sequence runs, the server now keeps a small file on disk recording what is running and how far it has got. The file is removed when the run ends for any reason. This lets the server tell after a crash that a sequence was cut short.

prs.title: port(§38j-6): ActiveSequenceCheckpoint — active/current.json per §28.1
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: While an imaging sequence runs, the server now saves a small progress record to disk. The record is written at the start and updated after each step. It is removed when the run finishes, is stopped, or fails. The file is written so that a crash mid-save can't leave it half-written, which gives a later startup check a reliable way to spot interrupted runs. This change only covers writing the record; the startup check that reads it arrived separately in #276.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-5 mock sequencer reads real instruction count (#272)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the work from #272 into the main line. The stand-in sequence runner now steps through as many instructions as the saved sequence actually contains, instead of always pretending there are 5. Progress numbers shown to users are therefore realistic for each sequence.

prs.title: port(§38j-5): mock sequencer reads real instruction count from stored body
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The temporary, simulated sequence runner used until the real one is connected now reads the saved sequence and steps through its actual number of instructions. Before, it always ran exactly 5, so progress totals like "3 of 12" now match the real sequence. If a sequence can't be found or has no instructions, it still falls back to 5. The change also untangles a startup dependency between the sequence library and the runner so the two can reference each other.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-3 SchemaValidator capturable-instruction check (#269)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saving or editing a sequence is now rejected if it contains no actual capture steps, so empty sequences can't be stored. Templates are exempt, since they may start out as empty shells. The description doesn't mention a second change the code also makes: the sequence list now shows each sequence's current run status, such as running or paused. This lets the interface display a "running" badge without checking each sequence one by one.

prs.title: port(§38j-4): list endpoint surfaces CurrentRunState per item
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The saved-sequences list now shows whether each sequence is currently running, paused, or stopped. The app can show a "running" badge directly in the list instead of checking each sequence one by one. The server looks up the status of every sequence each time the list loads, and new automated tests cover this.

prs.title: port(§38j-3): SchemaValidator gains capturable-instruction reachability check
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now refuses to save a new or edited sequence that contains no steps, so empty sequences are caught before they are stored. There is an option to skip this check for unfinished templates, but nothing in this change uses it yet except the tests. The check is looser than the description suggests: it counts any step anywhere in the sequence, including non-imaging steps like slewing or cooling, rather than confirming a picture will actually be taken.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38j-2 SequenceBodyInspector (#267)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the earlier change (#267) into the main line. The saved-sequences list now shows real step and target counts for each sequence instead of zeros. The code is identical to #267.

prs.title: port(§38j-2): SequenceBodyInspector — populate InstructionCount + TargetCount
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The saved-sequences list now shows how many steps and how many targets each sequence contains, instead of always showing zero. The counts are a best guess based on how each part of a saved sequence is labelled, not a full reading of the sequence, so unusual sequences could be counted slightly wrong. New automated tests cover the common cases.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38i FilenameTemplateValidator (#264)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges #264, which adds a check for the pattern used to name saved image files. The check flags unrecognized placeholders and flags patterns missing a frame number or timestamp, which would let new images overwrite earlier ones. The check is not yet connected to anything, so users won't see its errors yet. The merge also quietly includes the build change from #266 that turns off the server's compact build mode, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(§38j-1): pause PublishAot on Server to unblock §38 orchestrator wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This build setting change turns off a compact packaging mode for the server. The packaged server becomes larger (about 156 MB) and starts slightly slower, but it can now read sequence files saved in the original NINA format, which the upcoming sequence-running work needs. The team plans to restore the compact mode later, around version 0.1.0.

prs.title: Update copyright headers to 2025-2026 year range
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updated the copyright notice at the top of every project file from "2025" to "2025-2026", including the templates used to create new files. The code shows only these notice lines changed, so nothing works differently. Third-party license files were left alone.

prs.title: port(§38i): FilenameTemplateValidator — §38.6.1 sequence-start template check
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a check on the filename pattern used to name captured images. It rejects placeholders the app doesn't recognize, and it rejects patterns without a frame number or timestamp, which would let images overwrite each other. The description says this runs before a sequence starts so users get a clear error up front, but this change only adds the check and its tests. Nothing calls it yet, so users won't see it until a later change connects it.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38h NINA import enhancements (#262)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings the NINA import improvements from #262 into the main line, and the code is identical to #262. Imported NINA sequences now get the version label the app requires, so they save cleanly the first time. A copy of each original uploaded file is also kept in a dated folder for audit and recovery.

prs.title: port(§38h): NINA import — schemaVersion backfill + raw-upload persistence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Importing a sequence from NINA now adds the version label the app requires, which NINA files lack, so the imported sequence saves without errors. The original uploaded file is also saved into a dated "imported" folder so it can be reviewed or recovered later; if that save fails, the import still goes ahead. The import still does not translate NINA's steps or equipment, which the description lists as future work. However, the old warning telling users the import was only a placeholder has been removed, so users are no longer told this.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38g disk template loader (#260)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings the sequence template loading from #260 into the main line, and the code is identical to #260. The app now picks up extra sequence templates saved as files in the profile's templates folder, alongside the three built-in ones. This means the installer can ship new or updated starter templates without a code change.

prs.title: port(§38g): load disk-shipped sequence templates from §38.2 templates/ dir
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence template picker now includes templates saved as files in the profile's templates folder, alongside the three built-in ones. A file with the same name as a built-in replaces it, so the installer can update starter templates without a new build. Broken template files are skipped with a logged warning instead of causing errors.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38f dir scaffold (#258)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges #258 into the main line with the same code. When the app starts, it now creates all four folders where saved observing sequences will live: the main library, imported sequences, templates, and in-progress sequences. Before, it only created the library folder. Upcoming import, template, and resume features can now count on the other three folders already being there.

prs.title: port(§38f): scaffold all four §38.2 sequence subdirs on startup
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app starts, it now sets up the complete folder layout for saved observing sequences. That means an imported folder, a templates folder, and an in-progress folder alongside the existing library folder. Nothing uses the new folders yet. This is groundwork so the upcoming import, template, and resume features share one layout instead of each creating its own. Two small tests check that the folders are created and that restarting with existing folders is safe.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38e schema validation + 422 wiring (#256)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges #256 into the main line with the same code. When someone creates or edits a sequence, the server now makes a basic check first. The sequence must be a proper structured document tagged with the current format version. If it fails, the server rejects it with a short error message instead of saving it. Deeper checks, such as whether the named equipment and filters actually exist, are still to come.

prs.title: port(§38e): SequenceSchemaValidator — §38.5 structural validation + 422 wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When someone creates or edits a sequence, the server now makes a basic check first. The sequence must be a proper structured document tagged with the current format version. If it fails, the server rejects it with a short, readable error instead of saving it. Edits that don't change the sequence contents skip the check. As the description says, this is only a first layer; checks for real equipment, filter names, and endless loops come later.

prs.title: Add ZWO ASIair Plus (RK3568) Switch driver — ConformU 4.3.0 ✓
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for the four 12-volt power outputs on the ZWO ASIair Plus (the RK3568 model). Astronomy software can now switch each port on or off, or dim it by pulsing the power rapidly, at a default of 200 times per second. It passed the standard compatibility test with no problems and was tried on real hardware. The PR also adds a web setup option, fixes per-port settings for both ASIair models so they are kept after saving and reloading, grants the needed hardware access permission automatically in the setup script, and adds detailed setup and troubleshooting notes. Most of the actual driver code was cut from the diff provided, so only the documentation, build, and permission-file parts could be checked directly.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38d wire template-variable substitution (#254)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges #254 into the main line. Creating a sequence from one of the three built-in templates now fills in placeholders, such as the target name, with values the user supplies, for example turning the target into "M31". Until now the templates were empty; they now have simple stand-in contents rather than full real sequences. The user's values are inserted without special handling, so a name containing a quote mark can break the result. When that happens, the code quietly falls back to the unfilled template instead of reporting an error. The code comments say later validation will catch leftover placeholders, but the current validation (#256) only checks the format version and would not flag them.

prs.title: port(§38d): wire SequenceTemplateVariables.Substitute into template instantiate flow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Creating a new sequence from a built-in template now fills in the details you provide, such as the target name, so the saved sequence contains your real values instead of blank placeholders. The three built-in templates now include sample settings, but only the target name is actually fillable; the filter set, frame counts and exposure times are fixed values. If a value would break the saved format, for example a target name containing a quotation mark, the system quietly saves the unfilled template instead. Any placeholders left unfilled are not reported back to the user yet, even though the groundwork for that exists.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38c template-variable substitutor (#252)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This brings the placeholder-filling helper from #252 into the main line. It adds a behind-the-scenes tool that swaps markers like the target name in a sequence template for real values, along with 10 tests. On its own it does not change anything for users yet.

prs.title: port(§38c): SequenceTemplateVariables — §38.6 {{token}} substitutor + 10 tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a behind-the-scenes helper that fills in blanks in sequence templates, such as target name, sky position, filter set and exposure time, with real values. Blanks with no supplied value are left as they are so they can be flagged later. It includes 10 tests but is not yet connected to anything users can reach; that hookup came in #254.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: FilenameTemplateSanitizer §38.6.1 (#250)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This brings the filename clean-up helper from #250 into the main line. The helper makes image filenames safe to save on Linux, Mac and Windows. It also fills in stand-in words when information is missing and keeps file paths under 200 characters. It includes 10 tests and is not yet used by the actual image capture process.

prs.title: port(§38b): FilenameTemplateSanitizer — §38.6.1 sanitization helper + 10 tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a behind-the-scenes helper that cleans up image filenames so they save correctly on Linux, Mac and Windows. It replaces forbidden characters with underscores and uses stand-in words like "noFilter" or "noTemp" when camera details are missing. It also shortens overly long paths, trimming the target name first so the frame number and date stay intact. It comes with 10 tests but is not yet wired into image capture, which is planned for later.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: FileSequenceService — §38.2 filesystem-backed library (#248)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved observing sequences are now stored as files on disk instead of only in memory, so they survive a restart of the server; previously they were lost every time it restarted. This covers only the main sequence library. Actually running sequences still uses a stand-in, and the library list always shows zero instructions and zero targets per sequence. The list also returns everything in one go, with no page-by-page loading.

prs.title: port(§38a): FileSequenceService — filesystem-backed sequence library per §38.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Saved observing sequences are now stored as files on disk instead of only in memory, so they survive a restart of the server. Before this, anything you saved was lost whenever the server restarted. Actually starting and controlling a sequence run is still a stand-in and will be replaced in a later change. A small fix also makes the reported size of a shared sequence reflect its real contents instead of a fixed made-up number.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: close last Phase 15 sweep TODO (#246)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the change from #246 to the main branch. It records that a suspected problem with the format of image filename templates was checked and was not a real problem. No program code changed. The diff also refreshes the project status notes: it marks earlier cleanup tasks as done and updates the list of upcoming work, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(tracking): close filename-token-form TODO — render side uses $$TOKEN$$
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A note-keeping update to the project's to-do list. Someone had worried that image filename templates used the wrong placeholder format. The team checked and confirmed the current format is correct, so no fix is needed and the item is marked done.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Server ProjectReferences wired to 7 NINA libs (#244)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the change from #244 to the main branch. The server can now draw on all seven core libraries it inherited from the original NINA astronomy software. The diff also updates the project status notes, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(server): wire ProjectReferences to the 7 NINA-inherited libs per playbook §8
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal build setup change that connects the server to the seven core libraries inherited from NINA, covering things like equipment control, plate solving, and sequencing. This was blocked until recently because those libraries only worked on Windows. The change only links them in; the server does not use any new features from them yet, and image-processing parts are still unfinished placeholders.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 0.5p2 net10.0 conversion (#242)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves a large conversion (#242) to the main branch. It makes all of the inherited NINA libraries run on any operating system without a screen, instead of only on Windows. To get there, it removes about 400 files, mostly the old Windows desktop interface, which unblocks running the server on devices like the Raspberry Pi. No code diff was available, so this summary relies on the description alone.

prs.title: port(0.5p2): complete net10.0 conversion of all 7 NINA-inherited projects per playbook §5.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This large cleanup converts all the older projects inherited from NINA so they no longer depend on Windows. That lets the background service run the full sequencing and equipment stack on a Raspberry Pi. About 54,000 lines were removed, mostly old Windows screen code, plus a few dropped extras such as the update checker, plugin support and the online plate-solving service. The image-analysis features (star detection, focus aids and raw camera file reading) now fail with an error until a replacement library is wired in, and 46 tests still fail on non-Windows machines. No code diff was provided, so these details come from the description alone. The description's count of about 280 files also doesn't match the 496 files the PR reports.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: per-enum AOT-safe enum converters (#240)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the promotion to the main branch of the change in #240, with identical code. It changes how the server turns named values like device types and sequence states into text, so the project can later be packaged as a faster, self-contained build. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: port(server): per-enum AOT-safe JsonStringEnumConverter registrations
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to how the server turns eight kinds of named values (like device type, connection state and sequence state) into text in its responses. The output stays the same, but the new setup works with the faster, self-contained build style the team plans to use, and a suppressed warning is gone. The last open item on the team's hardening checklist is now marked done.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: real daemon_git_sha (#238)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the promotion to the main branch of the change in #238, with identical code. The server's version information now reports the actual code revision it was built from instead of the word "placeholder".

prs.title: port(server): real daemon_git_sha on /server/versions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's version information, used by the app's About screen and its compatibility check, now reports the actual code revision it was built from. Before, it always said "placeholder". If the build didn't come from the project's repository, as with some installer packages, it reports "unknown" instead.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §38 mock sequencer (#236)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This promotion of #236 adds a pretend sequencer to the server so the app's sequencing screens can be tried out end to end without real telescope equipment. Starting a sequence runs five fake one-second "captures" that can be paused, resumed, stopped or aborted. Live updates are sent to the app at each step, so the progress display behaves like the real thing. Real equipment control comes later.

prs.title: port(sequencer): §38 mock sequencer with run-state + WS events
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now has a pretend sequencer, so the app's sequencer screen can be tried out end to end without any real telescope or camera attached. Starting a sequence runs five fake one-second "captures" that can be paused, resumed, stopped, or aborted. The app receives live updates at each step and can also ask for the current status at any time. The description says starting an already-running sequence returns the original operation ID, but the code does not store that ID, so a repeat start appears to get a new acknowledgement instead.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: 3rd-party-licenses.txt — §15 ship-list complete
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This promotes the new third-party license list from #234 to the main branch. It is the last of the release paperwork the team planned for the first pre-release, so that set of documents is now complete.

prs.title: port(release): 3rd-party-licenses.txt inventory
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a hand-written list of the outside software bundled with the server and the app, along with each one's license. This lets the first release meet its legal and attribution obligations. It is the last missing item on the release document checklist. Future releases are meant to generate this list automatically.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: tracking refresh (#232)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This promotes #232, an update to the project's internal progress notes, to the main branch. It changes only documentation.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh for §60.9 polish + Phase 15 docs batch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Updates the internal progress tracker to record recent work: the first release documents and improvements to the server's status report. It also names the sequence runner as the next major piece of work. This is a documentation-only change.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 15 release-prep docs (#228 + #229 + #230)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This promotes three new release documents to the main branch. The first is an attribution and licensing notice crediting the project this one is based on. The second is release notes for the first pre-release that explain what works and what is still a placeholder. The third is a step-by-step guide for installing and running the server on a Raspberry Pi, covering storage setup, backup power advice, logs, and updates.

prs.title: port(release): DEPLOY.md — Pi installation guide
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a step-by-step guide for installing the Ara server on a Raspberry Pi. It covers a quick install that starts the server automatically, which folders it uses, and how to set up and format a USB SSD for saving captures (the server won't start without one set up correctly). It also covers an optional backup power recommendation, where to find logs, and how to update or remove the software. This is documentation only; nothing about how the software behaves changed.

prs.title: port(release): RELEASE_NOTES.md for v0.0.1-ara.1
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds release notes for the first pre-release, v0.0.1-ara.1, which will be shown on the GitHub release page. They explain that the server side works (image storage, image previews, settings, notifications, stats), while real camera and mount control and the automated imaging sequence are still stand-ins. They also list known gaps: no live captures yet, and one part of the codebase still does not build. Documentation only.

prs.title: port(release): §17.2 NOTICE.md — attribution + license inventory
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a formal notice file stating that Ara is based on the N.I.N.A. astronomy software and keeps its open-source license and original copyright credits. It also lists the main outside components the app relies on and includes trademark disclaimers for N.I.N.A. and Raspberry Pi. This is legal and attribution paperwork ahead of the first release, with no change to the software itself.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §60.9 server-state polish (#224-#226)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings three earlier changes into the main line together. The server's status report now includes real values: a live reconnect marker, an overall health reading, and counts of unread and urgent notifications. The server also warns connected apps just before it restarts. Equipment status and the running imaging sequence are still reported as empty, because those features don't exist yet.

prs.title: port(server): §34.7 server.restart_imminent WS event
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When someone asks the server to restart, it now first tells connected apps that a restart is coming, with the reason and the expected time. That way the app can show a "restarting…" message instead of a generic lost-connection warning. A code comment claims the warning goes out before the server answers the request, but the code actually sends it in the background, so that ordering isn't guaranteed. The reason text is only partly cleaned up, so a reason containing something like a line break would cause the warning to be quietly skipped, though the restart still happens.

prs.title: port(state): real diagnostics_health + notifications_summary on /server/state
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's status report used to leave its health and notification sections empty. They are now filled with real data: an overall health color, counts of open and recent issues, and counts of unread, critical and warning notifications. If looking up that data fails, the section falls back to empty so the status report itself never breaks. The unread count stops at 200. Unlike the critical and warning counts, it also includes notifications the user has already dismissed.

prs.title: port(state): §60.9.6 real ws_resume_token from broadcaster seq
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's status report now gives connected apps a real "resume point" based on the latest event it has sent, instead of a fake placeholder value. After a dropped connection, an app can use it to catch up on events it missed. The only check listed was that the project builds; no tests were added.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §65.4 storage-pressure eviction (#222) — §65 server-side closeout
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This routine merge brings in the low-disk-space cleanup of extra preview images from #222. The authors say it completes the server-side work for the image "stretch" (brightness and contrast) preview feature. The code changes are identical to #222.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.4 storage-pressure eviction + variant.evicted WS event
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the disk holding captured images drops below 1 GB of free space, the server now deletes all extra saved preview images for a frame, rather than only trimming them to the usual limit of six. Original image files are left alone. Connected apps now get a notice each time a preview image is removed, including the reason. The space check only runs when previews for a particular frame are being tidied, so it is not a disk-wide cleanup, and the only testing was a build plus a manual check under normal disk conditions.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §65.5 batch worker + §65.7 terminal events (#219 + #220)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This routine merge brings in #219 and #220, which let users re-process all images in a session with new brightness and contrast settings as a background task. Users can check the task's progress, cancel it, and get notified when it finishes or fails.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.7 terminal restretch WS events
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When re-processing a session's images finishes, connected apps now get a "complete" notice with how many images were done and how long it took, or a "failed" notice with the error. A "complete" notice is also sent when the user cancels, so the app can clear its progress banner, even though the task itself is then recorded as cancelled. Errors on individual images are skipped quietly, so a "failed" notice should be rare. The code also shows each run only takes the first 200 images in a session.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.5 batch re-stretch job system
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now ask the server to re-process every image in a session with new brightness and contrast settings, and it does the work in the background. The app can check how far along the task is or cancel it, and asking again while one is already running returns the existing task instead of starting a duplicate. Task records are kept only in memory and are lost when the server restarts. At this stage only progress updates were sent; finished and failed notices came later in #220.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §65.4 cache + §65.6 DELETE + tracking refresh (#215-#217)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles three earlier changes into the main branch. Image previews are now saved to disk and reused instead of being redrawn on every view, there is a new way to clear those saved previews for a frame, and the project status notes were updated. The code matches the description, with no extra changes.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh for §65 + §28.8 + §13 + cache batch
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This only updates the project progress notes. It records the recently finished work on image brightness adjustment, recovering lost images at startup, and server restarts, and it names the camera-sequence engine as the next major piece. No software behavior changed.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.6 DELETE /api/v1/frames/{id}/preview/variants
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a way to clear all saved alternate preview images for one captured frame, so they are redrawn fresh the next time someone views them. This is useful after changing default brightness settings, or for a future 'force redraw' button in the app. It reports 'not found' only when the frame is unknown, and it quietly skips files it cannot delete, so the request always appears to succeed.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.4 variant cache — disk-backed, LRU-evicted
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Frame previews in different brightness styles are now saved to disk next to the original image and reused, instead of being recalculated on every request. This makes repeat viewing much faster. Each frame keeps at most six saved versions, and the least recently viewed ones are removed first. One gap: saved previews are labeled only by style name, so changing default settings such as contrast strength keeps showing old versions until the saved ones are cleared. Testing was limited to confirming the project builds.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §65.2 + #211 + §28.8 + §13 (#210-#213)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles four earlier changes into the main branch. Each profile now stores default image brightness settings, and those settings are used when showing previews. At startup, the server now deletes leftover half-written files and adds any image files missing from the catalog. The restart button now actually restarts the server on Linux. The startup scan runs before the server accepts connections, so a large image folder could delay startup.

prs.title: port(server): §13 systemd-driven /server/restart
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 'restart server' request now actually restarts the server on Linux machines like the Raspberry Pi, after a two-second pause so the app gets its confirmation first. On other systems, or where the restart command is not permitted, nothing happens, but the app is still told the request was accepted. The 'restart when idle' option still does nothing, because it must wait until the software can tell whether a capture is in progress.

prs.title: port(catalog): §28.8 startup orphan scan + stale .tmp sweep
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now does a one-time cleanup and recovery pass on the captures folder every time it starts, before it begins handling requests. It deletes leftover temporary files more than five minutes old, which are assumed to come from interrupted saves. It also adds any image files it finds that are missing from the catalog, filling in details from the image itself or falling back to the file date and "Unknown Target". If the storage folder can't be written to, the server only writes a warning to its log and does not alert the user. Recovering real images hasn't been tested yet, because nothing produces real captures so far.

prs.title: port(stretch): thread profile stretch_defaults through preview resolution
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The display settings saved in a user's profile now actually control how frame previews look when the request doesn't pick its own style. Before this, those saved settings had no effect. The code only partly matches the description for thumbnails: they follow the profile's chosen style, but ignore the profile's other brightness and contrast values. One side effect is that manual-mode previews now start from slightly different default brightness limits than before.

prs.title: port(profile): §65.2 stretch_defaults profile section
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Each user profile now has a new saved section for how captured images are brightened for display: the default style for regular photos, starting values for manual sliders, and a few tuning values. The settings can be read and changed through the server, and they survive a restart. This PR only stores the settings; they don't yet change the images shown, which a follow-up PR handles. According to the description, profile files saved before this change will be treated as invalid and reset to defaults, which is acceptable only because there are no real users yet.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §65 stretch algorithms + preview pipeline (#207 + #208)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a periodic merge into the main branch that brings in the image brightening tools (#207) and the real preview pipeline (#208). After it lands, frame previews and thumbnails are generated from the actual captured image files. When a file can't be found, a tiny blank placeholder is shown instead. The automated build now also runs the new image-brightening tests.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65 preview pipeline — FITS → stretch → JPEG
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Frame previews and thumbnails now show real pictures made from the captured image files, replacing the blank placeholder. Calibration frames always use a plain, unenhanced look, and thumbnails are shrunk to at most 320 pixels. If a file is missing, the blank placeholder is still shown so the app doesn't display a broken image. The code does not handle a file that exists but is damaged or unreadable, so such a file would likely cause an error instead of falling back to the placeholder.

prs.title: port(stretch): §65.1 stretch algorithms — pure-math + tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds a new building block with seven ways to brighten raw astronomy images so faint detail becomes visible on screen, along with automated tests for it. Nothing in the app uses it yet; later PRs connect it to previews. One small mismatch: the description says all seven methods are tested for full brightness range, but the test actually covers six and leaves out manual mode, which is tested separately.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §51 diagnostics + tracking refresh (#204 + #205)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles two earlier changes into the main release line: the diagnostics panel now keeps its data in the app's saved database instead of in temporary memory, and the project's progress notes were updated. In practice, the diagnostics setting you choose (such as off, observe, suggest, or auto-correct) now survives a restart, where before it quietly reset every time. The panel still shows three sample events for now, because the part that actually watches the equipment and records real problems has not been built yet.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh for §72 + §46.5 + §50 + §51 SQLite swaps
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It records that several features now save their data permanently: image file storage, notifications, statistics, and diagnostics. It also names the next planned work: better image previews and the component that runs an imaging session from start to finish.

prs.title: port(diagnostics): §51 SqliteDiagnosticsService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The diagnostics panel, which reports the health of an imaging session and lists problems, now stores its events and its operating setting in the app's saved database. Before, it used fixed demo data held in memory. The chosen mode now stays in place after a restart, where previously it always went back to 'Observe.' The panel still shows three sample events at first startup, since the part that detects and records real problems will arrive later.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §46.5 notifications + §50 stats SQLite-backed (#201 + #202)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles two earlier changes into the main release line. Notifications and notification preferences are now saved permanently, so they survive a restart. The statistics screens are now calculated from the real catalog of captured images instead of made-up sample numbers. Some charts, such as focus versus temperature, will stay empty until the app starts recording that information.

prs.title: port(stats): §50 SqliteStatsService — catalog-backed aggregations
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The statistics screens now show numbers calculated from the images actually recorded in the catalog, replacing the invented sample figures used before. This covers totals, per-target summaries, guiding accuracy, image quality, best frames, a calendar view, and a spreadsheet export. The focus-versus-temperature chart and some finer guiding details are empty for now because that data is not recorded yet. The 'last session score' figure is also left blank, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(notifications): §46.5 SqliteNotificationService — persistent log
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Notifications and notification preferences are now saved in the app's database, so they are kept after a restart. Before, they were held only in memory and reset each time the app restarted. Marking notifications as read, dismissing them, and changing preferences all now last, and three sample notifications are added the first time the app runs.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §72 FITS storage series (#196–#199) — last 501 closed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This release bundle adds support for FITS, the standard astronomy image file format, and makes the "download frame" feature work. The software can now save and read these image files safely, so a crash mid-save won't leave a half-written file. The download feature was the last one that only replied "not built yet." In practice, downloads will return "not found" until the app actually captures and saves images, which is the next planned piece of work, and image previews and thumbnails still show a placeholder rather than real pictures.

prs.title: port(fits): §72 wire /api/v1/frames/{id}/download — last 501 closed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "download frame" feature now sends the actual saved image file for a frame instead of replying "not built yet," which was the last unfinished feature of this kind. If the frame isn't in the catalog or its file is missing from disk, the user gets a clear "not found." Because the app doesn't capture and save real images yet, downloads will return "not found" for now. The automated checks were updated to expect this new behavior.

prs.title: port(fits): §72 FitsImage managed wrapper + atomic-write + tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the ability to create and read FITS astronomy image files, including setting and reading the descriptive information stored with each image. Images are first saved to a temporary file and only given their real name once fully written, so a crash never leaves a broken image behind. Leftover temporary files from an earlier crash are cleaned up automatically. Five automated tests confirm images survive a save-and-reload unchanged, and the build system now installs the image library those tests need.

prs.title: port(fits): §72 scaffold — OpenAstroAra.Fits project + CFitsIO P/Invoke
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Groundwork only: this sets up a new, cross-platform component that connects the app to a standard library for reading and writing FITS astronomy image files. Nothing uses it yet, so there is no change users can see. The automated build now also checks that this new component compiles.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh for §28 catalog series + Phase 14c/14d
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It records the recently finished image catalog database work and the expanded automated testing across operating systems and processor types. It names FITS image storage as the next major task.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §28 frame catalog DB series (#190–#194)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The app's catalog of imaging sessions and frames is now stored in a real database file, replacing temporary sample data that was lost on every restart. Rating, tagging and deleting frames now actually save changes, and session summaries are calculated from the stored frames. A small set of sample frames is still loaded on first run for testing. Not mentioned in the description, the change also fixes where the app keeps its data when running in a Docker container with no proper home folder, which could otherwise have stopped it from saving anything.

prs.title: port(catalog): delete PlaceholderFrameRepository + PlaceholderSessionService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This removes the temporary stand-in code that used to serve fake frame and session data. The app's image library and imaging-session views now run entirely on the real saved catalog, so data survives restarts and edits actually stick. It also updates two outdated code comments. Previews are still a tiny placeholder image until real image rendering is built.

prs.title: port(catalog): §28 SqliteSessionService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imaging sessions are now read from the real saved catalog instead of a fixed fake example. The session list and detail views work out the target name, frame counts, and filters used from the stored frames, and the focus-quality analysis for a session now returns a proper 'not found' when the session doesn't exist. The 'resume target' and 're-stretch' actions still only acknowledge the request without doing anything, because the systems they depend on aren't built yet.

prs.title: port(catalog): §28 bulk ops actually mutate the catalog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Bulk actions on captured frames now take effect: rating, adding or removing tags, and deleting frames change the saved catalog, where before they were only acknowledged and ignored. Tag changes ignore upper and lower case, so 'Favorite' and 'favorite' count as the same tag. The 'also delete from disk' option is accepted but does nothing yet. Deleting only removes the catalog entry, not the image file.

prs.title: port(catalog): §28 SqliteFrameRepository — read path + sample seed
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Frame listing and frame details now come from the real saved catalog instead of hard-coded sample data. On first startup the catalog is filled with the same three sample frames and one sample session, so existing checks and UI testing keep working. Bulk edits, image previews, and downloads were still placeholders at this stage.

prs.title: port(catalog): §28 SQLite scaffold — IAraDatabase + schema + PRAGMAs
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This lays the groundwork for a permanent catalog of imaging sessions and frames. The server now creates a small local database file at startup, sets it up for reliable use, and stops immediately if that setup fails. Nothing uses the database yet. The change also includes an unmentioned fix to where the server keeps its data when run in a minimal Docker container, so it falls back to a writable temporary folder. The automated checks now confirm the database file is created.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 14c + 14d CI matrix expansion (#187 + #188)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to the automated checks, bundling two earlier updates. The client app's tests now run on Linux, macOS, and Windows instead of Linux only. The server's ARM build is now started in an emulated container and checked to confirm it responds correctly. Nothing changes for users.

prs.title: ci(phase-14d): server-e2e — docker run arm64 image + health probe
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated checks now actually start the server's build for small ARM-based computers (like a Raspberry Pi) and confirm it responds, rather than only checking that it builds. This catches problems that only show up on that kind of hardware before they reach users. The description says the check looks for a version field, but the code actually checks for the server's unique ID instead. This is a behind-the-scenes testing change with no effect on the app itself.

prs.title: ci(phase-14c): client-test cross-platform matrix (linux + macos + windows)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The automated tests for the desktop client app now run on Linux, Mac, and Windows instead of only Linux. The app ships on all three, so problems specific to one system should now be caught early. A failure on one system no longer hides the results from the others. This is an internal testing change only.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: doc cleanup (#184 + #185)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This moves two documentation-only updates (#184 and #185) into the main branch. One refreshes the project progress page and the other rewords outdated notes in the code. The app's behavior does not change.

prs.title: port(docs): replace stale Phase 13.x doc comments
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This rewords eight outdated notes in the server code that said unfinished work would arrive in an earlier project phase that has already ended. They now say the work comes in the later phase that builds the real, non-placeholder pieces. This is a wording-only cleanup with no change to how the app works.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh PORT_PROGRESS.md for post-§60.9 placeholder cleanup
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The project progress page now records the four recent changes that filled in the last batch of unfinished server features with stand-in responses. It notes that only one feature is still unbuilt: downloading an image file, which needs real file storage. It also says the next steps need real infrastructure decisions rather than more stand-ins. This is a documentation-only update.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §40.7/§40.8 + session ops + server restart placeholders (#179-#182)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Several server features that used to return a "not built yet" error now give working responses, so the client app can be developed against them. These features are: a report on image sharpness trends across an imaging session, rating, tagging, or deleting many images at once, resuming a target or reprocessing images in a session, and restarting the server. Most of these are stand-ins that say "request accepted" without doing anything yet. For example, the restart request does not actually restart the server. Downloading an image file is now the only feature still marked as not built, and the automated checks were updated to match.

prs.title: port(server): /server/restart + /restart-on-idle placeholder wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's "restart now" and "restart when idle" requests now return a proper "request accepted" reply instead of a "not built yet" error. This is still a stand-in: the server does not actually restart, and the optional reason is accepted but not used. The real restart is planned for a later hardening phase. For now, the companion app can build its restart-pending banner against realistic replies.

prs.title: port(images): session resume-target + restretch placeholder wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The requests to resume a paused target in an imaging session and to re-stretch a session's images (adjust their brightness and contrast for display) now reply "accepted" instead of "not built yet." If the session doesn't exist, they now return "not found." These are still stand-ins that don't actually resume or reprocess anything. The real work depends on the sequence planner and image-processing pieces that haven't been built yet.

prs.title: port(images): frame bulk ops placeholder + endpoint wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Bulk actions on captured frames (rating, tagging, and deleting many at once) now reply "accepted" instead of "not built yet." This lets the companion app's library screen be built against realistic replies. These are still stand-ins, so nothing is actually rated, tagged, or deleted yet. The real behavior waits on the frame catalog database.

prs.title: port(images): hfr-analysis placeholder + smoke-gate probe migration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The session focus-quality report now works. It measures how sharp stars are across a session's frames and reports the average, how much it varies, and whether focus is improving, degrading, or stable over time. It is currently calculated only from the built-in sample session; any other session, including real ones, returns "not found." The automated build check was updated to test this report and now uses the frame-download feature as its example of something not yet built.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: WS handler sub-PR D + tracking refresh (#176 + #177)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a routine merge that brings two earlier changes into the main line. The first makes the server close live-update connections from apps that have stopped responding for 60 seconds, which completes the real-time connection work. The second is a progress-document update describing that work.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh PORT_PROGRESS.md for §60.9 WS upgrade handler closeout
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It records the completed real-time connection work, including which connection-closing cases are handled now and which are deferred. It also points "next up" at the remaining real-infrastructure tasks.

prs.title: port(ws): §60.9 heartbeat enforcement via KeepAliveTimeout (sub-PR D)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now drops a live-updates connection if the connected app goes silent for 60 seconds, so dead or frozen clients no longer tie up the server. This completes the four-part series that brought the live-updates connection online. The change itself is one setting that relies on built-in behavior, so it waits for any 60-second silence rather than counting two missed replies as the description suggests. Real-world testing of the timeout is deferred to a later phase, and access controls are still to come.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: §60.9 WS upgrade handler (sub-PRs A/B/C — #172/#173/#174)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges three earlier changes (#172, #173, #174) into the main line, so the server's live-updates connection is now actually working instead of returning a "not implemented" error. Apps can connect and receive events in real time, must state which protocol version they speak, and can catch up on events they missed after a brief disconnect. The automated build checks now confirm that connections are accepted and that connections without the version header are refused. Dropping unresponsive clients and access controls were still to come at this point.

prs.title: port(ws): §60.9 resume protocol (sub-PR C)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: An app that reconnects to the live-updates feed can now ask to catch up on events it missed while it was away. The server either replays those events, reports that the gap is too old or the request is malformed, or treats the connection as fresh if nothing is asked for within 5 seconds. The code also fixes a timing gap, which the description doesn't mention, where events arriving during the catch-up could be lost, and it makes sure none are sent twice. For now the catch-up marker is just the last event number the app saw. A proper test with a real client is deferred.

prs.title: port(ws): §60.9 X-Ara-WS-Version: 1 validation (sub-PR B)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now requires apps connecting to the live-updates feed to declare that they speak protocol version 1. Connections with a missing or wrong version are politely refused before they are established, which lets the format change safely in the future. The automated build checks now test both the accepted case and the refused case.

prs.title: port(ws): real /api/v1/ws upgrade handler — accept + drain channel (sub-PR A)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's live-updates connection now actually accepts connections and streams events to connected apps as they happen, replacing the previous "not implemented" response. The code also includes a change the description doesn't mention: previously, each event would have reached only one of several connected apps, and now every connected app gets every event. A slow app can't hold up the others. The automated build checks now verify that a connection can be opened.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13 placeholder library closeout (#169 + #170)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This wraps up Phase 13, which replaced unfinished server features with stand-ins that return realistic sample data, so the user interface can be exercised end to end before real hardware support exists. The final piece adds the behind-the-scenes machinery for broadcasting live events, which remembers the last 1,000 events so reconnecting apps can catch up. It also fixes the list of available event types, which had been failing every time, and adds a build check that watches for that failure. Nothing can connect to the live feed yet, and the project progress notes were updated.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh PORT_PROGRESS.md for Phase 13 placeholder library
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker, with no code changes. It records the 17 recent pieces of work that gave every planned server feature a stand-in response with realistic sample data. It also marks that stage as essentially finished and says the next work is the real live-update connection, followed by features that need actual hardware and files.

prs.title: port(ws): Phase 13.17 — InMemoryWsServices placeholder + /ws/catalog AOT fix
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the behind-the-scenes plumbing the server will use to push live updates to the app. It keeps the last 1,000 updates so a briefly disconnected app can catch up later. Nothing is actually sent to apps yet, because the live connection itself is still unbuilt and is planned for the next step. It also fixes a hidden bug: the list of available update types had been failing every time it was requested, and an automatic check now makes sure that can't happen again unnoticed.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13.15 + 13.16 — sequence extras + last small 501s
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This moves two recent pieces of work into the main branch. One adds stand-in versions of sequence templates, importing sequences from the older NINA app, and the automatic-flats decision step. The other adds a "server is ready" check and suggested sky-data downloads. The code matches #166 and #167. The remaining unfinished features all need real hardware, real files, or a database: restarting the server, downloading images, bulk image actions, some session tools, and live updates.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.16 — /readyz + sky-data-recommendations placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Two previously unfinished server features now respond. The "is the server ready" check replies "ready", and a profile can now be asked which sky-data packages it should install. Both are simplified stand-ins. The readiness check always says ready without checking anything. The recommendations return every not-yet-installed package no matter which profile is asked about, even one that doesn't exist, rather than tailoring them to the user's location.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.15 — sequence templates + NINA import + auto-flats placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Four sequence-related features that previously answered "not built yet" now work with stand-in behavior. You can list three built-in templates (color, narrowband, and all-night multi-target), create a new sequence from one, import a sequence from the older NINA app, and answer the automatic-flats prompt. New sequences from templates or imports appear in the sequence list right away. However, the templates are empty shells with no actual steps, and the import doesn't translate the NINA file yet; it just stores it and attaches a warning saying so.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13.12-13.14 — equipment + sequencer + calibration/darks/mosaic placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This moves three recent pieces of work into the main branch, so roughly 70 more server features now return realistic sample data instead of "not built yet." That includes controls for all 12 equipment types, creating and running sequences, calibration and dark-frame libraries, and mosaics. It also makes a matching-flats request for a session that doesn't exist correctly report "not found." These are still stand-ins that don't talk to real hardware. The equipment and sequence code was trimmed from the review, so those parts could not be checked against the description.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.14 — Calibration + DarkLibrary + Mosaic placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now gives working answers, instead of "not built yet" errors, for about a dozen requests covering calibration sessions, the library of dark calibration frames, and mosaics (large images stitched from several panels). Mosaics can actually be created, viewed, and deleted while the server is running, but they are forgotten on restart. Calibration and dark-library answers are fixed sample data only. This lets the app's screens be built and tested before the real features exist.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.13 — Sequence + Sequencer placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Imaging sequences, the step-by-step plans for a night of shooting, can now be created, viewed, edited, and deleted through the server. They are kept only until the server restarts. Start, pause, resume, abort, and stop commands are accepted and acknowledged but do not run anything yet, and asking for a sequence's running status always comes back as not found. Templates, importing plans from the older NINA program, and the automatic-flats prompt still return "not built yet."

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.12 — placeholder equipment services (all 12 device types)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All 12 kinds of astronomy equipment the server supports, including camera, telescope mount, focuser, dome, guider, and polar alignment, now respond to requests instead of returning "not built yet." This covers about 50 requests. No real hardware is connected yet: checking a device always reports nothing is attached, while commands like connect, slew, or open the dome are simply acknowledged. Starting a camera exposure returns a fake image that feeds into the existing preview system, so that path can be tested from start to finish.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13.8-13.11 — log + bug-report + data-manager + profile-share + backup-stream + backup-zip placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This PR brings four earlier changes into the main line: working placeholder answers for server logs, bug reports, data package management, profile sharing, and both kinds of backup. More than 20 more server requests now return sample data instead of "not built yet" errors. Downloading a bug report or a log file still comes back as not found. The changes themselves were reviewed in PRs #157 to #160.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.11 — placeholder IBackupService (§43 ZIP snapshots)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The four backup requests (create a backup file, restore one, list past backups, and check restore progress) now return placeholder answers instead of "not built yet." Creating or restoring is only acknowledged and no backup is actually made. The list always shows one sample backup, and progress always says idle. This gives the backup settings screen something to work with.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.10 — DataManager + ProfileShare + BackupStream placeholders
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Eleven more server requests now return sample data instead of "not built yet." They cover managing downloadable star-catalog and data packages, sharing equipment profiles between users, and a live backup feed. Download, cancel, and share actions are acknowledged but not actually carried out. The package list and profile-share preview are fixed samples, and the backup feed never has any images to hand out. This is meant to let the app's screens be built against realistic responses.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.9 — placeholder IBugReportService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "send a bug report" feature on the server now responds instead of returning a "not built yet" error, so the app's bug report window has something real to work with. Preparing a report always says it is ready right away, with a made-up size of about 256 KB, but trying to download it still says "not found" because no actual report file is created yet. That part is planned for a later phase.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.8 — placeholder ILogService (tail + rotate + download)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's log controls now work with sample data instead of returning "not built yet" errors. Viewing recent log lines returns eight made-up entries that look like a real imaging night, and they can be filtered by how serious they are or by a search word, newest first. The "start a new log file" button is accepted but doesn't do anything real yet, and downloading the log still says "not found" until actual log files are saved in a later phase.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13.4-13.7 (notifications + diagnostics + stats + server-state placeholders) + README arm64-only
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles five earlier changes into the main branch: notifications, the diagnostics panel, the statistics charts, and server status/version info now return sample data instead of "not built yet" errors. The README now says the project supports ARM64 Linux only. The automated check that starts the server was also updated to expect a working diagnostics response. Most of the data is still placeholder, so screens can be developed against it before real tracking exists.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.7 — placeholder IServerStateService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Three server information requests now work instead of returning "not built yet" errors: an overall status snapshot, a list of software versions, and release notes. The version list reports real details like the operating system and runtime, but the app's own build ID is still a placeholder, and the status snapshot leaves the equipment, sequence, diagnostics, and notification sections empty for now. The server restart commands still don't work and will fail if used, as the description says.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.6 — placeholder IStatsService (8 chart views)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All eight statistics views on the server, such as overview, targets, focus vs. temperature, guiding, frame quality, best frames, and calendar, now return realistic sample data instead of "not built yet" errors. The Stats tab can show sensible charts for a small made-up library of about five sessions. Exporting stats to a spreadsheet file still returns "not found" until real image records are available.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.5 — placeholder IDiagnosticsService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The diagnostics panel's server side now works with sample data: it reports a "yellow" health status with one open issue (a target sinking toward the horizon limit) and a short history of three past events. Users can change the diagnostics mode, but only in memory, so the change is lost when the server restarts, and it is kept separate from the similar setting stored in the user's profile. The automated server check was updated to expect this working response and now uses a different, still-unbuilt feature to confirm error messages look right.

prs.title: docs(readme): server is ARM64-only — drop x64 mention
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Corrected the project's front-page description to say the server runs only on ARM64 Linux, the type of chip in a Raspberry Pi, rather than also on standard PC hardware. Raspberry Pi 4/5 is named as the main supported device, and other similar small boards are 'best effort.' Only the front-page wording changed. Other planning documents still mention the PC option in places.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.4 — placeholder INotificationService
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's notification features now respond with sample data instead of 'not built yet' errors. The app can list, dismiss, and mark notifications as read, and view and change notification preferences. There are three example alerts: a sequence start, a low-disk warning, and an unsafe-weather pause. This lets the app's notifications screen be built against realistic responses. Changes are kept only in memory and are lost when the server restarts.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 13.1-13.3 (placeholder frame + session catalog) + PORT_PROGRESS backfill
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merge promotes a batch of earlier work to the main line. With it, the server can serve a full browse-your-images flow using sample data: list imaging sessions, open one, see its frames, view a frame's details, and get a small preview picture. It bundles the frame preview, sample frames, and sample session changes, plus a progress-tracking document update. All data is still placeholder, and many other features still return 'not built yet.'

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.3 — placeholder ISessionService matching sample frames
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now list imaging sessions, show one session, and list the frames in that session, using one sample session of the Andromeda Galaxy (M31). This completes a sample browse-your-images flow from session list down to frame preview, so the app's Library screens can be built against it. Asking for a session that doesn't exist now correctly returns 'not found.' Resuming a target and reprocessing images are still not supported.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.2 — placeholder GET /frames/{id} + ListAsync sample data
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now list captured frames and show details for a single frame, using three made-up example images: two Andromeda Galaxy shots and one calibration 'dark' frame. The list can be filtered by session or target, and unknown frames return 'not found.' One example includes a full quality score so the app's detail view can show it. The frame list itself leaves out quality scores, and there is still only one page of results.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 13.1 — IFrameRepository placeholder + real preview/thumbnail endpoints
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server's image preview and thumbnail features now return a real, tiny plain-gray picture instead of a 'not built yet' error. This lets the app's image display be tested from end to end before real image processing exists. The same gray picture is returned for any frame, including ones that don't exist, so these features never actually report 'not found' yet.

prs.title: docs(progress): backfill Completed section through Phase 14b
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation-only update to the project's progress tracker. It fills in the list of completed work that had fallen about 40 changes behind, covering settings search, guider settings, the device picker, saving settings to the server, and the recent server fixes. It also names the image preview feature as the next big piece of work. One small gap: an old note saying this catch-up 'will happen later' was left in the file, and the 'current phase' line still shows an older phase.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 14a + 14b — AOT JsonSerializerContext + CI server smoke gate
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings two recent changes into the main branch. The first fixes the server so it actually starts and answers requests when run for development. The second adds an automatic check that starts the server on every change and makes sure it responds properly. Together they mean the new save-your-settings feature can finally be tested end to end. The code also reshapes how the server's basic 'about this server' information is produced, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: feat(ci): Phase 14b — server runtime smoke step
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal change to the automated checks. Every server change is now tested by starting the server, confirming it responds, and confirming it saves the settings file in the expected format. Before this, a serious bug went unnoticed across several changes because the checks only confirmed the code compiled, never that it ran. This check runs only on a standard PC-type machine, not on the Raspberry Pi hardware the product targets.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 14a — AraJsonSerializerContext source-gen (unblocks dotnet run smoke)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a long-standing problem that stopped the server from answering requests when started for development. Until now, nobody could manually check that saved settings actually come back after a restart. With this fix, that full save-and-restart path was confirmed to work. The change also reshapes how the server's basic 'about this server' information is produced, which the description does not mention. One minor compatibility warning is still hidden on purpose and is logged as a follow-up.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 12h.6 + 12h.7 — §37 profile round-trip + file persistence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brings a large batch of work into the main branch. Every settings screen in the app can now load its values from the server and save changes back, covering 11 areas such as imaging defaults, storage, notifications, site, safety rules, autofocus, guiding and equipment auto-connect. The server keeps these settings in a file on disk, so they survive a restart. It also corrects the API documentation, which had listed the wrong field-name style. At merge time, the full save-and-restart path could not yet be tested by hand because the server would not start in development mode, which a later change fixed.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 12h.7 — file-based profile store (settings survive daemon restart)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now saves all user settings to a file on disk instead of keeping them only in memory, so settings are no longer lost when the server restarts. Saves are written safely, so a crash mid-save leaves the previous settings in place. If the file is missing or damaged, the server falls back to the default values. The full save-and-restart flow could not be tested by hand at the time because of a separate server startup problem, which was fixed shortly after.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6L — equipment-connection daemon round-trip (closes §37 surface)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The on/off choices for which equipment connects automatically when the telescope server starts (camera, mount, focuser, dome and so on) are now saved on the server instead of only in the app. Each toggle saves on its own the moment you flip it, with no Save button, but a failed save is silently ignored. This finishes the effort to have every settings screen load from and save to the server. The server still keeps these settings only in memory, so they reset when it restarts. The change also quietly fixes the API reference document so the field names for several other settings sections match what the server actually uses, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6k — PHD2 settings daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guider (PHD2) settings screen now loads its values from the server when opened and saves them back when you press Save. Those values cover connection details, dithering and calibration options. Before this, Save only kept them in the app. Errors now appear on screen. The auto-connect toggle on the same screen was left for a follow-up change. As with the other sections, the server holds these settings in memory only, so they reset if it restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6j — diagnostics-mode daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The diagnostics mode choice is now saved on the server. This setting controls whether serious problems just notify you, pause the session, or abort it. Unlike other settings screens, it saves as soon as you tap an option, with no Save button. If saving fails, or no server is connected, you get a message and the choice stays only in the app. The server's default is the safest option, notify only.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6i — plate-solve settings daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The plate-solving settings screen now loads its values from the server when opened and saves them back when you press Save. These settings control how the app works out exactly where the telescope is pointing, including which solver to use, search limits and re-centering behavior. Previously Save only kept the values in the app. Load and save errors are now shown on screen. The server stores these in memory only, so they reset on restart.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6h — autofocus settings daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The autofocus settings screen now loads from and saves to the server. It covers the focus method, step counts, which filter to focus with, when to refocus, and what to do if focusing fails. Previously pressing Save only kept the values in the app. Now it reports success or shows an error. The server keeps these values in memory only, so they reset when it restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6g — safety policies daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The safety policies screen now loads from and saves to the server. These policies decide how the system reacts to bad weather, meridian flips, a target dropping too low, or losing the guide star. Previously pressing Save only kept the choices in the app. Now it confirms the save or shows an error. The server holds these settings in memory only, so they reset if it restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6f — filenames settings daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The file-naming settings screen now saves two options to the telescope control server and loads them back when opened: which character separates parts of the date in file names, and whether calibration images (darks and bias) are compressed. Before this, those choices were only kept in the app and were lost when it closed. The server still keeps saved settings only in memory, so they reset whenever the server restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6e — site preferences daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The site preferences screen now saves to the server and loads from it. These settings cover location, time zone, horizon, sky darkness and typical seeing conditions. The Save button now actually sends the values, and shows an error if no server is connected or the save fails. The allowed value ranges, such as latitude between -90 and 90, are written into the server's documentation, but the server does not yet reject values outside them. As with the other sections, saved values reset when the server restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6d — notifications settings daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The notifications settings screen now saves to the server and loads from it when opened. This covers which alert channels are on, the Pushover and Telegram tokens, and which events trigger an alert. The tokens are stored and sent as plain text for now. The description says this is acceptable on a trusted home network and that proper secret handling comes later. Saved values reset when the server restarts.

prs.title: feat: Phase 12h.6c — storage settings daemon round-trip (server + client)
prs.author: joeytroy
