prs.summary: The storage settings screen now saves to the server and loads from it when opened, instead of only keeping values in the app. This covers where images are saved, the file format, the compression, and the file-name pattern. This PR includes both the server and app changes, which sets the pattern for the other settings sections. A full end-to-end manual test is still blocked by a known server startup issue, and saved values reset when the server restarts.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.6b — ProfileApi + imaging-defaults daemon round-trip
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The imaging defaults screen in the app now loads its values from the server when opened and sends them back when you press Save. Before, pressing Save just showed a "saved in memory" placeholder message. Save now shows a spinner while working, a confirmation when done, and a clear error if no server is connected or the request fails. It also adds the shared connection piece that later settings screens reuse. The app treats the most recently added server as the active one.

prs.title: feat(server): Phase 12h.6a — imaging-defaults profile endpoint (real, not 501)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now store and return the imaging defaults (exposure time, gain, offset, binning, frame type and camera cooling settings). Before, it only answered with a "not implemented" response. Its starting values match the app's own defaults, so the two agree from the start. Values are kept only in memory and reset whenever the server restarts; saving to disk is planned for a later phase. While testing, the author found an older, unrelated problem that makes the server fail when run locally, and logged it for later rather than fixing it here.

prs.title: Merge port/ara → master: Phase 12h.4 + 12h.5 (PHD2 settings, Alpaca chooser, search affordance)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundles five recently finished pieces of work into the main branch. The app now has a search icon in the top bar. The telescope-guiding settings (the PHD2 guiding program) can be edited instead of just viewed. Nine of the ten equipment screens gain a 'Choose…' button that scans the network and lets you pick a device. This is the first time the app actually talks to the background service to find equipment, but the chosen device is only held while the app is open and is not yet saved.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.5c — wire AlpacaDeviceRow on 7 remaining equipment panels
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 'Choose…' device picker now appears on seven more equipment screens: focuser, filter wheel, rotator, flat panel, dome, weather, and safety monitor. Optional devices show a short note explaining when you would need them. The guiding screen is deliberately left out because the guiding program connects differently. With this, nine of ten equipment screens let users pick their hardware from a network scan.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.5b — lift AlpacaDeviceRow to shared + wire mount + polish
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The telescope mount screen now has the same 'Choose…' device picker the camera screen got in the previous change. Behind the scenes, the picker row was turned into one shared building block so the other equipment screens can reuse it. Two small cleanups were also made: the app now expects one consistent data format from the background service, and it flags unknown device types during development instead of quietly treating them as cameras.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.5a — Alpaca device chooser foundation + camera wiring
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The camera settings screen now has a 'Choose…' button that scans the local network for compatible cameras and lets you pick one from a list. The list includes a re-scan option and clear messages when nothing is found or something goes wrong. This is the first time the app uses the background service's existing device-discovery feature. The choice is only kept while the app is running and is not yet saved, and no new tests were added.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.4 — §63 PHD2 settings state + full guider panel migration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The guiding settings screen, which controls the PHD2 guiding program, is now editable instead of showing fixed placeholder values. Users can change the connection details, how often and how far the telescope is nudged between shots, how long to wait for it to steady, and whether to recalibrate every session. The app rejects invalid values such as an out-of-range port. Plain-language help notes were added for the trickier options, and one related setting is shown read-only here with a pointer to the Safety settings, so it is only edited in one place.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3l — visible search affordance in AppShell top bar
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A magnifying-glass search button now sits on the right side of the app's top bar. It opens the same settings search as the keyboard shortcut, and its tooltip shows the right shortcut for Mac or other computers. The equipment icons in the bar still scroll, but the search button stays fixed in place.

prs.title: Merge port/ara → master: Phase 12h.3 complete (Smart Settings Search + Help Registry)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges a large batch of settings work into the main version of the app. Users can now press a keyboard shortcut to open a search box and find any of about 83 settings by describing what they want (for example "dither" or "twilight"). About 46 settings now have a small info icon that opens a plain explanation. A new automatic check blocks future changes that add a setting without a description, at least one search keyword, and a unique name. The contributor template was also rewritten and asks for 3 or more keywords, while the description claims every setting has 4 or more; the automatic check itself only requires one.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3k — bulk-register Plate Solve + Diagnostics Mode (final 12h.3 panel batch)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 11 plate-solving settings (how the app works out exactly where the telescope is pointing) are now findable in settings search. Six of the harder ones get info-icon explanations, covering which solving program to use and how precisely to center a target. This also fixes the explanation for Diagnostics Mode, which described options that don't exist. It now describes the real choices: notify only, pause, or abort on critical problems. The Diagnostics Mode screen still has no info icon, so that explanation can only be reached through search.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3j — bulk-register Autofocus + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All 12 autofocus settings are now findable in settings search. Six of the trickier ones gain info-icon explanations, covering which focusing method to pick, how many test positions to use, and when to refocus automatically (temperature change, blurrier stars, or on a timer). The method picker now uses the app's standard dropdown. The PR description quotes one formula for the step-size guidance, but the help text that shipped uses a different, smaller one.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3i — bulk-register Safety Policies + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All 12 safety-policy settings are now findable in settings search, up from 3. These cover bad weather, the telescope's mid-night side swap ("meridian flip"), targets sinking too low, and losing the guide star. Info icons were added to eight of these controls, with five new explanations written; the description says six. It also corrects a wrong default (resume delay is 10 minutes, not 5). Not mentioned in the description: the guide-star option label changed from "retry once" to "retry until timeout."

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3h — bulk-register Equipment auto-connect + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "auto-connect on startup" switch for each of the 10 equipment types is now findable in search, for example by typing "guider connect." Each of those switches now has an info icon. They all share one explanation of why some devices connect automatically by default and others don't: the guider, dome, and weather station are off by default because connecting them can start programs or move hardware.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3g — bulk-register Filter Wheel labels + wire help icon
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The filter-wheel slot names (like L, R, G, B, Ha) can now be found through settings search as one setting. An info icon on the first slot explains where these names show up: in file names, in image data read by stacking tools, in imaging plans, and when matching calibration frames. It also suggests common naming conventions. A code comment says the icon sits on the section header, but it actually appears next to Slot 1.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3f — bulk-register Filenames + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Filenames settings page now has both of its options, the date separator and the switch for compressing calibration frames, findable through the app's settings search. Each also gets a help icon with a plain explanation. The date separator help explains how each choice organizes saved files into folders or flat names. The compression help explains why shrinking these bulky reference frames saves a lot of disk space. The dropdown was also switched to the app's shared building block, with no visible change in behavior.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3e — bulk-register Site preferences + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All ten site settings, such as location, horizon, sky darkness and typical seeing, can now be found through the settings search. Help icons were added to the five less obvious ones: custom horizon, default horizon altitude, Bortle dark-sky class, typical seeing, and the twilight definition that decides when night starts. The twilight dropdown was switched to the shared building block used elsewhere.

prs.title: Speed up build_and_run.sh: incremental by default, ccache + Ninja auto
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The developer script that builds and starts the server no longer throws away previous work on every run. A rerun with no changes now takes about 5 seconds instead of 5 to 10 minutes, and a small edit rebuilds in under half a minute. The first time it runs, the script also installs two standard speed-up tools, using the administrator permission prompt it already had. It also skips repeat device-setup steps when nothing has changed. A leftover unused build option that caused a warning on every build was removed. Setting CLEAN=1 still forces a full rebuild from scratch.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3d — bulk-register Notifications + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: All twelve notification settings, covering delivery methods like Pushover and Telegram and alert triggers like disk space running low, can now be found through the settings search. Help icons explain the less obvious ones, including how to set up Pushover and Telegram. The description lists five help entries, but the code actually adds six: it also includes an explanation for the Safety event alert. A custom text field used for the two tokens was replaced with the shared version used across the app.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3c — bulk-register Storage + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The four Storage settings (save location, file format, compression, and filename pattern) can now be found through the settings search. They also gain help icons explaining file format choices, compression trade-offs, and the placeholders allowed in filename patterns. The description says the save location was left without help, but the code also adds a help entry for it. That entry warns that saving to the SD card wears it out and recommends using external storage. The two dropdowns were switched to the shared building block.

prs.title: Drop JSON report from /conformu skill — text log is sufficient
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to the step-by-step instructions the team's AI coding assistant follows when running driver compatibility tests. The tests no longer produce or save a separate summary data file. Pass or fail is now judged from the plain text test log alone, which already contains the same information. No product code changed, and previously saved reports are left as they are.

prs.title: Add ZWO ASIair Pro 12V power Switch driver (ConformU 4.3.0)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge can now control the four 12V power outputs on a ZWO ASIair Pro. Astronomy apps like NINA can switch each port on or off, or set it to a 0–100% power level for dew heaters and flat panels. The ASIair Pro must first be re-installed with a 64-bit operating system, and the new driver cannot run alongside ZWO's own app. It also passed the standard ASCOM compatibility test with no errors, and a new setup guide was added. Disconnecting an app deliberately leaves the ports powered, so users should turn a port off before disconnecting if they want it off.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3b — bulk-register Imaging Defaults + wire help icons
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The eight Imaging Defaults settings (such as exposure, gain, binning and cooler options) can now be found through the app's quick settings search. Five of the less obvious ones now have a small info icon that explains them in plain terms, for example why gain affects noise or why warming up a cooled camera slowly matters. The panel's dropdown and on/off switch now use the app's shared building blocks, and an outdated help entry for the cooler warm-up setting was replaced. This is the first of about ten similar updates, one per settings panel.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3a — Smart Settings Search + Help Registry foundation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This lays the groundwork for a quick-search box (opened with ⌘K) that finds settings by what you're trying to do, plus small info icons that explain settings in place. Only a handful of settings and help entries are included so far, and the rest will be added panel by panel. It also adds an automatic check that blocks changes whose settings or help entries are missing descriptions or search words, and replaces a pull request template that had been copied from another project. Beyond what the description lists, the code also adds a new "System" settings group (Monitoring and About) and briefly highlights a setting after you jump to it from search.

prs.title: Add GPIO transport to /conformu skill input/output schema
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to a helper script's instructions. It lets the team record ASCOM compatibility test results for devices controlled directly through the host computer's hardware pins, such as the ASIair Pro power ports. It only edits two lines of instructions, and nothing changes for users.

prs.title: docs(rules): switch reviewer from Augment to Sonnet
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is a documentation-only update to the team's code review rules. It records that code reviews are now done by Sonnet instead of the earlier bots, which were dropped because of usage limits or overreach. The rules now use reviewer-neutral wording, and the merge process itself is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-filter-labels — editable filter wheel slot labels
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Users can now rename the eight filter wheel slots in the Filter Wheel settings panel instead of seeing fixed labels. The slots start as L, R, G, B, Hα, OIII, SII and one blank slot, and leaving a slot blank marks it as unused. For now the names are only kept while the app is running and are not yet saved to the server; that, and matching the slot count to the real hardware, are planned for a later update.

prs.title: Fix self-deadlock at startup when log dir falls back
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a bug where the server froze during startup and never came online if it couldn't write to its preferred log folder. This hit fresh installs where that folder was never set up. The server was waiting on itself: it tried to write a warning to the log while it already had the log locked. It now sets the warning aside, finishes its setup, and writes the warning afterward, so the server starts normally and falls back to a different log folder.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-equipment-connect — auto-connect per device type
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the app's equipment settings, the "Auto-connect on boot" option is now an on/off switch for all 10 device types instead of fixed text. The camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, rotator, flat panel, and safety monitor start switched on. The guider, dome, and weather devices start off because connecting them can make things happen, such as moving the dome shutter. The other fields on these screens are still display-only. As with the earlier settings work, these choices appear to be kept only while the app is running and are not yet sent to the server.

prs.title: refactor(client): consolidate _DropdownRow + _NumberRow into shared widgets
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal cleanup with no visible change. The safety policies settings screen now uses the app's shared building blocks for its drop-down menus and number fields instead of its own private copies. This removes about 125 lines of duplicate code.

prs.title: Add /conformu skill and block commit/PR on failing ConformU reports
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal change to the step-by-step instructions the team's AI coding assistant follows, with no change to the product itself. It adds a guided routine for running the standard compatibility test suite (ConformU) against a device, saving the results, and updating the list of supported devices. It also makes the assistant refuse to commit or open a pull request if any saved test report shows errors, issues, or slow responses. The goal is to stop a device from being listed as tested when its tests actually failed.

prs.title: refactor(client): consolidate _SwitchRow into shared SettingsSwitchRow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal cleanup with no visible change. Six settings screens each had their own nearly identical copy of the on/off switch row. They now share one common version, which removes about 150 lines of duplicate code.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 12h.2 editable settings (autofocus + plate-solve + diagnostics + filenames + site)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This batch brings five settings screens in the app from display-only to editable: Autofocus, Plate Solving, File Naming, Site location, and Diagnostics Mode. Each screen checks entries, for example rejecting a latitude outside the valid range or a blank name. It also includes a small follow-up, not listed in the description, that trims stray spaces from text entries and rejects entries that are only spaces. The changes are kept only while the app is running; saving them to the server is planned for a later step.

prs.title: fix(client): trim + reject whitespace-only on string setters
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Text settings in the desktop app now ignore input that is only spaces, and they strip stray spaces from the start and end of what you type before saving. This covers the autofocus filter name, the site name and time zone, the plate-solving program location and download folder, and the image save folder and file naming pattern. Before this, typing just spaces into one of these fields would be accepted as a real value. It was a small follow-up to review comments raised before a larger release could go out.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-diagnostics — editable Diagnostics Mode picker
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Diagnostics Mode picker in Settings now actually works: users can click to choose whether problems only trigger a notification (the default), pause the current imaging run when something critical happens, or abort and park the telescope. Before this, the three options were for display only and could not be changed. The choice is only kept while the app is open for now; saving it to the server is planned for a later update.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-platesolve — editable Plate Solve panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Plate Solving settings screen, which controls how the app works out exactly where the telescope is pointing, can now be edited instead of only showing fixed values. Users can pick which solving program to use, where it lives, and fine-tune options like search area, speed/accuracy trade-offs, timeouts, and whether to re-center or sync the mount after a solve. Out-of-range numbers are blocked or pulled back into sensible limits. As with the other settings screens so far, changes are not yet saved to the server.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-autofocus — editable Autofocus panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Autofocus settings screen can now be edited instead of only showing fixed values. Users can choose the focusing method, the number and size of focus steps, exposure length, and which filter to use, plus when autofocus should run automatically (after a filter change, a temperature shift, image blurring, or every few hours) and what to do if it fails. Unreasonable values are rejected or pulled back into safe limits; changes are not yet saved to the server.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-filenames — editable File Naming panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The File Naming settings screen now lets users choose how dates appear in saved image names (as folders, or joined with underscores or dashes) and whether dark and bias calibration frames get compressed. Settings that belong to the Storage screen, like file format and the naming pattern, are now shown here as read-only with a pointer to where to change them, so there is only one place to edit each setting. Changes are not yet saved to the server.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-site — editable Site preferences
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The observing Site settings screen can now be edited instead of only showing fixed values. Users can set the site name, location, elevation, time zone, sky darkness rating, typical sky steadiness, and which twilight definition to use, with numbers kept within realistic ranges. There is also a switch for a custom horizon, which hides the default horizon height when turned on, though actually loading a custom horizon comes later. Changes are not yet saved to the server.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: editable settings panels (imaging + storage + notifications + safety) + display-sync refactor
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This bundle brings four settings screens in the app from display-only to fully editable: Imaging Defaults, Storage, Notifications, and Safety Policies. Each screen checks input and ignores values that make no sense, such as negative numbers or an empty save folder. If a value is rejected, the box now snaps back to the last accepted value, so the screen never shows a setting that did not take. Changes are only kept in memory for now; the Save buttons show a confirmation, but nothing is sent to the telescope server yet.

prs.title: refactor(client): Phase 12h.2-display-sync — shared editable widgets
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is an internal cleanup of the settings screens with no new features. The Imaging Defaults and Storage screens now share one set of input boxes, which snap back to the last accepted value when you type something invalid. The Safety Policies screen still uses its own copy, even though the description implies all three screens now share the new boxes.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-safety — editable Safety Policies panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Safety Policies settings screen is now editable instead of display-only. Users can choose what happens when the weather turns unsafe, when the telescope hits its altitude limit, or when guiding is lost, and they can set wait times and turn behaviors like auto-resume and re-centering after a meridian flip on or off. Negative numbers are rejected, and during review the input boxes were fixed to snap back when a value is rejected. Settings are kept in memory only for now.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-notifications — editable Notifications panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Notifications settings screen is now editable. Users can turn in-app banners, desktop notifications, and sound alerts on or off, and enter Pushover and Telegram tokens, with stray spaces removed automatically. They can also choose which of seven events trigger an alert, such as a sequence finishing, autofocus failing, or low disk space. Changes are saved in memory only for now.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-storage — editable Storage panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Storage settings screen is now editable. Users can set the save folder and the filename pattern, and pick the image file format and compression from dropdown lists. Blank folder or filename values are rejected. The free-space figure is still a placeholder, and changes are kept in memory only for now.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-imaging-b — editable Imaging Defaults panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Imaging Defaults settings screen is now editable. Users can set the default exposure, gain, offset, binning, frame type, camera cooling temperature and cooling speed, and whether the camera warms up at the end of a session. Changes take effect when you tab or click out of a box, and out-of-range values are quietly ignored. The Save button only shows a confirmation for now; nothing is stored on the telescope server yet.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2-imaging — Imaging Defaults state
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the behind-the-scenes groundwork for 'imaging defaults': the starting values for a camera session, such as exposure length, gain, binning, target cooling temperature, cooling speed, and whether to warm the camera back up at the end. Values that make no physical sense, like a zero-length exposure or an extreme cooler temperature, are ignored rather than saved. Nothing changes on screen yet: the settings panel comes in a later update, and for now these values live only in memory and are not saved anywhere. It also adds 8 automated checks.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: tests-5 + tests-6 (85 tests total)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves two batches of new automated checks from the working branch into the main line, bringing the total to 85. One batch covers the framing, live-view, and image-library grouping settings. The other confirms that a storage failure on some Linux setups won't block a user from getting past the first-run screen. Internal testing work only, with no change to the app itself.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests-6 — saved_server_state coverage
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds 3 automated checks for how the app remembers saved servers. The key check confirms that if the computer's secure storage fails, which can happen on some Linux setups, a newly added server still takes effect and the user isn't stuck on the first-run screen. Internal testing only, bringing the total to 85.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests-5 — framing + live-view + library-grouping
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds 12 automated checks covering the framing controls (rotation and mosaic settings), target search text, the live-view on/off switch, and how the image library groups sessions. The description counts 7 checks for the framing area, but the code actually adds 6. Internal testing only, bringing the total to 82.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: help dialog + 14 more tests + cleanup-5
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves three pieces of work into the main line; the most visible is a working Help / Report-a-bug button. The button opens a dialog showing the app version, the current server, and links to the project's issue tracker and wiki, plus a button that copies a ready-to-fill bug report template to the clipboard. The dialog now reads the app version from the build itself instead of a hard-coded number, which the description does not mention. The batch also includes 14 new automated checks and some small cleanup.

prs.title: fix(client): help dialog version error state + CHANGELOG nit
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes a small issue in the Help dialog. Before, if the app couldn't look up its own version number, the dialog showed 'loading...' forever. Now it shows 'unknown' in that case. It also corrects an outdated changelog entry that listed an old hard-coded version number.

prs.title: fix(client): help dialog reads app version from package_info_plus
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Help dialog now shows the app's real version number, read from the app itself, instead of a value typed by hand that had already fallen out of step with the actual version. The "Copy diagnostics" button also fetches the current version when pressed, and shows "(unknown)" if it can't be read instead of failing. A new supporting library was added to make this possible.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests-4 — stats + sky atlas state coverage
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal testing only: adds 14 automated checks for the statistics dashboard numbers and the Sky Atlas settings, bringing the total to 70. No change to how the app behaves.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12i — §54 Help / Report-a-bug dialog
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Help button in the app's bottom bar, which had been greyed out, now opens a "Help / Report a bug" window. It shows the app version, the current server, how many servers are saved, and clickable links to the project's issue tracker and wiki. A "Copy diagnostics" button puts a ready-made bug report template, with those details filled in, on the clipboard to paste into a new issue. The version shown here was typed in by hand, which a later change replaced.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: tests (55) + library multi-select
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This batch release brings four earlier changes into the main version of the app. The Image Library now lets you long-press images to select several at once, with a bar at the bottom showing how many are picked. The bar's actions (Rate, Tag, Move, Export, Delete) are visible but can't be used yet. It also adds 55 automated tests and a new automatic check that runs them on every change.

prs.title: fix(client): Phase 12 CR cleanup round 5 — 4 findings on promotion #80
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Small fixes from code review of the Image Library multi-select feature. The list of selected images can no longer be changed by accident from outside the part of the app that manages it, which could have left the screen out of sync. The bottom action bar also no longer slides under system areas like phone navigation bars or desktop docks. Also includes one new test and corrections to the project notes.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests-3 — SequenceController coverage
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal testing only: adds 14 automated checks for the sequence editor, covering adding, moving, and deleting steps and the rules that block invalid changes. This brings the total to 55 tests. No change to how the app behaves.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests-2 — wizard + exposure + tab-index coverage
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal testing work only, with nothing changed in the app itself. It adds 18 more automated checks, bringing the total to 41. The new checks confirm that the setup wizard moves between steps without going out of bounds, that the camera exposure settings refuse invalid values like zero or negative numbers, and that the app only switches to tabs that actually exist.

prs.title: test(client): Phase 12-tests — initial unit tests + CI integration
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the desktop app's first set of automated tests, 23 in total. They cover selecting images in the library, searching settings, and how imaging sequences are stored. It also adds a new step to the automatic build checks, so these tests and a code-quality scan now run on every change. Nothing users see has changed.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12f.3a — Library multi-select skeleton
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the Image Library, you can now press and hold a picture to start selecting several at once, then tap others to add or remove them. While anything is selected, a bar slides up at the bottom showing how many are selected, with a button to clear the selection. The bar also shows Rate, Tag, Move to session, Export and Delete buttons, but these are switched off for now and will start working in a later update.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 12 partial — through 12h trio + 12g.3 + 12d.5
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A large batch of desktop app work moves onto the main line of the project in one go. It adds the dark-themed main window with Imaging, Framing, Sequencer, Sky Atlas and Options tabs, plus a setup wizard, an Image Library with a picture viewer, a stats dashboard with charts and spreadsheet-style export, a settings area, and a quick-search command box. The app now remembers which servers you have saved. Much of this is still early-stage: many screens show placeholder or demo data and are not yet connected to real telescope equipment.

prs.title: fix(client): Phase 12 CR cleanup round 4 — 5 real findings
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A round of small polish fixes found during code review. The bottom status bar and the Image Library header were made taller so their buttons no longer get cut off, and long target or site names now shorten neatly instead of breaking the layout. Screen readers can now tell which diagnostics mode is selected. If saved servers fail to load, users see a plain "please try again" message and the technical details go to a log instead.

prs.title: fix(client): deep-freeze SequenceNode.params
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A behind-the-scenes fix to how imaging sequence steps are stored. Some settings stored inside a step, such as a list of filters, could still be changed by accident after the step was created. That could quietly confuse the app's check for whether two steps are the same. Those inner settings are now locked as well, and users should see no difference.

prs.title: fix(client): Phase 12 CR cleanup round 2 — 8 promotion-PR findings
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A second round of small fixes from automated code review of the upcoming release. Identical sequence steps that contain lists, such as a loop over the L/R/G/B filters, are now correctly recognized as the same. The exposure controls now reject impossible values like negative exposure times, the image library's filter buttons now scroll on narrow windows, and star ratings can no longer display more than five stars. The stats calendar ignores sessions outside its seven-week window so they no longer wash out the shading, the Help button is greyed out until its dialog exists, and a placeholder catalog size now reads "TBD".

prs.title: fix(client): Phase 12 CR cleanup — address 13 promotion-PR findings
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes 13 of 14 issues flagged by automated review of the upcoming release. The fourteenth, adding a filter-slot control to the exposure panel, is postponed as a separate feature. The setup wizard's "Save & Exit" now always closes the wizard, and a storage error when saving your first server no longer blocks you from getting into the app, though that server may not be remembered next time. The stats calendar now uses today's real date instead of a fixed demo date, and a few other fixes land too: buttons that don't work yet are greyed out, the sequencer toolbar no longer overflows on narrow windows, and a chart axis label is corrected.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12g.3 — Stats CSV export
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The "Export CSV" button on the Stats dashboard now works. It offers either a one-row-per-session summary or a detailed one-row-per-image export, and a confirmation shows how many rows were copied. The data goes to the clipboard rather than to a file; saving directly to a file is planned for a later update. Names containing commas or quotes are handled correctly so the spreadsheet columns don't get scrambled.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12d.5 — Sequencer Add Child / Add Sibling actions
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: In the sequence editor, you can now add new steps: "Add Child" puts a step inside a group, and "Add Sibling" puts one right after the selected step. Each opens a menu of 13 ready-made choices, including group types, a target, and common actions like slewing, autofocus, taking exposures, and parking the mount. The new step is selected automatically, but its settings can't be edited yet; that is planned for a later update.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12d.4 — Sequencer node reorder + delete
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor now has Move Up, Move Down, and Delete buttons for the selected step, so users can rearrange or remove steps in an imaging plan. These buttons are greyed out for the top-level sequence itself, and deleting a step also clears the selection. Drag-and-drop reordering is planned for later.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12d.3 — Sequencer conditional/loop UI
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The sequence editor now shows clear, colored explanations for two kinds of steps: loops, which repeat actions such as once per filter, and conditions, which only run when something is true, like the weather being safe. For conditions, it also explains what happens otherwise. The built-in example sequence was updated to show one of each; in doing so, its original single "capture 30 luminance frames" step was replaced by a four-filter loop that captures 20 frames per filter.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12g.2 — Real fl_chart visualizations
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Stats dashboard now shows four real charts instead of placeholder boxes: focus position versus camera temperature, guiding accuracy over time, image sharpness per session (color-coded good/okay/poor), and a calendar grid of imaging activity over the last seven weeks. The built-in sample library grew from 2 to 7 imaging sessions so the charts have enough data to be meaningful, and sessions can now store guiding accuracy numbers. Everything still runs on sample data; connecting to real server data is planned for the next step. The earlier placeholder promised a combined image-quality score, but this chart only uses star sharpness.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.3 — §61 ⌘K smart search palette
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Pressing Cmd+K on Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere now opens a quick-search box that finds settings pages by name or by related words. For example, typing "dither" finds the guiding settings and "park" finds the mount and safety settings. You can pick a result with the arrow keys and Enter to jump straight to that page, and the previously disabled "Search settings" button now opens the same box. For now it only searches settings pages, not other parts of the app.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.2 — Remaining settings panels (read-only stubs)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Every entry in the Settings menu now opens its own page, covering all 22 areas, including each piece of equipment, autofocus, plate solving, file naming, notifications, safety rules, site location, and profiles. These pages are view-only and show fixed example values, not your actual saved settings. Editing and saving will come in later updates. The Sky Data page and the "Run wizard again" page open the existing data manager and setup wizard.

prs.title: feat(client): Phase 12h.1 — Settings shell + tree nav + basic panels
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Options tab now opens a real Settings screen, with a menu of six groups on the left and the selected page on the right. Three pages have content: default imaging values, storage (including a warning about wearing out SD cards), and how the app should react to equipment problems. All other entries show a placeholder for now. Nothing can be changed or saved yet, and the problem-handling choices only look like selectable options without actually letting you switch between them.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12g.1 — Stats dashboard skeleton
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A new Stats dashboard, opened from the bottom bar, shows headline totals: nights, targets, sessions, frames, total exposure time, and average star sharpness. It also has a summary for each target and a top-10 list of the sharpest images. All numbers come from the built-in sample data rather than a real server. The chart areas are placeholders, and the CSV export button is shown but disabled.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12f.1 — Image Library skeleton
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: A new Image Library, opened from the bottom bar, lists past imaging sessions with their date, target, total exposure time, filters used, and a strip of thumbnails. Tapping a thumbnail opens a detail view with the image's settings and quality numbers plus its star rating. Everything runs on built-in sample data with placeholder thumbnails. The action buttons, such as delete, download, and rate, are visible but not yet working.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12e.1 — Sky Atlas tab + Data Manager scaffold
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sky Atlas tab now has a real layout. It includes a switch between a catalog view and a "tonight's sky" view, a search box, and a Data Manager window that lists the sky images, star catalogs, thumbnails and solar-system data that can be downloaded. Most of it is still a mock-up: the sky map is a placeholder, search does not look anything up yet, and every download button is disabled. Because nothing can be downloaded yet, the amber "sky data missing" warning banner will always show for now.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12d.1 — Sequencer skeleton (tree + toolbar + editor)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Sequencer tab now shows the basic shape of the sequence editor. On the left is a tree of steps built from a built-in demo plan (two example targets with slew, focus, capture and wait steps). On the right, a panel shows the details of whichever step you click. It is view-only for now: editing is not possible, and the toolbar buttons (New, Load, Save, Run, Pause, Abort and others) are all greyed out until the app is connected to the server in a later update.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12c.2 — Live View Notifier + Diagnostic Panel
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Live View on/off switch on the Imaging tab now remembers its setting when you move to another tab and come back; previously it reset. Other parts of the app can also now see whether Live View is on. A collapsible diagnostics panel was added under the image area to list recent events. It is not connected to real data yet, so both the panel and the status light still just say "not connected."

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12c.1 — Imaging + Framing tab cores
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The Imaging and Framing tabs now show their intended layouts instead of placeholder text. Imaging has an image area, a histogram strip, and controls for exposure time, gain, offset, binning and frame type. Framing has a target search box plus sliders for rotation, mosaic size and overlap. These are layout and settings only: no real images, sky chart or catalog lookup yet, and the Take One and Live View buttons do nothing. In this version the Live View switch also reset when you changed tabs; a follow-up change fixed that.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12b — Profile wizard shell + 18 placeholder screens
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a step-by-step equipment and profile setup wizard with 18 screens. It opens from a new "Run profile wizard" button in the bottom status bar. You can move back, forward, skip screens and exit, and a progress bar tracks where you are. Each screen currently only describes what it will eventually ask for, and the final "Save Profile" step does not yet save anything to disk. The change also makes the bottom status bar slightly taller to fit the new button.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 12a — App shell + global infrastructure
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The desktop app now has its main window layout. This includes a dark theme, a left-hand menu with five sections (Imaging, Framing, Sequencer, Sky Atlas, Options), a row of equipment indicators across the top, and a status bar along the bottom. After connecting to a server for the first time, a new "Save & continue" button remembers it, so later launches open straight into the main window. All five sections are still placeholders, and clicking the equipment indicators or the help icon does nothing yet.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 11 (Flutter WILMA scaffold + first-run flow) + CHANGELOG init
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This moves the latest batch of work into the main branch: the first version of the desktop companion app, plus a new project changelog. The app runs on Mac, Windows and Linux (mobile comes later), and its opening screen can find telescope servers on the local network or let you type one in, then check that it can connect. A review before merging found four Mac permission gaps that would have blocked local network access, and they were fixed before merge. The detailed changes are in #52 and #53.

prs.title: port(client): Phase 11 — Flutter WILMA scaffold + first-run flow
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the first working version of the desktop app that people will use to control the telescope server, for Mac, Windows and Linux. On first launch it automatically scans the local network for servers, lets you type in an address instead, and checks the connection and shows the server's version. The screen is a plain placeholder; the real design comes in a later phase. There are no automated tests yet (the template's sample test was removed), and the description notes that it has not yet been tried against a live server.

prs.title: infra(docs): init CHANGELOG.md + wire the going-forward convention
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds a changelog to the project: a single running record of what changed, filled in for every past phase, plus a section at the top for upcoming changes. The automated workflow instructions now ask each future change that users would notice to add an entry there. This is documentation only, with no effect on how the software behaves. One small mismatch: the changelog says the reminder is in step 4 of the instructions, but it was actually added as step 2.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 10.5 (.deb packaging)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This moves the new installable package for the Raspberry Pi server into the main branch. The automated build now produces a ready-to-install package on every change, which people can download and install on a Pi for testing. The description lists only the original packaging work (#49), but the code also includes the follow-up fix from #51, which stops internal milestone labels from being used as version numbers.

prs.title: fix(ci, packaging): tag filter + systemd unit comment style
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This fixes two problems that broke the new server package build. First, the build was reading an internal milestone label as the version number, which the packaging tool rejected; now only real release labels count, and everything else gets a development version. Second, a comment in the server's startup settings was written in a format the system could not read, so it was moved onto its own line.

prs.title: port(packaging): Phase 10.5 — arm64 .deb packaging
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds an installable package so the server can be put on a Raspberry Pi with one standard install command. The package sets up a dedicated account with access to cameras and USB devices, starts the server automatically with tightened security limits, and handles log cleanup. The automated build now creates this package on every change and keeps it available to download for 30 days. A public download site and package signing are still planned for later. As first written, the version numbering could pick up internal milestone labels by mistake; #51 fixed this afterwards.

prs.title: Merge port/ara: Phase 10 (Dockerfile + CI Linux publish, arm64-only)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This merges the latest batch of work from the porting branch into the main branch. It brings in the build cleanup that removed several hardware drivers (a Canon camera, four flat-panel light boxes, and the MGEN guider), a new automated check that builds the server for Raspberry Pi-style computers and packages it as a container, and an instruction file that lets an AI assistant carry the port forward on its own. The code also includes a small formatting fix to that instruction file (from #48), which the description does not list.

prs.title: docs(skill): add fence languages to SKILL.md (MD040)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal documentation tidy-up only. It labels the example blocks in the AI assistant's instruction file so a formatting checker stops flagging them. The instructions themselves are unchanged.

prs.title: port(server): Phase 10 — Linux smoke test (Dockerfile + CI publish, arm64-only)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server can now be packaged as a small, locked-down container for Raspberry Pi-style (ARM) computers. The automated checks now build it for that hardware on every change. The team deliberately dropped building for regular PCs, since no one deploys there, and recorded that decision in the project's decision log. The container is only built as a test and is not published anywhere yet. It also uses an Ubuntu base rather than the Debian one the plan called for, because Microsoft no longer offers Debian versions.

prs.title: infra(claude-code): add port-driver skill for autonomous port driving
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds a written playbook that lets an AI coding assistant keep the porting project moving on its own. It picks up the next task, opens and reviews changes, merges them when checks pass, and stops for a human when anything is unclear. It also updates the progress notes. There is no change to the app itself.

prs.title: port(buildfix): Phase 0.5p-followup — Core + Astrometry + Equipment cleanup
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cleans up leftover pieces from the old Windows desktop app so almost the whole project builds again, except the sequencing part, which still has 96 errors and is scheduled for later. Along the way it removes support for a Canon camera, four flat-panel light boxes, the MGEN guider and older hardware helpers. It also cuts the star and object database lookups down to a placeholder, and switches off pop-up dialogs, and it fixes a bug in how network-connected equipment is found. The description says pop-up dialogs just return their default answer, but the code actually turns a default 'Yes' or 'OK' into 'No' or 'Cancel', a safer choice that means nothing is auto-confirmed.

prs.title: port(tracking): refresh PORT_PROGRESS.md (stale since Phase 0.5b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only: the project's progress page had not been updated for about 14 phases and now accurately shows what is finished and what comes next (the Linux test phase). It also marks each completed phase with a label in the project history so milestones are easy to find.

prs.title: port(equipment): Phase 6 — equipment endpoint scaffold + Alpaca discovery service
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The server now has a full set of addresses for controlling astronomy equipment such as cameras, telescopes, focusers, filter wheels, domes and more. Only one of them actually works so far: finding compatible devices on the local network. Every other equipment action (connecting, slewing, taking exposures and so on) replies "not implemented yet." This gives the app team a stable target to build against while the real device control is filled in piece by piece.

prs.title: port(stream): Phase 9 — log/state + WS + notifications + stats + sys scaffold
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds placeholders for the server's remaining features: notifications, statistics, logs, bug reports, sky-data downloads, backups, profile sharing and live updates. It brings the planned set of server addresses to completion. Only one of them works today, a list of the live-update event types the app can subscribe to. Everything else replies "not implemented yet," and the PR says openly that the goals for this stage, like live updates and a working notification feed, are not yet met.

prs.title: port(image): Phase 8 — image + session + backup + diagnostics endpoint scaffold
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds placeholders for browsing captured images and imaging sessions, streaming backups, and a health monitor that watches imaging quality. All of these currently reply "not implemented yet," so no user-visible behavior changes. The aim is to lock in the shape of these features so the app can be built against them while the real work happens.

prs.title: port(sequence): Phase 7 — sequence + calibration + mosaic endpoint scaffold
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds placeholders for managing imaging sequences (the scripted plan for a night's session), calibration frames, and mosaics that stitch multiple sky panels together. Every one of them currently replies "not implemented yet," so nothing works end to end. It sets out the planned shape of these features so the app and server work can proceed in parallel.

prs.title: port(api): Phase 5 — define OpenAPI v1 contract
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the written blueprint describing how the app and server talk to each other, covering equipment, sequences, images, logs and live updates. It also records the key design choices, such as long tasks answering right away and reporting progress later. It is documentation only and changes no behavior.

prs.title: port(promote): merge phase-0.5p-complete to master (covers 0.5g–0.5p)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This brings a large batch of behind-the-scenes work into the main codebase. Every part of the project was renamed from its original NINA name to OpenAstro Ara, and the project moved to the newest version of its underlying platform (.NET 10). Unused pieces were stripped out, including old screens, an old database and some automatic update features. The project does not fully build yet, which the PR acknowledges and leaves for a follow-up. No code diff was available to double-check the details.

prs.title: port(server): Phase 4 — scaffold OpenAstroAra.Server (ASP.NET Core daemon)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds the first version of the new background server program, which runs on Mac and Linux as well as Windows. For now it only answers a basic 'I'm alive' check and a request that reports its name, version and ID, and it serves a built-in page documenting its web interface. The ID it reports changes every time the server restarts, and some add-ons such as local-network discovery and a database are included but not yet used. Real features like controlling equipment, running imaging sequences and handling images are planned for later phases, and this is the first part of the project that builds cleanly on the new .NET 10 platform.

prs.title: port(equipment): Phase 3 — PHD2 client logs openastro-phd2 vs upstream identification
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: When the app connects to the PHD2 guiding program, it now records in its log whether it is talking to the project's own version of PHD2 or the standard version. If it is the standard one, it logs a warning that some features may not work. To do this, the app now waits up to two seconds after connecting for PHD2 to report its version, so connecting can take slightly longer. The change is somewhat larger than the description suggests, but it only affects logging and the connection timing.

prs.title: port(buildfix-2): clean orphan NINA.* imports across OpenAstroAra.* projects
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal cleanup with no effect on how the app behaves. Across about 100 source and test files, it removes leftover references to parts of the old NINA code that were renamed or deleted, and updates the rest to the new project names.

prs.title: port(equipment): Phase 2 — collapse equipment layer to Alpaca-only
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Restructures how the app finds astronomy equipment so that everything goes through the ASCOM Alpaca network standard. There is now a single way to search the local network for cameras, mounts, focusers and other devices, and that search works. Actually connecting to a device that was found is not built yet and will produce an error until a later phase. An older equipment helper and the previous, more complex setup were removed.

prs.title: port(net10+buildfix): Phase 0.5p — .NET 10 bump + first build cleanup pass
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moves the project to Microsoft's newer .NET 10 platform and removes a large amount of leftover code from the original Windows desktop app, about 14,000 lines in total. The removed code includes old screen layouts, an unused communication system, and the old database code for star and sky-object catalogs. It also removes the feature that downloaded Earth-rotation data used for precise pointing calculations. The project still does not fully build after this change, and fixing that is left to follow-up work.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5o — NINA.sln → OpenAstroAra.sln + .gitignore rewrite
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Internal housekeeping that renames the main project file from its old NINA name to OpenAstroAra. After this change, no file or folder in the project carries the NINA name. It also rewrites the list of files that version control should ignore, so it fits the new setup (the new mobile/desktop client, .NET 10, and keeping secrets out of the repository). It does not change how the app behaves.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5n — NINA.Test → OpenAstroAra.Test (final project rename)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The collection of automated tests has been renamed from the old N.I.N.A. name to OpenAstro Ara, as part of the ongoing rebrand of this fork. This is internal only and changes nothing for users. The description calls this the final component rename, but a few references to old N.I.N.A. names still appear in the test code, and the main solution file keeps its old name until a follow-up change.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5l — NINA.Sequencer → OpenAstroAra.Sequencer
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The part of the app that runs automated imaging sequences has been renamed from its old N.I.N.A. name to OpenAstro Ara, and the tests that depend on it were updated to match. This is an internal rebranding step with no intended change in behavior. No code changes were available to review, so this summary is based only on the description, which also says the app may not build cleanly until later rename steps land.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5k-1 — NINA.Equipment → OpenAstroAra.Equipment (rename only)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The equipment-control part of the app (cameras, mounts, guiders, focusers and so on) has been renamed from its old N.I.N.A. name to OpenAstro Ara. This is internal rebranding with no change in behavior, and a companion change (#26) updates the code that uses it. The links from other parts of the project to this component appear to still point at the old folder name, which could stop the app from building until that is corrected.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5k-2 — cascade scrub 'using NINA.Equipment' in dependents
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This companion to #25 updates the imaging-sequence code and the tests so they refer to the equipment component by its new OpenAstro Ara name. It is internal cleanup with no user-facing change. The description says a few plate-solving files were also updated, but the changes shown touch only the sequence code and the tests.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5m — NINA.Platesolving → OpenAstroAra.PlateSolving
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The plate-solving part of the app has been renamed from its old N.I.N.A. name to OpenAstro Ara. Plate solving is the feature that works out where the telescope is pointing by matching the stars in an image. The rename also fixes an inconsistent upper- and lower-case spelling in the old name, and behavior is unchanged. The test project's link to this component still points at the old folder name, which may cause build problems until it is fixed.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5j — NINA.Image → OpenAstroAra.Image
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The image-handling part of the app (reading and saving image files, star detection, image statistics) has been renamed from its old N.I.N.A. name to OpenAstro Ara. Everything that uses it was updated to the new name, with no change in behavior. Several other components still link to it through the old folder name, which may break the build until later cleanup; the description notes the build may be unstable between rename steps.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5i — NINA.Profile → OpenAstroAra.Profile
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Renamed the part of the app that stores user profiles and settings from its old NINA name to the new OpenAstro Ara name, and updated every other part of the app that relies on it. Nothing changes for users; this is one step in the project-wide rebrand. As planned, the app will not fully build again until a later step in the renaming series.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5h — NINA.Astrometry → OpenAstroAra.Astrometry
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Renamed the part of the app that handles astronomy calculations (sky coordinates, sunrise and sunset, moon position and similar) from its old NINA name to the new OpenAstro Ara name, and pointed everything that uses it to the new name. Nothing changes for users; this is another step in the rebrand. As planned, the app will not fully build until the remaining parts are renamed.

prs.title: port(rename): Phase 0.5g — NINA.Core → OpenAstroAra.Core
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Renamed the app's shared foundation code, which almost everything else is built on, from its old NINA name to the new OpenAstro Ara name. This is the first project rename in the rebrand and has no user-facing effect. The original author and copyright credits were deliberately kept. Other parts of the app will not build until they are renamed in later steps, which the team expects.

prs.title: port(promote): merge phase-0.5f-complete to master (covers 0.5c + 0.5d + 0.5e+0.5f + audit)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Moved a batch of earlier cleanup work onto the main branch in a single merge, removing about 240,000 lines. The bundle drops built-in support for many camera brands (including ASI, Atik, FLI, Nikon, QHY, SBIG, SVBony, PlayerOne and ToupTek) and their matching filter wheels and focusers. It also removes the old Windows device-connection layer and the old branding and translations, tightens the automated checks, and adds an audit record. No code changes were available to confirm this, so the summary relies on the description alone.

prs.title: port(audit): retroactive review of 4 PRs merged without CodeRabbit walkthrough
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Documentation only: adds an entry to the project's decision log recording a later review of four earlier pull requests that were merged without the usual automated review. The review found that all four only deleted the files they said they would, with no surprises. It also corrects an earlier note so the list of unreviewed pull requests includes all four instead of three.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5e+0.5f — strip Stefan branding + non-English locales
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removed the 25 non-English translations, so the app is now English-only. The product name and project links now point to OpenAstro Ara instead of NINA, and the README was rewritten for the new project. Old NINA leftovers were also cleared out: the translation tool setup, the release notes, the old Bitbucket build pipeline (which ran unit tests), the linked documentation repository, the logo and splash image, and the code-signing step. Original author and copyright credits were kept, though some internal package descriptions still mention N.I.N.A.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5c — delete vendor SDKs + vendor concrete impls
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removed the built-in drivers that talked directly to specific camera, filter wheel, focuser and flat-panel brands, including ZWO, QHY, Atik, FLI, SBIG, Nikon, PlayerOne, SVBony, ToupTek-family cameras and Alnitak and Pegasus flat panels. The project is committing to talk to equipment only through the Alpaca network standard, so this brand-specific code is no longer needed. The general device definitions were kept so Alpaca support can be built on them later. The project does not build in this state, and that is expected until later phases rewire the equipment setup code. No code diff was shown to confirm the details.

prs.title: port(promote): merge phase-0.5b-complete to master (covers 0.5a + 0.5b)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Brought the first batch of rewrite work from the working branch into the main branch. This includes removing the old Windows desktop interface, the MGEN autoguider support, the plugin system, the Windows installer, CI security hardening and new progress-tracking documents. The removal of brand-specific equipment drivers is not part of this batch and will come in a later one. The main branch still does not build after this merge, which is expected for now. No code diff was shown to confirm the details.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5d — delete ASCOM COM glue
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removed the Windows-only ASCOM connection layer that let the app control telescopes, cameras, domes, focusers, filter wheels, rotators, switches, flat panels, safety monitors and weather sensors. The cross-platform Alpaca libraries were kept, and new Alpaca-based device support is planned for a later phase. Until then, the app has no working way to control equipment and does not build. The removed code also handled Alpaca devices over the network, not just Windows COM ones, so network-device support goes away too for now.

prs.title: port(ci): harden ci.yml — pin checkout SHA + persist-credentials: false
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Tightened security on the automated checks by locking them to one exact, trusted version of a GitHub tool. It also stops the checks from keeping repository write access they never use. The project's progress and to-do notes were updated at the same time. This is internal only and does not change the app.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5b — delete MGEN + nikoncswrapper + WiX + Plugin
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Removed support for the Lacerta MGEN autoguiders, the Nikon camera connection layer, the plugin system and the old Windows installer. The Windows installer will eventually be replaced by a Linux package. The project's build setup was cleaned up so it no longer points at these removed pieces. Some remaining code still refers to them, so the project does not build yet, and this is expected for now.

prs.title: port(setup): add four §1 tracking files (retroactive)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Added four planning documents that track the rewrite: a decisions log, a to-do list, a progress page and a placeholder for future server API design notes. This is documentation only and does not change the app.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-6 — delete NINA.WPF.Base part 2 (final)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the last cleanup step that removes the old Windows desktop interface code the project inherited from N.I.N.A. It deletes the camera and safety-monitor simulators, the sky survey and framing assistant tools, the autofocus analysis tools, and various on-screen controls and dialogs. This clears the way for the new headless (no screen) version of the app. The project still will not build until later planned phases fix the other parts that relied on this code.

prs.title: port(rules): tighten §19.1 merge-gate + add §22 periodic port/ara → master cadence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This updates the team's written rules for how the AI assistant reviews and merges its own pull requests. It will no longer merge when the automated code reviewer was rate-limited and never actually reviewed the work, a gap that had let four earlier changes merge unreviewed. Finished work will now be copied to the main branch after each completed phase instead of all at once at the end. The changes also formally record that the AI, not a person, does the merging, and add practical notes on how to check review status, which the description does not mention.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-5 — delete NINA.WPF.Base part 1 (ViewModel + Resources + Interfaces)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the fifth of six cleanup steps that remove the old Windows desktop interface. It deletes the screen logic for equipment such as cameras, focusers, telescopes, domes, and guiders, along with the interface's visual styles and supporting definitions. It is part of moving toward a version of the app that runs without a screen. The project is expected to stay unbuildable until later phases.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-4 — delete remaining NINA/ (ViewModel + Utility + Database + Resources + External)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the fourth cleanup step and removes everything left in the original desktop app's main folder. That includes screen logic, helper code, the old local database setup, icons and images, and bundled third-party hardware driver files. The old database is removed because it does not fit the new headless design. No code diff was available, so these contents could not be checked against the actual changes.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-3 — delete rest of NINA/View/
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the third cleanup step and finishes removing the old desktop app's screens. It covers the About, Options, Sequencer, thumbnail, plugin, and flat-frame wizard screens, plus standalone screens such as the sky atlas, plate solving, histogram, and framing assistant. It is part of moving to a version of the app that runs without a screen. The project remains unbuildable until later phases.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-2 — delete NINA/View/Equipment + Imaging
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the second cleanup step and removes the old desktop screens for connecting and controlling equipment. That covers cameras, domes, filter wheels, flat panels, focusers, guiders, rotators, safety monitors, switches, telescopes, and weather sensors, plus the dockable imaging panels. The work was split out from the next step to stay within the automated reviewer's file limit. The project remains unbuildable until later phases.

prs.title: port(demolish): Phase 0.5a-1 — deregister WPF from .sln + delete shell files
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This removes the first batch of the old Windows desktop app from the project: its main window and startup code, its settings and license files, example sequence templates, a star-catalog downloader, and a whole library of custom on-screen controls. It is the first of five planned cleanup steps, split up so the automated reviewer can handle each one. The author notes that the Windows build will stay broken until later steps finish removing the remaining links to these deleted pieces. The code changes match the description, with no new behavior added.

prs.title: port(ci): swap stale NINA Windows CI for progressive port placeholder
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This replaces the old automated Windows build and release checks, which would have failed as soon as the old desktop app was removed, with a small placeholder check that only confirms the key planning documents exist. That check is meant to grow into real build and test checks as the port moves forward. It also fixes the branch-naming rules, which as written could not actually be used. The code also does two things the description leaves out: it adds a settings file for the automated code reviewer, and it updates a planning note to say the AI will now merge pull requests itself instead of a person doing it.

prs.title: Port/ara
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds the planning documents for turning the existing astronomy imaging app into a new two-part product: a small server that runs the telescope gear overnight, and a separate app for planning and watching sessions. The largest document is a step-by-step porting plan of about 12,500 lines, alongside the rules for how the work will be split into reviewable chunks and notes on open gaps. It also tells the project to ignore junk files created by Mac and Linux computers. The description is an empty template, so this summary is based only on the code changes.

prs.title: Drop amd64 support: arm64-only build, packaging, and validation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now supports only 64-bit ARM Linux machines, such as a Raspberry Pi, and no longer builds or installs on standard Intel/AMD PCs. The builds now stop with an error on other machines, and about 141 MB of unused camera and device vendor files and old test reports were removed. The supported-devices list was updated, and five devices (ASI290MM Mini, ASI462MM, AM5, AM5N and AM7) are now marked as waiting to be re-tested, because their earlier "validated" status had no test report to back it up. This redoes #50, which had been merged too early and then undone; no code diff was available, so this summary relies on the description alone.

prs.title: Drop amd64 support: arm64-only build, packaging, and validation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This was the first attempt to make AlpacaBridge work only on 64-bit ARM Linux machines and drop support for standard Intel/AMD PCs. According to the follow-up PR, it was merged before the automated review could finish and was then undone by resetting the main branch. The same change was merged again as #51. No code diff was available to check.

prs.title: Add on-disk daily log files + log-level persistence
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: AlpacaBridge now saves its logs to one file per day on disk, so the history survives crashes and restarts. A new section in the web portal lets users view, download and delete these files. Log-level changes made in the portal are now remembered after a restart, and the old in-memory log history option was removed. The code also does things the description leaves out: it automatically deletes log files older than 90 days by default, and caps how much of a file can be viewed in the browser at once. Contrary to the description's claim of an unlimited in-memory buffer, the code no longer keeps logs in memory at all and reads today's file from disk instead. No new automated tests were added.

prs.title: Fix Alpaca discovery dying on AP-mode Wi-Fi when multicast join fails
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Astronomy apps such as NINA can now automatically find AlpacaBridge when it runs on a Raspberry Pi that hosts its own Wi-Fi hotspot. Before this fix, the search feature shut itself off completely when one optional network step failed on that kind of setup, so searches found nothing. It now logs a warning and keeps answering searches. The code change matches the description, and normal home-router setups are unaffected.

prs.title: Add ToupTek AAF focuser driver, ConformU validated x64+arm64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ToupTek's motorized focuser (the AAF), so users can control it through AlpacaBridge the same way they already control ToupTek cameras. It can move to a position, stop, report its range, and report temperature. It does not report step size or offer temperature compensation. The focuser can be chosen and saved in the web setup page, and it passed the official ASCOM compatibility checker on both regular PCs and Raspberry Pi-class hardware, with new automated tests to match.

prs.title: Mount driver cleanup: iOptron, SynScan, ASCOM contract tests
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Despite the "cleanup" title, this is a large change. iOptron and Sky-Watcher SynScan mounts are now found automatically over USB or Wi-Fi, so there is no manual port setup, and it fixes a batch of iOptron and SynScan behavior bugs, including slew-status and guiding issues. It also adds automated checks for all 12 device drivers, merges the developer docs into one place, and lets devices that fail to load show up in the web page in red so they can be removed. It also adds AI-assistant helper instructions for contributors, and the iOptron HEM27 and HAE43 mounts and the Sky-Watcher HEQ5 PRO passed the official ASCOM compatibility checker.

prs.title: Feature/player one
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for Player One astronomy cameras, including cooling, guiding, and the web setup page, and bundles the vendor's software for both regular PCs and Raspberry Pi-class hardware. It also reworks the Celestron CGX-L mount for more accurate guiding, correct side-of-meridian reporting, and better go-to accuracy, and it bumps the version to 1.0.3. The description calls the PC test of the Player One camera and the Pi test of the Celestron mount "pending," but the change includes compatibility-checker results for both.

prs.title: Feature/1.0.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The 1.0.2 release adds support for SVBONY and ToupTek cameras and adds early, unfinished work on Bisque Paramount and Celestron mounts. It also greatly expands the automated tests and makes sure the vendors' camera software gets installed so companion tools can use it. The code changes were not available for review, so this summary is based only on the description, which was itself cut off.

prs.title: SynScan V3/V4: Add Sky-Watcher HEQ5 PRO support
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Fixes Sky-Watcher SynScan mounts reporting which side of the pier the telescope is on backwards, which could confuse apps that plan meridian flips. It also renames the driver to "SynScan V3/V4" throughout the web page so users know which hand controllers are supported. The PR adds compatibility-checker results for the HEQ5 PRO mount and bumps the version to 1.0.1. The included checker results still show the old device name, so they appear to have been recorded before the rename.

prs.title: Release 1.0.0 — Linux-Only (Debian 13 Trixie)
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This is the 1.0.0 release, and AlpacaBridge now runs only on Linux (Debian 13), on standard PCs and Raspberry Pi 4/5. Windows, macOS and older Raspberry Pi support are gone, and the bundled files for those systems were deleted. It adds support for the Gemini Automatic Astro Focuser Pro and a proper Debian install package that sets itself up as a background service and includes the ZWO camera files other tools like SmartGuider need. The description also lists stability fixes for ZWO and iOptron mounts over Wi-Fi and other drivers; those code changes were too large to check here, though the refreshed test reports and new tests are present.
