prs.title: QHY Camera Support Linux x64
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The QHY268C camera is now listed as working on regular Linux PCs, in addition to Raspberry Pi, backed by a new passing compatibility test report. The code also adds a small fix the description doesn't mention: the camera now rejects zero or negative binning values with a clear error instead of accepting them. Binning is combining pixels together to produce a smaller, brighter image.

prs.title: Add QHY camera driver (v0.13.0)Feature/qhy
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds support for QHY astronomy cameras, including exposures, cooling, image size and binning options, guiding, and correct detection of color cameras. QHY cameras also appear in the setup web page, and the install scripts now handle the camera's firmware. It also fixes a freeze that could lock up imaging software like NINA, plus two other crashes, and the camera passed the standard compatibility test on Raspberry Pi. No code changes were available to confirm any of this, and the author's own checklist shows the regular Linux PC build was not yet tested.

prs.title: Feature/zwo mount
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This follow-up to ZWO AM5/AM5N mount support updates the documentation to show the mounts working on Windows, macOS and Linux, over both USB and Wi-Fi. The description presents it mainly as documentation, test and setup-page tweaks. However, the code also changes how the mount behaves: it adds a way to sync the mount's position to a known star, and handles guide-speed settings that different firmware versions report differently. It also drops the earlier warning about unreliable guiding and bundles an extra rotator library for Linux PCs.

prs.title: Feature/zwo mount
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds telescope-mount control for ZWO AM-series mounts, tested with the AM5N over a USB cable on a Mac. Users can now set up the mount from the web page, including connection type, port and network address. It passed the standard compatibility test and includes reference notes on the mount's commands, with a known firmware issue that makes mount-only guiding unreliable. The supported-hardware list was also reorganized, and it quietly marks the WeeWX weather driver as verified on Windows and Raspberry Pi, which the description doesn't mention.

prs.title: Release 0.10.0 with WeeWX observing conditions.
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: This adds weather conditions from a WeeWX home weather station, such as temperature, humidity, wind, pressure and sky darkness. The data is pulled over the network and converted to metric units. The station can be set up from the web page, passed the standard compatibility test on a Mac, and the version moves to 0.10.0. It also corrects a developer note stating that the averaging period is measured in hours, not seconds.

prs.title: Features/mounts
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for Sky-Watcher SynScan telescope mounts, so they can be connected and controlled through the bridge and set up from its web settings page. It has been checked with the official compatibility tester on an Orion Atlas EQ-G mount connected through its hand controller on an Apple Silicon Mac only, and the release moves to version 0.9.0. Beyond what the description says, the change also rewrites the internal guidelines for AI coding assistants and adds a reference manual for Losmandy Gemini mounts, which this PR does not yet support.

prs.title: Enable ImageBytes response
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Cameras can now send captured images to astronomy apps in a compact binary format when the app asks for it, instead of a much larger text-based format. This should make image downloads noticeably faster and lighter, and errors are still reported in a form apps can understand. The description only references the issue it closes, so this summary is based on the code and changelog; version moves to 0.8.4.

prs.title: Add Windows 11 x64 platform support and update to version 0.8.2
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: The bridge now officially runs on Windows 11 (64-bit), and all ZWO cameras, filter wheels, focusers, rotators and dew heaters, plus iOptron mounts, are marked as tested there. It includes Windows fixes to networking, device discovery and log timestamps, adds the Windows files needed for the ZWO rotator, and notes that ZWO cameras need ZWO's own Windows driver installed. The EAF Pro focuser was removed from the supported list because it could not be tested; version moves to 0.8.2.

prs.title: Fix iOptron WiFi connection parsing issues
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Makes iOptron telescope mounts more reliable when connected over WiFi. Some WiFi adapters add stray line-break characters or leftover status digits to the mount's replies, which could confuse the bridge when reading position, status, site or time information; these are now ignored consistently everywhere.

prs.title: Rpi5
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds Raspberry Pi 5 and other 64-bit ARM Linux support, with all ZWO devices and the iOptron mount now tested there, plus a new one-step install script that builds the bridge and sets it up to run automatically as a background service. The build now also installs the USB permission rules needed for ZWO devices on Linux, and tests run in parallel for speed. The ZWO manufacturer libraries are now bundled for many platforms, not just ARM; version moves to 0.8.1.

prs.title: Release 0.8.0: ZWO EFW Filter Wheel Driver with ConformU Validation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ZWO electronic filter wheels, so they can be connected, configured from the web settings page, and controlled by astronomy apps. It passed the official compatibility tester with no errors on an Apple Silicon Mac, and the release moves to version 0.8.0.

prs.title: Add ZWO CAA Rotator Driver and update to version 0.7.0
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ZWO's CAA camera rotator, a motorized device that turns the camera to a chosen angle. Users can now set it up, move it, stop it, and sync its angle through the web setup page. It passed the official ASCOM compatibility test with no errors on Apple Silicon Macs, and the release is version 0.7.0. The code also changes the existing ZWO focuser to report its step size as 0 instead of 1, which the description does not mention; the supported-devices list was reorganized to include placeholders for device types not yet supported.

prs.title: Release 0.6.0: ZWO EAF Focuser Driver with ConformU Validation
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ZWO's EAF and EAF Pro electronic focusers. Users can connect them over USB, set them up in the web setup page, and control focus position, movement, and stopping, as well as read the temperature. Both models passed the official ASCOM compatibility test on Apple Silicon Macs, and the release is version 0.6.0. Bluetooth on the EAF Pro is not supported yet; only USB works.

prs.title: Feature/zwo camera support
prs.author: joeytroy
prs.summary: Adds support for ZWO astronomy cameras (six models tested) and exposes the dew heater on two of those cameras as a switch that can be turned on and off. All of these passed the official ASCOM compatibility test. The server also gains a restart button in the web page, and it now fills in device numbers automatically. The code also bundles ZWO's camera software files directly into the project so nobody has to download them separately, a notable change the description does not spell out. The description's own count of changed files is also out of date (the real change is about 63 files and 9,000 added lines, not 35 and 5,850).
